findings.title: Every code-carrying alarm verb runs N argon2id derivations (measured 622 ms each) plus a full alarm_codes SELECT while holding the engine's single global mutex, stalling every zone's sensor events and countdown timers for seconds.
findings.claim: Engine.DisarmWithCode takes the engine's one global mutex at engine.go:697 (`e.mu.Lock(); defer e.mu.Unlock()`) — the mutex whose doc at engine.go:229-231 states that ALL mutating entry points (verbs, sensor events, timer fires) serialize on it. Still holding it, line 723 calls e.authorize, which at engine.go:605 calls e.validator.Validate. The validator is the codes facade (wired at internal/alarm/service.go:758 `Validator: s.codes`). codes.Facade.Validate (internal/alarm/codes/facade.go:159) first does a full table read — f.pinCandidates -> f.store.GetAll(ctx) (facade.go:176 / facade.go:337), a SQLite SELECT — and then loops every applicable enabled pin row calling VerifyPIN (facade.go:200-201). VerifyPIN (internal/alarm/codes/pin.go:55) runs argon2.IDKey with m=65536 KiB, t=1, p=4 (pin.go:63). Measured on this 4-core host: 622 ms per derivation (reproducer at $S/repro/K1/argon.go, 5 derivations in 3.109 s). A wrong code verifies ALL N candidates (no early exit); a correct code averages N/2. The same shape applies to Engine.Arm (engine.go:443), Engine.SilenceWithCode (engine.go:762) and — on the already-disarmed path — Engine.DisarmWithCode's MatchDuress call (engine.go:704 -> facade.go:243, which also loads candidates and verifies every row under the same lock). While the mutex is held, Engine.HandleSensorEvent (engine.go:866-871) blocks, and so do onStateTimerFired (engine.go:1352), onAutoRearmFired (engine.go:1777), Engine.Zones/Zone (engine.go:368/381, read by the MQTT reconcile and REST), and every other zone's Disarm/Silence. HandleSensorEvent is reached from alarm.Service.onDataPoint (internal/alarm/inputs.go:120), which runs as an event-bus handler; internal/central/events/bus.go's package doc states 'Publishing is synchronous by default; handlers run on the publisher's goroutine', so the block propagates to the publishing central's whole event dispatch (MQTT bridge, history, security domain, Matter all wait behind it).
findings.failure_scenario: A household with 5 enabled PINs on a zone. A resident comes home, the entry delay is running, and mistypes the PIN on the HA/MQTT panel. The engine holds its global mutex for ~3.1 s verifying all five hashes (each 622 ms) before returning ErrInvalidCode. During those 3.1 s: the entry-delay expiry timer cannot fire (the trigger is late by up to that amount), no sensor activation in ANY zone is processed, the countdown tick chain stalls so the SPA/WS countdown freezes, and the central's whole event fan-out is blocked. Five wrong attempts (the lockout threshold) freeze the alarm domain for ~15 s cumulatively. On a Raspberry Pi the per-derivation cost is higher still. The path is reachable by anyone who can publish to the MQTT alarm command topic (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_north.go:500).
findings.verified_by: code trace engine.go:697->723->605 -> facade.go:159,176,200 -> pin.go:63; cost measured with reproducer at $S/repro/K1/argon.go (5x argon2.IDKey m=64MiB t=1 p=4 -> 621.8 ms each)
findings.fix_sketch: Resolve the code outside the engine lock: have the REST/WS/MQTT/hardware call sites (or a thin engine wrapper) call the validator first and pass the resolved (identity, duress, refused) triple into a lock-holding verb, so e.mu is only taken after the hash work is done. Alternatively make Facade.Validate itself cheap by pre-filtering candidates (a per-row non-secret selector) and by caching the parsed rows instead of re-SELECTing per attempt.
findings.verify_reasoning: Re-derived independently and reproduced. Engine.DisarmWithCode takes e.mu (engine.go:697, `e.mu.Lock(); defer e.mu.Unlock()`) and calls e.authorize -> e.validator.Validate while still holding it; the validator is codes.Facade (wired at service.go:758 `Validator: s.codes`), whose Validate does a full alarm_codes SELECT (pinCandidates -> store.GetAll) and then argon2.IDKey per enabled PIN row (pin.go:63, m=64MiB t=1 p=4). Every other mutating entry point takes the same mutex: HandleSensorEvent (engine.go:866), onStateTimerFired (engine.go:1353), onAutoRearmFired (engine.go:1778). Measured on this 4-core host: 492.7 ms per wrong-PIN verification (finder said 622 ms; same order, host load differs). A real-engine concurrency test (engine.New via the package harness, no hand-built collaboration) shows HandleSensorEvent blocked 547 ms behind one 600 ms verification. Applicability: the alarm domain is enabled by default (Alarm.Enabled nil->true, config.go:1907) but this path costs nothing until the operator has >=1 enabled PIN row, which is the intended configuration whenever a code policy is used; cost scales linearly with PIN count and a wrong code verifies all N (no early exit). Two bounds the finding did not state, neither of which refutes it: (a) the rate limiter is checked BEFORE the candidate load (facade.go:167), so after 5 wrong attempts a source is locked out for >=60 s and further attempts are free - the MQTT-reachable DoS is bounded at ~5 x N x 0.5 s per lockout window per source; (b) events.Publish uses TryLock and defers rather than blocks (bus.go:245-278), so other publishers do not block - the central's dispatcher goroutine is stalled and its events queue, which still delays MQTT/history/security/Matter delivery for the stall duration exactly as claimed, but does not stall the south-bound callback threads.

findings.title: Stopping the alarm service cancels the smoke-sounder stop watchdog without writing INTRUSION_ALARM_OFF, leaving the only bound on an unbounded device class gone — the sounder keeps screaming after the daemon exits.
findings.claim: The smoke-sounder class has no device-side duration: internal/model/custom/siren/smoke.go:197 TurnOn writes SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND=INTRUSION_ALARM and smoke.go:209 TurnOff writes INTRUSION_ALARM_OFF — the value latches until the OFF write, and it fans out to every peer detector in the smoke group. internal/alarm/outputs/manager.go:507-529 (fireSmokeSounder) says so explicitly ('The device has no duration parameter ... the engine watchdog is the only bound') and arms m.armStopWatchdog before the activation write. alarm.Service.Stop (internal/alarm/service.go:498) calls m.StopWatchdogs(), which at watchdog.go:52-64 cancels every pending watchdog and clears m.active and m.demands WITHOUT issuing any stop write; it also drops the shared-channel demands. Nothing else stops outputs on shutdown: grepping StopAll callers shows only engine-side transitions (engine.go:800/817/839/1280/1682, restore.go:469/512) and the unrelated bridge/central registries (internal/north/bridge/registry.go:124, internal/central/central_registry.go:308). Engine.Stop (engine.go:329-347) only persists and cancels timers. So after alarm.Service.Stop the INTRUSION_ALARM stays set on the hardware indefinitely. notes/concepts/alarm-concept.md:723 asserts the opposite for this case: 'Daemon crash/restart | ... engine-sent sirens bounded per S1'.
findings.failure_scenario: A zone armed in a mode with Outputs.SmokeSounders enabled triggers; the manager writes INTRUSION_ALARM to the HmIP-SWSD group and arms a 180 s watchdog. The operator stops the daemon (add-on stop, `docker stop`, systemctl stop, an add-on update that does not come back, a crash with restart disabled) inside that window. StopWatchdogs cancels the watchdog, no OFF is written, and every smoke detector in the house keeps sounding until someone pulls the batteries or drives the OFF from the CCU by hand. A restart heals it (restore.go:393 re-fires and re-arms, or finishTriggeredOnRestore issues StopAll), so the permanent case is a daemon that stays down — which is exactly the state an operator reaches for when they want the noise to stop.
findings.verified_by: code trace service.go:498 -> watchdog.go:52-64 (no stop write) with manager.go:507-529 and internal/model/custom/siren/smoke.go:197/209 establishing that the class has no device-side auto-off; cross-checked against notes/concepts/alarm-concept.md:723
findings.fix_sketch: Give Manager a Shutdown(ctx) that, for every entry in m.active whose class is AlarmOutputClassSmokeSounder (and arguably AlarmLight), issues the class stopper's stop write at critical priority before cancelling the timer; call it from alarm.Service.Stop instead of (or before) StopWatchdogs. Keep the existing cancel-only path for the shared-channel arbitration reset.
findings.verify_reasoning: Traced end to end and searched hard for a second stop path; there is none. SmokeSiren.TurnOn writes SMOKE_DETECTOR_COMMAND=INTRUSION_ALARM and only TurnOff writes INTRUSION_ALARM_OFF (siren/smoke.go:197,209); the class has no device-side duration (corroborated independently against the reference implementation: aiohomematic/model/custom/siren.py:68-69 exposes exactly the same two commands and no duration for this device), so manager.go:503-506's own comment - 'the engine watchdog is the only bound' - is the whole safety story. alarm.Service.Stop (service.go:498) calls Manager.StopWatchdogs, which cancels every pending timer and clears m.active and m.demands with no stop write (watchdog.go:52-64). Engine.Stop (engine.go:329-347) only persists and cancels timers. I enumerated every StopAll caller: engine-side transitions and restore only - no shutdown caller anywhere in cmd/. The shutdown path really is a clean one: daemon.go:375 registers alarmSvc as a north bridge and daemon.go:420 defers northBridges.StopAll, so Service.Stop runs on SIGTERM/`docker stop`/add-on stop, cancels the only bound, and exits with the sounder latched. A SIGKILL reaches the same end state by a different route. Configuration: NON-DEFAULT - OutputPolicy.SmokeSounders is opt-in per mode (engine/config.go:161, zero value false, gated at manager.go:562). Severity kept at high rather than lowered for the non-default gate: the harm is physical and house-wide (the command fans out to the whole smoke group), the recovery path an operator reaches for first (stop the daemon) is the very action that removes the bound, and notes/concepts/alarm-concept.md:723 promises the opposite ('engine-sent sirens bounded per S1'). A restart heals it (restore.go:469/512), so the permanent case is a daemon that stays down.

findings.title: An enrolled sensor whose device disappears from the CCU model keeps available=true and its last activation value forever — the zone reports ready-to-arm and arms with a member sensor that can never fire, and no journal, health or readiness surface says so.
findings.claim: sensorState is created with available:true (engine/restore.go:143 and engine/reload.go:161). The only writers of that field are Engine.SetSensorAvailability (engine.go:1015) and Engine.HandleCentralConnectivity (engine.go:1078). SetSensorAvailability is called from exactly two places, both in internal/alarm/inputs.go: line 130, driven by UNREACH / STICKY_UNREACH data-point events on the device, and line 240, re-asserting per-interface truth after a central-wide restore. HandleCentralConnectivity fires only on a whole-central reachability transition (inputs.go:227-230), and allEnrolledDownLocked (inputs.go:259) requires EVERY enrolled interface of the central to be down. alarm.Service.attachUnit (inputs.go:66-101) subscribes to DataPointValueChangedEvent, ConnectivityChangedEvent, SysvarChangedEvent and CentralSouthboundReadyEvent — there is NO DeviceRemovedEvent subscription anywhere under internal/alarm (grep confirms the only DeviceRemovedEvent subscriber in the two domains is internal/security/subscribe.go:96). A deleted device emits no UNREACH, so nothing ever flips available to false. The restore/refresh reads degrade silently too: sensorReader.CurrentActive (internal/alarm/resolver.go:158-166) returns (false,false) when u.GetChannel returns nil, and engine.refreshSensorValues (restore.go:572-582) only overwrites on known==true, so the stale value survives. readinessDetail (engine/readiness.go:77) then sees s.available==true and s.active==false, classifies no blocker, and Ready stays true. notes/concepts/alarm-concept.md:725 promises the opposite for this row: 'Single sensor lost while armed | Per-sensor trigger_when_unavailable or warn; health badge; journal.'
findings.failure_scenario: A window contact enrolled in the 'away' mode is unpaired/deleted from the CCU (or re-paired and gets a new address, or is simply absent from the model after a CCU factory-restore). The alarm SPA and MQTT keep showing the zone Ready. The household arms 'away' and leaves. That window is unmonitored: no activation can ever arrive on the removed data point, the readiness verdict never listed it as unreachable, the default Blockers.Unreachable=block policy never engaged, no fault-class journal entry was written, and /api/v1/health reports the alarm component healthy. The break-in through that window produces no alarm and no trace.
findings.verified_by: code trace: writers of sensorState.available (engine.go:1015/1078) vs callers (inputs.go:130/240) — no device-removal path; resolver.go:158-166 + restore.go:572-582 show the stale value is preserved; readiness.go:77 shows Ready stays true; grep for DeviceRemovedEvent across internal/alarm returns nothing
findings.fix_sketch: Subscribe the alarm service to DeviceRemovedEvent / DeviceCreatedEvent per central (same seam as internal/security/subscribe.go:95-96) and, on removal, call Engine.SetSensorAvailability(id,false) for every enrolled sensor of that device; symmetrically restore on re-create. Belt-and-braces: have refreshSensorValues distinguish 'channel missing from the model' from 'no value yet' and mark the sensor unavailable in the first case, so a boot against a model that lacks the channel also blocks the arm.
findings.verify_reasoning: Every writer of sensorState.available is engine.go:1025 (SetSensorAvailability) and engine.go:1078 (HandleCentralConnectivity); the initial value is `available: true` at restore.go:143 and reload.go:161, so it is re-asserted true on every boot too. The only callers are inputs.go:130 (UNREACH / STICKY_UNREACH data-point events), inputs.go:240/252 (per-interface re-assertion after a central-wide reachability transition) and inputs.go:230 (whole-central transition, which requires every enrolled interface of the central to be down, inputs.go:259). I looked for the availability writer other than UNREACH the brief asks about: there is none. attachUnit (inputs.go:66-101) subscribes to exactly four event types - DataPointValueChanged, ConnectivityChanged, SysvarChanged, CentralSouthboundReady - and grep confirms no DeviceRemovedEvent / DeviceCreatedEvent subscriber anywhere under internal/alarm (the only domain subscriber is internal/security/subscribe.go:96). A removed device emits no UNREACH, so nothing flips the flag. The refresh path degrades silently in the same direction: sensorReader.CurrentActive returns known=false when GetChannel is nil (resolver.go:163-166) and refreshSensorValues only overwrites when known (restore.go:572-582), so the last-seen value survives. computeReadiness then sees available==true and active==false and records no blocker, so Ready stays true (readiness.go:64-84,98). No FK or cascade deletes the alarm_sensors row on device removal (migration 027 has none; no production caller deletes sensor rows), so the enrollment survives forever. Configuration: DEFAULT - Blockers.Unreachable defaults to `block` (config.go:170-172), i.e. the defect defeats the default protective policy rather than needing a non-default one.

findings.title: A MASTER-paramset value change is never re-published to any push plane: the MQTT master state topic and the WS stream keep the boot-time value forever
findings.claim: The MASTER plane is a full read/write MQTT surface. Boot publishes it: internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:765-767 calls registerAndLoadDP(..., hmenum.ParamsetKeyMaster) for every MASTER DP, which emits HA discovery (a writable number/switch/select with entity_category=config -- pinned by internal/north/mqtt/entity_category_master_test.go) plus the retained slot topic channels/<n>/master/<param>/state (bucket selected at eventbridge.go:1865). Writes work in both directions: internal/north/mqtt/command_subscriber.go:849 routes .../master/<param>/set to MQTTCommandSink.SetMasterValue (internal/central/adapter/mqtt_sink.go:203-231, ch.Set with hmenum.ParamsetKeyMaster), and REST/MCP write through ParamsetsDomain.PutParamset (internal/central/adapter/paramsets.go:140). But NOTHING re-publishes the state after a change. (1) The only runtime producer of hmevent.DataPointValueChangedEvent is the CCU push path, internal/central/coordinators/event.go:177-181, which hard-codes ParamsetKey: hmenum.ParamsetKeyValues before publishing at :221 -- so a MASTER key can never appear on the bus. (2) The CCU emits no event() callback for MASTER writes at all. (3) After the write, internal/central/adapter/paramsets.go:321-355 refreshAfterPut only calls dp.OnWireValue(v) on the model; no generic data point's OnUpdate is bridged to the event bus -- grep of every OnUpdate( registration under internal/central (device_pipeline.go:1439/1443, hub_mqtt_publisher.go, combined_bridge.go, eventbridge.go:3272/3318/3365) shows bridges for calculated sensors, hub entities and combined DPs only. (4) The CONFIG_PENDING settle hook (internal/central/adapter/auto_refresh.go:89-128) reloads week profiles and writes the MASTER cache to SQLite but publishes nothing north-bound, and it is HmIP-only. (5) The three publishSlotState call sites are eventbridge.go:1027 and :1115 (boot/unobserved) and :1414, reached only from publishValueChangedMQTT on a bus event -- i.e. VALUES only. The comment at eventbridge.go:757-764 asserting 'Subsequent MASTER edits flow through the configuration coordinator's regular bus events so the runtime case is covered' is refuted: internal/central/coordinators/configuration.go contains no events.Publish call at all.
findings.failure_scenario: A user has HA discovery on. HmIP-BWTH exposes MASTER TEMPERATURE_OFFSET as an HA number entity built from channels/1/master/TEMPERATURE_OFFSET/state with optimistic:false (internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:669/690/790/846/890). The user drags the number in HA from -1.0 to 0.5. The command reaches SetMasterValue, the CCU accepts the write, the model is updated by refreshAfterPut -- and the retained state topic is never re-written, so HA's number snaps straight back to -1.0 and stays there until the daemon restarts. The same happens for every MASTER switch (INHIBIT) and select. Editing the same parameter in the OpenCCU-Loom SPA has the identical effect on HA, and a second SPA tab shows the old value too because no WS frame is broadcast either.
findings.verified_by: code trace: eventbridge.go:757-767 + :1414 + :1865, coordinators/event.go:177-221, coordinators/configuration.go (no events.Publish), paramsets.go:140-190 + :321-355, mqtt_sink.go:203-231, command_subscriber.go:849, auto_refresh.go:89-128, exhaustive grep of OnUpdate( registrations under internal/central
findings.fix_sketch: Publish a DataPointValueChangedEvent with ParamsetKey=MASTER from refreshAfterPut / the MASTER write path (or bridge each MASTER DP's OnUpdate onto the bus in wireDataPointLifecycle, which already walks ch.MasterDataPoints()). onValueChanged already routes the MASTER bucket correctly, so the whole fan-out follows for free. Add a round-trip guard in internal/north/mqtt/ asserting every declared master state_topic is re-published after a write.
findings.verify_reasoning: Re-derived independently and hunted for every second path. (a) Producers of hmevent.DataPointValueChangedEvent are exactly 7 non-test sites; all hard-code ParamsetKeyValues (coordinators/event.go:180, device_pipeline.go:1427 calculated, eventbridge.go:801/999/1027/1115 boot snapshot) or ParamsetKeyCombined (combined_bridge.go:78). None can carry MASTER. (b) internal/central/coordinators/configuration.go contains zero events.Publish calls (grep over the whole 286-line file), so the eventbridge.go:757-764 comment ('subsequent MASTER edits flow through the configuration coordinator's regular bus events') is refuted. (c) The write paths end in the model: MQTTCommandSink.SetMasterValue -> ch.Set(MASTER) and ParamsetsDomain.PutParamset -> ch.SetMany + refreshAfterPut -> dp.OnWireValue. internal/model/device and internal/model/generic import no event bus at all (no events.Publish / hmevent construction anywhere under internal/model/device), and the only datapoint.EventPublisher installed in production is the week-profile one (device_pipeline.go:1604) - no generic or MASTER DP ever gets a publisher. (d) MASTER DPs receive exactly two lifecycle hooks (device_pipeline.go:1504 rollback bridge, :1593 availability provider); the rollback bridge fires only when the write FAILS. (e) Second-path candidates checked and eliminated: the CONFIG_PENDING settle hook (auto_refresh.go:89-146 -> refreshDeviceMasterCache:179-216) only calls applyMasterValuesToChannel + SQLite save, no publish, and is HmIP-only; the DataPointSourceChangedEvent path (values_source_lifecycle.go:56) does carry key.ParamsetKey into eventbridge.onSourceChanged:490, but walkWireDPs (values_source_lifecycle.go:118-141) iterates ch.DataPoints() only - MASTER DPs are excluded, so not even a reconnect re-emits MASTER; DeviceCoordinator.CheckParamsetConsistency (device.go:1014-1078) only reports, never applies; PublishInitialSnapshot has no periodic trigger (call sites: daemon.go:295/347, daemon_southbound.go:401, reload_deps.go:74 - boot, southbound-ready, MQTT reload, broker reconnect); the WS plane has no paramset broadcast at all and ws sessionSaveHandler (commands_default.go:1729-1783) returns the applied map without publishing anything. (f) The consumer side is as described: MASTER DPs are discovered as writable HA entities in the master bucket with optimistic=false (discovery.go:471, 571, 637, 788-790, 844-845) and entity_category=config, and the command topic .../master/<param>/set routes to SetMasterValue (command_subscriber.go:845-859). So an HA write is accepted, the CCU applies it, and the retained state topic keeps the boot value until a daemon restart / broker reconnect / MQTT config reload. Severity stays high: it is a documented read/write plane where every write silently reverts in the consumer UI.

findings.title: The readiness interface tally is written once at bring-up and never afterwards, so after 0.61.3 an interface that recovers leaves the central permanently reporting "ready, N-1/N"
findings.claim: Before 0.61.3 the ready event always carried `len(cc.Interfaces)` for both numbers, so the pair was trivially self-consistent for the whole life of the daemon. 0.61.3 replaced the first number with the boot-time `loaded` tally (internal/central/adapter/ccu_wiring.go:272) but did not add any producer that updates it later. `recordCentralReadiness` / `Unit.SetReadiness` are called from exactly four places, all inside the bring-up path or the waiting gate (ccu_wiring.go:272, 313, 370, 434, 463 - verified by grepping every caller of `recordCentralReadiness` and `SetReadiness` in non-test code); nothing in the recovery pipeline, the reconciler or the hot-plug ingestor touches readiness. An interface whose boot ingest exhausted is deliberately left DISCONNECTED so the recovery pipeline can repair it (that is the stated purpose of `runXMLRPCActivation`'s DISCONNECTED walk, ccu_wiring.go:1296-1308) - and the pipeline does repair it: `RecoveryStageDeps.Reconnect` re-runs init()+callback registration (ccu_wiring.go:945-953), after which the CCU's `newDevices` push reaches the hot-plug ingestor installed at ccu_wiring.go:481. The interface then serves devices while the readiness pair stays at its boot value.
findings.failure_scenario: A CCU with two interfaces boots; one interface's RPC service is still warming up and its ingest exhausts the 5 retries. Thirty seconds later the recovery pipeline reconnects it and its devices materialise. GET /system/ccu, the `central.readiness.changed` WebSocket push and the SPA's central status badge report `ready - 1/2 interfaces` for as long as the daemon runs; only a restart clears it. The operator is told a healthy central is half-dark.
findings.verified_by: code trace: exhaustive grep of `recordCentralReadiness` / `SetReadiness` callers (all in internal/central/adapter/ccu_wiring.go, none post-bring-up); recovery path ccu_wiring.go:894-962 + hot-plug ingestor ccu_wiring.go:470-486
findings.fix_sketch: Recompute the tally from live state instead of latching a boot counter - e.g. re-emit `recordCentralReadiness(ReadinessReady, <interfaces with >0 devices in unit.ModelRegistry>, total)` from the recovery-completed handler and from the hot-plug ingest, or derive `interfaces_loaded` on read from the model registry rather than storing it.

findings.title: The HmIP-MP3P status-LED dispatcher entry routes through the embedded FixedColorLight, so the LED's own TurnOn/TurnOff (COLOR, ON_TIME_LIST_1, REPETITIONS, ON_TIME) are still dead code and a turn_on writes LEVEL only
findings.claim: 0.61.3 added `if l, ok := dp.(*light.SoundPlayerLED); ok { return d.dispatchFixedColorLight(ctx, l.FixedColorLight, ...) }` (internal/central/adapter/custom_dp_dispatcher.go:184-186) and the CHANGELOG claims "HmIP-DRG-DALI / HmIP-MP3P-LED are controllable again". `dispatchFixedColorLight` handles only `set_color` and rejects `set_color_temperature`/`set_effect`; every other operation falls through to `d.dispatchLight(ctx, l.Light, ...)` (custom_dp_dispatcher.go:421), whose `turn_on` is `l.TurnOn(ctx, prio)` on the base `*light.Light` (custom_dp_dispatcher.go:269). `Light.TurnOn` (internal/model/custom/light/light.go:573-608) ends in `SetLevel(turnOnLevel())` - LEVEL only. `SoundPlayerLED` is not a plain FixedColorLight: it overrides `TurnOn(ctx, cfg LedOnConfig, w, addr, prio)` and `TurnOff(ctx, w, addr, prio)` with different signatures (internal/model/custom/light/sound_led.go:167 and :197) which write LEVEL+COLOR(+WHITE fallback via currentColorOrWhite)+ON_TIME_LIST_1+REPETITIONS+RAMP_TIME+ON_TIME, resp. COLOR=BLACK+ON_TIME=0, in one put_paramset. Because the dispatcher hands the *embedded* pointer down, those two methods plus `Flash`, `AvailableOnTimes` and `AvailableRepetitions` have zero production callers - verified by grepping the whole non-test tree for `LedOnConfig`, `.Flash(`, `AvailableOnTimes`, `AvailableRepetitions`: the only hits outside sound_led.go belong to siren/textdisplay. The reference implementation confirms the intended wire shape: `CustomDpSoundPlayerLed.turn_on` in ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/light.py:885-937 sends level, color, on_time_list, repetitions, ramp_time and on_time, and `turn_off` (:872-882) sends level=0, color=BLACK, on_time=0.
findings.failure_scenario: The MP3P status LED sits at COLOR=BLACK (its power-on default, and the value the CCU/WebUI writes to switch it off). Home Assistant sends the light `turn_on`; the daemon writes LEVEL=1.0 and nothing else, the LED stays dark, and HA reports the light as on. Separately, an LED previously put into a flashing pattern keeps its ON_TIME_LIST_1/REPETITIONS across a plain turn_on (it flashes instead of lighting steadily), and a turn_off leaves a running ON_TIME timer that switches the LED again later - both of which the type's own TurnOn/TurnOff were written to prevent.
findings.verified_by: code trace: custom_dp_dispatcher.go:184-186 -> :421 -> :269 -> internal/model/custom/light/light.go:573-608; dead-code grep for the SoundPlayerLED-specific API; reference comparison against ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/light.py:837-937
findings.fix_sketch: Add a `dispatchSoundPlayerLED` that maps `turn_on`/`set_level(state=ON)` onto `SoundPlayerLED.TurnOn(ctx, LedOnConfig{...}, l.Writer, l.Address(), prio)` (brightness/hs_color/on_time/ramp_time/repetitions/flash_time from params) and `turn_off`/`set_level(state=OFF)` onto `SoundPlayerLED.TurnOff`, delegating only the remaining operations to the embedded FixedColorLight path - the same shape `dispatchDRGDaliLight` uses for `set_effect`.
findings.verify_reasoning: Traced independently and it holds. custom_dp_dispatcher.go:180-186 hands the embedded l.FixedColorLight to dispatchFixedColorLight, whose switch handles only set_color and rejects set_color_temperature/set_effect; every other operation falls to `d.dispatchLight(ctx, l.Light, ...)` (custom_dp_dispatcher.go:418-422), whose turn_on is Light.TurnOn (custom_dp_dispatcher.go:266-270) ending in SetLevel(turnOnLevel()) — LEVEL only (internal/model/custom/light/light.go:573-608). An exhaustive non-test grep for LedOnConfig, .Flash(, AvailableOnTimes, AvailableRepetitions and SoundPlayerLED finds no production caller of SoundPlayerLED.TurnOn/TurnOff/Flash/AvailableOnTimes/AvailableRepetitions (the AvailableRepetitions hits belong to siren and textdisplay). The reference confirms the intended wire shape: ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/light.py:872-882 (turn_off: level=0, COLOR=BLACK, on_time=0) and :885-937 (turn_on: level, colour defaulting to WHITE when the current colour is in _NO_COLOR, on_time_list, repetitions, ramp_time, on_time). Two refinements to the finder's framing, neither of which weakens it: (a) the same LEVEL-only turn_on already applies to a plain FixedColorLight and to the MQTT service plane (registerLightServices at internal/model/custom/light/payload.go:223-229, invoked via Source.Invoke from internal/north/mqtt/command_subscriber.go), so 0.61.3 turned a hard 'unsupported data point type' error on REST/WS into a partially-correct write rather than introducing a regression; (b) FixedColorLight.TurnOnFixedColor (color.go:670) is likewise dead. So this is an incomplete fix plus dead type-specific API, and the CHANGELOG's 'controllable again' overstates what landed.

findings.title: The 423 handling change makes every locked-channel write show an untranslated English REST path instead of the localized channel-lock guidance, and leaves `api.error.locked` unreachable in production
findings.claim: friendlyError's 423 branch now reads `const reason = err.problemDetail || err.problemTitle` and, when either is present, returns ``${t("api.error.locked_reason", {status})} — ${reason}`` (client.ts:2538-2542); the localized `api.error.locked` text is returned only when the body carries neither. Every 423 the daemon can emit carries both: internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:852-856 (`writeChannelLocked`) sends title `Channel locked` and detail `"the channel is locked against control writes; lift the lock via PUT /devices/{addr}/channels/{no}/flags"`; internal/north/rest/handlers/paramsets.go:44-47 sends `Edit lock required` + `"hold an edit session (<key>) and present its token via X-Edit-Token"`; internal/north/rest/handlers/session.go:173-174 sends `Resource already locked`. `problem.New(t, r, title, detail)` maps arg3->title and arg4->detail (internal/north/rest/problem/problem.go:85-90). So the `api.error.locked` branch is dead code, and the channel-lock case — the one the removed comment explicitly protected ('the daemon's detail names the REST path that lifts the lock, which is the wrong instruction for someone looking at the SPA') — now renders exactly that path. The new fix's own unit test only exercises the dead branch by passing a bare string body (`errorFrom(423, "")`, client.test.ts), a shape the daemon never produces.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator uses a control tile on a channel whose control-write lock is set. assets/ui/src/lib/control/ChannelControl.svelte:107-124 (and AutoTile.svelte:132/156, ActionButton, TogglePill, NumericActionFeature) catch the error and toast `friendlyError(err, t)`. With the German locale the toast now reads `Gesperrt (423). — the channel is locked against control writes; lift the lock via PUT /devices/{addr}/channels/{no}/flags` — an English sentence with a raw URL template and literal `{addr}`/`{no}` placeholders. Before the change it read the localized, actionable `Gesperrt — dieser Kanal ist gegen Steuerbefehle gesperrt. Die Sperre lässt sich in den Kanal-Flags aufheben.` (i18n.ts:7305-7306). findings.title: `SecuritySourceView.override_included` was added to the DTO/OpenAPI but the only consumer still guesses from `relevant`, so the silent-re-exclusion the field exists to prevent is still live in the SPA
findings.claim: Commit 3914578d does both halves of this in one change and only lands one. Server side: pkg/hmapi/security.go:135-140 adds `OverrideIncluded *bool json:"override_included,omitempty"`, internal/north/rest/handlers/security.go:366-369 fills it when `s.Overridden`, internal/security/index.go:402 sources it from `override.Included`, and assets/openapi.yaml + types.generated.ts document it. Client side, the same commit rewrites freshDraft to `included: !s.overridden || s.relevant` (SecuritySources.svelte:118) and adds a comment stating 'SecuritySourceView does not carry the stored override's raw `included` bit ... exposing the raw bit on the DTO would remove that ambiguity' (SecuritySources.svelte:106-113) — a claim the same commit falsified. The residual ambiguity is reachable: internal/security/index.go:225-296 computes `excluded = override.Parameter != "" && !override.Included`, so for an override row with `Class == ""` and `Included == true` (a note-only override, which SetSourceOverride persists because index.go:426-429 only deletes on `class == "" && included && note == ""`) the switch falls to the `default:` arm and sets `src.relevant = cls.Class.Hazard() || deviceRelevant` — false for a non-hazard class on a device with no alarm role. The view then reports `overridden=true, relevant=false, override_included=true`, and freshDraft computes `!true || false = false`.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator adds a note ('known false positive') to a `problem`- or `tamper`-class source on a device that is not enrolled in any alarm zone, leaving class blank and the Included switch on. The save persists `{included:true, note:"…"}`. On the next load of Security -> Sources the Included switch for that row is rendered OFF, because relevant=false. The operator edits the note again, or picks a class, and clicks Save: saveOverride (SecuritySources.svelte:132-141) sends `included: d.included` = false. The source is now genuinely excluded — internal/security/index.go:294-296 forces `relevant=false` and it drops out of every security aggregate, fault surface and alarm evaluation — without the operator ever touching the switch.
findings.verified_by: code trace across both halves: pkg/hmapi/security.go:131-141, internal/north/rest/handlers/security.go:355-370, internal/security/index.go:225-296 and :396-404, assets/ui/src/routes/security/SecuritySources.svelte:101-141; `grep -rn override_included assets/ui/src` matches only types.generated.ts. The three new SecuritySources.test.ts cases cover only the unambiguous combinations (overridden+relevant=false, not overridden+relevant=true), so nothing catches the note-only override.
findings.fix_sketch: In freshDraft use `included: s.override_included ?? !s.overridden` and drop the `relevant` proxy plus the now-false comment; add a vitest case for `{overridden:true, relevant:false, override_included:true}` asserting the switch renders ON.

findings.title: The system_health not-ready sentinel is suppressed on both REST surfaces and on MQTT but still leaves the daemon raw on the `hub.metrics_changed` WebSocket broadcast, which declares the value as a percentage
findings.claim: The wave suppresses the negative sentinel on three of four north-bound surfaces: internal/north/rest/handlers/system_hub.go:210 (`ok && s.Value >= 0`), internal/north/rest/handlers/hub_data_points.go:135-137 (`continue` on `sample.Value < 0`), and internal/north/mqtt/bridge.go:1508-1516 (clears the retained topic). The WS broadcast was not touched: internal/north/rest/ws/hub_events.go:487-499 subscribes with `hm.Metrics.OnAny(...)` and forwards `Value: sample.Value` verbatim together with `Unit: hubmodel.MetricSensorUnit(sample.Kind)` = `"%"`. The sentinel is genuinely observed through that callback chain: internal/central/coordinators/reconciler.go:374-386 (`emitNotReadyHealth`) calls `r.Metrics.Observe(hub.MetricSystemHealth, hub.MetricSystemHealthUnknown)` (= -1.0, internal/model/hub/metrics.go:32), and internal/model/hub/metrics.go:67-92 fires every `anySubs` callback whenever the value changed. assets/openapi.yaml's `HubMetricChangedPayload` declares `value: {type: number}` with `unit` documented as `"%"` and no sentinel semantics, so a conforming client has no way to know -1 means 'unknown'. The reconciler's own comment (reconciler.go:355-357) claims the sentinel is one 'which the consumers render as unknown' — true for REST and MQTT after this wave, false for the WS plane.
findings.failure_scenario: A CCU goes offline. The central turns FAILED, EmitNotReady demotes system_health from e.g. 97 to -1, and every WebSocket subscriber on topic `hub.<central>.metrics` receives `{"central":"ccu1","metric":"system_health","value":-1,"unit":"%"}`. A client that mirrors the metric onto a gauge (the documented consumer contract in docs/external-clients/topic-hierarchy.md:262) shows -1 % rather than 'unknown' — precisely the 'frozen/bogus value' failure the 0.61.3 fix was written to remove — while the same daemon's REST and MQTT surfaces correctly report the metric as absent.
findings.verified_by: code trace: internal/north/rest/ws/hub_events.go:487-499; internal/model/hub/metrics.go:32 + :67-92 (Observe fans out to anySubs on change); internal/central/coordinators/reconciler.go:366-386; contrasted against the three surfaces that were fixed. The user-visible rendering depends on the external client (openccu-loom-client / the HA integration are out of tree and were not inspected), so the -1 on the wire is measured from source, the downstream gauge value is inferred from the declared schema.
findings.fix_sketch: In hub_events.go's Metrics.OnAny callback, skip publishing (or publish an explicit null/`unknown` marker) when `sample.Kind == hubmodel.MetricSystemHealth && sample.Value < 0`, matching system_hub.go and hub_data_points.go; document the chosen representation on HubMetricChangedPayload.

findings.title: The new central-scoped branch of the WS config-session paramset write bypasses descriptor coercion, min/max validation, the post-write model refresh and the audit row that the domain path performs
findings.claim: wsParamsetWriter.PutParamset (cmd/openccu-loom/ws_adapters.go:1117-1128) now routes around adapter.ParamsetsDomain whenever `key.CentralName != firstMatchCentralName(...)`, calling `b.PutParamset(ctx, addr, psKey, values, CommandPriorityHigh, CommandRxModeUnset)` on the raw backend. The domain method it replaces (internal/central/adapter/paramsets.go:140-191) does four things this branch does not: (1) `anyMapToParamValues(ch, key, values)` converts the wire map against the parameter DESCRIPTOR — its own doc at paramsets.go:567 states 'JSON draws no int/float distinction', which is exactly why it exists; (2) `validateParamsetValues` for the no-channel case; (3) `p.refreshAfterPut(...)` re-reads authoritative values into the model so the SPA sees post-write state; (4) `p.recordParamsetWrite(...)` writes the audit/change-log row with per-parameter before/after. Values reaching this path come from the `config.session.save` WS command as decoded JSON, so an INTEGER MASTER parameter arrives as Go `float64`; internal/central/adapter/xmlrpc_caller.go:79-80 encodes `float64` as `<double>`, which the CCU rejects for an INTEGER parameter. The visibility check the branch does keep (`w.domain.VisibleValues`) resolves the channel through ParamsetsDomain.resolveChannelInfo (paramsets.go:504-522), i.e. through the FIRST-match central, not the scoped one. Reachability: only `config.session.save` carries a CentralName (cmd/openccu-loom/ws_adapters.go:137 -> wsSessionBackend); `paramset.put` builds `configui.SessionKey{ChannelAddress, ParamsetKey}` with no central (internal/north/rest/ws/commands_extended.go:731) and always takes the domain path.
findings.failure_scenario: A two-CCU operator opens the config editor for a channel whose address exists on both CCUs — which is the normal case for the virtual-remote buses (BidCoS-RF:*, HmIP-RCV-1:*), the INT000* internal devices and CUxD devices, all documented in internal/routingkey/uniqueid.go as repeating verbatim on every CCU — on the alphabetically-second CCU, and saves a MASTER change. The write leaves no row in the change history (so 'who changed this' is unanswerable for exactly the multi-CCU case), the editor keeps showing the pre-write values because nothing refreshes the model, and an INTEGER parameter is sent to the CCU as an XML-RPC <double>, which faults instead of applying.
findings.verified_by: code trace: ws_adapters.go:1108-1128 vs internal/central/adapter/paramsets.go:140-191 and :483-498; float64 -> <double> at internal/central/adapter/xmlrpc_caller.go:79-80; reachability via ws_adapters.go:137 (SessionBackend) and internal/north/rest/ws/commands_extended.go:731 (paramset.put carries no central).
findings.fix_sketch: Give ParamsetsDomain a central-scoped variant (GetParamsetOn/PutParamsetOn(centralName, ...)) that reuses the whole domain body with a scoped backend/channel resolution, and have wsParamsetWriter/wsDeviceQuery call that instead of writing directly to backends.Operations.
findings.verify_reasoning: The bypass is real and I found no compensating layer below it. wsParamsetWriter.PutParamset (cmd/openccu-loom/ws_adapters.go:1102-1129) keeps only the visibility gate and then calls b.PutParamset on the raw backend resolved by scopedParamsetBackend (ws_adapters.go:1137-1158), which returns writer.Backend(...) — a plain backends.Operations with no coercion, no validation, no model write. The domain method it replaces does four further things: anyMapToParamValues descriptor coercion, validateParamsetValues for the no-channel case, refreshAfterPut, and recordParamsetWrite with per-parameter before/after (internal/central/adapter/paramsets.go:140-190). The wire claim also checks out as far as it can be checked statically: CcuBackend.PutParamset -> putParamsetViaCaller -> caller.CallAt (backends/ccu.go:189-194, backends/wire_shared.go:147-161) and goToXMLRPCValue maps float64 to xmlrpc.DoubleValue (internal/central/adapter/xmlrpc_caller.go:79-80), while session values are decoded JSON (`Value any` in sessionMutateArgs, ws/commands_default.go:1592) i.e. float64 for every number. NOT verified by me: that a real CCU faults on <double> for an INTEGER MASTER parameter — that needs a live write and is out of scope; the domain's own doc ('JSON draws no int/float distinction') and aiohomematic's typed send path are strong circumstantial support, no more. Reachability is narrower than the headline: the branch runs only when key.CentralName != firstMatchCentralName(...), i.e. multi-CCU with the same device address on two centrals and the scoped one not first in name-sorted registry order (the virtual-remote/INT000x/CUxD addresses that repeat verbatim per CCU), or when the device is in no registry at all — where scopedParamsetBackend errors out instead. Medium stands: the lost audit row is exactly for the multi-CCU case where 'which CCU did this change land on' matters most.

findings.title: Wiring EditLocks into the MCP server made MASTER paramset writes permanently impossible over MCP, because MCP exposes no tool to open an edit session or obtain an edit token
findings.claim: mountMCP now passes `EditLocks: d.editSessions` (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest_mount.go:703-706). internal/north/mcp/tools.go:549-555 therefore runs `d.EditLocks.Verify("channel:"+address+":"+key, strings.TrimSpace(in.EditToken))` for MASTER and LINK writes, and internal/north/rest/handlers/session.go:113-115 returns false immediately for an empty token and otherwise only for a live lock held by exactly that token. The MCP tool inventory (internal/north/mcp/tools.go: list_centrals, list_devices, get_device, list_audit, list_incidents, read_paramset, get_health, set_datapoint, write_paramset, trigger_program) contains no session-open / lock-acquire tool, so an MCP client has no way to produce a valid `edit_token`. Before this commit `d.EditLocks` was nil and the gate was skipped entirely (the comment at tools.go:548 calls nil 'a test-only escape hatch'), so MASTER writes worked. The tool's own description still advertises 'Write a device paramset (MASTER configuration or VALUES state)'.
findings.failure_scenario: An assistant driving the daemon over MCP calls write_paramset with key=MASTER (e.g. to change a thermostat's MASTER configuration). It always fails with 'edit lock required for MASTER write on <addr>; open an edit session and pass edit_token' — an instruction the assistant cannot follow, because MCP offers no session tool. The advertised MASTER half of the tool is dead for every MCP consumer; only VALUES writes still work.
findings.verified_by: code trace: daemon_rest_mount.go:700-707 -> internal/north/mcp/server.go:116-120 -> internal/north/mcp/tools.go:522,548-555 -> internal/north/rest/handlers/session.go:113-121; MCP tool name inventory enumerated by grep over internal/north/mcp/tools.go (`Name:` literals) — no open/close-session tool exists.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `open_edit_session` / `close_edit_session` MCP tools (thin wrappers over EditSessions.Open/Close, admin-gated like write_paramset) so an assistant can acquire the token the gate demands, or let write_paramset acquire-and-release the lock itself when it is currently free.
findings.verify_reasoning: Verified once for both units; both framings are accurate. mountMCP wires EditLocks: d.editSessions unconditionally (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest_mount.go:703-707; d.editSessions is created in daemon.go:713 and never nil in production), so the nil escape hatch documented at mcp/server.go:114-119 is test-only. registerWriteParamset then requires d.EditLocks.Verify("channel:"+address+":"+key, edit_token) for MASTER and LINK (internal/north/mcp/tools.go:546-556), and EditSessions.Verify returns false for an empty token and otherwise only for a live lock held by exactly that token (internal/north/rest/handlers/session.go:113-123). I enumerated every registered MCP tool name from the source (26 entries: list_centrals, list_devices, list_channels, get_device, read_paramset, write_paramset, set_datapoint, list_sysvars, list_programs, trigger_program, list_rooms, list_functions, get_health, get_system_info, list_audit, list_incidents, list_inbox, list_service_messages, list_alarm_zones, list_alarm_messages, arm_alarm_zone, disarm_alarm_zone, reset_motion, list_triggered_motion, get_security_status) — there is no open/close-edit-session tool and no second token source on the MCP surface. git confirms the regression: EditLocks first appears in the MCP Deps in 3914578d, so before it the gate was skipped entirely. Two qualifiers worth recording, neither of which refutes anything: the lock key format is byte-identical across REST (handlers/paramsets.go:101), WS (ws/commands_extended.go:726) and MCP, so a token minted out of band over REST/WS does satisfy the MCP gate — an MCP-only client still cannot mint one; and the whole path is behind north.mcp.allow_writes (default false), so this is a dead capability on an opt-in surface, which is why it stays medium rather than high. The tool's own schema still tells the caller to 'obtain it by opening an edit session for the channel' (tools.go:431) — an instruction no MCP client can follow.

findings.title: GuardBasicAuth charges the shared per-IP login bucket for every request carrying a Basic header that the auth chain did not resolve — including when Basic auth is administratively disabled and on unauthenticated/static routes — so a client replaying a stale Basic header locks its source out of POST /auth/login
findings.claim: GuardBasicAuth (internal/auth/bruteforce.go:56-79) charges a token whenever the request carries parseable Basic credentials and `IdentityFrom(ctx)` is unresolved. It is mounted with `r.Use(...)` on the whole /api/v1 router (internal/north/rest/router.go:610-617), i.e. also on the SPA mount `/app/*`, the root redirect, and the unauthenticated bootstrap surface `/about`, `/health`, `/ui/*` (router.go:634-676). The tokens come from the SAME per-IP buckets that guard POST /auth/login: middleware.LoginRateLimiter.Charge and .Budget both go through `l.store.get(loginClientIP(r))` (internal/north/rest/middleware/login_bruteforce.go:87-101), burst 5, refill 1/s (:21-26), keyed by RemoteAddr only, so all clients behind a reverse proxy share one bucket (:103-115, documented). 'Unresolved' is not the same as 'wrong password': gatedAuthMiddleware sets `mwUsers = nil` when `north.rest.auth.basic_enabled` is false (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_north.go:78-83), and auth.Middleware.resolve skips Basic entirely when Users is nil (internal/auth/middleware.go:89-99), so in that supported hardening mode EVERY request carrying a Basic header — correct credentials included — is scored as a failed guess.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator sets `north.rest.auth.basic_enabled: false` (or removes a user, or switches to session/OIDC-only) while a script, an old integration or a browser that once answered the daemon's `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="openccu-loom"` challenge keeps sending the Basic header. Each such request burns one token; a client polling more than once per second holds the bucket at zero indefinitely. The operator then gets HTTP 429 on POST /auth/login from the same source address — behind a reverse proxy or HA Ingress, from every source address — and cannot log into the SPA at all, with a Retry-After that never clears while the offending client keeps polling. A single SPA page load by a browser with cached-but-unusable Basic credentials burns the burst in one go, because the guard also sits in front of /app/* and its asset requests.
findings.verified_by: code trace: internal/auth/bruteforce.go:56-79 -> internal/north/rest/router.go:610-617 (global r.Use, before the /app, /about, /health mounts at :634-676) -> internal/north/rest/middleware/login_bruteforce.go:21-26,52-58,87-101,109-115; the 'Basic disabled still charges' path via cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_north.go:78-87 and internal/auth/middleware.go:89-99.
findings.fix_sketch: Skip the charge when the Basic scheme is not installed at all (pass a `basicEnabled` flag, or have Resolve mark 'Basic present but scheme disabled'), mount the guard only on the /api/v1 subtree rather than on the SPA/bootstrap routes, and give failed-Basic its own bucket instead of depleting the one POST /auth/login needs.
findings.resolution: the per-IP Basic-credential throttle is scoped to /api/v1 so a stale cached credential cannot drain the login budget from SPA asset requests; the shared bucket is kept deliberately (by_design BD-Auth-BasicGuessingSharesTheLoginBucket)

findings.title: The re-landed climate offset binding surfaces the raw ENUM index instead of the label for every classic RF thermostat, because TEMPERATURE_OFFSET on the device-root MASTER paramset is an ENUM and OnTemperatureOffset has no int32 case.
findings.claim: 0.61.4 changed the Subscribe binding from `paramFromAnyParamset(ch, TEMPERATURE_OFFSET)` (climate channel only) to `resolveConfigParam(ch, TEMPERATURE_OFFSET)` (climate.go:1716, helper at climate.go:2049-2067), which now also walks `dev.RootChannel()`. Ground truth for the classic RF family (pydevccu paramset_descriptions/HM-CC-RT-DN.json, HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU.json): TEMPERATURE_OFFSET lives on the DEVICE-ROOT MASTER paramset and its TYPE is ENUM, MIN 0 / MAX 14, VALUE_LIST ['-3.5K' … '3.5K'] — not FLOAT. The device-root MASTER paramset is hydrated in production (internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:1647-1683 `hydrateDeviceRoot` → `hydrateParamset(..., ParamsetKeyMaster)`), and an ENUM read+write parameter is built by `resolveWritable` (internal/central/adapter/datapoint_resolver.go:151) as `generic.NewSelect`, i.e. a `DataPoint[int32]` (internal/model/generic/select.go:16-18). `OnAnyUpdate` boxes the typed value (internal/model/generic/datapoint.go:1121-1128) and `RawValue()` returns `d.value` of type T (datapoint.go:811-821), so `applyTemperatureOffset` (climate.go:1703) receives an `int32`. `Climate.OnTemperatureOffset` (climate.go:732-748) switches only on string/float64/float32 and its `default:` at climate.go:741 does `s = fmt.Sprintf("%v", v)`, so the stored value becomes the decimal index. That value is returned by `Climate.TemperatureOffset()` (climate.go:690-698) and serialised into `payload.ClimateState.TemperatureOffset` (`json:"temperature_offset"`, internal/payload/state.go:52), i.e. onto REST, MQTT and WS. The very next binding in the same function (HEATING_COOLING, climate.go:1720-1733) routes through `custom.EnumWireLabel` for exactly this reason — its comment records that a bare assertion left the value on its default while the installation cooled — so the correct helper exists and is used two lines away. The re-land's own regression test (internal/model/custom/climate/root_master_paramset_test.go, `putFloatMaster` / `TestSubscribeTemperatureOffsetRootMaster`) attaches a FLOAT data point to the root of an RF device, a wire shape no RF thermostat has, so it passes while the real device is wrong.
findings.failure_scenario: An HM-CC-RT-DN or HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU is configured with TEMPERATURE_OFFSET = '0.0K' (index 7). After upgrading to 0.61.4 the climate state payload reports `"temperature_offset": "7"` on REST, MQTT and the WebSocket instead of `"0.0K"`. Before 0.61.4 the field was simply absent for these devices, so the upgrade replaces 'missing' with 'wrong'. A UI or automation that echoes the reported value back through `set_temperature_offset` then writes the string "7" into the root MASTER paramset for an index-based ENUM.
findings.verified_by: code trace through climate.go:1716 → 1703 → 732/741 → payload/state.go:52, plus the real wire descriptors read from pydevccu paramset_descriptions (HM-CC-RT-DN: TEMPERATURE_OFFSET on VCU0000050/MASTER, TYPE=ENUM, VALUE_LIST 15 entries) and the DP factory at datapoint_resolver.go:151 / select.go:16
findings.fix_sketch: Route the offset through the existing enum helper: `applyTemperatureOffset := func(next any) { if label, ok := custom.EnumWireLabel(dp, next); ok { c.OnTemperatureOffset(label); return }; c.OnTemperatureOffset(next) }` (dp must be captured per binding, as the HEATING_COOLING branch does), and add an int32/int64 case to OnTemperatureOffset as a backstop. Rebuild the regression test with a Select DP carrying the real 15-entry VALUE_LIST instead of putFloatMaster.
findings.verify_reasoning: Re-derived the wire truth independently: TEMPERATURE_OFFSET is TYPE=ENUM, MIN 0 / MAX 14, 15-entry VALUE_LIST ('-3.5K'..'3.5K'), DEFAULT 7, on the DEVICE-ROOT MASTER paramset of exactly three models (HM-CC-RT-DN, HM-CC-RT-DN-BoM, HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU). On the other 35 instances in the fleet it is FLOAT on a channel MASTER (HmIP family) and unaffected. An ENUM read+write MASTER parameter builds a generic.Select (DataPoint[int32]) at datapoint_resolver.go:151, so OnAnyUpdate/RawValue hand climate.go:1703 an int32 and OnTemperatureOffset's default branch stringifies the index. Reproduced with the real 15-entry descriptor: TemperatureOffset() returns "7" (push) and "9" (seedMasterValues/OnWireValue) instead of "0.0K"/"1.0K"; the value reaches REST/MQTT/WS through climate/payload.go:360 -> payload/state.go:52. Severity re-rated from high to medium: the field is a config-display value on three models, previously absent rather than wrong, and no automatic writer echoes it back — the bad write requires an operator action.

findings.title: The duress-probe fix makes MatchDuress argon2id-verify every enabled code on the disarm path, multiplying a ~270 ms hash by the number of household codes while the alarm engine's global mutex is held.
findings.claim: Before 0.61.3, `MatchDuress` collected only the duress rows and verified those (`for _, c := range duressCandidates { if VerifyPIN(...) }`). The fix replaced that with a single pass over EVERY candidate (facade.go:278-292) so that a correct ordinary PIN can be told apart from an unknown probe. The loop does not break once `knownCode = true` (facade.go:282) — it only returns early on a duress match — and it does not filter by `permits(c.perms, verb)` first, so an ordinary correct PIN costs one argon2id verification per enabled code in the installation. The parameters are m=64 MiB, t=1, p=4 (internal/alarm/codes/pin.go:23-27); measured on this 4-core machine at 268.9 ms per verification (reproducer below), with a 64 MiB working set each. `MatchDuress` is reached from `Engine.matchDuress` (internal/alarm/engine/engine.go:625-630), called from `DisarmWithCode` (engine.go:704) — inside `e.mu.Lock()` taken at engine.go:697 and held for the whole method. That same mutex serialises `HandleSensorEvent` (engine.go:866), `SetSensorAvailability` (engine.go:1015), `HandleCentralConnectivity` (engine.go:1064) and the state-timer callback `onStateTimerFired` (engine.go:1352), so the sweep blocks sensor ingest and delay-timer expiry across every zone. The scenario the fix itself names makes this worst-case: an HA aggregate ('master') panel disarm is looped over every zone, and the `matchDuress` branch is precisely the already-disarmed-zone branch, so each already-disarmed zone pays a full sweep. The new `recordSuccess` on a known code (facade.go:295-296) also means the probe ledger is cleared on every such press, so the per-source limiter never engages and the cost cannot be capped by it. An installation with no duress code is unaffected (the `hasDuress` early return at facade.go:266 still fires).
findings.failure_scenario: A household with one duress code and six ordinary PINs presses 'disarm' on the HA master panel across four zones, three of which are already disarmed. Each of those three zones runs 7 × 269 ms ≈ 1.9 s of argon2id under the engine mutex, ~5.6 s total, during which no sensor activation, availability change or entry/exit-delay timer of ANY zone is processed and the daemon transiently allocates 64 MiB per hash. Repeating the press (or any consumer that republishes the retained disarm) re-incurs it indefinitely, because a correct PIN resets the probe ledger instead of charging it.
findings.verified_by: code trace facade.go:278-296 → engine.go:625-630 → engine.go:696-704 (lock at :697) plus the lock scope grep over engine.go; timing measured with the repo's own argon2 parameters at $S/repro/A4 (`argon2id m=64MiB t=1 p=4: 10 hashes in 2.689s => 268.9ms per hash`)
findings.fix_sketch: Verify the duress rows first and return on a match; only then, and only until the first match, verify the remaining `permits`-eligible rows to decide `knownCode` — i.e. `break` out of the second loop as soon as a hash matches. Better still, have the engine pass the `Validate` result (which already knows whether the code was known) into `matchDuress` instead of re-hashing, and move the sweep outside `e.mu`.
findings.verify_reasoning: The code reading is right and the constant is right, but the headline scenario is refuted. Confirmed: 3914578d replaced the duress-only loop with a single pass over every candidate (facade.go:277-292); it does not break on knownCode and does not pre-filter by permits; MatchDuress is called only from DisarmWithCode's already-disarmed branch (engine.go:704) with e.mu held from :697 through the whole method, and that mutex also serialises HandleSensorEvent (:867), SetSensorAvailability (:1016), HandleCentralConnectivity (:1065) and onStateTimerFired (:1353). I measured VerifyPIN at m=64MiB,t=1,p=4 on this 4-core box: 316 ms per verification, so the per-hash cost is if anything understated. REFUTED is the amplifier: the HA aggregate 'master' panel disarm carries NO code. CommandSubscriber.dispatchAlarm routes the master zone to alarmSink.MasterDisarm(ctx) (command_subscriber.go:1122-1126, interface at :139 has no code parameter), and MasterDisarm loops eng.Disarm(ctx, a.ID, "", ...) (daemon_north.go:551-563) → DisarmWithCode with code=="" → matchDuress returns at engine.go:626 before any hashing. The subscriber's own comment says 'the master verbs stay code-free', and Validate's comment at facade.go:190-195 says the same. So the claimed 3 zones x 7 codes = 5.6 s never happens on that path. Second over-statement: N-hashes-under-the-mutex is not new — Validate already verifies every candidate for any WRONG code on an armed zone (facade.go:200-217, break only on match). Real residual, and it is worth fixing: a per-zone coded disarm (MQTT per-zone panel, REST, WS) of an ALREADY-DISARMED zone in an installation that has a duress code now costs N x ~300 ms under the engine lock — ~0.9 s at 3 codes, ~2.2 s at 7 — where it previously cost only the duress rows, and recordSuccess on a known code (facade.go:288-293) means a repeated press is never throttled. Medium: a real availability stall on a reachable but non-routine action, not the seconds-per-press freeze on the household's normal disarm gesture.

findings.title: The new outstanding-failure set is never pruned on Reload, so an output the operator deletes after it failed pins the alarm domain degraded until the daemon restarts.
findings.claim: 0.61.3 added `Manager.failed map[string]struct{}` (manager.go:110, initialised :151). `noteFailure` inserts an output id (manager.go:646-652) and is the only producer of `health(false, …)`; `resolveFailure` (manager.go:662-669) is the only producer of `health(true, …)` and reports recovery only when `len(m.failed) == 0`. `resolveFailure` is called from exactly one place — the verified-stop branch of `verifyStop` (internal/alarm/outputs/watchdog.go:124) — and only ever with `act.outputID`, i.e. an output that is currently activated and stops cleanly. `Manager.Reload` (manager.go:166-192) rebuilds `byZone` and calls `pruneDemands(rowIDs)` (arbitration.go:65-73) to drop stale arbitration state, but leaves `m.failed` untouched. There is therefore no path that removes an id from `failed` once the row behind it is gone: `StopAll` (manager.go:328-347) iterates `m.byZone[zoneID]`, which no longer contains the deleted row, so its stop is never issued and `verifyStop` never runs for it. Health goes to the daemon health tracker and to the alarm bus via `s.health` (internal/alarm/service.go:162), so every north-bound alarm-health surface stays degraded.
findings.failure_scenario: A siren fails to fire (device unreachable) — alarm health reports degraded, correctly. The operator removes that broken siren from the zone's outputs in the UI. `Reload` runs, the row is gone, and nothing can ever call `resolveFailure("sirA")` again. Every subsequent verified stop of every remaining, healthy output finds `len(m.failed) == 1` and stays silent, so the alarm system reports 'degraded' with the note of a device that no longer exists, until the daemon is restarted. Renaming an output id has the same effect.
findings.verified_by: code trace: grep of every `m.health(`, `noteFailure`, `resolveFailure` and `failed[` site in internal/alarm/outputs (only manager.go:637/646-669 and watchdog.go:124/130), plus Reload/pruneDemands at manager.go:166-192 and arbitration.go:65-73
findings.fix_sketch: In `Reload`, after `pruneDemands(rowIDs)`, drop every id from `m.failed` that is not in `rowIDs`, and if that empties the set emit the recovery `health(true, …)` — mirroring exactly what `pruneDemands` does for arbitration state.

findings.title: SecuritySources still seeds the include toggle from the lossy `relevant` proxy although the same release added the exact `override_included` bit to the DTO, so a note-only override on a non-relevant source silently excludes it on the next save.
findings.claim: `freshDraft(s)` seeds `included: !s.overridden || s.relevant` (SecuritySources.svelte:117-119) and its comment asserts "SecuritySourceView does not carry the stored override's raw `included` bit". That claim is refuted by the same commit range: `SourceView.OverrideIncluded` was added (internal/model/security/snapshot.go:204-208), populated from the stored row (internal/security/index.go:402 `OverrideIncluded: override.Included`), projected onto the REST DTO as the optional `override_included` (internal/north/rest/handlers/security.go:367-368, pkg/hmapi/security.go:135-140) and emitted into the generated SPA types (assets/ui/src/lib/api/types.generated.ts, changed in 3914578d together with assets/openapi.yaml). The proxy is lossy in a reachable direction: `classifySource` (internal/security/index.go:242-297) sets `relevant = true` unconditionally only when the override carries a CLASS (index.go:244-245); an override row with `Class == ""` and `Included == true` — which `SetSourceOverride` stores whenever a note is supplied (index.go:423-428: the delete shortcut only fires for `class == "" && included && note == ""`) — falls through to the `default:` branch and gets `relevant = cls.Class.Hazard() || deviceRelevant` (index.go:288). For a diagnostic-class source on a device with no alarm role that is `false`, so the row reads `overridden=true, relevant=false, override_included=true` and the toggle is seeded OFF.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator adds a note ("false positive, checked 2026-08") to a diagnostic-class source on a device with no alarm role, leaving it included. The row comes back `overridden=true, relevant=false`. On the next visit — or when they edit the note again, or set a class — the include switch renders OFF, and the very next Save posts `included: false`, silently excluding a source that was never meant to be excluded. This is the mirror image of the bug the change was written to fix.
findings.verified_by: code trace: SecuritySources.svelte:117-134 against internal/security/index.go:242-297 and :402, internal/north/rest/handlers/security.go:367-368, pkg/hmapi/security.go:135-140; `git diff --stat d281e2e2~1..HEAD -- pkg/hmapi assets/openapi.yaml assets/ui/src/lib/api/types.generated.ts` confirms the field landed in the same range (3914578d)
findings.fix_sketch: Seed from the exact bit: `included: !s.overridden || (s.override_included ?? s.relevant)`, and delete the comment paragraph that claims the DTO lacks it. Add a test case with `overridden: true, relevant: false, override_included: true` asserting the switch renders ON.

findings.title: The new MCP edit-lock gate makes MASTER paramset writes over MCP permanently unreachable, because no MCP tool can open an edit session and mint the required token.
findings.claim: `registerWriteParamset` now refuses a MASTER/LINK write unless `d.EditLocks.Verify("channel:"+address+":"+key, editToken)` returns true (tools.go:546-555). `EditSessions.Verify` (internal/north/rest/handlers/session.go:113-123) returns false for an empty token and false unless a live lock exists whose token matches exactly, so a token is required unconditionally — the same strictness as REST `enforceEditLock` (internal/north/rest/handlers/paramsets.go:37-49). The difference is that REST and WS both expose the session-open verb that mints the token, while the MCP surface does not: the registered tool set is list_centrals / list_devices / list_channels / get_device / read_paramset / write_paramset / set_datapoint / list_sysvars / list_programs / trigger_program / list_rooms / list_functions / get_health / get_system_info / list_audit / list_incidents / list_inbox / list_service_messages / list_alarm_* / arm_alarm_zone / disarm_alarm_zone / reset_motion / list_triggered_motion / get_security_status — there is no open/close-edit-session tool. `EditLocks` is wired unconditionally in the composition root (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest_mount.go:706), so the nil escape hatch is test-only. The tool's own schema still advertises `key: "MASTER or VALUES"` and its edit_token description says "obtain it by opening an edit session for the channel" — an instruction an MCP client cannot follow.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator enables `north.mcp.allow_writes` and asks an assistant to change a MASTER configuration value (e.g. a thermostat's MIN_SETPOINT). Every `write_paramset` with key=MASTER returns 'edit lock required …; open an edit session and pass edit_token', and the assistant has no tool to satisfy it, so the capability that worked in 0.61.2 is now dead over MCP while remaining available over REST/WS.
findings.verified_by: code trace tools.go:546-555 → session.go:113-123, composition root at daemon_rest_mount.go:706, plus an exhaustive listing of the registered MCP tool names in internal/north/mcp/tools*.go
findings.fix_sketch: Add `open_edit_session` / `close_edit_session` MCP tools backed by the same `*handlers.EditSessions` registry (as CLAUDE.md's 'a new capability has more surfaces than the one you are editing' rule requires), or make write_paramset acquire-and-release the lock itself for the duration of the write when no token is supplied and no other session holds it.
findings.verify_reasoning: Verified once for both units; both framings are accurate. mountMCP wires EditLocks: d.editSessions unconditionally (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest_mount.go:703-707; d.editSessions is created in daemon.go:713 and never nil in production), so the nil escape hatch documented at mcp/server.go:114-119 is test-only. registerWriteParamset then requires d.EditLocks.Verify("channel:"+address+":"+key, edit_token) for MASTER and LINK (internal/north/mcp/tools.go:546-556), and EditSessions.Verify returns false for an empty token and otherwise only for a live lock held by exactly that token (internal/north/rest/handlers/session.go:113-123). I enumerated every registered MCP tool name from the source (26 entries: list_centrals, list_devices, list_channels, get_device, read_paramset, write_paramset, set_datapoint, list_sysvars, list_programs, trigger_program, list_rooms, list_functions, get_health, get_system_info, list_audit, list_incidents, list_inbox, list_service_messages, list_alarm_zones, list_alarm_messages, arm_alarm_zone, disarm_alarm_zone, reset_motion, list_triggered_motion, get_security_status) — there is no open/close-edit-session tool and no second token source on the MCP surface. git confirms the regression: EditLocks first appears in the MCP Deps in 3914578d, so before it the gate was skipped entirely. Two qualifiers worth recording, neither of which refutes anything: the lock key format is byte-identical across REST (handlers/paramsets.go:101), WS (ws/commands_extended.go:726) and MCP, so a token minted out of band over REST/WS does satisfy the MCP gate — an MCP-only client still cannot mint one; and the whole path is behind north.mcp.allow_writes (default false), so this is a dead capability on an opt-in surface, which is why it stays medium rather than high. The tool's own schema still tells the caller to 'obtain it by opening an edit session for the channel' (tools.go:431) — an instruction no MCP client can follow.

findings.title: The newly enabled AccessControl.Extension write path accepts writes matter.js rejects and never emits the AccessControlExtensionChanged event it advertises.
findings.claim: 0.61.3 added `decodeExtensionList` (internal/north/matter/bridge/attribute_value_reader.go:1381-1408) so a write to AccessControl.Extension (0x001F/0x0001) reaches `AccessControl.MatterWrite`'s Extension branch (access_control.go:593-630) instead of failing its type assertion — the path was dead before, so its validation is only now reachable. The Go branch enforces one rule (`len(e.Data) > 128`, access_control.go:602-606). matter.js's `AccessControlServer` enforces two more on the same write: `#validateAccessControlExtensionChanges` throws `StatusResponseError("Extension list must contain a single entry", Status.ConstraintError)` when more than one entry targets the writer's fabric (../matter.js/packages/node/src/behaviors/access-control/AccessControlServer.ts:359-366), and `extensionEntryValidator` rejects data that is not a decodable TLV structure (AccessControlServer.ts:424-430). Neither exists in the Go branch, so a controller writing two extension entries, or 3 bytes of garbage, gets SUCCESS where the gold standard answers CONSTRAINT_ERROR. Separately, `MatterEvents()` advertises `accessControlEventExtensionChanged` (0x0001, access_control.go:673) but that constant appears nowhere else in the tree — only `accessControlEventEntryChanged` is ever emitted (access_control.go:580) — while matter.js emits `accessControlExtensionChanged` on every extension change (AccessControlServer.ts:401-410). Matter §9.10.7.2 makes the event mandatory where the Extension attribute is supported, and the cluster advertises the EXTS feature bit in its FeatureMap (access_control.go:280-284).
findings.failure_scenario: A controller (or a TC-ACL conformance run) writes an Extension list with two entries for its own fabric: OpenCCU-Loom stores both and answers SUCCESS, then a read-back returns two entries where the spec permits one, and no AccessControlExtensionChanged event is ever reported on the subscription the controller opened for it. The daemon looks conformant on the read path and diverges on the write path.
findings.verified_by: code trace attribute_value_reader.go:1381-1408 → access_control.go:593-630, :673, :580; matter.js HEAD read at ../matter.js/packages/node/src/behaviors/access-control/AccessControlServer.ts:352-430 and ../matter.js/packages/model/src/standard/elements/access-control.element.ts:204-208
findings.fix_sketch: Mirror matter.js: reject a per-fabric extension list longer than one entry with a constraint error, validate that `Data` is a decodable TLV structure (length ≥ 2), and emit `accessControlEventExtensionChanged` with the added/changed/removed change type from the same branch that emits `accessControlEventEntryChanged`. Extend the behavioural negative-write parity table with both cases.

findings.title: SoundPlayer caps soundfile indices at 189 while HmIP-MP3P really offers SOUNDFILE_001..252, so 65 of the 256 tones the daemon advertises to Home Assistant silently do nothing
findings.claim: Ground truth: HmIP-MP3P's SOUNDFILE parameter (ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER and ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL_TRANSMITTER, VALUES paramset) has a 256-entry VALUE_LIST = INTERNAL_SOUNDFILE, SOUNDFILE_001 .. SOUNDFILE_252 (252 entries, no gaps), RANDOM_SOUNDFILE, OLD_VALUE, DO_NOT_CARE -- extracted to $S/repro/B1/valuelists_by_channel.json. NewSoundPlayer copies that list verbatim into sp.availableSF (sound.go:127) and AvailableSoundfiles() (sound.go:145) publishes it as the HA discovery key `available_tones` (payload.go:284-285). Home Assistant's siren integration then returns the operator's choice by label in the command JSON, which arrives as params["tone"] (payload.go:376-381). soundfileIndexFor (sound.go:160-182) converts the label back to an integer and rejects anything outside minSoundfileIndex=1 .. maxSoundfileIndex=189 (sound.go:25-26, 179). For SOUNDFILE_190..SOUNDFILE_252 it returns (0,false); for INTERNAL_SOUNDFILE / RANDOM_SOUNDFILE / OLD_VALUE / DO_NOT_CARE the strings.CutPrefix at sound.go:174 fails and it also returns (0,false). The caller at payload.go:379-381 is `if i, ok := ...; ok { cfg.SoundfileIndex = i }` -- no else, no error -- so cfg.SoundfileIndex stays 0, and PlaySound's gate `cfg.SoundfileIndex >= minSoundfileIndex && <= maxSoundfileIndex` (sound.go:310) is false, so the SOUNDFILE parameter is never staged on the collector. The command still succeeds and the other parameters (volume, duration, repetitions) are written, so the device plays whatever file was previously selected. This is a port defect, not an inherited limitation: aiohomematic bounds 1..189 only for the *integer* form (siren.py:289-293) and passes a string soundfile straight through to the wire (siren.py:348-350 `if isinstance(soundfile, int): soundfile = self._convert_soundfile_index(soundfile)`).
findings.failure_scenario: An operator with more than 189 MP3 files on the HmIP-MP3P's SD card picks 'SOUNDFILE_200' (or 'RANDOM_SOUNDFILE') from the tone list Home Assistant built out of the daemon's own available_tones. The siren turns on at the requested volume and plays the previously selected file instead. No error is reported on MQTT, in the log or in the UI.
findings.verified_by: code trace (sound.go:25-26, 127, 145, 160-182, 310-312; payload.go:284-285, 373-381) + ground-truth VALUE_LIST at $S/repro/B1/valuelists_by_channel.json (ACOUSTIC_SIGNAL_VIRTUAL_RECEIVER / VALUES:SOUNDFILE, 256 entries, SOUNDFILE_001..252) + reference comparison against ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/model/custom/siren.py:289-293, 348-350
findings.fix_sketch: Stop round-tripping the label through an index: when params["tone"] is a member of availableSF, write that label to SOUNDFILE directly (a PlayConfig.SoundfileLabel field alongside SoundfileIndex). Keep the numeric bound only for ConvertSoundfileIndex and raise it to 252 to match the device, and make the tone-resolution failure return an error instead of silently dropping the parameter. Also filter OLD_VALUE / DO_NOT_CARE out of available_tones -- they are link-profile sentinels, not playable files.
findings.verify_reasoning: Re-extracted the descriptor myself: HmIP-MP3P SOUNDFILE (VCU1543608:1 and :2, VALUES) is an ENUM with a 256-entry VALUE_LIST = INTERNAL_SOUNDFILE + SOUNDFILE_001..252 + RANDOM_SOUNDFILE + OLD_VALUE + DO_NOT_CARE; it is the only device in the 399-device fleet carrying SOUNDFILE. The whole list is copied to availableSF (sound.go:127) and published as available_tones (payload.go:284). soundfileIndexFor rejects >189 and every non-SOUNDFILE_ label (sound.go:174-181); the caller drops the failure silently (payload.go:376-381, no else branch) and PlaySound's gate (sound.go:310) then omits the SOUNDFILE parameter entirely, so the command succeeds and the previous file plays. Reference comparison holds: aiohomematic bounds 1..189 only in _convert_soundfile_index and passes a string soundfile straight through (siren.py:289-293, 348-350). Not in by_design.md. Severity re-rated from high to medium: one device model, and the >189 half needs an SD card with more than 189 files; the likelier everyday hit is the four non-numeric entries (INTERNAL_SOUNDFILE / RANDOM_SOUNDFILE plus the two link-profile sentinels the daemon should not advertise at all). Caveat: godevccu is the only source for this VALUE_LIST — openccu-data carries no SOUNDFILE strings, so the 252 upper bound is single-sourced (from a real-CCU dump).
