findings.title: EffectLight advertises four invented effect names to Home Assistant for HM-LC-RGBW-WM; PROGRAM has no VALUE_LIST on that device, so selecting any of them is rejected and the reported effect is permanently empty
findings.claim: The EffectLight profile 'RfDimmer_Color' is registered for exactly one device: hm-lc-rgbw-wm (internal/model/custom/generated_profiles.go:666-675, constructor at internal/model/custom/light/init.go:68). newEffectLightOn sources the effect labels from the PROGRAM data point's VALUE_LIST (effect.go:50-53). Ground truth from godevccu (paramset_descriptions/HM-LC-RGBW-WM.json, channel VCU3747418:3 / RGBW_AUTOMATIC): PROGRAM is {"TYPE":"INTEGER","MIN":0,"MAX":255,"OPERATIONS":7} with **no VALUE_LIST at all**. So `effects` is nil on every real device, and Effects() (effect.go:91-96) returns nil. EffectLight.HADiscoveryPayload (payload.go:888-892) sees len(effects)==0 and substitutes the hard-coded literal list []string{"NONE","SLOW_COLOR_CHANGE","MEDIUM_COLOR_CHANGE","FAST_COLOR_CHANGE"} into body["effect_list"]. None of those four strings exists in any VALUE_LIST across the 399-device fleet ($S/repro/B1/valuelists.txt) nor anywhere in openccu-data's OCCU string-table extract (checked case-insensitively); the CCU's own easymode for RGBW_AUTOMATIC (../occu/WebUI/www/config/easymodes/RGBW_AUTOMATIC/KEY.tcl) treats the colour program as a bare number 0..6 / 253 / 254 with labels ${dec_Program}/${inc_Program}/${set_Program}. When HA sends the chosen label back, registerEffectLightServices (payload.go:548-563) does `slices.Contains(l.Effects(), label)` -> false (Effects() is nil), then strconv.ParseInt("SLOW_COLOR_CHANGE") -> error, and returns `effectlight: unknown effect label`. The WS/REST path is equally dead: dispatchEffectLight (custom_dp_dispatcher.go:436) calls SetEffectByLabel, which iterates the empty l.effects (effect.go:162-168) and always errors. The read side is dead too: EffectLight.State (payload.go:530-543) sets out.Effect from l.Effect(), which indexes l.effects (effect.go:108-110) and yields "" for every index, so HA never sees a current effect. aiohomematic does not invent a fallback: it sets _effect_list = () when the DP carries no values (light.py:807-811).
findings.failure_scenario: An HM-LC-RGBW-WM appears in Home Assistant as a light with an 'Effect' dropdown offering NONE / SLOW_COLOR_CHANGE / MEDIUM_COLOR_CHANGE / FAST_COLOR_CHANGE. Selecting any of them fails with 'effectlight: unknown effect label' and the lamp does not change program; the effect attribute stays empty forever. The whole effect surface of the device is dead while looking fully wired.
findings.verified_by: code trace (light/init.go:68; custom/generated_profiles.go:666-675; light/effect.go:50-53, 91-96, 100-111, 140-169; light/payload.go:530-543, 888-892; central/adapter/custom_dp_dispatcher.go:429-442) + ground-truth descriptor godevccu/internal/embed/data/paramset_descriptions/HM-LC-RGBW-WM.json (PROGRAM: INTEGER 0..255, no VALUE_LIST) + absence of the four labels from $S/repro/B1/valuelists.txt and from openccu-data's translation_extract.json.gz
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the invented fallback at payload.go:891 and omit effect_list / effect:true when Effects() is empty, so HA renders no effect picker for a device that advertises no program vocabulary. If a program surface is wanted for HM-LC-RGBW-WM, expose PROGRAM as a plain 0..255 number entity instead of a named-effect select, and add a parity test asserting every EffectLight label comes from the PROGRAM VALUE_LIST.
findings.verify_reasoning: The mechanism is confirmed and reproduced: HM-LC-RGBW-WM's PROGRAM (VCU3747418:3, RGBW_AUTOMATIC) is INTEGER 0..255 with NO VALUE_LIST, so Effects() is nil, HADiscoveryPayload substitutes the four hard-coded labels (payload.go:891), and a label round-trip dies — set_effect("SLOW_COLOR_CHANGE") returns `effectlight: unknown effect label "SLOW_COLOR_CHANGE"`, Effect() returns an empty label for observed index 2, so the effect surface is advertised and dead. Second source agrees the device has no named-effect vocabulary: openccu-data's translation extract labels rgbw_automatic|program as 'Program number' / 'Programmnummer'. But two of the finding's supporting claims are wrong and change the framing. (1) 'aiohomematic does not invent a fallback' is false for THIS class: CustomDpColorDimmerEffect hard-codes a seven-element tuple ('Off', 'Slow color change', 'Medium color change', 'Fast color change', 'Campemit', 'Waterfall', 'TV simulation') and indexes PROGRAM by position (light.py:478-486, 495-511) — the cited light.py:807-811 empty-list behaviour belongs to the IP RGBW colour-behaviour class, a different device family. So the effect concept is inherited; what the port did is re-spell it in UPPER_SNAKE, truncate it to 4 of 7, and wire it only into the discovery payload. (2) The divergence is documented in notes/parity/by_design.md A2-BD04 as a 'deliberate improvement' — but on a false premise ('the dynamic approach reflects firmware-added effects'), since the only device on the profile ships no VALUE_LIST at all. Severity medium: one device model, feature fully dead but visibly offered.

findings.title: ListScheduleDevices misses HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU entirely and points HM-CC-RT-DN / HM-CC-RT-DN-BoM / HM-CC-VG-1 at a channel that carries no schedule
findings.claim: scheduleChannelByType (schedules.go:373-385) backs the fleet-wide overview GET /api/v1/schedules (handlers/schedules.go:84, router.go:926). It considers only two candidates: a channel whose type ends in WEEK_PROFILE, or a channel whose type is in climateScheduleChannelTypes = {CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER, CLIMATECONTROL_REGULATOR, HEATING_CLIMATECONTROL_TRANSCEIVER} (schedules.go:107-111). It deliberately skips FindScheduleChannel's Path 3, the device-root MASTER probe (schedules.go:182-192). Ground truth ($S/repro/B1/sim_list_schedule_devices.py over the 399-device fleet) finds exactly one device whose schedule lives only at the device root and which carries none of those channel types: HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU (channels MAINTENANCE, REMOTECONTROL_RECEIVER, SWITCH_TRANSMIT, THERMALCONTROL_TRANSMIT, WEATHER_TRANSMIT, WINDOW_SWITCH_RECEIVER; its device-root MASTER carries the full P1..P3_ENDTIME_*/TEMPERATURE_* set plus WEEK_PROGRAM_POINTER). It is therefore never listed, even though the device-level route GET /devices/{addr}/schedule resolves it correctly via Path 3. The same simulation finds three devices listed on a channel that provably carries no schedule keys: HM-CC-RT-DN, HM-CC-RT-DN-BoM and HM-CC-VG-1 are all reported with Channel = <addr>:4 (resp. :1) CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER while their schedule sits in the device-root MASTER; the summary row shows that wrong channel address to the operator (ScheduleList.svelte:143) although the click-through re-resolves via the device route.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator with an HM-TC-IT-WM-W-EU wall thermostat -- a very common classic HomeMatic device -- opens the Schedules page and does not find it, concluding the daemon cannot edit its week programs; the schedule is in fact fully editable via the device detail page's Zeitplan tab. Three other classic thermostats are listed with a channel address that does not hold their schedule.
findings.verified_by: code trace (schedules.go:336-385, 146-198; north/rest/handlers/schedules.go:84; assets/ui/src/routes/ScheduleList.svelte:77-78, 143) + fleet simulation $S/repro/B1/sim_list_schedule_devices.py and $S/repro/B1/sim_climate_channels.py against godevccu's paramset descriptions
findings.fix_sketch: Give scheduleChannelByType a third, still type-derived case: a device whose model is known to carry a device-root week profile (or, cheaper, whose channel set contains THERMALCONTROL_TRANSMIT) is reported with Channel.Number = device.ChannelNumberDevice. Use the same synthetic device channel for HM-CC-RT-DN / HM-CC-VG-1 rather than their CLIMATECONTROL_RT_TRANSCEIVER, so the summary agrees with what FindScheduleChannel resolves.

findings.title: The alarm sensor-candidate table keys on a channel type no device carries (MOTIONDETECTOR) and omits ROTARY_HANDLE_TRANSCEIVER, so HmIP-SRH window-handle sensors are never offered as alarm sensors
findings.claim: sensorTypeByChannelType (sensor_candidates.go:69-80) is the only gate that turns an intrusion sensor into an enrollable candidate: sensorCandidateFor returns false for any data point that safety.Classify does not classify as a hazard and whose channel type is not in that map (sensor_candidates.go:138-167). Diffed against the real channel-type universe: (a) the key "MOTIONDETECTOR" appears on no device in godevccu's 399-device fleet and in no entry of openccu-data's 234-entry OCCU channel-type table -- the real spellings are MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER, MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER and MOTION_DETECTOR, so that map entry is dead. (b) ROTARY_HANDLE_TRANSCEIVER is real and is missing: HmIP-SRH (the current-generation Homematic IP window-handle sensor) and HmIP-HEATING carry it, with VALUES:STATE as an ENUM [CLOSED, TILTED, OPEN] -- verified in $S/repro/B1/valuelists_by_channel.json. safety.Classify has no rule for (ROTARY_HANDLE_TRANSCEIVER, STATE) either, so sensorCandidateFor returns (SensorCandidate{}, false) and the data point never reaches the response of GET /api/v1/alarm/sensor-candidates (router.go:1053, handlers/alarm_sensor_candidates.go:24-38). The predecessor device HM-Sec-RHS is covered, because its channel type ROTARY_HANDLE_SENSOR *is* in the map -- so the table covers the legacy BidCos sensor and not its HmIP successor. MOTIONDETECTOR_VIRTUAL_TRANSCEIVER (HmIP-SMO230-A) is likewise absent, though that device is saved by also carrying MOTIONDETECTOR_TRANSCEIVER.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator (or an external client / MCP-driven assistant) enumerating enrollable alarm sensors via GET /api/v1/alarm/sensor-candidates gets every SHUTTER_CONTACT and MOTION_DETECTOR in the house but not a single HmIP-SRH, and has to fall back to typing the channel address and parameter by hand -- exactly the unvalidated free-text path this endpoint's doc comment (sensor_candidates.go:17-22) says it exists to remove.
findings.verified_by: code trace (alarm/sensor_candidates.go:69-80, 89-124, 128-167; model/safety/classify.go:67-101, 184-216; north/rest/router.go:1053) + channel-type universe at $S/repro/B1/channel_types.txt / occu_channel_types.txt / channel_type_by_device.json / valuelists_by_channel.json

Back it with a contract test that asserts every channel type in the embedded fleet whose name contains MOTION / PRESENCE / SHUTTER_CONTACT / ROTARY_HANDLE / TILT either maps to a sensor type or is explicitly listed as deliberately excluded.

findings.title: EffectLight (RF colour dimmer HM-LC-RGBW-WM) never binds the profile's COLOR field, so every colour command fails while HA discovery advertises the hs colour mode
findings.claim: The RfDimmer_Color profile maps FieldColor -> Parameter COLOR at channel offset 1 and FieldProgram -> PROGRAM at offset 2 (generated_profile_configs.go:653-660), faithfully mirroring RF_DIMMER_COLOR_CONFIG (profile.py:393-407). newEffectLightConstructor (init.go:287-296) consumes only the PROGRAM mapping via programChannel(); nothing in the light package resolves FieldColor (`grep -rn 'FieldColor\b' internal/model/custom/light/*.go` returns only bindChannelColor for the *FixedColor* FieldChannelColor). EffectLight embeds *ColorLight (effect.go:24-29), whose hue/saturation slots are resolved from ParameterHue / ParameterSaturation on the light's own channel (color.go:36-37). HM-LC-RGBW-WM carries COLOR on channel :2 and has no HUE and no SATURATION parameter on any channel (godevccu paramset_descriptions/HM-LC-RGBW-WM.json: VCU3747418:1 = LEVEL/ON_TIME/RAMP_TIME/..., :2 = COLOR/USER_COLOR/..., :3 = PROGRAM/...). Both slots therefore resolve nil and ColorLight.SetColor returns `errors.New("colorlight: channel missing HUE or SATURATION")` (color.go:139-141) for every call. The command is reachable and advertised: custom_dp_dispatcher.go:446-452 routes 'set_color' to EffectLight.SetColor, payload.go registers the set_color service, and EffectLight.HADiscoveryPayload (payload.go:880-895) inherits ColorLight's body which sets `supported_color_modes: ["hs"]` and `hs: true` (payload.go:802-805). The read side is equally dead: ColorLight.Color() returns observed=false forever (color.go:97-104), so no colour ever appears in the state payload. The reference implements this device family through the single COLOR integer: CustomDpColorDimmer.turn_on (light.py:462-473) computes `color = 200 if saturation < 0.1 else int(round(max(min(hue/360,1),0) * 199))` and writes it to _dp_color, and hs_color (light.py:448-460) reads it back as `(color/200*360, 100)` with color >= 200 meaning white.
findings.failure_scenario: HM-LC-RGBW-WM (the only device on the RfDimmer_Color profile). Home Assistant renders a colour wheel because the discovery payload declares supported_color_modes: ["hs"]. The user picks any colour; openccu-loom answers 'colorlight: channel missing HUE or SATURATION' and nothing reaches the CCU. The lamp's colour also never appears in the state payload, so the entity shows no colour at all. aiohomematic sends COLOR=<0..199|200> on channel :2 and the lamp changes colour.
findings.verified_by: code trace: effect.go:24-66, color.go:33-59 and :122-161, init.go:287-296, payload.go:802-805 + 880-895, custom_dp_dispatcher.go:425-457; device data ../godevccu/internal/embed/data/paramset_descriptions/HM-LC-RGBW-WM.json; reference light.py:440-473
findings.fix_sketch: Give EffectLight (and any RfDimmer_Color light) a COLOR-integer colour path: resolve the profile's FieldColor DP on the sibling channel the rebased ChannelFields name, and implement SetColor/Color with the reference's hue<->COLOR mapping (200 == white, otherwise round(clamp(hue/360,0,1)*199); read back color/200*360 with saturation 100). Until then the discovery payload must not advertise the hs colour mode for this profile.
findings.verify_reasoning: Independently confirmed on the real wire shape: HM-LC-RGBW-WM has COLOR (INTEGER 0..255) on :2 / RGBW_COLOR and PROGRAM on :3 / RGBW_AUTOMATIC, and no HUE and no SATURATION parameter on any channel. ColorLight resolves its hue/saturation slots from ParameterHue / ParameterSaturation on the light's own channel (color.go:36-37) and nothing in the light package consumes the profile's FieldColor mapping (generated_profile_configs.go:654-656) — the only FieldColor reader is the FixedColorLight path, which expects an ENUM COLOR. Built the device through the production constructor newEffectLightConstructor with the profile's rebased channel fields: SetColor(120,100) returns `colorlight: channel missing HUE or SATURATION`, Color() reports observed=false, and the writer records zero calls — while HADiscoveryPayload inherits supported_color_modes:["hs"] and hs:true from ColorLight (payload.go:802-805). The reference implements the same device through the single COLOR integer (light.py:440-473: 200 == white, else round(clamp(hue/360)*199); read back color/200*360). Not in by_design.md. Severity medium: complete failure of the device's primary feature, but the profile covers exactly one model.

findings.title: Climate.SetTemperature clamps the already-validated setpoint to a Go-only capability bound (30.0 °C), so a setpoint the daemon itself advertises as legal (30.5 °C) reaches the CCU as 30.0 °C
findings.claim: SetTemperature validates the requested value against MinTemp()/MaxTemp() (climate.go:947-957) and then unconditionally applies `v = clamp(v, c.Capabilities.MinTemperature, c.Capabilities.MaxTemperature)` (climate.go:958) before writing. MaxTemp() (climate.go:602-623) resolves, in order, the operator-config TEMPERATURE_MAXIMUM value, the setpoint descriptor MAX, and only then the capability fallback — so it legitimately returns 30.5. Capabilities.MaxTemperature for every IP thermostat is the hard-coded 30.0 in ipCapabilities (init.go:117-118). Both HmIP paths reach 30.5: every HmIP thermostat in the fleet declares SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE MIN=4.5 MAX=30.5 (verified over all godevccu paramset descriptions — 20 models incl. HmIP-BWTH, HmIP-eTRV-2, HmIPW-STH, HmIPW-SCTHD, ALPHA-IP-RBG), and HmIP-eTRV-2 ships TEMPERATURE_MAXIMUM with DEFAULT 30.5 (MASTER on VCU3609622:1). clamp (climate.go:2240-2248) then returns 30.0 for any request above it. The value the daemon advertises is the un-clamped one: HADiscoveryPayload publishes `max_temp: c.MaxTemp()` (payload.go:59), so HA's slider maximum is 30.5. The reference has no clamp on this path at all — BaseCustomDpClimate.set_temperature (climate.py:330-352) validates against min_temp/max_temp and then sends `temperature` verbatim — and the reference ClimateCapabilities dataclass carries no temperature bounds whatsoever (capabilities/climate.py:25-38); MinTemperature/MaxTemperature are a Go-only addition being used as a write-path clamp. Reachable through every north-bound surface: payload.go:455-461 registers the 'set_temperature' service and custom_dp_dispatcher.go:515-521 dispatches it.
findings.failure_scenario: HmIP-eTRV-2 (factory TEMPERATURE_MAXIMUM = 30.5). The MQTT climate discovery advertises max_temp = 30.5, so HA lets the user select 30.5 °C. The user selects 30.5; SetTemperature accepts it (30.5 <= MaxTemp() = 30.5) and then writes SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE = 30.0 to the CCU. HA's slider snaps back to 30.0 on the next echo and the radiator runs 0.5 K below the requested setpoint. The reference sends 30.5.
findings.verified_by: code trace: climate.go:946-972 + 2240-2248 + 602-623, init.go:109-121, payload.go:56-60; device data: SET_POINT_TEMPERATURE MIN/MAX and MASTER TEMPERATURE_MAXIMUM defaults read from ../godevccu/internal/embed/data/paramset_descriptions/*.json; reference climate.py:330-352 and capabilities/climate.py:25-38
findings.fix_sketch: Drop the capability clamp from SetTemperature (and from SetTemperatureRaw, whose contract is 'no range validation' yet clamps identically at climate.go:980) and rely on MinTemp()/MaxTemp() — the descriptor-derived bounds the daemon already publishes — as the single source of truth, matching the reference.

findings.title: Light.SetOnTime writes ON_TIME_VALUE / ON_TIME_UNIT — parameters that exist on no device in the fleet — so the light `set_on_time` operation never reaches the hardware
findings.claim: Light.SetOnTime encodes the duration and stages it as the pair (hmenum.ParameterOnTimeValue, hmenum.ParameterOnTimeUnit) (light.go:801-808 -> stageTimerPair light.go:829-848), i.e. the literal wire names ON_TIME_VALUE / ON_TIME_UNIT (pkg/hmenum/parameter.go:107-108). No CCU device carries those parameters: a scan of every VALUES paramset in ../godevccu/internal/embed/data/paramset_descriptions (and the identical ../pydevccu set, 435 model files) finds 0 occurrences of ON_TIME_VALUE and ON_TIME_UNIT, against 137 files carrying ON_TIME and 29 carrying DURATION_UNIT/DURATION_VALUE. The reference never uses these names either: Field.ON_TIME_VALUE/ON_TIME_UNIT map to Parameter.ON_TIME for the plain dimmer profiles (profile.py:370, :387, :399, :415, :427, :443) and to Parameter.DURATION_VALUE/DURATION_UNIT for the signal-light and RGBW profiles (profile.py:458-459, :479-480, :493-494, :508-509, :530-531). openccu-loom's own generated profile map has it right (generated_profile_configs.go:94-95, :141-142, :267-268, :294-295, :317-318 map FieldOnTimeUnit/Value onto DURATION_UNIT/DURATION_VALUE; :116, :211, :426 onto ON_TIME) — the light code simply does not consult it and hard-codes the wrong constants. The operation is reachable and advertised: custom_dp_dispatcher.go:312-319 routes op 'set_on_time' on any Light to Light.SetOnTime, and the dispatcher is mounted on REST (daemon_rest_mount.go:101), WS (ws_adapters.go:59) and the MQTT command subscriber (mqtt_sink.go:55). A second consequence of the same wrong constant: Light.hasOnTimeUnit is computed as `cfg.Channel.Parameter(hmenum.ParameterOnTimeUnit) != nil` (light.go:133) and is therefore false on every device, which permanently disables the signal-light on-time reset guarded by `l.resetsOnTimeOnTurnOn && l.hasOnTimeUnit` (light.go:587) — the reference's equivalent `self._dp_on_time.has_unit` is true for HmIP-BSL because its unit field resolves to DURATION_UNIT (light.py:414-424, profile.py:458-459).
findings.failure_scenario: Any dimmable light. A REST/WS/MQTT client (or the Node-RED contrib) invokes `set_on_time` with seconds=30. openccu-loom writes ON_TIME_VALUE=30 / ON_TIME_UNIT=0 to the channel; the CCU has no such parameters, so the write is rejected (XML-RPC Fault -5) or dropped and the light never gets a shutdown timer. Separately, on HmIP-BSL the ON_TIME reset that the reference performs on every plain turn_on never happens, so a previously configured DURATION keeps switching the LED off again.
findings.verified_by: code trace light.go:133, :587-597, :799-848 and custom_dp_dispatcher.go:312-319; fleet scan: 0 hits for ON_TIME_VALUE/ON_TIME_UNIT across all paramset descriptions in ../godevccu and ../pydevccu (137 files carry ON_TIME, 29 carry DURATION_UNIT); reference profile.py:370/458-459/508-509 and light.py:414-424
findings.fix_sketch: Resolve the timer pair from the profile's FieldOnTimeValue/FieldOnTimeUnit mapping (which already resolves correctly to ON_TIME or DURATION_VALUE+DURATION_UNIT per family) instead of hard-coding ParameterOnTimeValue/Unit, and derive hasOnTimeUnit from that resolved unit DP.
findings.resolution: the on-time predicate asks what the channel describes; TurnOnWith stages whichever shape it resolved instead of a hard-coded ON_TIME

findings.claim: Profiles() unconditionally puts ProfileNone first in the advertised list (climate.go:496-497). SetProfile dispatches the 'mode profiles' first via setModeProfile, whose switch handles only Boost/Comfort/Eco and returns (false, nil) for everything else (climate.go:1117-1126). findings.title: Climate.DisableAway on classic RF thermostats writes an empty PARTY_MODE_SUBMIT instead of the reference's past-window party code, so leaving away mode does nothing
findings.claim: The KindRF branch of DisableAway writes `PARTY_MODE_SUBMIT = ""` (climate.go:1266) and then optimistically records profile=None locally (climate.go:1272-1276). The reference cancels party mode by submitting a *fully-formed party code whose window lies in the past*: CustomDpRfThermostat.disable_away_mode builds start = now-11h, end = now-10h, away_temperature = 12.0 and sends _party_mode_code(...) to PARTY_MODE_SUBMIT (climate.py:554-565, encoder at climate.py:645-652). PARTY_MODE_SUBMIT is a write-only STRING whose DEFAULT is the empty string (HM-CC-RT-DN VCU0000050:4: {"TYPE":"STRING","OPERATIONS":2,"DEFAULT":""}), i.e. the empty value carries no window for the firmware to evaluate. Go already has the encoder it needs — partyModeCode (climate.go:1320-1332) is a faithful port of _party_mode_code and is used by SetAway (climate.go:1211) — it is simply not used on the disable path. The command is reachable via the 'disable_away' dispatcher op and the registered service.

findings.title: MCP has zero read-tool coverage for Matter, schedules, backups, and addon self-update despite full REST surfaces existing for all four
findings.claim: The REST API (assets/openapi.yaml) has 14 Matter paths (/matter/status, /matter/endpoints, /matter/fabrics, /matter/compatibility, /matter/exposable, /matter/commissioning/window, etc.), a backups family (/backups, /backups/{id}/download, /backups/{id}/restore, /backups/upload), a schedules family (/devices/{addr}/schedule, /devices/{addr}/channels/{no}/schedule, /schedules), and an addon-update family (/system/addon-update, /system/addon-update/check, /system/addon-update/install). None of these four domains has any corresponding tool in internal/north/mcp/tools.go, tools_hub.go, or tools_alarm.go -- grep for matter/schedule/backup/addon across the mcp package (excluding get_system_info's unrelated CCU-firmware fields) finds no registrar. get_health (tools.go:390-406) reports only Health.Snapshot() component names, which do not include a Matter/backup/addon component. ADR 0025 (the MCP adapter's own design rationale) names 'agent-driven diagnosis' -- reading state, reasoning over it, answering questions -- as the concrete use case the server exists to serve, and CLAUDE.md's own completion checklist calls out exactly these four areas ('Matter pairing/topology, security & safety, alarm, schedules, backups, addon self-update') as the ones to check when a new REST capability ships without its MCP counterpart.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator asks an MCP-connected agent 'is my Matter bridge exposing any devices right now', 'when did my last CCU backup run and did it succeed', or 'is there a pending addon update' -- all read-only status questions the REST API can already answer -- and the agent has no tool that can reach any of that state, even though it is exactly the kind of diagnostic question ADR 0025 describes as MCP's reason to exist. The gap is invisible in CI: nothing fails when a REST endpoint ships without an MCP counterpart (CLAUDE.md explicitly documents this as 'reviewed, not guard-enforced').
findings.verified_by: code trace: grep -inE 'matter|schedule|backup|addon' over internal/north/mcp/tools*.go (excluding _test.go) returns only CurrentFirmware/AvailableFirmware fields (CCU firmware, not addon self-update) and unrelated 'group'/'link' word matches; cross-checked against assets/openapi.yaml path list (grep of top-level paths) which lists the 14 Matter + 4 backup + 5 schedule + 3 addon-update paths.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a small set of read-only tools (get_matter_status, list_backups, get_addon_update_status, get_device_schedule) mirroring the existing get_health/get_system_info pattern; leave the higher-risk write paths (commissioning, backup restore, addon install) out unless a future ADR extends the write tier.
findings.resolution: read-only MCP tools for Matter status, backups and add-on update, wired in the composition root

findings.title: assets/wsapi.json omits `args` for ~15 client-callable commands that have real (often required) parameters, unlike sibling commands in the same category that are fully documented
findings.claim: links.add (wsapi.json:779) has no `args` block, but linksAddHandler (internal/north/rest/ws/commands_default.go:1170-1184) hard-requires sender+receiver ('sender and receiver required' at :1177) -- while its sibling links.set_info IS fully documented with {sender, receiver, name?, description?}. The same pattern repeats for: links.remove (wsapi.json:825; handler commands_default.go:1202-1216, requires sender+receiver) vs. documented links.list/links.activate_paramset; links.get_paramset (wsapi.json:802; commands_default.go:1250-1264, requires address+peer_address); links.put_paramset (wsapi.json:820; commands_default.go:1271-1286, requires address+peer_address+parameters); links.list_all (wsapi.json:815; commands_default.go:1156-1168, optional `central`); paramset.copy (wsapi.json:892; commands_extended.go:1185-1198, requires source_channel_address+target_channel_address, optional paramset_key) vs. documented paramset.get/paramset.put; service_messages.disable (wsapi.json:1090; commands_extended.go:931-947, requires id) and service_messages.unsuppress (wsapi.json:1100; commands_extended.go:962-980, requires channel, optional interface/parameter) vs. documented service_messages.ack/list; change_history.list (wsapi.json:235; commands_extended.go:880-898, optional limit/channel_address); and the five session-lifecycle commands config.session.save/discard/undo/redo/changes (wsapi.json:256-298; commands_default.go:1659-1714, all key off the same channel_address+paramset_key+central_name identity config.session.open documents) vs. the fully-documented config.session.open/set.
findings.failure_scenario: A generated client (the file's own header says a missing `args` field can mean either "no args" or "look at the Go handler" -- but a code generator or a hand-written Node-RED/Python client built purely from the schema cannot tell the two apart) calls links.add or paramset.copy with no body, gets a 400 'sender and receiver required' / 'source_channel_address and target_channel_address are required' instead of the schema having told it what to send in the first place -- unlike the fully-documented sibling commands in the same category, which do carry this information.
findings.verified_by: code trace of each handler body listed above, cross-referenced against the corresponding wsapi.json entry's `args` field via `python3 -c "json.load(...)"`; scripted extraction at $S/repro/D2/extract_handlers3.py + diff_args2.py resolves embedded/named Go struct types to their json tags and flags every command whose code-read field set is a superset of its declared args.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `args` blocks to the ~15 commands listed, mirroring the format already used for their documented siblings (links.set_info, paramset.get, service_messages.ack, config.session.open).

findings.title: matter.fabric_added broadcast can ship a payload missing every field its declared OpenAPI schema marks required
findings.claim: assets/wsapi.json declares matter.fabric_added's payload as schema `MatterFabric` (wsapi.json:1286-1291), which in assets/openapi.yaml lists fabric_index, fabric_id, fabric_id_hex, node_id, node_id_hex, vendor_id, compressed_id, root_public_key as `required`. fabricPayload() (cmd/openccu-loom/matter_event_publisher.go:86-117) resolves this from the fabric store on a best-effort basis: when p.fabrics is nil (comment at :24-26: "Nil in minimal wirings") or the store lookup errors or finds no matching record (:92-95, :96-116), it returns `map[string]any{"fabric_index": fabricIndex}` -- a bare one-field object, dropping the other 7 required fields. This is deliberate (the code comment at matter_event_publisher.go:73 says a lookup miss 'degrades to the index rather than dropping the event', and cmd/openccu-loom/matter_event_publisher_test.go:191-213 TestPublishFabricAddedStillEmitsWhenTheFabricCannotBeResolved pins exactly this degrade), but the wsapi.json/openapi.yaml contract was never updated to reflect that the payload can take this shape -- the docs for the broadcast (docs/external-clients/mcp.md is unaffected; the relevant claim is the MatterEvent doc comment at internal/north/rest/handlers/matter_events.go:79-81, 'Payload: MatterFabricResponse') assert the full shape unconditionally.
findings.failure_scenario: A commissioning event fires while the fabric store read is slow/erroring (the lookup has an explicit 3s timeout at matter_event_publisher.go:32,90) or before the just-written AddNOC record is visible to a subsequent read. The daemon still publishes matter.fabric_added (by design, so the frontend commissioning-progress UI doesn't stall), but a strictly-typed generated client (per docs/external-clients/mcp.md's sibling promise that generated client type packages resolve broadcast payloads from the OpenAPI components) fails to decode the frame because 7 required fields are absent -- turning the Go side's 'never swallow the notification' resilience choice into a swallowed notification at the client's parse boundary instead.
findings.verified_by: code trace: matter_event_publisher.go:86-117 (fabricPayload fallback branches), matter_event_publisher_test.go:191-213 (test pinning the degrade), assets/openapi.yaml components.schemas.MatterFabric `required` list (8 fields) read via python3+yaml.
findings.fix_sketch: Either make the openapi.yaml MatterFabric schema used for this broadcast optional-fields (or introduce a MatterFabricDegraded variant covering the fabric_index-only shape) so generated clients can decode both cases, or block the fabric_added publish until the store read succeeds (bounded by the existing 3s timeout) and fall back to matter.fabric_removed-style minimal event only as a last resort with a distinct `type`.

findings.claim: internal/alarm/codes/facade.go:196 and :216 call f.recordInvalid(ctx, zoneID, source, "code_missing"/"invalid_code", ...) on a required-but-absent or wrong/unknown alarm-code attempt; recordInvalid (facade.go:384-396) forwards the literal event string into journalFault -> engine.JournalEntry{Event: event, Class: AlarmJournalClassFault}. assets/ui/src/routes/alarm/AlarmJournal.svelte:62-66 renders each entry via eventLabel(event), which looks up `alarm.journal_event.${event}` and - by deliberate design (comment at lines 57-61) - falls back to the RAW event token (not the dotted key) on a catalogue miss. assets/ui/src/lib/i18n.ts has no `alarm.journal_event.code_missing` / `alarm.journal_event.invalid_code` entry in EITHER the EN or DE catalogue (grep of both blocks returns no match), even though the adjacent "code_lockout", "code_permission_denied", "code_locked_out" events from the same file are all translated. The Alarm Journal view shows the raw machine token "code_missing" or "invalid_code" in the event column instead of a translated phrase, in BOTH English and German (German users see the English snake_case token verbatim, unlike every neighbouring journal row which reads as a normal sentence in their locale).

findings.title: Operator-set channel Hidden/Locked flags survive device unpair and central removal: both purge methods exist, are documented as being called, and have no production caller
findings.claim: ChannelFlagsStore.DeleteForCentral (channel_flags.go:131-141) carries the doc-comment 'Called on live central removal' and ChannelFlagsStore.DeleteDevice (channel_flags.go:111-128) carries 'Called on device-remove / unpair'. Neither claim holds. `grep -rn 'DeleteForCentral|DeleteDevice' internal/ cmd/ | grep -v '^internal/store/sqlite/' | grep -v _test` resolves every production call site: the only DeleteForCentral calls in the daemon are cmd/openccu-loom/central_adopt.go:744 (historyStore) and :749 (recordingStore); the DeleteDevice calls are on ValuesCacheStore (values_cache_evict.go:52), Paramsets/Values/Master (cachereset.go:327/335/347) and the backend unpair op — none on ChannelFlagsStore. purgeCentralState (central_adopt.go:715-754), which exists precisely to delete 'every derived SQLite row keyed to a removed central', takes only valuesCacheStore, masterValuesStore, historyStore and recordingStore as parameters; channel_flags is not in the list. The in-memory half has the same gap: channelflags.Overlay (internal/channelflags/overlay.go:26-33) is hydrated once at boot from ChannelFlagsStore.List (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:100-111) and exposes only Get/Set — no per-device or per-central removal, and no re-Load. The flags are load-bearing on two hot paths: DevicePipeline re-applies them to every channel on every (re)ingest, hot-plug and reconnect (internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:448-451, ch.SetOperatorFlags(f.Hidden, f.Locked)), and channelHiddenGate (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_infra.go:259-265) is the predicate the MQTT bridge consults to drop a channel from discovery. Per the type's own doc (channel_flags.go:13-17) Hidden removes the channel from operation lists / MQTT discovery / Matter exposure and Locked blocks VALUES writes.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator hides two channels of CCU 'haus' (say a technical channel and a maintenance channel) and locks a third, then removes 'haus' from Settings -> CCUs to fix its host/credentials and re-adds it under the same name — the flow purgeCentralState was written for. values_cache, master_values and the measurement history are purged; channel_flags is not. On re-adopt the pipeline re-applies the stale rows at ingest, so the two channels are silently missing from MQTT discovery and Matter exposure again and the third still rejects control writes, for a CCU the operator believes was removed and re-added clean. The same rows also survive an unpair: re-pairing the same physical device (which keeps its address) silently restores its old Hidden/Locked state. For a central that is removed for good, the rows and their overlay entries stay in the database and in memory forever.
findings.verified_by: code trace: channel_flags.go:111/131 (doc claims) -> repo-wide grep for callers of both methods (only the store's own tests) -> central_adopt.go:715-754 (purgeCentralState parameter list omits the store) -> daemon.go:100-111 (overlay hydrated once) -> overlay.go (no delete-by-central/device) -> device_pipeline.go:448-451 and daemon_infra.go:259-265 (effect).
findings.fix_sketch: Pass channelFlagsStore into purgeCentralState and call DeleteForCentral there, and add an Overlay.DeleteCentral that the same path invokes so the in-memory copy follows the row. Call ChannelFlagsStore.DeleteDevice plus an Overlay.DeleteDevice from the device-remove path (adapter/callback_handlers.go dropDevice and adapter/device_admin.go UnpairDevice), and pin both through the composition root asserting the effect, not the call.
findings.resolution: the channel-flags evictor is wired into the daemon and honours ModelTeardown so a cache clear does not wipe the operator overrides

findings.title: Removing a central deletes its per-datapoint history recording overrides from SQLite but not from the in-memory overlay, so the two disagree until the next restart
findings.claim: RecordingOverrides is the authoritative hot-path overlay for the per-datapoint 'always record / never record' toggle: Decide (overrides.go:72-83) is consulted on every value-changed event (internal/history/recorder.go:343) and Effective (overrides.go:88-99) backs GET /api/v1/history/recording (router.go:944). It is populated exactly once, at wire time: wireRecordingOverrides calls overlay.Load(ctx) at cmd/openccu-loom/history_wiring.go:110, and Load's own doc says 'Called once at wire time' (overrides.go:50). `grep -rn 'RecordingOverrides' cmd/ internal/ | grep -v _test` shows no second Load, no OnRegister/Unregister hook and no per-central purge on the overlay; the only mutators are Set and Clear, both single-datapoint. Meanwhile the removal path does purge the durable half: purgeCentralState calls recordingStore.DeleteForCentral(ctx, cc.Name) at cmd/openccu-loom/central_adopt.go:749, deleting every measurement_recording_overrides row for that central. Nothing tells the overlay. Note the store also has DeleteDevice (recording_overrides.go:118) with no production caller at all.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator force-excludes a noisy data point of CCU 'haus' from history (PUT /history/recording, record=false). They later remove 'haus' and re-adopt it under the same name at runtime. The DB rows are gone, but the overlay still holds the entry, so Decide keeps returning false and the data point records nothing — while a fresh install with the identical configuration records it. GET /history/recording still reports source='override' for a row that no longer exists. After the next daemon restart Load reads the now-empty table and the override silently disappears, so the same data point starts recording without anyone changing anything. The inverse case (a force-*include* override) leaves history being written for a data point the DB says has no override.
findings.verified_by: code trace: history_wiring.go:100-114 (single Load) -> overrides.go:51/72/88 (no invalidation path, no second Load; grep over cmd/ and internal/ returns no other caller) -> central_adopt.go:749 (DB rows deleted) -> recorder.go:343 (Decide on the hot path).
findings.fix_sketch: Give RecordingOverrides a DeleteCentral(central string) that drops the matching keys under o.mu, and call it from purgeCentralState right after recordingStore.DeleteForCentral; wire RecordingOverrideStore.DeleteDevice + an overlay DeleteDevice into the device-remove path the same way.

findings.title: The three-tier measurement deletes are not one transaction, so a failure after the raw-table statement leaves the removed CCU's or device's rollups behind — the exact resurfacing the code comments say the multi-tier delete exists to prevent
findings.claim: DeleteDevice (measurements.go:1460-1481), DeleteForCentral (:1505-1524) and DeleteAll (:1528-1542) each loop over three separate statements — one per tier (measurements, measurements_hourly, measurements_daily) — issuing each through s.db.ExecContext, i.e. three independent autocommit transactions with no BeginTx around the loop, and returning on the first error. Every other multi-statement write in the package (RollupHourly :1210, RollupDaily :1321, config_sections Put :103, users Delete, areas, alarm_outputs, alarm_sensors) uses BeginTx. The consequence is spelled out by the functions' own comments: DeleteForCentral :1509-1513 says deleting only `measurements` 'left a removed CCU's aggregates behind — and re-adopting the same central name resurfaced them in the energy views as if the CCU had never been away'; DeleteDevice :1467-1469 says the same for an unpaired device. A partial run reproduces that state exactly. The caller does not retry or escalate: purgeCentralState logs the error at warn level and continues (central_adopt.go:744-747), and the removal proceeds regardless.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon removes CCU 'haus' while the history database is busy (a concurrent rollup or retention pass holds the writer past the 5 s busy_timeout, or the process is stopped mid-removal). The raw `measurements` DELETE commits, the `measurements_hourly` DELETE returns SQLITE_BUSY, and DeleteForCentral returns; the operator sees only a warn line in the log. The daily tier is never touched at all, and the daily tier has no retention by default ('keep daily rows forever', :1440). When the operator re-adds a CCU under the name 'haus', the energy view shows the removed CCU's consumption and feed-in history as that CCU's own. Nothing ever cleans it up.
findings.verified_by: code trace: measurements.go:1470-1479 / 1514-1522 / 1532-1540 (three autocommit statements, early return on error) vs. the transactional shape used at :1210 and :1321 in the same file; central_adopt.go:744-747 (error only logged).
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap each of the three loops in s.db.BeginTx / tx.ExecContext / tx.Commit with the usual `defer func(){ _ = tx.Rollback() }()`, so the tiers are cleared atomically; optionally surface a hard error from purgeCentralState for the central-removal case rather than a warn.

findings.title: After migration 037 blanked the repaired zone slugs, the security domain re-derives them per boot instead of persisting them, so those zones lose the frozen-identifier guarantee and can collide
findings.claim: A zone slug is meant to be frozen at creation: it is assigned once by uniqueZoneSlug (internal/north/rest/handlers/alarm_config.go:85), and AlarmZoneStore.Upsert deliberately omits slug from its ON CONFLICT update list with the comment 'it is frozen at creation. Letting a rename move it would orphan every consumer entity of that zone' (internal/store/sqlite/alarm_zones.go:46-58). Migration 037 (migrations/037_alarm_zone_slug_charset.sql:31) repairs the slugs that migration 034's SQL backfill produced outside the identifier grammar by setting them to the empty string, relying on 'the security domain derives one with HubSlug whenever the stored value is empty, which is the same value a freshly created zone gets'. That derive exists — refreshZoneSlugs, internal/security/index.go:161-176 — but it writes only into the in-memory aggregate (s.agg.zones[...]) and never back through AlarmZoneStore, so the stored slug stays ''. Two consequences follow. (a) For every repaired zone the effective identifier is now a function of the CURRENT name, re-evaluated each boot: a rename goes through Upsert (which keeps slug='') and the next refresh derives a different slug. That slug is the MQTT state topic and the discovery entity key — securityZoneEntity builds key 'zone_'+slug and topic securityZoneTopic(base, slug) (internal/north/mqtt/security_entities.go:123-137) — and the reconciler retires the discovery of a slug that disappears (internal/north/mqtt/security_reconcile.go:216-231). (b) refreshZoneSlugs applies no collision suffix, unlike uniqueZoneSlug (alarm_config.go:508-522), while the snapshot is a map keyed by slug: `snap.Zones[z.Slug] = cloneZone(z)` (internal/security/aggregate.go:234-236). Two zones that derive the same slug therefore collapse into one entry.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) A German install has a zone 'Küche'. Migration 034 stored 'küche', migration 037 blanked it, and the daemon now serves it as 'kuche'. Home Assistant has an entity built from that slug. The operator renames the zone to 'Küche EG'. Every other zone keeps its entity across a rename; this one does not — the derived slug becomes 'kuche-eg', the reconciler retires the old discovery topic, HA drops the old entity and creates a new one, and every dashboard card and automation referencing the old entity_id breaks with no warning. findings.title: A program's last-execution timestamp is never recorded: the CCU's lastExecuteTime is decoded and thrown away and hub.Program.OnExecution has no production caller, so last_executed / last_result_success are permanently absent on REST, WS, MQTT, MCP and the SPA column.
findings.claim: Two independent halves are both missing. (1) CCU side: `programEntry` (internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:780-786) declares `LastExecuteTime json.RawMessage \`json:"lastExecuteTime"\`` and `loadPrograms` decodes `Program.getAll` into `[]programEntry` (hub_wiring.go:944-945), but the per-program loop (hub_wiring.go:951-989) only ever reads `p.ID`, `p.Name`, `p.IsActive`, `p.IsInternal` — `LastExecuteTime` has no reader anywhere (`grep -rn LastExecuteTime --include=*.go internal/` returns only the declaration at hub_wiring.go:785 plus unrelated method names in internal/model/hub/program.go). aiohomematic, the CCU-side reference, does consume it: aiohomematic/client/json_rpc.py:276 (`LAST_EXECUTE_TIME = "lastExecuteTime"`), :989, :998 -> ProgramData.last_execute_time -> aiohomematic/model/hub/data_point.py:313. (2) Daemon side: `hub.Program.lastExecute` is written in exactly one place, `Program.OnExecution` (internal/model/hub/program.go:336-353). `grep -rn OnExecution --include=*.go .` finds NO production caller — only *_test.go files. `Program.Execute` (program.go:358-371) and `ExecuteWithConditionCheck` (program.go:386-403) call `p.ExecuteNotifier`, which the hub coordinator wires (internal/central/coordinators/hub.go:241-243) to `NotifyProgramExecuted` (hub.go:209-222), which only publishes a `hmevent.ProgramExecutedEvent`. The event's subscribers are internal/north/rest/ws/hub_events.go:270 (WS broadcast) and cmd/openccu-loom/program_execute_audit.go:64 (audit row); neither calls back into `OnExecution`. Consequence: `Program.LastExecution()` (program.go:210-214) always returns `(zero, false)` and `LastResult()` (program.go:232-236) always returns `(false, false)` in a running daemon. Every consumer therefore emits nothing: REST internal/north/rest/handlers/hub.go:427-430 (`if ts, hasTS := p.LastExecution(); hasTS { e.LastExecuted = ... }`), MQTT/payload internal/model/hub/payload.go:87-92 (`LastExecuted` and `LastResultSuccess`), WS cmd/openccu-loom/ws_adapters.go:511, MCP internal/north/mcp/tools_hub.go:88. The field is documented in assets/openapi.yaml:9293-9295 ('last_executed: RFC3339 timestamp of the most recent execution') and rendered by the SPA in assets/ui/src/routes/ProgramList.svelte:186-189 and :284-288 (column `programs.col.last_executed`, formatted via `formatDate`).
findings.failure_scenario: An operator opens Einstellungen -> Programme (SPA /app/#/programs). The 'Zuletzt ausgefuehrt' / 'Last executed' column is empty for every program, on every CCU, forever — including for a program the operator just ran from that very page, and including programs the CCU itself ran minutes ago (the CCU knows: Program.getAll returned e.g. lastExecuteTime='2026-08-17T09:14:22'). The same field is absent from GET /api/v1/hub/programs, from the WS program list, from the MQTT program state topic, and from the MCP hub tool, so no external client can build a 'program ran' automation either. `last_result_success` is dead for the same reason.
findings.verified_by: code trace: exhaustive grep of `OnExecution` (only *_test.go callers), of `LastExecuteTime` (declaration-only), and of `LastExecution()` (4 read sites, all gated on the never-true `ok`); cross-checked against the reference implementation in ../aiohomematic (json_rpc.py:276/989/998, model/hub/data_point.py:313) and against the documented contract in assets/openapi.yaml:9293 and assets/ui/src/routes/ProgramList.svelte:186.
findings.fix_sketch: In loadPrograms, parse `p.LastExecuteTime` (the CCU sends a bare local wall clock such as "2026-08-17T09:14:22", so use time.ParseInLocation against time.Local, not time.Parse, or it lands 2 h off in CEST) and seed it onto the Program (a new `SeedLastExecution(t)` that does not fire subscribers). Separately, have the hub coordinator's ProgramExecutedEvent path — or Program.Execute itself — call `p.OnExecution(success, trigger)` so a daemon-observed run updates the stamp, and add a wiring pin under tests/contract/wiring_pins/ that asserts last_executed is non-empty after a program is executed through the real REST handler.

findings.title: hub.InboxDevice.FirstSeen has no writer, so the inbox 'first seen' timestamp is permanently 0 (1970-01-01) on REST/WS/MQTT and blank in the SPA — which is also the inbox table's default sort key.
findings.claim: `hub.InboxDevice.FirstSeen int64` (internal/model/hub/inbox.go:35-37) documents itself as 'a Unix-second timestamp set by the coordinator on first detection'. There are exactly two production construction sites for the struct and neither sets the field: internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:1378-1384 (the CCU inbox scan, sets DeviceID/Address/Name/Model/Interface only) and internal/central/adapter/pending_devices.go:33-38 (the deferred-creation queue, sets Address/Model/Interface/PendingCreation only). `grep -rn 'FirstSeen' --include=*.go .` over the whole tree (excluding the unrelated internal/store/sqlite/incidents.go rows) yields only those two literals, the field declaration, three pure copy sites, and one test literal (cmd/openccu-loom/ws_hub_messages_test.go:166). So the value is always the int64 zero. It is then published as-is on three planes: REST `first_seen` (internal/north/rest/handlers/hub.go:258 with `omitempty`, so the key silently disappears; assigned at hub.go:1079) — the field is declared in assets/openapi.yaml:12715; WS (cmd/openccu-loom/ws_adapters.go:925, `"first_seen": e.FirstSeen` — no omitempty, emits literal 0); MQTT/payload (internal/payload/state.go:324, `FirstSeen int64 \`json:"first_seen"\`` — no omitempty, and the doc comment at state.go:317-319 claims it 'is the Unix-epoch second the device first appeared in the inbox'). The SPA renders it as a dedicated column (assets/ui/src/routes/Inbox.svelte:567-570, label `inbox.col.first_seen`, cell at :777-780 via `formatTs`, which returns "" for a falsy value at :536) and — the second effect — uses it as the table's default sort: `initialSort={{ key: "first_seen", asc: false }}` (Inbox.svelte:749) over a getter that always returns 0 (:570).
findings.failure_scenario: An operator pairs three devices over an afternoon and opens the Inbox view. The 'Erstmals gesehen' / 'First seen' column is empty for all of them, and because the table's default sort key is a constant 0 the three entries are not ordered newest-first as the `asc: false` default intends — the operator cannot tell which device just arrived. An MQTT consumer subscribed to the inbox topic reads `"first_seen": 0` and, taking the documented contract at internal/payload/state.go:317 at face value, renders 1970-01-01 01:00 (CET) for every pending device.
findings.verified_by: code trace: exhaustive tree-wide grep of `FirstSeen` plus inspection of both `hub.InboxDevice{...}` composite literals (hub_wiring.go:1378, pending_devices.go:33); publication sites confirmed at hub.go:1079, ws_adapters.go:925, payload/state.go:324; SPA column + default sort confirmed at Inbox.svelte:567/570/749/777.
findings.fix_sketch: Set `FirstSeen: time.Now().Unix()` when an entry first enters the inbox — but preserve it across the periodic rescan, since `Inbox.Replace` rebuilds the whole list every hub scan (carry the previous value over for an address already present, otherwise the timestamp resets on every refresh). Alternatively drop the field from the three payloads and the SPA column rather than shipping a permanently-zero one. Add `omitempty` to the WS and MQTT encodings either way so a 0 never renders as 1970.

findings.title: The HA entity-description Multiplier override is generated but never applied, so every LEVEL data point whose CCU descriptor carries no UNIT is published to Home Assistant as a raw 0..1 value labelled "%" (100x low)
findings.claim: The reference HA integration resolves the scaling factor as `entity_description.multiplier if ... is not None else data_point.multiplier` -- the per-entity registry override WINS over the unit-derived one (../homematicip_local/custom_components/homematicip_local/sensor.py:196-201, applied at :238 `new_value = value * self._multiplier`; identical precedence in number.py:226-235,258,274). OpenCCU-Loom ported the registry table verbatim including the override field (`HARegistryDescription.Multiplier *float64`, internal/north/mqtt/entity_descriptions_generated.go:45; e.g. rule :157 `{Key:"LEVEL", UnitOfMeasurement:"%", Multiplier: 100.0, Devices:["HmIP-eTRV","HmIP-HEATING","HmIP-FALMOT-C12","HmIPW-FALMOT-C12"], Category:"sensor"}`, plus :153/:158/:159/:160/:222/:251), but `applyEntityDescription` (internal/north/mqtt/entity_descriptions_apply.go:39-83) copies DeviceClass, StateClass, EntityCategory, Icon, TranslationKey, UnitOfMeasurement, SuggestedDisplayPrecision, EnabledByDefault and Options and NEVER reads `desc.Multiplier`. A repo-wide grep for `.Multiplier` outside the generated file and its own struct declaration returns only `generic.DataPoint.Multiplier()` (internal/model/generic/unit_cleanup.go:131) and `device.Channel.ParameterMultiplier` (internal/model/device/channel.go:535) -- i.e. only the descriptor-UNIT-derived factor. That factor is `MultiplierForUnit(d.Descriptor.Unit)` = 100.0 only when the wire descriptor's UNIT string is literally "100%" (unit_cleanup.go:51-53,99-107). The unit string, by contrast, comes from `CleanupUnit` (unit_cleanup.go:82-95), whose FIRST rule is the per-parameter override table -- `fixUnitByParam[LEVEL] = "%"` (unit_cleanup.go:22) -- which fires regardless of the raw UNIT. So for a LEVEL DP with an empty descriptor UNIT the discovery body ends up with `unit_of_measurement: "%"` (set at discovery.go:62 via the registry rule, or at discovery.go:761 via CleanupUnit) while `applyMultiplierSensor` (discovery.go:1022-1038) reads `ParameterMultiplier` = (1.0,false) and returns early, emitting no scaling `value_template`. Measured against the 399-device paramset-description corpus (../godevccu/internal/embed/data/paramset_descriptions): 29 VALUES-paramset LEVEL/LEVEL_2 parameters carry UNIT=null while 2200 carry "100%". The affected devices are exactly ones the registry rules name: HmIP-eTRV-2 / -2 I9F / -B / -B-2 R4M / -B1 / -C-2 / -E / -F and HmIP-HEATING (channel 1 LEVEL, OPERATIONS=7 -- the valve-position `pipe_level` sensor), HmIP-BDT ch3, HmIP-FDT ch1, HmIP-DRDI3 ch4/8/12, HmIPW-DRD3 ch1/5/9, HmIP-SCTH230 ch11 (`light_level`), HmIPW-WRC6 ch7..13 (OPERATIONS=7). `ev.Channel` is the real `*device.Channel` in production (set at internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:2286), so the interface assertion succeeds and the multiplier really is 1.0 rather than the reader being absent.
findings.failure_scenario: An HmIP-eTRV-2 valve thermostat reports LEVEL = 0.42 on channel 1 (valve 42 % open). The MQTT discovery config for that sensor declares `unit_of_measurement: "%"`, `state_class: measurement`, `translation_key: pipe_level` and no multiplying `value_template`; the state topic carries `{"value":0.42,...}`. Home Assistant shows `0.42 %`. The reference integration shows `42 %` for the same reading. The writable twin is worse: for the same parameter the `number` component seeds min/max/step straight from the descriptor (discovery.go:795-812 -> 0.0 / 1.01 / 0.01) and `applyMultiplierNumber` (discovery.go:1042-1073) also returns early, so HA renders a slider with range 0..1.01 labelled "%" and no `command_template`; an operator who types 50 into the box sends the literal 50.0 to a parameter whose MAX is 1.01 and the write is rejected. Correct behaviour per the registry rule the repo itself generated: value x100, min 0 / max 101 / step 1, and `command_template` dividing by 100.

Add a discovery test that pins the eTRV LEVEL sensor's `value_template` to `* 100` and the number's min/max/step to 0/101/1.

Confirmed: applyEntityDescription (entity_descriptions_apply.go:39-83) copies nine fields and never reads desc.Multiplier; the only multiplier readers in the tree are generic.DataPoint.Multiplier() (unit_cleanup.go:131, driven by UNIT=="100%") and Channel.ParameterMultiplier (channel.go:535). multiplierByParam holds only TIME_OF_OPERATION. Built an HmIP-eTRV-2 channel with the real descriptor (FLOAT, MIN 0.0, MAX 1.01, UNIT null) and ran the real discovery builder: ParameterMultiplier(LEVEL) = (1, false); the sensor body gets unit_of_measurement "%", translation_key pipe_level and a value_template with no scaling — HA renders 0.42 % where the reference renders 42 % (precedence rule verified verbatim at sensor.py:195-201 and applied at :238). REFUTED half: the 'writable twin' never exists. LEVEL on HmIP-eTRV / HmIP-HEATING is in switchDPToSensor (switch_to_sensor.go:22-25), so resolveComponent downgrades Number to Sensor (discovery.go:466-468) — my reproducer requested Category=Number and got component=sensor with no min/max/step and no command_template. Those two model families are also the only ones carrying a `number` LEVEL rule with a Multiplier, so no HA slider with range 0..1.01 and no rejected write exists anywhere. Severity down-rated to medium: every registry rule that would scale LEVEL/LEVEL_2 also sets EnabledByDefault:false, so the mis-scaled entities are disabled-by-default diagnostics an operator must switch on before seeing the 100x error.

""}` into HistoryChart.svelte, which renders it in the chart title at HistoryChart.svelte:187. findings.title: climate's celsiusToMatter clamps to the raw int16 bounds instead of the TemperatureMeasurement constraint range, so a fault reading is emitted as -327.68 C on the climate endpoint and -273.15 C on the standalone one
findings.claim: `celsiusToMatter` (internal/model/custom/climate/matter.go:194-204) rounds `c*100` and saturates at +32767 / -32768. Its sibling `celsiusToInt16` (internal/north/matter/cluster/measurement/measurement.go:394-403) saturates at +32766 / -27315 -- and that asymmetry is a deliberate, already-shipped fix: notes/parity/by_design.md:1511-1513 records it as item L01-D06 ("celsiusToInt16 clamp fixed: 32767 is TLV-null sentinel; -32768 is below kMinMeasuredValueRange"). The fix was never propagated to the climate encoder, and climate/matter.go:191-193 asserts the opposite in prose: "Matches internal/north/matter/cluster/measurement celsiusToInt16, the encoder behind the standalone TemperatureMeasurement endpoints." matter.js HEAD confirms the floor: ../matter.js/packages/model/src/standard/elements/temperature-measurement.element.ts:19-22 gives MinMeasuredValue `constraint: "-27315 to maxMeasuredValue - 1", default: -27315` and MeasuredValue `constraint: "minMeasuredValue to maxMeasuredValue"`, so -32768 is out of constraint for the mandatory attribute. `celsiusToMatter` feeds Thermostat LocalTemperature / OccupiedHeating- and CoolingSetpoint / the Min/Max setpoint limits (climate/matter.go:555,566,579,589,595) and `climateTempMeasServer.MatterRead` -> TemperatureMeasurement.MeasuredValue (climate/matter.go:846). The wrong bounds are pinned rather than caught: internal/model/custom/climate/climate_internals_test.go asserts `celsiusToMatter(-400.0) == -32768`.
findings.failure_scenario: A HomeMatic external temperature probe with a broken lead reports the classic invalid reading; the ACTUAL_TEMPERATURE descriptor range on 62 device descriptors in the corpus is MIN=-3276.8 / MAX=3276.7, so -3276.8 is a representable wire value. On a climate device the bridge emits `celsiusToMatter(-3276.8)` = round(-327680) -> clamped to -32768 -> Apple Home / Google Home shows -327.68 C, an out-of-constraint value for the cluster. The very same reading on a standalone temperature-sensor endpoint goes through `celsiusToInt16` and yields -27315 = -273.15 C. Two endpoints of the same bridge disagree on the same physical fault. Correct per matter.js: clamp to [-27315, 32766] on both paths (or emit TLV null).

findings.title: Every history/energy average is an unweighted mean of event-driven push samples, so a mostly-idle POWER series reports several times its true average
findings.claim: CCU parameters arrive push-driven, so sample spacing is irregular by construction. Every averaging step in the pipeline is a plain arithmetic mean over sample COUNT with no duration term anywhere: the raw-bucket fast path uses `AVG(value)` (internal/store/sqlite/measurements.go:469), the hourly rollup uses `SUM(value) OVER w / COUNT(*) OVER w` (rollupHourlySelectSQL, measurements.go:1176-1192), the daily rollup folds `SUM(sum) OVER w / SUM(count) OVER w` (:1274-1293), and the energy handler recombines with `b.AvgPowerW += row.Sum / float64(row.Count)` (internal/north/rest/handlers/energy.go:262). No `LAG`, no timestamp delta, no time weighting exists in any of these paths. The field is published as `avg_power_w` on `EnergyBucket` (energy.go:40) and as `avg` on the generic history buckets, with no documentation anywhere that it is a sample mean rather than a time average (grepped notes/parity/by_design.md and SPECIFICATION.md: no hit).
findings.failure_scenario: An HmIP-PSM feeding a washing machine: POWER pushes 0 W, then 600 W when the motor starts, then 0 W again five minutes later; three samples land in the hour bucket. `avg_power_w` = (0+600+0)/3 = 200 W. The true time-weighted average over that hour is (55*0 + 5*600)/60 = 50 W -- a 4x overstatement shown in the SPA energy view and in the `/api/v1/energy` response. The same bias applies to `avg` on the plain `/history` endpoint for every non-cumulative parameter (temperature, humidity, illumination). The Wh totals are unaffected: `ConsumedWh` / `FeedInWh` come from the ENERGY_COUNTER first/last delta, not from the POWER mean.
findings.verified_by: code trace (measurements.go:466-478 for AVG(value), :1176-1192, :1274-1293; energy.go:40, :259-266)
findings.fix_sketch: Compute the average as a time-weighted integral (sum of value_i * (ts_{i+1} - ts_i) over the bucket, divided by the covered span, carrying the last pre-bucket sample as the opening value), or -- if the sample mean is intentional -- rename the field and say so in the OpenAPI description so the SPA does not present it as a power average.
findings.resolution: time-weighted averaging behind its own weighted_sum/weight_ms columns (history migration 007); count keeps meaning a sample count and covered_ms carries the span to clients

findings.title: A cumulative-counter reset followed by a rise inside a single rollup bucket silently drops the pre-reset consumption from both the bucket and the range total
findings.claim: The rollup keeps only `FIRST_VALUE`/`LAST_VALUE` per bucket (rollupHourlySelectSQL, internal/store/sqlite/measurements.go:1170-1192; energyRawFoldSQL for the un-rolled tail, :866-890). Both consumers reduce a bucket to that pair: `energyDelta(first, last)` returns `last` when `last < first` (internal/north/rest/handlers/energy.go:374-380, used at :268 and :274), and `counterRangeTotal` walks the same flattened first/last sequence (:389-403). Neither consults the bucket's `min`/`max`, which are the only columns that retain the intra-bucket peak. The reset flag is set but the magnitude of the lost rise is neither reported nor recoverable. To be explicit about what IS correct: a reset that straddles two buckets is handled -- `counterRangeTotal`'s inter-reading segmentation exists precisely for that, and no path ever emits a negative or wrap-magnitude spike.
findings.failure_scenario: An HmIP-PSM's ENERGY_COUNTER within one hour reports 100 Wh (t=0), 150 Wh (t=10 min, 50 Wh consumed), 0 Wh (t=20 min, meter reset after a re-pair, load still running), 20 Wh (t=30 min, 20 Wh consumed since the reset). The hourly rollup stores first=100, last=20. `energyDelta(100,20)` sees last<first, returns 20 and reset=true. The bucket reports consumed_wh=20 and the device range total inherits the same 20; the true consumption in that hour was 70 Wh. The 50 Wh is gone from the energy view and from any cost derived from it, with only a boolean `reset` hinting that something happened.
findings.verified_by: code trace (measurements.go:866-890, 1170-1192; energy.go:259-276, 336-403)
findings.fix_sketch: Carry the bucket's `max` into the reset case: when `last < first`, the consumed amount is `(max - first) + last` rather than `last`. Alternatively segment on the raw rows for buckets flagged as reset instead of on the rolled-up first/last pair.

findings.title: Revoking a token through the legacy DELETE /auth/tokens/{id} leaves the token's WebSocket connections open, while the v2 sibling closes them
findings.claim: Two token-revocation routes exist. `DELETE /auth/tokens/v2/{fingerprint}` is wired with the socket revoker — `handlers.DeleteTokenAdmin(d.TokenAdmin, d.AuditRecorder, d.TokenSockets)` (internal/north/rest/router.go:1335-1336), and Deps.TokenSockets is documented as 'closes the WebSocket connections a revoked bearer token opened, so DELETE /auth/tokens/v2/{fingerprint} ends the token's command plane too' (router.go:234-238), wired in production to the ws.Hub (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest_mount.go:345 `TokenSockets: d.tokenSocketRevoker()`). The legacy route is `r.With(admin).Delete("/auth/tokens/{id}", handlers.DeleteToken(d.Auth))` (router.go:767) and `DeleteToken` (internal/north/rest/handlers/auth.go:179-200) does nothing but `d.Tokens.DeleteByID(id)` plus an audit record — it has no socket parameter at all. The legacy store is reachable in production: `restAuth.Tokens = d.tokens` is the MemoryTokenStore (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest.go:296) which is seeded from the YAML `north.rest.auth.tokens` map and written by the legacy `POST /auth/tokens` (auth.go:159 `d.Tokens.Put(...)`), and it authenticates as the Secondary of `auth.ChainedTokenStore{Primary: d.sqTokens, Secondary: d.tokens}` (daemon_rest.go:160). Combined with finding E5-authz-matrix-1 (the socket never re-resolves its credential), the revoked token's socket keeps dispatching until the client disconnects.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin issues an operator token via POST /api/v1/auth/tokens, a client uses it to open /api/v1/events, and the admin later revokes it via DELETE /api/v1/auth/tokens/{id} (the route the same legacy pair created it on). Every HTTP request with that token now answers 401, the SPA's token list shows it gone, and the audit log records the revocation — but the open socket continues to accept operator-tier commands (paramset writes, alarm disarm, program execution) for as long as it stays connected. Revoking the identical credential through the v2 route would have torn it down.
findings.verified_by: code trace: router.go:767 vs router.go:1335-1336; handlers/auth.go:179-200 has no TokenSocketRevoker; daemon_rest.go:296 + 160 show the MemoryTokenStore is a live authentication source through ChainedTokenStore.
findings.fix_sketch: Pass d.TokenSockets to handlers.DeleteToken and call CloseByToken with the deleted token's id (MemoryTokenStore's tokenID and the Identity.TokenID it reports are the same value), mirroring DeleteTokenAdmin — or retire the legacy route in favour of /auth/tokens/v2.
findings.verify_reasoning: The asymmetry is real and the legacy store is a live authentication source. router.go:767 wires `handlers.DeleteToken(d.Auth)` whose body (handlers/auth.go:179-200) is DeleteByID + audit and takes no TokenSocketRevoker, while router.go:1335-1336 wires DeleteTokenAdmin(..., d.TokenSockets) which calls sockets.CloseByToken(fp) (handlers/admin_tokens.go:175-177). The legacy pair is reachable: the MemoryTokenStore is always constructed (daemon_north.go:100 from buildTokenMap), is handed to AuthDeps.Tokens (daemon_rest.go:287) and authenticates as the Secondary of auth.ChainedTokenStore (daemon_rest.go:162,220), and POST /auth/tokens mints into it. ws.Hub.CloseByToken's own doc states the socket keeps its connect-time identity because the command router gates on that snapshot, and the hub's token store is consulted only for the in-band reauth op — so nothing else tears the socket down. One correction that makes the defect WORSE than the write-up: the fix sketch's premise ('MemoryTokenStore's tokenID and the Identity.TokenID it reports are the same value') is false. buildTokenMap and the legacy CreateToken (auth.go:163) build auth.Identity{Subject, Role, Scheme} with no TokenID, and MemoryTokenStore.AuthenticateToken returns entry.identity with only Scheme overwritten, so a legacy-token socket carries TokenID=='' and CloseByToken — which filters on `id.TokenID != fingerprint` — can never match it, from either route. Only sqlite.TokenStore sets TokenID (internal/store/sqlite/tokens.go:225). Severity kept medium: it needs the deprecated route (the SPA uses only /auth/tokens/v2, client.ts:1841-1852) plus an open socket.

findings.title: The MCP mount sits outside the chi router, so it bypasses the Basic-auth brute-force guard and the per-identity rate limiter that protect every other credential-accepting path
findings.claim: mountMCP builds `mcpHandler := d.restResolve(d.authMw.RequireRole(mcpRole, mcp.Handler(...)))` and mounts it on a bare http.ServeMux ahead of the router: `mux.Handle(path, mcpHandler); mux.Handle(path+"/", mcpHandler); mux.Handle("/", router)` (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest_mount.go:691-714). Go's ServeMux picks the most specific pattern, so a request to the configured mount path never enters the chi router and therefore never runs any of `r.Use(...)` from rest.NewRouter (internal/north/rest/router.go:593-631): decodedPathRouting, RequestID, SecurityHeaders, ReqContextWithCentral, Logger, Recover, timeoutExceptStreaming, StatusCounter, CORS, and — the two that matter — `auth.GuardBasicAuth(d.LoginRateLimit)` (router.go:616) and `middleware.RateLimit` (router.go:630). d.restResolve is only `authMw.Resolve(sessionResolve(ingressMW(next)))` (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest.go:246-248), i.e. credential resolution with no throttle. GuardBasicAuth exists precisely to close this class of gap — its doc says it 'closes the gap where the login limiter only guards POST /auth/login while GET /auth/me — and every other route behind Resolve — accepts an unlimited stream of Authorization: Basic probes' (internal/auth/bruteforce.go:31-35) — and the MCP mount is the one route behind Resolve that it does not wrap. Each attempt costs a full bcrypt-cost-12 verify: sqlite.UserStore.AuthenticateBasic runs CompareHashAndPassword on a hit and a dummy compare against dummyBcryptHash on a miss (internal/store/sqlite/users.go:205,211), and MemoryUserStore does the same (internal/auth/auth.go:343,347). With CCU-delegated login configured the same unthrottled stream also reaches the CCU (internal/auth/ccuauth/store.go:102), bounded only by a 4-slot semaphore.
findings.failure_scenario: With `north.mcp.enabled: true` (the MCP surface is off by default, which is why this is medium rather than high), an unauthenticated attacker POSTs to the mount path with `Authorization: Basic <guess>` in a loop. The per-IP token bucket that limits POST /api/v1/auth/login and every other Resolve-protected route to ~1 attempt/s never fires, so password guessing runs at whatever rate the CPU allows and the 429 the operator would see on any other route never appears. Independently, each request forces a bcrypt cost-12 hash on a 4-core CCU/RPi-class host, so the same loop is an unauthenticated CPU-exhaustion vector against the daemon (and, with ccu auth on, a login storm against the CCU). Requests to the mount also produce no `rest.*` log record, no request id and no 4xx/5xx status metric, so the sweep is invisible on the diagnostics surface.
findings.verified_by: code trace: daemon_rest_mount.go:691-714 (ServeMux precedence) vs router.go:593-631 (the middleware chain the mount never enters); daemon_rest.go:246-248 (restResolve carries no throttle); bruteforce.go:31-73 and login_bruteforce.go:64-78 (the guard and limiter that are skipped); sqlite/users.go:205,211 (bcrypt on every attempt). CSRF is NOT part of this finding: the go-sdk streamable handler rejects any request whose Content-Type is not application/json (go-sdk@v1.7.0/mcp/streamable.go:388), which a cross-site simple request cannot set.
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap mcpHandler in the same guards the router mounts — at minimum `auth.GuardBasicAuth(loginRateLimit)` immediately after restResolve plus `middleware.RateLimit` — or, cleaner, mount MCP as a chi route inside NewRouter (outside the AuthRequire group, with its own RequireRole) so it inherits the whole chain by construction.
findings.verify_reasoning: The bypass is real and I measured it; one of the two consequences is not MCP-specific. mountMCP (daemon_rest_mount.go:663-719) builds mcpHandler = restResolve(RequireRole(...)) and registers it on a bare http.ServeMux ahead of the chi router (mux.Handle(path), mux.Handle(path+'/'), mux.Handle('/', router)); restResolve is only authMw.Resolve(sessionResolve(ingressMW(next))) (daemon_rest.go:245-248) and carries no throttle, so nothing from rest.NewRouter's r.Use chain (router.go:590-631) runs — including auth.GuardBasicAuth(d.LoginRateLimit) and middleware.RateLimit. The code's own comment concedes the mount 'sits outside the REST router's own middleware stack'. RUN PROOF against the shipped binary with north.mcp.enabled and a Basic user: 30 concurrent bad-Basic probes to /api/v1/health produced 429s (guard bites, per-IP bucket 1/s burst 5), while 30 concurrent bad-Basic probes to /mcp produced 30x401 and zero 429; mcp2.log contains 24 http.request records (all the REST 429s) and none for /mcp, confirming the missing request log, request id and status metrics. REFUTED sub-claim: the 'unauthenticated CPU-exhaustion vector' is not a property of the MCP mount. GuardBasicAuth is mounted AFTER AuthResolve, so the bcrypt verify has already run when the 429 is written — measured ~1.4-1.8 s per attempt on REST too (rest log elapsed=36s under the 30-way burst). The distinguishing loss is the password-guessing throttle, the per-identity limiter and the observability, not the CPU cost. Severity kept medium (MCP is off by default).

findings.title: Two existing payload fields changed value semantics under a minor and a patch API bump, against the policy documented on APIVersion itself, and nothing enforces the bump class
findings.claim: 1) internal/north/rest/handlers/info.go:12-18 states the contract: "addition of capabilities is a minor bump, removal or rename of an existing capability or payload field is a major bump". 2) Release 0.61.1 (commit f356cb40) changed the per-interface reachability id from the bare interface name to the wire id — `git diff v0.60.0..v0.61.1 -- internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go` shows `iface := hmenum.Interface(reachability[i].InterfaceID)` / `reachability[i].InterfaceID = WireInterfaceID(centralName, iface)` — and that value is what `GET /hub/data-points`.`connectivity[].interface_id` and `GET /interfaces` report. APIVersion moved 6.0.0 → 6.1.0 (`git show v0.61.1:internal/north/rest/handlers/info.go`), a MINOR bump. 3) Release 0.61.4 (commit 34b0f4c9) did the same to `install_mode[].interface_id`: internal/north/rest/handlers/hub_data_points.go:153-160 now emits `hmtypes.NewWireInterfaceID(central, hmenum.Interface(im.InterfaceID)).String()` where it previously emitted `im.InterfaceID` (the bare name). APIVersion moved 6.2.0 → 6.2.1 — a PATCH bump, described in CHANGELOG as "a backward-compatible value correction, no shape change". A client keying on the old value is not backward compatible with it. 4) No guard catches this. The only version-related contract tests are `TestOpenAPIVersion` (tests/contract/openapi_test.go:38, pins `openapi: 3.1.0` only) and `TestOpenAPIInfoVersionMatchesAPIVersion` (tests/contract/schema_digest_test.go:63-80, pins the two declarations to each other, not the bump class). 5) `SchemaDigest` (internal/north/rest/handlers/schema_digest_gen.go:14) is a digest of the contract asset FILES, so it moves on a description-only edit and cannot distinguish additive from breaking; it also cannot see a value-semantics change whose JSON shape is unchanged.
findings.failure_scenario: A client pinned to `>=6.2.0 <7.0.0` (the range the documented policy invites) upgrades the daemon from 0.61.3 to 0.61.4. It indexes `GET /interfaces` or its own interface list by the bare interface name it has always received in `install_mode[].interface_id`, matches nothing, and its pairing/install-mode surface goes dead — with the reported API version telling it that only a patch-level change happened. The same shape hit `connectivity[].interface_id` one minor bump earlier.
findings.verified_by: git diff/show over v0.60.0..HEAD for the two handlers plus `git show <tag>:internal/north/rest/handlers/info.go | grep APIVersion` for each of v0.59.0/v0.60.0/v0.61.1/v0.61.2/v0.61.3/v0.61.4 (5.22.0 / 5.34.0 / 6.1.0 / 6.1.0 / 6.2.0 / 6.2.1), plus a grep of tests/contract/ for APIVersion.
findings.fix_sketch: Treat a value-semantics change to an existing field as breaking: bump the major, or add the new spelling as a new field and deprecate the old one for a release. Add a contract test that diffs the committed openapi.yaml/wsapi.json against the previous release tag and requires a major bump for any removed/renamed/retyped field, and keep an explicit hand-maintained list for value-semantics changes, which no schema diff can detect.
findings.resolution: TestAPISurfaceChangesCarryTheRightBump enforces the bump class against a committed API-surface inventory, plus a hand-maintained value-semantics register
