findings.title: Migration 037 blanks alarm-zone slugs but the uniqueness check ignores blank stored slugs, so a zone created after the upgrade can be handed a slug an existing zone already resolves to
findings.claim: 1) Migration 037 sets `slug = ''` for every zone whose stored slug carries a character outside the identifier grammar: `UPDATE alarm_zones SET slug = '' WHERE slug GLOB '*[^a-z0-9_-]*'` (internal/store/sqlite/migrations/037_alarm_zone_slug_charset.sql). 2) The security domain repairs that at read time only, in memory: `refreshZoneSlugs` substitutes `routingkey.HubSlug(rows[i].Name)` when the stored slug is empty (internal/security/index.go:162-171); the derived value is never written back, so the DB column stays `''` forever. 3) `uniqueZoneSlug`, which is supposed to guarantee a new zone gets a free slug, builds its `taken` set from stored slugs and explicitly skips empty ones: `if existing[i].Slug != "" { taken[existing[i].Slug] = true }` (internal/north/rest/handlers/alarm_config.go:508-513). A blanked zone therefore reserves nothing. 4) `HubSlug` transliterates rather than expands umlauts (internal/routingkey/slug.go:24-34,44-66: `ü`→`u`), so `HubSlug("Küche")` and `HubSlug("Kuche")` are both `kuche`. 5) The slug is the identity: `snapshot()` keys the whole zone map by it — `snap.Zones[z.Slug] = cloneZone(z)` (internal/security/aggregate.go:236) — and the MQTT security plane iterates that map one entity per key (internal/north/mqtt/security_reconcile.go:66,122,142,218,264).
findings.failure_scenario: An operator upgrades with an existing zone named `Küche` (034 stored `küche`; 037 blanks it; the domain now derives `kuche`). They later add a zone named `Kuche`. `uniqueZoneSlug` sees no `kuche` in `taken` — the old zone's stored slug is the empty string — and assigns `kuche` to the new zone. The two zones now share one key: one silently overwrites the other in `aggregate.snapshot()`, and the MQTT/HA security plane shows a single entity whose state is whichever zone won the map iteration. The zone that lost has no entity and no state anywhere on the north-bound surface.
findings.verified_by: Code trace across the migration SQL, internal/security/index.go:150-177, internal/north/rest/handlers/alarm_config.go:503-523, internal/routingkey/slug.go:44-66 and internal/security/aggregate.go:234-237. Not reproduced end to end (would need a seeded DB and a live daemon).
findings.fix_sketch: Make the uniqueness check see the effective slug, not the stored one: have `uniqueZoneSlug` fall back to `routingkey.HubSlug(existing[i].Name)` when the stored slug is empty, exactly as `refreshZoneSlugs` does. Better still, persist the derived slug once on the first read after the migration so the DB column and the effective identity stop diverging.

findings.title: north.ui.embedded_scope was added with a default that narrows the pre-existing embedded=true behaviour, so an upgrading add-on operator silently gets a different UI without changing anything
findings.claim: 1) `NorthUI.EmbeddedScope` does not exist at v0.55.0 (`git show v0.55.0:internal/config/config.go | grep -c EmbeddedScope` = 0); there, `embedded: true` selected the reduced profile unconditionally. 2) At HEAD `EmbeddedScopeOrDefault` (internal/config/config.go:1370-1375) maps the Go zero value "" to `EmbeddedScopeInsideHA`, not `EmbeddedScopeAlways`. 3) `ActiveProfileFor(insideHA bool)` (config.go:1395-1402) now returns `ProfileEmbedded` only when the scope is Always OR the request arrived through Home Assistant; otherwise `ProfileStandalone` — even with `Embedded == true`. It is the per-request resolver behind `GET /api/v1/ui/surfaces` (internal/north/ui/surface/resolve.go, internal/north/rest/handlers/ui_surfaces.go), with insideHA derived from the Supervisor's X-Ingress-Path header. 4) NorthUI is a DB-tier section, and `ConfigSectionSchemaVersion` is still 1 (internal/store/sqlite/config_sections.go:21, unchanged since #91), so an existing row written before the field existed is NOT wiped — it is decoded with `embedded_scope` at its zero value and therefore lands on the narrower behaviour, with no migration and no prompt.
findings.failure_scenario: An HA add-on operator on 0.55.x set `embedded: true` to get the reduced Config UI everywhere, including on the daemon's own directly-exposed port. After upgrading to 0.61.4 with no config change of their own, any access that does not carry the Ingress header now serves the full standalone admin editor instead of the reduced view they configured. The only notice is a CHANGELOG entry.
findings.verified_by: Independently re-verified after a sub-agent reported it: read config.go:1365-1405 at HEAD, confirmed `git show v0.55.0:internal/config/config.go | grep -c EmbeddedScope` = 0, and confirmed ConfigSectionSchemaVersion is still 1 so no wipe compensates.
findings.fix_sketch: Normalise once on the DB-tier read/seed path: set `embedded_scope: always` for any pre-existing row that already carried `embedded: true`, so the upgrade preserves the behaviour the operator configured. Failing that, emit a one-time startup notice / SPA banner naming the flag that restores it.

findings.title: The CCU edit dialog pre-fills the password field with the daemon's `***` mask and always sends it back, so an operator who types into the field persists `***`-prefixed garbage as the CCU credential.
findings.claim: GET /api/v1/centrals is served by handlers.ListCentrals (internal/north/rest/router.go:1339), which runs every row through maskCentralRow: `if row.PasswordPlain != "" { row.PasswordPlain = maskSentinel }` (internal/north/rest/handlers/admin_centrals.go:63-65), and maskSentinel is the literal "***" (internal/north/rest/handlers/admin_config.go:359). The SPA loads those rows with api.listCentralsV2() -> `request<CentralRow[]>('/centrals')` (assets/ui/src/lib/api/client.ts:1857-1859). openEdit() then seeds the form with `fPassword = row.password_plain ?? ""` (CentralsAdmin.svelte:317) — i.e. the literal "***" whenever a password is stored — and the dialog renders `<input type="password" bind:value={fPassword} ...>` with no placeholder and no clearing (CentralsAdmin.svelte:881-887). buildRow() then unconditionally sends `password_plain: fPassword` (CentralsAdmin.svelte:395); the comment above it states the key is always sent on purpose. UpdateCentral restores the stored credential only for the two exact cases `!passwordSent || row.PasswordPlain == maskSentinel` (admin_centrals.go:260-268); anything else is persisted verbatim through svc.Put. A value of "***" + typed text matches neither branch. The sibling generic editor gets this right — SectionEditor renders `value={isMaskedSecret(v) ? "" : String(v ?? "")}` with a `••••` placeholder precisely so the sentinel can never be appended to (assets/ui/src/lib/components/settings/SectionEditor.svelte:708-712) — which shows the contract exists and CentralsAdmin was missed.
findings.failure_scenario: Settings -> CCUs -> pencil/Edit on a CCU that has a stored password. The password input shows three masked characters (the sentinel), which reads as 'the password is stored'. The operator changes the CCU password: they click into the field and type/paste the new one without first select-all-deleting (the field looks like it holds a real 3-char value, and browsers place the caret at the click point). Save. The daemon stores `***<newpassword>`. Every south-bound JSON-RPC / ReGa login for that CCU now fails with bad credentials; the central stops coming up, and the Settings dialog still shows `***` on the next open so nothing points at the cause. Recovery requires the operator to clear the field completely and retype.
findings.verified_by: code trace across both sides: assets/ui/src/lib/components/settings/CentralsAdmin.svelte:317,395,881-887 + assets/ui/src/lib/api/client.ts:1857 + internal/north/rest/router.go:1339 + internal/north/rest/handlers/admin_centrals.go:63-65,260-268 + internal/north/rest/handlers/admin_config.go:359
findings.fix_sketch: Mirror SectionEditor: keep the sentinel out of the input (`value={fPassword === '***' ? '' : fPassword}` with a `••••` placeholder and a 'leave blank to keep' hint), track a `passwordTouched` flag, and have buildRow() omit `password_plain` entirely when untouched — the daemon already reads an absent key as 'unchanged'. Add a unit test asserting the dialog never binds the sentinel into the form value.
findings.verify_reasoning: The mechanism holds exactly as described and I traced the full data flow rather than stopping at the cited line. GET /centrals -> ListCentrals -> maskCentralRow sets PasswordPlain to maskSentinel whenever one is stored, unconditionally for an admin caller (admin_centrals.go:63-67, maskSentinel = "***" at admin_config.go:359); the SPA loads exactly that route (client.ts:1857) and openEdit seeds fPassword = row.password_plain ?? "" (CentralsAdmin.svelte:317); the input is a plain bind:value with no sentinel guard and an empty placeholder unless password_env is set (:881-891); buildRow always sends password_plain: fPassword (:395) and saveModal passes it straight to updateCentralV2 (:449-451). grep for '***' / isMaskedSecret over the whole component returns nothing, so there is no sanitisation on either side, and UpdateCentral restores the stored value only on exact equality with the sentinel (admin_centrals.go:260-268). SectionEditor.svelte:706-712 does implement the guard, so the contract exists and this component misses it. What is overstated is the framing, hence PARTIAL. It is not a security finding: nothing is disclosed, the mask itself works, and the round-trip of an untouched dialog is correct. The consequence is conditional on the operator appending rather than select-all-replacing — a select-all-and-type edit produces a correct password. The real consequence is a correctness/UX footgun: the field misrepresents a stored secret as a real 3-character value, and an append-style edit persists '***<newpassword>' verbatim, breaking every CCU login. One detail makes the diagnosis harder than the finding says and is worth keeping: a password change already triggers the 'restart required' toast (centralNeedsRestartSignal mirrors centralConfigNeedsRestart), so the corrupted credential typically only bites at the next restart, well after the edit.

findings.title: Logs.svelte opens its SSE stream after an await inside onMount, so leaving the view while the initial fetch is in flight leaks a self-reconnecting EventSource that lives for the rest of the tab session.
findings.claim: onMount is async: it awaits `Promise.all([api.getLogs({limit:500,...}), api.getDefaultLogLevel()])` and only afterwards calls `openStream()` (assets/ui/src/routes/Logs.svelte:278-298). openStream() constructs `new EventSource(url, {withCredentials:true})` and assigns it to the component-scoped `eventSource` (Logs.svelte:177-184). The only teardown is `onDestroy(() => { eventSource?.close(); eventSource = null; })` (Logs.svelte:300-303), and there is no destroyed/cancelled flag anywhere in the file (grep for eventSource/everConnected/onDestroy returns only lines 29,33,178-184,200-211,300-302). Svelte runs onDestroy synchronously at unmount; the promise continuation of an async onMount is a plain microtask continuation and still runs afterwards. So on unmount-during-seed the sequence is: onDestroy closes a still-null eventSource -> the await resolves -> openStream() creates a live EventSource that nothing owns. EventSource additionally auto-reconnects on error, so the leak is not self-limiting. The route is unmounted by a plain route change: App.svelte renders Logs only inside `{:else if route.kind === 'logs'}` (assets/ui/src/App.svelte:506-521).
findings.failure_scenario: Operator (admin) clicks 'Logs' in the sidebar and, before the 500-record seed request returns — routinely a second or more through HA Ingress or over a WAN link — clicks another nav entry. The Logs view is gone from the screen but one SSE connection to /api/v1/logs/stream stays open forever, streaming every log record into a destroyed component and reconnecting whenever it drops. Repeating the click a few times accumulates several. Because a browser allows only ~6 concurrent HTTP/1.1 connections per origin and the daemon serves plain HTTP/1.1 by default, a handful of leaked streams saturates the pool and the SPA's own REST calls stop completing: every view shows its loading state and never resolves, with no error. Daemon-side each leaked stream also holds a log subscriber.
findings.verified_by: code trace: assets/ui/src/routes/Logs.svelte:177-184, 278-298, 300-303; App.svelte:506-521. (The connection-pool consequence is standard browser behaviour, not measured here; the leak itself is traced.)
findings.fix_sketch: Add a `let destroyed = false;` set in onDestroy and return early from openStream() (and from the onMount continuation) when it is set; alternatively call openStream() before the awaits and let the seed only backfill. Same guard belongs on the `resyncAfterReconnect()` re-open path.
findings.verify_reasoning: MECHANISM CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, CONSEQUENCE OVER-STATED. A vitest reproducer ($S/wt/assets/ui/src/routes/LogsV4leak.test.ts, mirroring the existing Logs.resync.test.ts MockEventSource) renders the real Logs.svelte with the seed promise held open, unmounts via cleanup(), then resolves the seed. Output: `instances after unmount+resolve: 1 closed flags: [ false ]` -- a live EventSource exists after the component is destroyed and is never closed. The control case (seed resolves BEFORE unmount) printed `control closed flags: [ true ]`, so the teardown works whenever the race is not hit. The code is exactly as traced and I found no compensating teardown anywhere: onMount is `async` and awaits Promise.all([api.getLogs({limit:500,...}), api.getDefaultLogLevel()]) before calling openStream() (Logs.svelte:278-298); openStream() constructs `new EventSource(url, {withCredentials:true})` and registers three listeners (Logs.svelte:177-218); the only teardown is onDestroy closing whatever `eventSource` holds at that instant (Logs.svelte:300-303), which is null while the seed is in flight; there is no destroyed/cancelled flag in the file. Svelte 5.56 runs onDestroy synchronously at unmount and does not cancel an async onMount's promise continuation, and a repo-wide grep confirms Logs.svelte is the ONLY EventSource owner in the SPA and that App.svelte's single beforeunload listener is the dirty-editor guard, unrelated. The leaked object is not GC-eligible either: per the HTML spec an EventSource whose readyState is CONNECTING/OPEN and which has registered listeners must not be collected. Note also the catch block does not return, so the 403/error path opens a stream too, and resyncAfterReconnect() (Logs.svelte:232-241) re-opens after an await with the same missing guard. WHAT IS OVER-STATED IS THE IMPACT. (1) The window is the in-flight seed only -- the operator must leave the view between the click and the 500-record response; on a LAN that is milliseconds, and the finder's own 'a second or more through HA Ingress' is the worst case, not the norm. (2) It is per-tab-session: any reload clears every leaked stream. (3) The claimed cascade -- '~6 concurrent HTTP/1.1 connections saturate and every view shows its loading state forever' -- is asserted from generic browser behaviour and was explicitly not measured by the finder; it needs roughly half a dozen repeats of a narrow race in one uninterrupted tab. (4) The view is admin-only. Re-rated high -> medium: a measured, unguarded resource leak worth fixing (the guard is three lines), but the SPA-wide hang the entry describes is an unmeasured inference stacked on a narrow race.

findings.title: Toggling the UI language or the expert switch reloads the channel paramset editor and silently discards the operator's unsaved working copy and undo stack.
findings.claim: `$effect(() => { void load(address, channel, paramset, locale, peer, expertMode); })` (assets/ui/src/lib/components/channel/ChannelPanel.svelte:182-184) reads `locale` and `expertMode` inside the effect body, so both are tracked dependencies. load() unconditionally re-seeds the editor: `serverValues = seed; values = { ...seed }; stack = emptyStack(); lockedParams = new Set();` (ChannelPanel.svelte:159-167). There is no dirty guard on this path, unlike the other two reload paths in the same file, which both start with `if (dirtyNames.length > 0) return;` (ChannelPanel.svelte:285 for the CONFIG_PENDING settle reload, ChannelPanel.svelte:296 for the resync reload) — the asymmetry is what makes this a defect rather than a decision. `locale` is a live prop: App.svelte derives it from `prefs.locale` (App.svelte:258) and passes it to DeviceDetail, which forwards `{locale}` to every ChannelPanel (DeviceDetail.svelte:1063-1067, 1074-1078, 1085-1089, 1253-1257); the sidebar's globe button calls setLocale() on every click (App.svelte:428). `expertMode` is a checkbox rendered inside the panel itself (ChannelPanel.svelte:1034-1035 -> setExpert -> line 127). Because the working copy is replaced, `dirtyNames` also collapses to empty, so the App-level leave guard stops warning too.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator opens a device -> Configure -> a channel, edits three MASTER parameters (each field shows the amber 'modified' badge), then clicks the expert-mode checkbox in that same panel to look for one more field — or clicks the language toggle in the sidebar. The panel refetches its ui-schema and every edit is gone: no confirm, no toast, no undo (the change stack is emptied in the same call). The operator has to redo the edits, and typically only notices because the 'modified' badges vanished.
findings.verified_by: code trace: assets/ui/src/lib/components/channel/ChannelPanel.svelte:145-176, 182-184, 285, 296, 121-134, 1034-1035; assets/ui/src/App.svelte:258, 428; assets/ui/src/routes/DeviceDetail.svelte:1063-1067
findings.fix_sketch: Apply the same guard the other two reload paths use — skip the locale/expert refetch while `dirtyNames.length > 0`, or prompt via confirmStore and re-apply the working copy onto the fresh schema after the reload. For the expert toggle specifically, the refetch only adds/removes fields, so merging `values` back over the new seed for keys still present is enough.

findings.title: The config section editor never registers with the global unsaved-changes guard, so navigating away or switching a settings tab discards edited daemon settings with no prompt.
findings.claim: SectionEditor tracks its own dirty state (`const isDirty = $derived(JSON.stringify(working) !== JSON.stringify(original))`, assets/ui/src/lib/components/settings/SectionEditor.svelte:536) but never calls `dirty.set(...)`: the module imports api, Button, Badge, Select, Switch, SourceBadge, ExpertGate, prefs, t, toastStore, confirmStore and refreshRestartPending (SectionEditor.svelte:1-15) and `$lib/stores/dirty.svelte` is not among them. A repo-wide grep for `dirty.set|dirty.clear` yields only four participants — surfaces.svelte.ts:97, matter.svelte.ts:246, visibility.svelte.ts:43 and ChannelPanel.svelte:305 — so the config forms are outside the guard. Both guards therefore see nothing: App.svelte's route guard (`if (dirty.any())` in onHash, App.svelte:119-136) and the beforeunload handler (`if (dirty.any())`, App.svelte:227). Tab switching inside Settings does not warn either: each SectionEditor lives in its own `{:else if activeTab === ...}` branch (routes/Settings.svelte:611-770), so changing activeTab destroys the instance outright, and the two tab effects (Settings.svelte:317-333, 368-374) contain no dirty check.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator opens Settings -> MQTT, changes the broker URL and two other fields, then clicks 'Matter' in the settings sidebar (or 'Devices' in the main sidebar, or closes the tab). Everything typed is discarded instantly and silently — no confirm dialog, no browser 'leave site?' prompt, no toast. The same holds for every section: REST, callback ports, reliability, persistence, discovery, OIDC. Every other editor in the SPA (channel paramsets, Matter exposures, un-ignore patterns, navigation profiles) does prompt, so the behaviour also reads as 'the settings page lost my input' rather than 'I forgot to save'.
findings.verified_by: code trace: assets/ui/src/lib/components/settings/SectionEditor.svelte:1-15,536; assets/ui/src/App.svelte:119-136,227; assets/ui/src/routes/Settings.svelte:611-770; grep for dirty.set/dirty.clear across assets/ui/src
findings.fix_sketch: Add `$effect(() => { const id = 'config:' + section; dirty.set(id, isDirty, resetWorking); return () => dirty.clear(id); })` to SectionEditor, and gate the Settings tab switch on confirmStore when the active editor is dirty. The same gap exists in SimpleScheduleEditor (isDirty at line 84) and ClimateScheduleEditor (isDirty at line 82) — a half-edited week profile is more work to lose than a config field.

findings.title: The shared free-text search compiles the term as a regular expression first, so typing a device or channel name that contains `(`, `[` or `+` — common in CCU names — returns no results at all.
findings.claim: makeTextMatcher builds `new RegExp(q, 'i')` and only falls back to a case-insensitive substring match when the pattern fails to COMPILE (assets/ui/src/lib/utils.ts:44-56). A term that compiles but means something different than the literal text silently matches nothing — there is no second-chance substring pass. The matcher is the search predicate of the shared DataTable, which filters every column through it (`const match = makeTextMatcher(query); list = list.filter(r => columns.some(c => ... match(String(v))))`, assets/ui/src/lib/components/ui/DataTable.svelte:112-122), so it backs the search box of every table view (devices in table mode, sysvars, programs, links, signal quality, firmware, messages, backups, audit). It is also the DeviceList card-mode filter (`const nameMatch = $derived(makeTextMatcher(filter))`, assets/ui/src/routes/DeviceList.svelte:238, applied at 240-250). Measured with node against the exact function body: 'Taster (Kanal 1)' -> false, 'Wohnzimmer (Decke)' -> false, 'Bad [oben]' -> false, 'Licht+Steckdose' -> false; 'HmIP-BSM' -> true.
findings.failure_scenario: A channel is named 'Wohnzimmer (Decke)' — parentheses are the CCU WebUI's own convention for qualifying a channel. The operator types or pastes that exact name into the device-list search. The regex `Wohnzimmer (Decke)` matches the literal text 'Wohnzimmer Decke' (the parens are a capture group), which no row carries, so the list empties and the DataTable renders its EmptyState ('no devices'). The operator concludes the device is gone or the filter is broken; the only way out is to delete characters until the term happens to compile into something that matches. The same happens for any name with `[`, `]`, `+`, `?`, `*` or `|`.
findings.verified_by: measurement (node, exact function body, five cases) + code trace: assets/ui/src/lib/utils.ts:44-56; assets/ui/src/lib/components/ui/DataTable.svelte:112-122; assets/ui/src/routes/DeviceList.svelte:238-250
findings.fix_sketch: Match literally first and treat the regex as an additional, not a replacing, pass: `return (text) => text.toLowerCase().includes(lower) || (re ? re.test(text) : false)`. That keeps the power-user regex search working while making an exact name always findable.

findings.title: Every cache-clear scope wipes the whole central's persistent VALUES cache, because the re-init's model teardown fires DeviceRemovedEvent for every device and the values-cache evictor deletes on it
findings.claim: cachereset.Service.Clear deletes only the scoped rows (internal/central/cachereset/cachereset.go:310-357 clearUnit, scoped by ifaceUnit / scope.Device) and then re-initialises the whole owning central (cachereset.go:244 -> adapter.BringUpManager.ReinitCentral, internal/central/adapter/central_bringup.go:347-356 -> b.reinit, :180 b.clearModel). clearModel loops every device of the central and calls b.unit.RemoveDevice(d.Address) (central_bringup.go:204-218). Unit.RemoveDevice publishes hmevent.DeviceRemovedEvent with the device's own wire InterfaceID on the central's EventBus (internal/central/central.go:961-968). ValuesCacheEvictor.StartCentral subscribes exactly that event on every registered central (internal/central/adapter/values_cache_evict.go:44-62, wired via reg.OnRegister at :93 and daemon_southbound.go:277) and calls sqlite.ValuesCacheStore.DeleteDevice(ctx, ev.CentralName, ev.InterfaceID, ev.Address) — a DELETE of every values_cache row of that device (internal/store/sqlite/values_cache.go:427-444). The central is NOT unregistered during a re-init, so the subscription is live throughout. Net effect: a ScopeDevice or ScopeInterface clear deletes the persisted VALUES rows of every device on every interface of that central, not just the ones the operator scoped. docs/caching.md:141 states the opposite: 'The scope decides which rows are cleared; the re-pull always re-initializes the whole owning central'.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator runs `hmcli cache clear --scope device --central ccu1 --interface HmIP-RF --device 0001D8A9…` (or the SPA's device-scoped 'Clear CCU cache') to fix one misbehaving device. The report says values=-1 for that one device, and the audit row records the device scope — but the whole central's values_cache table is emptied. The re-pull re-seeds from the CCU's own value database, so the loss is usually invisible; when the CCU is itself cold, or when the re-pull stalls in the readiness gate (CCU unreachable) and the daemon is restarted in that window, the next boot is a full cold start with no cache at all for the entire CCU — exactly the outcome the values-cache GC goes out of its way to avoid (see the GCSweep rationale at internal/store/sqlite/values_cache.go:503-521).
findings.verified_by: code trace: cachereset.go:244 -> central_bringup.go:347/180/217 -> central.go:961-968 -> values_cache_evict.go:48-58 -> values_cache.go:427-444; docs/caching.md:141 read for the contradicted claim
findings.fix_sketch: Suppress the values-cache eviction for removals that are part of a re-init teardown — e.g. carry a `Reason`/`Teardown bool` on DeviceRemovedEvent (or gate the evictor on the unit's readiness/state) so only a genuine CCU-side removal deletes rows — or have cachereset temporarily detach the evictor around ReinitCentral. Alternatively state the real behaviour in docs/caching.md.
findings.resolution: clearModel honours the requested clear scope; docs/caching.md brought in line
findings.status_verified_at: dea785a1 (pre-#606 HEAD); the open two re-checked on 4eecb1e6

findings.title: Persisted MASTER values are never evicted on device removal / unpair / replace, so a re-pair at the same address is seeded cache-first with the old device's configuration and never reads the CCU
findings.claim: seedMasterValues is cache-first: on a hit from sqlite.MasterValuesStore.LoadChannel it applies the persisted values and returns WITHOUT issuing GetParamset against the CCU (internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:1946-1995, early return at :1968; hit semantics at internal/store/sqlite/master_values.go:50-84). It runs on every MASTER hydration, including the hot-plug re-pair path (device_pipeline.go:1925-1927, reached from IngestNewDevices :699-703). No device-removal path deletes master_values rows: UnpairDevice drops model + DeviceRegistry + DescRegistry + ParamsetReg only (internal/central/adapter/device_admin.go:97-119), CallbackHandlers.dropDevice likewise (internal/central/adapter/callback_handlers.go:616-635), DeviceCoordinator.HandleDeleteDevices likewise (internal/central/coordinators/device.go:505-519), and ReplaceDevice likewise (device.go:1329-1353). DeviceCoordinator.InvalidateFirmwareCache (device.go:1369-1378) also clears only the in-memory description/paramset registries. Grepping every caller of MasterValuesStore.DeleteDevice/DeleteChannel yields only internal/central/cachereset/cachereset.go:347/335 (the explicit admin clear) and cmd/hmcli/cache.go:295 — i.e. no automatic path at all. The VALUES cache has exactly such an evictor (internal/central/adapter/values_cache_evict.go); the MASTER cache has no sibling.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator unpairs an HmIP device with the reset flag (backends.DeleteFlagReset, device_admin.go:78-84), which factory-resets it, then re-pairs the same physical device — the address is the serial, so it is identical. The hot-plug ingest hydrates MASTER, gets a cache hit on the pre-unpair rows, applies them and never contacts the CCU. The SPA channel-configuration view, REST and the config UI show the OLD configuration (e.g. previous temperature offsets, boost duration, LED behaviour) for a device that is now at factory defaults, indefinitely and across daemon restarts, until the operator happens to run POST /api/v1/admin/cache/clear. Secondarily, master_values rows for permanently removed devices are never garbage-collected (the VALUES cache has GCDeadRows; master_values has no equivalent).
findings.verified_by: code trace (independently reproduced by a second reviewer): device_pipeline.go:1946-1995 + :1925-1927, master_values.go:50-84, device_admin.go:97-119, callback_handlers.go:616-635, coordinators/device.go:505-519 + :1329-1353 + :1369-1378, and a repo-wide grep of MasterValuesStore.DeleteDevice/DeleteChannel callers
findings.fix_sketch: Add a MasterValuesEvictor mirroring ValuesCacheEvictor exactly (reg.OnRegister -> subscribe DeviceRemovedEvent -> masterValuesStore.DeleteDevice(ctx, ev.CentralName, ev.InterfaceID, ev.Address)) and wire it next to WireValuesCacheEviction in cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_southbound.go:277.
findings.verify_reasoning: Mechanism confirmed and re-derived: seedMasterValues returns unconditionally on a SQLite hit (device_pipeline.go:1953-1969) with no TTL or staleness column (master_values.go:50-84), and no removal path deletes master_values rows — UnpairDevice (device_admin.go:107-118), dropDevice, HandleDeleteDevices and ReplaceDevice touch only the in-memory registries, while central.Unit.RemoveDevice publishes DeviceRemovedEvent (central.go:963) that ONLY the values-cache evictor consumes (values_cache_evict.go:47-60). The only MasterValuesStore deleters in production are the admin cache-clear (cachereset.go:353), hmcli, and central removal (central_adopt.go:737). Consequence over-stated on three points. (a) 'replace' is not a correctness case: ReplaceDevice ingests the NEW address (device.go:1354-1356), which is a cache miss and reads the CCU; the old rows are only garbage. (b) 'indefinitely, until POST /admin/cache/clear' ignores two self-heal writers the finder did not cite: the CONFIG_PENDING True→False settle hook re-reads MASTER for every channel of the device and SaveChannel-s it (auto_refresh.go:180-214, HmIP-RF only), and the classic-HM MasterPoller does the same after every MASTER write (auto_refresh.go:249-283). A re-pair drives a CCU-side config push, so on HmIP the window is plausibly ~10 s rather than forever — unverified without a live CCU, but it is a real repair path the finding does not account for. (c) The exposure is confined to the MASTER config view (GetParamset serves the cached channel snapshot, paramsets.go:96-120); writes go straight to the backend, so no wrong value is written to a device. Real residual: after unpair(+reset)/CCU-side delete and re-pair at the SAME address, the MASTER view can show the pre-unpair configuration, and master_values rows of permanently removed devices are never GC'd (no equivalent of the values cache's GCDeadRows).

findings.title: A CCU backup restore never invalidates the persisted MASTER-values cache, so the daemon keeps serving the pre-restore configuration across restarts
findings.claim: BackupAdapter.Restore (internal/central/adapter/stubs.go:498-518) validates the archive and delegates to HTTPBackupRestorer.Restore (internal/central/adapter/backup_restorer.go:71-121), which performs only the multipart POST; its own doc states the CCU restores asynchronously and reboots and that 'callers poll the device list / health tracker afterwards'. No caller on the restore path invokes cachereset.Service.Clear or MasterValuesStore.DeleteForInterface/DeleteDevice. Because seedMasterValues is cache-first with an unconditional early return on a hit (internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:1953-1969), the stale rows survive the CCU reboot AND any number of daemon restarts. This is asymmetric with the description caches, which are re-pulled and upserted unconditionally on every bring-up (device_pipeline.go:1662, :1746). The post-reconnect refresh path only reloads hub metadata (internal/central/coordinators/connection_recovery.go RefreshHubDataAfterRecovery), not device MASTER values.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator restores an older CCU backup precisely to roll back a bad device configuration (e.g. a mis-set thermostat calibration). The CCU comes back with the older values; the daemon's master_values rows still hold the newer ones and, being cache-first, are applied on every subsequent hydration. REST / WebSocket / SPA show a MASTER paramset that disagrees with the CCU forever, with no error and no restart-based recovery, until the operator manually runs POST /api/v1/admin/cache/clear.
findings.verified_by: code trace: stubs.go:498-518 -> backup_restorer.go:71-121 (no cache call), device_pipeline.go:1953-1969 (cache-first early return), plus a repo-wide grep showing cachereset.Service.Clear has no caller on the restore path
findings.fix_sketch: After a successful restore upload, call cachereset.Service.Clear(ctx, Scope{Kind: ScopeCentral, Central: <name>}) — ideally once the post-restore CCU-readiness probe succeeds — reusing the machinery already proven for the admin cache-clear and central-removal paths.
findings.verify_reasoning: Mechanism confirmed: BackupAdapter.Restore (stubs.go:497-516) inspects the archive and delegates to HTTPBackupRestorer.Restore (backup_restorer.go:71-118), which does the multipart POST and nothing else; a repo-wide grep shows cachereset.Service.Clear has exactly two callers, the REST admin handler (admin_cache.go:67) and the WS command (ws_adapters.go:1358) — neither on the restore path. Combined with the cache-first early return, the pre-restore MASTER snapshot survives the CCU reboot and any number of daemon restarts. Consequence over-stated the same way as F1-2: description caches self-heal (hydrateParamset calls b.GetParamsetDescription against the CCU on every boot, device_pipeline.go:1746; IngestFromBackend re-runs ListDevices, :617), VALUES are re-seeded from the CCU, and any post-restore CCU→device config push repairs the MASTER rows through the CONFIG_PENDING settle hook / MasterPoller. So the stale surface is the MASTER paramset view only, and only for channels whose configuration the restore actually changed without triggering a device re-sync. Rated medium: real invalidation gap, narrow blast radius, documented operator workaround (admin cache clear).
findings.resolution: not worked in #606: a CCU backup restore still never invalidates the persisted MASTER cache. internal/central/adapter/stubs.go and internal/north/rest/handlers/backup.go are untouched.

findings.title: PUT /visibility/unignore re-marks only the requesting central's data points, so HA discovery for sibling centrals never learns about the newly un-ignored parameter
findings.claim: visibilityAdapter.LoadUnIgnore computes the fleet-wide union and loads it into the shared decider (cmd/openccu-loom/visibility_adapter.go:110-136), but re-runs visibility.ApplyUnIgnoredMarks — which writes the materialised per-DataPoint Usage/ForcedUsage mark (internal/store/visibility/operation_mode.go:247-284) — only for the one central named in the request (visibility_adapter.go:145-156). MQTT HA-Discovery gates on that materialised mark, not on the live decider: ev.Usage is read off the DataPoint at event-build time (internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:1689-1696) and DiscoveryBuilder.Build drops NoCreate/Ignored (internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:407-430). The boot/adopt path does it correctly for every registered central (cmd/openccu-loom/visibility_wiring.go:171), so this is specific to the live REST edit.
findings.failure_scenario: On a multi-CCU install, after the PUT the sibling central's raw MQTT value topic starts carrying the newly un-ignored parameter (via the shared decider, finding F1-cache-coherency-4) but no HA-Discovery config message is ever published for it, so Home Assistant never shows the entity — until that central goes through a full pipeline Init/Reassemble (CCU reboot, cache clear, or daemon restart), which on a stable install may be months away.
findings.verified_by: code trace: visibility_adapter.go:110-156 vs. visibility_wiring.go:171, operation_mode.go:247-284, eventbridge.go:1689-1696, discovery.go:407-430
findings.fix_sketch: In visibilityAdapter.LoadUnIgnore, iterate v.centralRegistry.Names() and run visibility.ApplyUnIgnoredMarks over every central's devices, matching what applyVisibilityUnIgnore already does at boot/adopt time.

findings.title: Central removal leaves visibility_unignore and channel_flags rows behind and the OnRegister observer silently revives them when the name is re-used
findings.claim: purgeCentralState claims in its own doc comment to delete 'every derived SQLite row keyed to a removed central' (cmd/openccu-loom/central_adopt.go:709-714) and is called on every live removal (:608). It purges values_cache, master_values, measurements and recording_overrides (:724-753) and nothing else. VisibilityUnIgnoreStore has no delete-by-central method at all (internal/store/sqlite/visibility_unignore.go exposes only Close/List/Patterns/Replace/SeedIfEmpty). ChannelFlagsStore.DeleteForCentral exists and its comment says 'Called on live central removal' (internal/store/sqlite/channel_flags.go:131-141) — a repo-wide grep of DeleteForCentral callers shows cmd/openccu-loom/central_adopt.go:744 (history) and :749 (recording overrides) only; the channel-flags one has zero production callers. wireVisibilityUnIgnore installs a central.Registry.OnRegister observer (cmd/openccu-loom/visibility_wiring.go:74-90) that re-applies whatever SQLite still holds the moment a central with that name registers, and the channel-flags overlay is hydrated once at boot and never purged per central (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:95-112).
findings.failure_scenario: An operator deletes central 'ccu-attic' after configuring un-ignore patterns and hidden/locked channels on it, then later adopts a different CCU under the same name (or re-adopts the same one). On registration the OnRegister observer replays the orphaned un-ignore rows onto the new central's devices, and the boot-loaded channel-flags overlay still hides/locks the old channel addresses — overrides the operator never configured for this incarnation, with no prompt and no visible source.
findings.verified_by: code trace: central_adopt.go:709-753 (what it purges), visibility_unignore.go method list, channel_flags.go:131-141 + repo-wide DeleteForCentral caller grep, visibility_wiring.go:74-90 (OnRegister replay), daemon.go:95-112 (boot-once overlay)
findings.fix_sketch: Add VisibilityUnIgnoreStore.DeleteForCentral and call it from purgeCentralState together with the already-existing ChannelFlagsStore.DeleteForCentral (threading both stores through centralOrchestrator like historyStore/recordingStore), and drop the removed central's entries from the in-memory channelflags.Overlay at removal time.

findings.title: MQTT entity names come from the data point's ingest-time cached NameData, which no rename ever rebuilds — so MQTT and REST report different names for the same entity until a restart
findings.claim: The pipeline caches the name quadruple on each data point once, at construction (device.BuildDataPointName -> init.SetNameData, internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:1906-1917 and :947); those two sites are the only SetNameData callers in production. A rename mutates the live model only: Unit.RenameDevice sets dev.Name (internal/central/central.go:1063-1067) and RenameDeviceWithChannels / RenameChannel call ch.SetName (central.go:1107-1113, :1133-1140) — nothing re-runs BuildDataPointName or SetNameData. The MQTT event builder prefers the cached quadruple whenever it is non-zero (internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:1601-1626, `if cached, ok := datapointNameDataOf(dp); ok && !cached.IsZero()`), and that label is carried into the HA-Discovery payload as payload.GenericConfig.Label (eventbridge.go:1698-1702). The REST handler, by contrast, recomputes live from the channel on every request (device.TranslatedDataPointNameData -> BuildDataPointName, internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:951-957; internal/model/device/namedata.go:177-182). Both DeviceName and ChannelName participate in the composed label (internal/model/naming/namedata.go:109-114 -> composeName :157-171, which also strips the device-name prefix from the channel name). The same MQTT payload carries the FRESH device name (ev.DeviceName comes from a live lookupDevice, internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:1327 and :1647) next to the STALE label, so the device-name prefix strip in composeName no longer matches.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator renames a device (or a channel) in the OpenCCU-Loom SPA. REST/SPA immediately show the new name; every subsequent MQTT value publish and every HA-Discovery config message keeps the pre-rename channel/device name in the entity `name` field. Because composeName strips the CURRENT device name from a channel name that still carries the OLD one, the HA entity ends up named with both (e.g. device 'Neuname' + entity 'Altname Status') instead of just 'Status'. Nothing recovers this except a daemon restart or a cache clear.
findings.verified_by: code trace: device_pipeline.go:947/1906-1917 (only SetNameData callers) -> central.go:1063-1067/1107-1113/1133-1140 (rename writes model only) -> eventbridge.go:1601-1626 + :1698-1702 (cached label wins, goes into discovery) vs. devices.go:951-957 + namedata.go:177-182 (REST recomputes) + naming/namedata.go:109-171 (both names participate)
findings.fix_sketch: Have the rename paths re-run device.BuildDataPointName + SetNameData for every data point of the affected device/channel (the pipeline already has the helper), or drop the DP-level NameData cache in the MQTT builder and always recompute like REST does.

findings.title: Device.Name is written without synchronisation by the rename path while REST / WebSocket / MQTT / Matter read it concurrently
findings.claim: device.Device.Name is a plain exported field (internal/model/device/device.go:83). Unit.RenameDevice writes it from a REST/WebSocket handler goroutine with no lock: `dev.Name = name` (internal/central/central.go:1063-1067) — the only post-construction writer in production (repo-wide grep of `dev.Name = ` / `d.Name = `). Concurrent readers on other goroutines include the REST device list and detail handlers (internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:570, :902), the WebSocket device commands (internal/north/rest/ws/commands_missing.go:209, :263), the MCP tool surface (internal/north/mcp/tools.go:37), the Matter endpoint/eligibility builders (internal/north/matter/endpoint/helpers.go:40, internal/north/matter/eligibility/eligibility.go:206), the name composer on the MQTT/REST hot path (internal/model/device/namedata.go:56, :107; internal/model/device/naming.go:77, :98) and internal/central/queryfacade.go:269. The sibling operator-assigned fields on the same struct were explicitly moved behind assignmentMu for exactly this reason — the comment at internal/model/device/device.go:119-137 states 'the device-admin path rewrites them from a REST / WebSocket handler goroutine long after the device went live, while north-bound readers … are serving requests — as plain exported fields they were a torn slice-header read for every one of those readers'. Name was left out of that fix.
findings.failure_scenario: A rename issued while any north-bound surface is listing devices is an unsynchronised concurrent write/read of a string header: under the Go memory model this is a data race (the race detector flags it), and a torn ptr/len read can surface a corrupted device name in a REST response, an MQTT discovery payload or a Matter NodeLabel. It is timing-dependent and therefore invisible in normal testing.
findings.verified_by: code trace: device.go:83 (plain field) + device.go:119-137 (the documented rationale applied to the sibling fields) + central.go:1063-1067 (unsynchronised write) + the reader list above
findings.fix_sketch: Move Name behind the existing assignmentMu with Name()/SetName() accessors (as rooms/functions/room/function already are) and convert the readers; keep the `payload:"info"` tag by exposing it through the accessor the payload assembler already uses for the guarded fields.
findings.resolution: Device.name is mutex-guarded behind an accessor; payload.ExtraProperties keeps it in the HA-Discovery harvest
findings.status_verified_at: dea785a1 (pre-#606 HEAD); the open two re-checked on 4eecb1e6

findings.title: The 5-minute devicedetails refresh has no consumer outside hot-plug ingest, so a rename or room change made in the CCU WebUI never reaches the running model — three comments claim otherwise
findings.claim: A scheduler job 'devicedetails.refresh.<central>' runs every 5 minutes per central and issues three JSON-RPC round-trips (Device.listAllDetail, Room.getAll, Subsection.getAll) to refill unit.DeviceDetails (internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:368-388; loader at internal/store/devicedetails/loader.go:103-218). Its stated purpose is 'so the cache stays current after operators rename devices or change room assignments via the CCU WebUI' (hub_wiring.go:357-360). A repo-wide grep of every DeviceDetails getter (GetName, GetAddressID, GetChannelRooms, GetDeviceRooms, GetFunctions, GetFunctionText, HasName, GetInterface, DeviceChannelISEIDs) finds production readers ONLY inside the device-ingest pipeline (internal/central/adapter/device_pipeline.go:461-462, :490-497, :521-539). Names/rooms/functions are stamped onto channels and devices once per ingest (device_pipeline.go:452-455, :506-531) and nothing re-stamps them afterwards — the file says so itself at hub_wiring.go:304: 'The periodic detail refresh only re-fills the cache, it never re-names an already-built model.' Two other comments assert consumers that do not exist: internal/central/central.go:100-106 claims 'Consumers (MQTT-Discovery, REST list view, NameData builder) read it on every render', and internal/store/devicedetails/cache.go:215-219 claims DeviceChannelISEIDs is 'Used by the configui' — that method has zero production callers, and the rename hook resolves ISE-IDs through the backend instead (internal/central/adapter/ccu_wiring.go:823-840).
findings.failure_scenario: An operator renames a device or moves a channel to another room in the CCU WebUI (the normal way to do this on a Homematic install). OpenCCU-Loom's SPA, REST, MQTT entity names and `suggested_area`, Matter NodeLabels and the alarm room grouping all keep the old name/room indefinitely — the refresh job burns three CCU round-trips per central every five minutes updating a cache that nothing reads. Recovery requires a CCU reboot, a daemon restart, or an explicit admin cache clear; the periodic job that exists for exactly this case does nothing.
findings.verified_by: code trace: hub_wiring.go:357-388 (the job) + :304 (its own contradiction), device_pipeline.go:452-455/461-462/490-497/506-539 (ingest-only stamping and the only readers), repo-wide grep of every DeviceDetails getter, ccu_wiring.go:823-840 (the rename hook's actual ISE-ID source)
findings.fix_sketch: Make the refresh job re-stamp the model: after loader.Load succeeds, walk the central's devices/channels and re-apply GetName/GetDeviceRooms/GetChannelRooms/GetFunctions (plus the NameData rebuild from finding F1-cache-coherency-7) for entries whose value changed, emitting the existing update events. Failing that, drop the job and correct the three comments.
findings.resolution: restampDeviceDetails re-stamps the live model on the periodic refresh
findings.status_verified_at: dea785a1 (pre-#606 HEAD); the open two re-checked on 4eecb1e6

findings.title: locale and ccu_data.*_path are baked in at boot but the config surface reports restart_required:false for them
findings.claim: restartRules() (internal/config/restart.go:51-59, seven rule groups) contains no rule for `locale` (internal/config/config.go:216, DB-tier section configstore.SectionLocale) nor for `ccu_data.translations_path` / `ccu_data.easymode_path` (SectionCCUData) — grep for 'locale' and 'ccu_data' in restart.go returns nothing, while `data_dir` is present at :78. That same table feeds both operator-facing signals: RestartRequiredDiff drives the PUT /api/v1/config response's restart_required flag (restart.go:482-490) and RestartRequiredFieldPaths drives the per-field badge in GET /api/v1/config/schema (restart.go:465-473). In reality cfg.Locale is captured once into adapter.ParameterLabelAdapter at boot (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:259 and daemon_rest_mount.go:321; constructor at internal/central/adapter/labels.go:21-23), which serves REST labels and — wrapped as MqttParameterLabelAdapter — every MQTT HA-Discovery entity name via eventbridge.go:1606-1626; the ccu_data paths are read once by loadTranslations/loadEasymode (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_ccudata.go) at boot. The YAML-file reload path already knows this and warns 'daemon.reload.restart_required' for locale (cmd/openccu-loom/reload.go:183-186) — the two mechanisms disagree about the same field.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator changes the daemon locale (or points translations_path at a corrected extract) in Settings and saves. The response says restart_required:false, no badge appears, the toast reads success — and every REST/MQTT/config-UI label keeps the old locale until the process is restarted, with nothing telling the operator a restart is pending.
findings.verified_by: code trace: restart.go:51-59/78/465-473/482-490 (rule table and both consumers) vs. config.go:216 + configstore/sections.go:53-55 (editable DB-tier section) and daemon.go:259 / labels.go:21-23 / daemon_ccudata.go (boot-only reads); reload.go:183-186 for the contradicting warning
findings.fix_sketch: Add restart rules for `locale`, `ccu_data.translations_path` and `ccu_data.easymode_path` alongside the existing `data_dir` rule in processRestartRules(), so both the PUT response and the schema badge report them.

findings.title: An operator-supplied translations archive skips the curated translation_custom overlay that the embedded one gets, silently losing the primary-parameter markers
findings.claim: LoadTranslations(path) parses the archive and returns translationsFromRaw(raw) directly (internal/ccudata/translations.go:52-74) — it never calls overlayCustomTranslations. LoadTranslationsEmbedded() is the only caller of that overlay (internal/ccudata/embed.go:43-55, :49; overlay defined at :103-123), which merges the curated translation_custom/*.json patches, including the explicit-empty entries that mark a 'primary parameter'. cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_ccudata.go picks between the two loaders purely on whether cfg.CCUData.TranslationsPath is set. Downstream, the explicit-empty marker is the ONLY producer of labelOmitted (internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:1606-1615 sets it when ParameterLabelOk returns ("", true); the semantics are documented at internal/ccudata/translations.go:242-246), and labelOmitted drives HA-Discovery entity-name suppression (internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go and bridge.go) plus the REST device response composition (internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:951-957).
findings.failure_scenario: An operator sets ccu_data.translations_path to a custom or regenerated extract (the field's own help text invites exactly that for testing). Every parameter the curated overlay would mark as 'primary' now gets an ordinary label instead of the empty marker, so HA-Discovery entity names and REST labels gain a redundant parameter suffix ('<Device> <Parameter>' where '<Device>' was intended) — a visible naming regression triggered purely by setting the path override.
findings.verified_by: code trace: translations.go:52-74 (no overlay) vs. embed.go:43-55 (overlay) + grep showing overlayCustomTranslations has exactly one caller; translations.go:242-246 and eventbridge.go:1606-1615 for the marker semantics
findings.fix_sketch: Call overlayCustomTranslations(t) from LoadTranslations(path) as well, or factor the post-processing into one helper both loaders invoke.

findings.title: `hmcli cache clear --offline` leaves the persisted device- and paramset-descriptor rows in SQLite that the online path deletes, while reporting `devices: 0 / paramsets: 0` and exiting 0.
findings.claim: Descriptor persistence is wired unconditionally in production: cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_infra.go:121 calls wireDescriptorStores, which returns sqlite.NewDeviceStore(db) + sqlite.NewParamsetStore(db) (cmd/openccu-loom/descriptor_stores_wiring.go:42-45). internal/central/adapter/central_bringup.go:273 calls WireDescriptorPersistence, which attaches descriptorSink to DescRegistry/ParamsetReg (internal/central/adapter/descriptor_persistence.go:253-258); every registry Put then writes a `devices` / `paramsets` row (descriptor_persistence.go:108-120, :152-162). The ONLINE clear deletes those rows: cmd/openccu-loom/cachereset_wiring.go:143-148 wires deps.Devices/deps.Paramsets (with the comment 'without this an operator clear caches + re-pull would leave stale descriptions on disk for the next boot'), consumed at internal/central/cachereset/cachereset.go:313-331. The OFFLINE path in cmd/hmcli/cache.go:283-321 constructs only sqlite.NewValuesCacheStore and sqlite.NewMasterValuesStore and deletes only from those two; it never opens the device or paramset store. printSummary (cmd/hmcli/cache.go:439-444) nevertheless prints `devices: %d` / `paramsets: %d` from a clearSummary whose devices/paramsets fields are never assigned in the offline path, i.e. always 0, and finishOfflineClear returns nil so the process exits 0. On the next daemon start WireDescriptorPersistence (descriptor_persistence.go:213-251) hydrates exactly those surviving rows back into DescRegistry/ParamsetReg and seeds sink.devHashes/psHashes with their stored hashes, so an identical re-pull will not even rewrite them. ADR 0042's 'Implementation note — descriptor persistence' (docs/adr/0042-clear-ccu-cache-and-repull.md:135-148) states the devices/paramsets tables 'are not written on the pipeline persistence path' — that claim is refuted by descriptor_persistence.go:108 and is why the offline path was written this way.
findings.failure_scenario: A device is re-paired / re-configured on the CCU and the daemon is holding a stale description; the daemon is wedged, so the operator uses the documented 'always works' escape hatch (docs/caching.md:150-158): `hmcli cache clear --offline --scope global --config /etc/openccu-loom.yaml`. It prints `Cache cleared: scope=global / devices: 0 / paramsets: 0 / values: 4213 / master: 87 / Restart the daemon to re-pull the cleared caches.` and exits 0. After the restart the daemon hydrates the same stale device descriptions and paramsets from SQLite, so the exact state the operator tried to drop is back — with no error, no non-zero exit, and a report line that says there were zero descriptor rows.
findings.verified_by: code trace: cmd/hmcli/cache.go:283-321 vs cmd/openccu-loom/cachereset_wiring.go:143-148 + internal/central/cachereset/cachereset.go:313-331; persistence wiring cmd/openccu-loom/descriptor_stores_wiring.go:42-45 -> internal/central/adapter/central_bringup.go:273 -> internal/central/adapter/descriptor_persistence.go:108/152/213-251
findings.fix_sketch: Open sqlite.NewDeviceStore / sqlite.NewParamsetStore in runCacheClearOffline and call their scoped Clear/ClearForInterface (device scope: Delete/DeleteDevice) alongside the values/master deletes, accumulating into sum.devices/sum.paramsets; correct the stale 'Implementation note' in ADR 0042 and add a hmcli test that asserts an offline global clear empties all four tables.
findings.verify_reasoning: The defect is real and I could not find a guard that saves it: runCacheClearOffline opens only NewValuesCacheStore + NewMasterValuesStore and deletes from those two (cache.go:283-320), while the online service clears four stores including Devices/Paramsets (cachereset.go:313-331, wired at cachereset_wiring.go:143-148); printSummary prints `devices:`/`paramsets:` unconditionally from fields the offline path never assigns (cache.go:439-444) and finishOfflineClear returns nil, so the operator sees `devices: 0 / paramsets: 0` and exit 0. Descriptor rows ARE written in production (descriptor_persistence.go:108-120/152-162, wired via central_bringup.go:270-276), so the ADR 0042 'Implementation note' at docs/adr/0042:136-148 claiming those tables 'are not written on the pipeline persistence path' is refuted by the code — that stale note is the likely origin of the offline gap and should be corrected too. The failure scenario is over-stated, though: on the next boot the daemon does a live ListDevices (device_pipeline.go:617) and an unconditional GetParamsetDescription per channel (device_pipeline.go:1746), both of which re-Put and re-upsert, so a device that still exists on the CCU with a changed description or paramset self-heals — the 're-configured device' case in the scenario is exactly the case that recovers. The durable residue is rows for devices/channels the CCU no longer reports, which CheckAndCreateDevicesFromCache (device_pipeline.go:629) can re-materialise — the resurrection that clearModel's own comment (central_bringup.go:196-199) warns about — plus the actively misleading zero-count report from a documented last-resort recovery tool.

findings.title: hmcli's sysvar and program subcommands have no `--central` flag, so every one of them fails with HTTP 400 on any multi-CCU daemon.
findings.claim: The daemon routes hub mutations by the `central` query parameter: internal/north/rest/handlers/hub.go:43-58 resolveHubForMutation returns nil when centralName is empty and len(idx.Hubs()) != 1, and requireMutationHub (hub.go:67-80) then writes 400 'central required (multiple CCUs)'. That gate guards PutSysvar (hub.go:980), SetProgramEnabled (hub.go:473) and ExecuteProgram (hub.go:753). Reads use resolveHubForRead (hub.go:88-114) which also returns nil — and the handler answers 400 — when the same sysvar name / program id exists on more than one central (GetSysvar hub.go:885-892, GetProgram hub.go:443-451). hmcli builds these requests with no `central` query parameter anywhere: cmd/hmcli/sysvar.go:135 (get), :183 (set), cmd/hmcli/program.go:143 (get), :188 (run), :230 (enable/disable). connFlags.bind (cmd/hmcli/conn.go:34-43) has no `central` flag either. The single exception is `sysvar fetch`, which does define and send one (cmd/hmcli/sysvar.go:195-212) — so the omission on the other five verbs is an oversight, not a design decision. CCU program ids are per-CCU ReGa numbers, so id collisions across two CCUs are the normal case, not an edge case.
findings.failure_scenario: On a two-CCU deployment (a first-class feature per ADR 0002), `hmcli sysvar set Urlaubsmodus true` and `hmcli program run 1234` always fail with `PUT http://…/api/v1/sysvars/Urlaubsmodus: HTTP 400 Bad Request: central required (multiple CCUs)` and exit 1. The operator has no flag to fix it — the commands are unusable, and the same holds for `program enable/disable` and for `sysvar get` / `program get` whenever the name/id exists on both CCUs.
findings.verified_by: code trace: cmd/hmcli/sysvar.go:135/183, cmd/hmcli/program.go:143/188/230, cmd/hmcli/conn.go:34-43 (no central flag) vs internal/north/rest/handlers/hub.go:43-58, :67-80, :88-114, :473, :753, :885-892, :980
findings.fix_sketch: Add a `-central` string flag to connFlags.bind (or to each of the six subcommands) and append `?central=<name>` to the sysvar get/set and program get/run/enable/disable request paths, mirroring cmd/hmcli/sysvar.go:210-212.
findings.verify_reasoning: Every claim holds and I found no compensating default. connFlags.bind defines host/token/user/password/cacert/insecure/timeout/json and no central (conn.go:33-43); the six hub verbs build their paths with no query string — sysvar get cache.go-style at sysvar.go:135, sysvar set at :183, program get at program.go:143, program run at :188, program enable/disable at :230 — while `sysvar fetch` alone declares and sends one (sysvar.go:194-212), which shows the omission is an oversight. On the daemon side requireMutationHub returns 400 'central required (multiple CCUs)' whenever the central query parameter is absent and len(idx.Hubs()) != 1 (hub.go:43-58, :67-80); it guards PutSysvar (hub.go:987), SetProgramEnabled (hub.go:480) and ExecuteProgram (hub.go:753). PutSysvar's body is SysvarSetRequest{Value} only — no body-level central escape hatch. Exact condition: the mutations fail on EVERY multi-CCU daemon (>= 2 registered hubs) unconditionally; single-CCU is unaffected because resolveHubForMutation falls back to the sole hub. The reads degrade more gently — resolveHubForRead only fails when the same sysvar name / program id exists on more than one central (hub.go:88-114, :452-461, :885-892) — but hub.programs is keyed by the bare CCU ReGa id (internal/model/hub/hub.go:384-389), so collisions across two CCUs are the normal case and `program get` is affected in practice too. Re-rated to medium rather than high: a missing flag on a secondary admin binary, multi-CCU only, with the REST/SPA/WS surfaces fully functional — but there is no workaround inside hmcli itself.

findings.title: Health components recorded once at boot are never refreshed, so 91 s after start every daemon reports /health status "unknown" and every boot-time failure signal (failed DB config overlay, plaintext secrets, alarm persistence unavailable) becomes indistinguishable from success.
findings.claim: health.Tracker decays any component whose last sample is older than Tracker.staleAfter to StatusUnknown (internal/health/tracker.go:298-309, applyStaleLocked), and NewTracker() installs the 90 s default (tracker.go:82, 161). ServiceAvailability then maps 'all healthy plus at least one unknown' to StatusUnknown (tracker.go:390-392), and Tracker.Overall does the same (tracker.go:338-340). Three daemon-global components are recorded exactly once and never again: `config.secrets` (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:221 -> secret_health.go:28-33), `config.overlay` (daemon.go:224 -> config_overlay_health.go:29-41) and `alarm` on the persistence-unavailable / construction-failed paths (alarm_wiring.go:26, 54). grep over the repo confirms recordSecretHealth and recordConfigOverlayHealth have exactly one production call site each (daemon.go:221 / :224); nothing re-records them. GET /api/v1/health reads the unioned snapshot through HealthAdapter.Snapshot (internal/central/adapter/config.go:234) and derives its verdict from health.ServiceAvailability (internal/north/rest/handlers/health.go:56); the no-JS page does the same (internal/north/ui/server.go:183), and the WS `health` command plus the MCP status tool use Overall (internal/north/rest/ws/commands_default.go:446, internal/north/mcp/tools.go:396). The periodic probes (sqlite/mqtt/matter, 30 s) and the per-central heartbeat keep their own components fresh, which is exactly why the stale ones are the only ones left voting 'unknown'. cmd/openccu-loom/matter_health.go:70-78 documents the same decay in a comment ('rather than the flap-damped UNKNOWN that staleness would produce') and re-records every tick to avoid it — the boot-only recorders do not.
findings.failure_scenario: Two effects. (1) On a completely healthy daemon with a working database, `GET /api/v1/health` returns HTTP 200 with body status "healthy" for the first 90 seconds and "unknown" from t+91 s onwards, forever; the SPA and the /health page render the localized `health.status.unknown` ("Unknown"/"Unbekannt") as the system verdict for the rest of the process lifetime, and HealthAdapter.IsAvailable() is permanently false. (2) The signal these components exist to carry is erased: if the boot-time DB-tier config overlay fails (configstore.OverlayInto error at daemon_boot.go:218 — e.g. a lost or corrupted var/secret.key, which makes Cipher.Open return 'encrypted value but no master key available' for every sealed section, internal/secret/secret.go:150-152), `config.overlay` is recorded UNHEALTHY once. 90 seconds later it reads `unknown` — byte-identical in status to the success case — while every config section the operator saved in the SPA is silently not in effect and GET /api/v1/config fails. The same erasure hides `config.secrets` = 'plaintext at rest' and `alarm` = 'persistence-unavailable'.
findings.verified_by: Reproducer at $S/repro/F3/healthrepro (a verbatim copy of internal/health driven by clock.Fake). Output: t=0s healthy / t=30s healthy / t=1m0s healthy / t=1m31s overall=unknown serviceAvailability=unknown / t=6m31s unknown, with the component dump showing config.overlay=unknown, config.secrets=unknown while sqlite, mqtt, ccu1/central and ccu1/ccu1-HmIP-RF stay healthy. Run with `cd $S/repro/F3/healthrepro && go run ./staleness`.
findings.fix_sketch: Either re-record the boot-only verdicts on a ticker like the sqlite/mqtt/matter probes do (cheapest: one 30 s job that replays the captured ov.overlayErr / ov.secretsAvailable / alarm-availability), or give health.Sample a 'sticky' flag that applyStaleLocked skips so a one-shot verdict keeps its status. Add a guard that fails when a component recorded during boot has no periodic refresher.
findings.verify_reasoning: MEASURED. A daemon booted against the godevccu simulator (REST :18505, CCU :18501) reported `status: healthy` at t+35 s and `status: unknown` at t+95 s, and stayed non-healthy for the rest of the 175 s observation. Mechanism confirmed exactly: health.DefaultStaleAfter = 90 s (internal/health/tracker.go:82); Tracker.applyStaleLocked (tracker.go:298-310) rewrites ANY component whose LastSample is older than that to StatusUnknown; ServiceAvailability (tracker.go:357-401) returns StatusUnknown when `worst == Healthy && hasUnknown`. TWO components, not three, are recorded once and never again on a default daemon: `config.overlay` and `config.secrets`. Both are written from a single site, cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:220-225, inside `if ov.db != nil`, with no timer, no probe and no second caller (exhaustive grep for recordConfigOverlayHealth / recordSecretHealth returns only the definition and that one call each). Their recorded_at stayed frozen at 12:36:49 across every poll while `sqlite` (30 s probe), the interface, `central` and `scheduler` all re-recorded on a 60 s heartbeat. THE FINDING IS OVER-STATED IN TWO PLACES. (1) `central` IS refreshed -- it went 12:37:49 -> 12:38:49 -> 12:39:49 -> ... on the heartbeat, so it is not one of the never-refreshed components; on the default surface the count is two, and it only reaches three when a DB failure adds a one-shot `alarm` sample. (2) A failed overlay is NOT indistinguishable from success. applyStaleLocked overwrites only Status, and returns LastSample unchanged, so the note travels forever: the live body carries `"status":"unknown","note":"database sections applied"`, and the failure branch (config_overlay_health.go:33-38) would carry `"note":"database config sections not applied: <err>"` in the same field. The Prometheus gauge `config_overlay_failed` is also set once and holds its value, so a dashboard keeps reading 1. What IS genuinely wrong and operator-visible: on an otherwise perfectly healthy daemon, `GET /api/v1/health` and the SPA/`/about` status line read `unknown` instead of `healthy` from ~91 s after every boot, forever. HTTP stays 200 throughout (never 503), so liveness/readiness probes are unaffected -- the damage is an operator-facing status field that permanently lies about a healthy daemon, plus the loss of the status axis (not the note axis) for two config-integrity signals.

findings.title: When the shared SQLite database cannot be opened at boot the daemon runs on with no persistence at all and /health returns 200 with no `sqlite` component and no overlay/secret verdict — the one health component designed to be fatal is simply absent.
findings.claim: openLoomDB logs `loom_db.open_failed` at WARN and returns nil on any failure — file missing/unwritable data dir, read-only mount, disk full, corrupt page, a goose migration error (sqlitestore.Open returns the migration error at internal/store/sqlite/store.go:67-70), or the 10 s open timeout (daemon_boot.go:92-99). Nothing retries it for the process lifetime. Every downstream consumer is then guarded on `ov.db != nil` / `auditDB != nil`, and the guards include the two things that would have made the failure visible: the SQLite health probe is only started when `d.auditDB != nil` (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest.go:164-167), so the `sqlite` component — the one health.isCriticalComponent treats as fatal and maps to HTTP 503 (internal/health/tracker.go:445-448, handlers/health.go:56-60) — is never registered at all; and recordSecretHealth / recordConfigOverlayHealth are both inside `if ov.db != nil` (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:220-225), so `config.secrets` and `config.overlay` are absent too. ServiceAvailability only inspects the components present in the snapshot (tracker.go:357-394): an absent critical component cannot trip anything. The only residual signal is `alarm` = 'persistence-unavailable' (cmd/openccu-loom/alarm_wiring.go:23-28), one sample, non-critical, which then decays to `unknown` per finding F3-failure-paths-1. What is lost with ov.db == nil: the SQLite centrals table (so every CCU the operator adopted through the SPA or the onboarding wizard is gone — only cfg.Centrals from YAML survives), the DB-tier config sections, local users, API tokens and auth sessions, persisted audit, channel-flag overlays, alarm + security state, history, and the Matter fabric store.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator's data volume goes read-only (SD-card wear on a CCU3/RaspberryMatic add-on is the common case) or a migration fails after an upgrade. The daemon starts, the REST/SPA surface comes up, `GET /api/v1/health` answers 200 with status healthy (then `unknown` after 90 s per finding 1), and the SPA shows no error banner — while the CCU list is empty because the centrals table was never read, every SPA-saved config section is inactive, no audit row is persisted, and the Matter bridge has lost its fabrics. The only trace is a single WARN line, `loom_db.open_failed`, in the boot log.
findings.verified_by: Code trace: cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_boot.go:83-100 (nil on failure, no retry) -> daemon.go:220-225 (both health recorders behind `ov.db != nil`) -> daemon_rest.go:164-167 (sqlite probe behind `d.auditDB != nil`) -> internal/health/tracker.go:357-394 (ServiceAvailability only judges present components) -> internal/north/rest/handlers/health.go:56-60 (503 only on StatusUnhealthy). grep confirms `"sqlite"` is recorded from exactly one place, internal/store/sqlite/health_probe.go, which that guard skips.
findings.fix_sketch: Record the persistence verdict unconditionally: on a nil handle, register the `sqlite` component as UNHEALTHY with the open error as the note (and keep it re-recorded, see finding 1) so ServiceAvailability's critical rule fires and /health answers 503. Optionally retry openLoomDB on a bounded backoff so a transiently-busy or briefly read-only volume recovers without a restart.
findings.verify_reasoning: MEASURED. A second daemon (ports 18605/18610-18620, data dir $S/run/V4b/data) was booted with `<data_dir>/openccu-loom.db` created as a DIRECTORY so the open fails. It came up, logged `WARN loom_db.open_failed ... sqlite: ping: unable to open database file (14)` plus eight further `*_store_open_failed` warnings, and served `GET /api/v1/health` with HTTP 200. THE CORE OF THE FINDING HOLDS AND IS SHARPER THAN STATED: no `sqlite` component is ever recorded, because sqlitestore.StartHealthProbe returns a no-op stopper when `db == nil` (internal/store/sqlite/health_probe.go:48-50), and `sqlite` is precisely one of the two CRITICAL components whose Unhealthy status is the ONLY thing that maps /health to 503 (internal/health/tracker.go:445-448 isCriticalComponent -> handlers/health.go:56-59). So the guard designed to report a dead persistence tier is disabled by the very failure it exists to catch: a total persistence outage can never produce a 503, only 200. Likewise `config.overlay` and `config.secrets` are skipped entirely, since daemon.go:220 gates both on `ov.db != nil`. BUT 'no health signal at all' IS REFUTED. wireAlarmService (cmd/openccu-loom/alarm_wiring.go:24-29) is called unconditionally from daemon.go:368 and its `db == nil` branch records `alarm: unhealthy, note "persistence-unavailable"`. Measured at t+20 s: `{"status":"degraded",...{"name":"alarm","status":"unhealthy","note":"persistence-unavailable"}}`. That sample is never refreshed (grep: `s.health(` has exactly one call site, internal/alarm/service.go:446, for a start failure), so at t+~115 s it decayed to `unknown` -- but the note "persistence-unavailable" remained in the body permanently, and overall status stayed non-healthy (degraded/unknown) for the whole 175 s observation. So an operator reading /health does get a permanent, correctly-worded signal; what they never get is a 503, an `sqlite` component, or an `unhealthy` overall status. Re-rated from the implied high to medium: the daemon is loudly broken in the log and non-healthy in the body; the real defect is the unreachable critical-component/503 rule and the missing sqlite entry, not total silence.

findings.title: The SQLite health probe escalates merely elevated latency to UNHEALTHY, so two consecutive `SELECT 1` round-trips over 100 ms — or one over 1 s — make /health return HTTP 503 on a fully working daemon.
findings.claim: probeOnce records `Healthy: false` for the 'elevated probe' case (elapsed > healthyLatencyBudget = 100 ms, internal/store/sqlite/health_probe.go:108-116) and for the 'slow probe' case (> 500 ms, :103-107), with the comment at :109-112 stating the intent is DEGRADED via the flap-damp rule. The flap-damp only demotes to DEGRADED when the PREVIOUS status was StatusHealthy (internal/health/tracker.go:211-213); a second consecutive unhealthy sample therefore lands on StatusUnhealthy. `sqlite` is a critical component (tracker.go:445-448), so ServiceAvailability returns StatusUnhealthy immediately (tracker.go:370-374) and the handler maps that to HTTP 503 (internal/north/rest/handlers/health.go:56-60). The error branch is worse: the query context is bounded at degradedLatencyBudget*2 = 1 s (health_probe.go:84), while the connection's own busy_timeout is 5 s (internal/store/sqlite/dsn.go:20 and store.go:130) — so a lock wait the database is configured to tolerate for 5 s becomes a probe error at 1 s, and that branch deliberately double-records (:93-102), producing UNHEALTHY and 503 from a SINGLE slow probe.
findings.failure_scenario: On a CCU3 / RaspberryMatic add-on or a Pi with the data dir on SD, a WAL checkpoint (StartWALCheckpointLoop, cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:159), an audit-retention purge, an SPA-triggered backup or an upgrade migration saturates disk IO for a couple of seconds. The next `SELECT 1` exceeds the 1 s query deadline (or two probes 30 s apart each exceed 100 ms) and `GET /api/v1/health` returns 503 with status "unhealthy" until a fast probe lands up to 30 s later. Behind a load balancer or a k8s liveness probe the instance is drained or restarted; in the SPA the operator sees a red "system unhealthy" for a daemon that is serving every request correctly. The repo's own CCU add-on watchdog checks the TCP port rather than /health (packaging/ccu-addon/ccu/etc/monit-openccu-loom.cfg:15), so that specific deployment does not restart-loop.
findings.verified_by: Reproducer at $S/repro/F3/healthrepro (verbatim copy of internal/health, clock.Fake). `go run ./cmd` prints: 'probe ok -> healthy', '1st elevated probe -> degraded', '2nd elevated probe -> unhealthy HTTP 503'. Latency thresholds and the double-record read from internal/store/sqlite/health_probe.go:83-122.
findings.fix_sketch: Cap the latency-only samples at DEGRADED the way ping/pong noise is capped — use Tracker.RecordQuality (internal/health/tracker.go:248) for the 'elevated'/'slow' branches and reserve Record(Healthy:false) for a genuine query error. Also raise the probe's query deadline above the 5 s busy_timeout so a tolerated lock wait is not reported as a database failure.
