findings.title: The CCU serial resolved at bring-up is never persisted on the boot that resolves it, because the centrals row is seeded afterwards
findings.claim: `serialBackfiller` (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_southbound.go:95-110) hands the resolved serial to `CentralsStore.BackfillSerial`, whose UPDATE is `WHERE name = ? AND serial = ''` (internal/store/sqlite/centrals_store.go:203). When the row does not exist yet the statement affects 0 rows and the function returns `(false, nil)` — a silent no-op, not even logged (the `case updated:` branch at daemon_southbound.go:101-107 is the only log). On a boot that creates the centrals row from config.yaml, that row is written *after* the southbound bring-up has already resolved the serial, so the backfill always misses.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured on two independent first boots with an empty data dir. Boot A: ReGa `get_serial` dispatched at 12:19:14.97, `centrals` row created_at 12:19:24.16 — 9 s later; `serial` column stayed '' for the whole 22-minute run and `central.serial.backfilled` never appeared in the log. Boot B (fresh DB): `get_serial` at 12:48:41.03, row created at 12:48:48.94, `sqlite3 select name,serial from centrals` -> `('ccu-g3', '')`. Only the *next* boot logs `central.serial.backfilled`. The documented purpose of the field — letting SSDP recognise a host-configured CCU (e.g. one entered as `localhost`) as already configured — therefore fails on exactly the first run, which is when the operator is doing discovery.
findings.verified_by: measurement — daemon logs daemon-run1.log / daemon-cold.log timestamps, direct sqlite read of the centrals table, and the `central.serial.backfilled` line present only in daemon-run2.log
findings.fix_sketch: Seed the centrals table from config.yaml before the southbound bring-up starts, or re-run the backfill after the config seed (it is idempotent). Also log the `updated == false` case so a silent miss is visible.
findings.resolution: the centrals seed carries the serial the bring-up already resolved; the backfill miss is logged instead of silent

findings.title: A failed per-central read of the un-ignore store silently withdraws every un-ignore pattern and re-marks every device
findings.claim: `applyVisibilityUnIgnore` (cmd/openccu-loom/visibility_wiring.go:100-185) reads each central's persisted patterns; on error it logs a warning and `continue`s (line 133-137), i.e. treats that central as having none. It then calls `visReg.LoadUnIgnore(...)` (line 158) with the union of the *remaining* centrals, which REPLACES the shared registry's whole un-ignore set, and re-runs `visibility.ApplyUnIgnoredMarks` over every device of every central (lines 169-179). A single transient SQLite error (SQLITE_BUSY, a cancelled context) therefore un-applies patterns that are still persisted. The function is the `OnRegister` observer body (line 85-89), so it re-runs on every central registration and on every central removal.
findings.failure_scenario: Observed live in the shutdown log with a persisted `DUTY_CYCLE` pattern in place: `WARN visibility.unignore.read_failed central=ccu-g3 err="sqlite: list visibility_unignore: context canceled"` immediately followed by `INFO visibility.unignore.applied pattern_count=0 centrals_with_patterns=0 devices_touched=4`. At shutdown that is harmless, but the same code path runs when a central is adopted or removed at runtime: a store hiccup there makes every un-ignored data point disappear again from the model, REST, the SPA and MQTT until something else re-applies it.
findings.verified_by: observed log pair in $S/run/G3/logs/daemon-run1.log at 12:41:07 plus code trace of visibility_wiring.go:130-179
findings.fix_sketch: On a read error abort the whole apply (return early, keep the previous registry contents) instead of proceeding with a partial union; only replace the registry when every central's list was read successfully.

findings.title: A system variable the CCU reports without a value gets an HA discovery config but never a state publish, producing a permanently unknown entity
findings.claim: `wireOneSysvar` publishes the discovery config unconditionally and the state only `if observed` (internal/central/adapter/hub_mqtt_publisher.go:758-763). Nothing later retracts the config for a sysvar that stays unobserved, and `Bridge.PublishSysvar` (internal/north/mqtt/bridge.go:1233) is never reached for it. This is the declared-vs-published mismatch the project rules call out.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured: the simulated CCU exposes a BOOL sysvar `Presence` that GET /api/v1/sysvars reports with `"observed": false` and no value. The broker holds retained `homeassistant/sensor/ccu-g3_sysvars/presence/config` while `openccu-loom/ccu-g3/hub/sysvars/Presence/state` was never published in any of the 8 daemon runs. In Home Assistant that is an entity permanently stuck at `unknown`. (Secondary observation from the same payload: `Presence` is BOOL yet renders as component `sensor`, not `binary_sensor` — the LOGIC/ALARM branch of BuildSysvarDiscovery at internal/north/mqtt/hub_discovery.go:234 was not taken, so the value-type mapping fell through to the `default:` sensor branch.)
findings.verified_by: measurement — retained-topic snapshots ($S/run/G3/mqtt-topics-run2.txt) cross-checked against GET /api/v1/sysvars; code trace of hub_mqtt_publisher.go:758-763
findings.fix_sketch: Either skip the discovery config until the sysvar has a value (and publish it from the OnUpdate hook), or publish an explicit `None`/unavailable state alongside the config so the declared topic is always written. Add a discovery-round-trip assertion over the hub plane covering the unobserved case.

findings.title: Interface.getSuppressedServiceMessages returns a JSON string wrapping the array, so the result type-assertion fails silently and every parameter-scoped suppression is filtered out of the suppressed list
findings.claim: Live, OttoGo: `Interface.getSuppressedServiceMessages {"interface":"HmIP-RF","channelAddress":"00245A49949662:0"}` returns the JSON value `"[]"` - a *string* containing the array text, not an array. The CCU's own implementation explains it: /www/api/methods/interface/getsuppressedservicemessages.tcl builds `set result "\["` … `append result [json_toString $param]` … and finishes with `jsonrpc_response [json_toString $result]`, i.e. it json-encodes the already-rendered array text a second time. Go side: CcuBackend.GetSuppressedServiceMessages (ccu_extended.go:1023-1048) decodes into `any`, gets a Go string, and line 1037 `list, ok := raw.([]any)` fails, so line 1039 returns `nil, nil` - an empty list with NO error. That result flows to hub.ServiceMessages.Suppressed (internal/model/hub/messages.go:657): err is nil, so `live[k]` becomes a non-nil EMPTY set, and the keep-filter at messages.go:670-675 (`set == nil || e.Parameter == "" || set[e.Parameter]`) drops every record whose Parameter is non-empty. Suppressed() backs REST GET .../service-messages/suppressed (internal/north/rest/router.go:1274 -> handlers/hub.go:1317-1340) and the WS service_messages.suppressed command (internal/north/rest/ws/commands_extended.go:949-958). The write half is fine - SuppressServiceMessage sends interface/channelAddress/parameterId/suppress, which matches the CCU's suppressservicemessages.tcl args exactly - so the suppression is applied on the CCU and recorded locally, and only the read-back is broken. Bonus: the second wrapper, jsonrpc.Client.GetSuppressedServiceMessages (internal/client/transport/jsonrpc/methods.go:676-682), sends the parameter as "channel"; live that is rejected outright with `json-rpc error 402: missing argument (channelAddress)`.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator suppresses the LOW_BAT service message of one channel through OpenCCU-Loom. The suppression is applied on the CCU, but the very next read of the suppressed-messages view (REST or WS, and therefore the SPA management surface) returns an empty list, so the operator sees 'nothing suppressed', cannot review what is muted, and cannot un-suppress it from that list. Only channel-wide records (Parameter == "") survive the filter.
findings.verified_by: live JSON-RPC call returning the string "[]" (and 402 for the "channel" spelling) + the CCU's own getsuppressedservicemessages.tcl read off the device + code trace through messages.go's keep-filter ($S/repro/G4/EVIDENCE.md §2)
findings.fix_sketch: Decode the result defensively: when raw is a string, json.Unmarshal it a second time into []any before the loop (the CCU double-encodes it), and return a distinguishable error when neither shape parses so Suppressed() keeps the records (set == nil) instead of dropping them. Also fix the jsonrpc.Client wrapper's parameter name to channelAddress and its result type to match.
findings.verify_reasoning: Measurement reproduces exactly and the core consequence holds, but one of the two named north-bound surfaces does not exist in production. Live on OttoGo and KearneyGo, Interface.getSuppressedServiceMessages with the backend's parameter names ({interface, channelAddress}) returns the JSON value "[]" - a string containing the array text. The CCU's own /www/api/methods/interface/getsuppressedservicemessages.tcl, read off the device, builds `set result "\["` … `append result [json_toString $param]` … and finishes `jsonrpc_response [json_toString $result]`, so the result is a string for a non-empty list too. The jsonrpc.Client wrapper's "channel" spelling is rejected outright with 402 missing argument (channelAddress), as claimed. Go side proven by execution, not inspection (v9_suppressed_test.go drives the real CcuBackend through a Caller that decodes into `any` exactly as adapter/jsonrpc_caller.go:41-45 does): wire "[]" -> nil,nil; wire "[\"LOW_BAT\"]" -> nil,nil (silently empty, no error, even with content); wire ["LOW_BAT"] (a real array) -> [LOW_BAT]. In hub/messages.go:657-675 err==nil makes live[k] a NON-nil empty map (make(...) is never nil), so the keep-filter `set == nil || e.Parameter == "" || set[e.Parameter]` drops every record with a non-empty Parameter - and every record has one, because Disable stores msg.Parameter and serviceMessageParameter splits the CCU name at the last dot (AL-000D1A49A3D83F:0.UNREACH -> UNREACH), which is the shape of every live service message I captured. So the reconciled list is always empty. WHAT IS WRONG: the finding names the WS command service_messages.suppressed as a second affected surface. It is not registered in production - cmd/openccu-loom/ws_adapters.go:185 explicitly passes ExtendedHub as nil, and commands_extended.go:399-402 only registers those three handlers when it is non-nil; nothing in the tree implements ListSuppressedServiceMessages. The single production consumer is REST GET /service-messages/suppressed (router.go:1274 -> handlers/hub.go:1317-1340), which the SPA calls (client.ts:1400). ALSO NARROWING: the suppressed record set is in-memory only - the only writer is Disable, there is no store - so the effect is scoped to one daemon lifetime rather than being durable data loss. Re-rated high -> medium: one surface, ephemeral records, the suppression itself is correctly applied on the CCU (the write half matches suppressservicemessages.tcl); what breaks is that the management view can never show or undo it.

findings.title: The CCU's lastExecuteTime is decoded from Program.getAll and then never read, so last_executed is empty on REST, MCP and MQTT for every program the CCU ran by itself
findings.claim: Live, OttoGo: Program.getAll returns 35 programs, each carrying a real timestamp, e.g. {"id":"9490","name":"D:Licht bei Dämmerung","isActive":true,"isInternal":true,"lastExecuteTime":"2026-08-17 12:33:04"}. The Go decoder declares the field - programEntry.LastExecuteTime json.RawMessage `json:"lastExecuteTime"` at hub_wiring.go:785 - and a repo-wide grep for LastExecuteTime over all .go files returns exactly three non-test hits: this declaration, hub.Program.LastExecuteTimeString (internal/model/hub/program.go:223) and its MCP caller. Nothing ever reads programEntry.LastExecuteTime. The only writer of hub.Program.lastExecute is Program.OnExecution (internal/model/hub/program.go:339), i.e. an execution the daemon itself observes. Three north-bound surfaces expose the field: REST /hub programs (internal/north/rest/handlers/hub.go:143 + :428 `if ts, hasTS := p.LastExecution(); hasTS`), MCP (internal/north/mcp/tools_hub.go:61/88) and the MQTT program payload (internal/payload/state.go:226 via internal/model/hub/payload.go:87). All three omit last_executed (omitempty) until the daemon has run the program itself.
findings.failure_scenario: A CCU program that runs on its own schedule - 'D:Licht bei Dämmerung', last run 2026-08-17 12:33:04 according to the CCU - shows no last_executed value in GET /api/v1/hub (or via MCP, or in the MQTT program payload) after a daemon restart, and keeps showing none forever unless the operator triggers it through OpenCCU-Loom. The information exists on the CCU in the very response the daemon already parses.
findings.verified_by: live Program.getAll on OttoGo (35 programs with populated lastExecuteTime) + repo-wide grep proving the field has no reader + trace of the only lastExecute writer
findings.fix_sketch: In the program upsert, parse lastExecuteTime (CCU-local "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS", so parse in the CCU's timezone - get_backend_info.fn already reports it as Europe/Berlin - and treat 1970-01-01 01:00:00 as 'never'), then seed hub.Program's lastExecute through a setter that does not fire the execution callbacks.
findings.verify_reasoning: Re-measured: Program.getAll on OttoGo returns 35 programs, 33 of them with a real lastExecuteTime (e.g. {"id":"9490","name":"D:Licht bei Dämmerung","isActive":true,"isInternal":true,"lastExecuteTime":"2026-08-17 13:11:12"}); the remaining 2 carry the CCU's never-run sentinel "1970-01-01 01:00:00", which itself confirms the field is meaningful rather than always blank. Go side verified by repo-wide grep over non-test files: LastExecuteTime appears exactly three times - the decoder field programEntry.LastExecuteTime (hub_wiring.go:785), the unrelated model getter Program.LastExecuteTimeString (program.go:223) and its MCP caller (tools_hub.go:88). Nothing reads the decoded field. The only writer of Program.lastExecute is program.go:339 inside OnExecution, i.e. an execution the daemon itself observed. The three north-bound surfaces gate on that same zero value: REST via `if ts, hasTS := p.LastExecution(); hasTS` (handlers/hub.go:428, and LastExecution returns !IsZero), MCP via LastExecuteTimeString (empty when zero), and the MQTT program payload. So last_executed is omitted for every CCU-scheduled program until the daemon triggers it itself. Severity medium is right: no malfunction, but a documented API field is permanently empty although the data arrives in a response the daemon already parses.

findings.title: [C21-schedules-2] The SPA's simple-schedule save drops `domain`, so the lock encoding never runs on any write from the UI
findings.claim: The editor reads schedule.domain (SimpleScheduleEditor.svelte:30-40) and renders the domain-specific widgets from it, including the lock mode / lock action / permission pickers (:379-466). But save() rebuilds the PUT body from scratch as `{ channel, kind: "simple", simple_entries }` (:200-204) and omits `domain`, which hmapi.ClimateSchedule declares as `json:"domain,omitempty"` (pkg/hmapi/rest_contract.go:266). PutClimateSchedule therefore passes sched.Domain == "" into serializeSimpleScheduleWithDomain, whose only branch is `if domain == "lock"` — so applyLockEncoding is skipped for every save originating in the SPA. This is independent of finding C21-schedules-1: fixing the read-side domain mapping alone would still leave every SPA write unencoded.
findings.failure_scenario: On a lock device whose domain resolved correctly, the operator picks lock_action = "unlock_autorelock_end" in the SPA and saves. The PUT body carries lock_action but no domain, so serializeSimpleScheduleWithDomain (schedules.go:796-809) takes the non-lock path; applyLockEncoding never converts lock_action into (LEVEL 1.0, DURATION_BASE 7, DURATION_FACTOR 31). simpleScheduleToDomain (schedules.go:772-786) does not copy LockMode/LockAction/Permission into schedule.SimpleEntry either, so the fields are dropped entirely and the slot is written with whatever raw level the DTO happened to carry. The chosen lock action silently does not reach the device.
findings.verified_by: code trace against HEAD 34b0f4c9 (re-read the cited file:line region; unchanged since the audit that reported it, or independently re-derived)
findings.fix_sketch: SimpleScheduleEditor.svelte's save() must include `domain` in the PUT payload (`{ channel, kind: "simple", domain, simple_entries: entries }`); simpleScheduleToDomain should also copy LockMode/LockAction/Permission into schedule.SimpleEntry so REST/WS/MCP round-trips stay consistent.

findings.title: north.mqtt.payload_format is an editable, validated config knob that no production code reads, and its SPA help in both locales still describes the bare-scalar mode that no longer exists
findings.claim: The field is declared at internal/config/config.go:1450 with `cfg:"expert"`, so config.ClassifyFields puts it in GET /api/v1/config/schema and the SPA section editor renders it as an editable leaf. It is validated at internal/config/config.go:2246-2250 (accepts only `bare` or `json`), so a save round-trips successfully. Nothing reads it: `PayloadFormat` occurs in the entire non-test Go tree only at internal/config/config.go:1450 (declaration) and :2246/:2250 (the validator) — ripgrep over every *.go excluding _test.go returns no other production hit, and internal/north/mqtt has no PayloadFormat type or BridgeConfig field at all, which is why the two godoc links `[PayloadFormat]` at internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:165 and :1020 do not resolve. The mqtt package documents the retirement itself at internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:168-171: 'State topics carry the canonical JSON envelope {"value":..,"available":..,"modified_at":..} ... The earlier bare-scalar mode was retired with the ADR-0011 payload unification.' internal/north/mqtt/payload_format_test.go:38-42 says the same. Meanwhile the operator-facing help still promises the removed behaviour: assets/ui/src/lib/i18n.ts:1560 (EN) 'bare keeps primitive scalar payloads (backwards-compat); json wraps state with {value, available}. Flip only after every consumer is upgraded.' and :5666 (DE) the same, and the Go field doc at internal/config/config.go:1443-1449 says 'Empty / "bare" (default) keeps primitive scalar payloads — backwards-compatible with non-HA consumers ... Switching this BREAKS bare-value subscribers'. docs/admin/configuration.md:372-376 already carries the honest note ('currently a no-op / reserved'), so the doc, the code comment and the UI disagree with each other.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator running Node-RED or Telegraf against the raw plane opens Settings -> MQTT, reads the inline help, and leaves (or sets) payload_format at `bare` expecting primitive scalar payloads on `<base>/<central>/<iface>/<addr>/<ch>/values/<param>`. The save succeeds and no warning appears, but every state topic keeps carrying the JSON envelope, so the subscriber sees `{"value":true,...}` where the UI told it to expect `true`. The reverse is equally misleading: an operator told that `json` is opt-in has no way to learn from the UI that it is already the only mode.
findings.verified_by: code trace: declaration internal/config/config.go:1450; validator internal/config/config.go:2246-2250; ripgrep for `PayloadFormat` over all non-test .go returns only those three sites; internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:168-171 states the mode was retired; SPA help assets/ui/src/lib/i18n.ts:1560 (EN) and :5666 (DE); docs/admin/configuration.md:372-376 already declares it a no-op
findings.fix_sketch: Either delete the field together with its validator, its config.field/config.help entries in both locales and its docs/admin/configuration.md row, or wire it through BridgeConfig. At minimum, replace the EN+DE help and the Go field doc with the 'reserved, no effect today' wording the admin doc already uses, and drop the two dangling [PayloadFormat] doc links in internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go.

findings.title: TestEveryWiringSetterHasAProductionCaller matches only Set*/Attach*/Register*, leaving the codebase's fluent With* collaborator injectors outside the guard
findings.claim: isWiringVerb (wiring_setter_callers_test.go:220-228) accepts exactly the prefixes Set, Attach, Register. This codebase injects collaborators through fluent With* methods just as often: MQTTCommandSink.WithSelectionLabeler (internal/central/adapter/mqtt_sink.go:45), EventBridge.WithVisibility / WithParameterLabels (internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:170,181), and CommandSubscriber.WithCDPSink / WithWeekProfileSink / WithCombinedDPSink / WithScheduleSwitchSink / WithInstallModeSink / WithCentralNames / WithCollector (wired in cmd/openccu-loom/mqtt_supervisor.go:774-786). All satisfy the guard's own definition of a seam (one collaborator in, receiver or nothing out) and none of them can ever be reported. Measured: deleting the sole production call of WithSelectionLabeler (cmd/openccu-loom/mqtt_supervisor.go:772) leaves TestEveryWiringSetterHasAProductionCaller green (89s). The only other test that touches the seam, internal/central/adapter/selection_label_roundtrip_test.go:83,141, constructs the sink and calls WithSelectionLabeler itself — the bracketing shape — so it stays green too.
findings.failure_scenario: A With*-injected collaborator loses its call in a supervisor refactor. Per the production comment at mqtt_supervisor.go:769-771, an operator picking a localised siren tone or light effect in Home Assistant then has the command 'resolve to nothing'; with WithInstallModeSink or WithCDPSink it would be the whole install-mode or custom-DP command plane. Nothing in the suite reports it.
findings.verified_by: mutation in $S/wt: cmd/openccu-loom/mqtt_supervisor.go:772 call removed; `go test ./tests/contract/ -run TestEveryWiringSetterHasAProductionCaller` ok; reverted
findings.fix_sketch: Add With (and Use/Bind if they appear) to isWiringVerb; the collaborator-shape filter and the fluent returnsNothingOrSelf check already handle the rest. Expect a first run to surface real orphans — that is the point.

findings.title: TestAlarmSinkFansOutEveryEventType is driven by a hand-written literal list, not by the domain's event catalogue, so a newly added alarm event can fall into the sink's default branch with every guard green
findings.claim: CLAUDE.md states the fan-out guards are 'driven from the domain's EventType* constants'. They are not: sinkFanoutCases (sink_fanout_test.go:23-34) is a literal slice of ten values, and subscribeByType (sink_fanout_test.go:87-113) is a hand-written switch over the same ten. Nothing derives either from the twelve EventTypeAlarm* constants in pkg/hmevent/alarm.go:15-26 or from the producers. An event type added to internal/alarm and handed to Service.publish without a case in the switch (internal/alarm/service.go:568-616) therefore hits the default branch, is logged and dropped — and the guard cannot notice, because it only drives the events it already knows. TestEveryEventTypeHasASubscriber does not compensate: AlarmDuressEvent had a webhook subscriber throughout the original defect, so the subscriber guard was green while the sink dropped the event before it ever reached the bus. Verified that today's set is consistent: the six types the engine emits (engine.go, sources.go, readiness.go, walktest.go) plus panels/health/journal/reminder are all in the table, and the two alarm events that bypass the sink (AlarmNotificationEvent service.go:554, AlarmCodesChangedEvent service.go:241) publish directly.
findings.failure_scenario: The next alarm feature adds, say, AlarmTamperEvent, publishes it through the sink and subscribes to it in the MQTT publisher. The sink's default branch swallows it, the operator sees nothing on any surface, and the fan-out guard — the one written after exactly this happened to AlarmDuressEvent under coercion — passes because its table never learned the new type.
findings.verified_by: code trace of sink_fanout_test.go:23-113 vs pkg/hmevent/alarm.go:15-26 and the sink switch in internal/alarm/service.go:568-616; producer inventory measured by grepping every e.sink.Publish / s.publish call site
findings.fix_sketch: Derive the table from the catalogue: enumerate the EventTypeAlarm* constants (or a registry mapping constant -> zero value) and fail on any constant the sink drives into default, so adding an event forces the case. Keep subscribeByType exhaustive by generating it from the same list.
findings.resolution: refuted on re-verification: TestEveryEventTypeHasAPublisher (tests/contract/event_publisher_coverage_test.go, shipped 0.59.1) already catches the producer half this claims is unguarded

findings.title: Every hub / alarm / security / add-on-update / week-profile / device-update entity still sends the `object_id` discovery option, which Home Assistant removed in 2026.3 - the daemon's deterministic entity_ids are silently gone and no `default_entity_id` replaces them
findings.claim: 20 production call sites emit `"object_id": uniqueID` in the discovery body: internal/north/mqtt/hub_discovery.go:221,461,526,563,595,631,711,753,788,830,870,912,956; alarm_discovery.go:128,189,238; security_discovery.go:148; addon_update_discovery.go:50; discovery_update.go:137; discovery_week_profile.go:112. Home Assistant deleted `CONF_OBJECT_ID` from MQTT_ENTITY_COMMON_SCHEMA in core commit 87b83dcc1bc154f4d34749cef8639dd2a8ebb913 ("Remove the MQTT `object_id` option after 6 months of deprecation", #164460, 2026-02-28 -> HA 2026.3), after deprecating it in c7f05602088 (#151775, 2025-09-08) in favour of `default_entity_id`. In the local HA 2026.8.2 checkout `object_id` no longer appears in mqtt/const.py, mqtt/schemas.py or mqtt/abbreviations.py; the discovery schema is built with `extra=vol.REMOVE_EXTRA`, so the key is stripped without any error. `MqttEntity._set_entity_id` (mqtt/entity.py:1459-1470) now returns early unless `default_entity_id` is present. The daemon emits `default_entity_id` nowhere (grep over internal/ finds zero hits), so nothing takes over. Measured: 178 of the 190 hand-built entities carry `object_id`; the device plane does not (it never used the key).
findings.failure_scenario: On HA >= 2026.3 a fresh install no longer gets `sensor.loom_3014f711a0_system_health`, `alarm_control_panel.openccu_loom_alarm_zone1`, `update.loom_addon_update` etc.; HA derives the entity_id from the device name plus the entity name instead, so it varies with the operator's CCU naming and with the configured locale. On HA 2025.9-2026.2 each of these entities additionally logged a deprecation warning naming openccu-loom as the origin. notes/concepts/security-safety-concept.md:709 explicitly promises that every existing alarm_control_panel entity keeps `unique_id` **and** `object_id` `openccu-loom_alarm_<zoneID>`, and docs/contributor/source-interface.md:154 documents `object_id` as part of the payload contract - both guarantees no longer hold.
findings.verified_by: code trace (20 emit sites in internal/north/mqtt/) + HA core git history and HEAD source at /home/markus/Dokumente/GitHub/core (git show 87b83dcc1bc -- homeassistant/components/mqtt/schemas.py shows the `vol.Optional(CONF_OBJECT_ID)` line being deleted) + generated payload dump $S/repro/J1/nondevice.json validated by $S/repro/J1/validate.py against the extracted key sets (178 `*.object_id` violations).
findings.fix_sketch: Replace `"object_id": uniqueID` with `"default_entity_id": "<component>.<uniqueID>"` at all 20 sites (the value must carry the domain prefix), or drop the key and accept name-derived entity_ids and update the two documents that promise otherwise. A contract test that pins the emitted key set of each hand-built builder against a checked-in HA-allowed-key list would have caught the removal.

findings.title: `in_progress_template` is not a Home Assistant MQTT `update` option, and the declared `value_template` prevents HA from reading `in_progress` out of the state JSON - the CCU-firmware and add-on self-update entities never show an install in progress
findings.claim: Both update builders emit `"in_progress_template": "{{ value_json.in_progress }}"` (internal/north/mqtt/addon_update_discovery.go:55 and internal/north/mqtt/hub_discovery.go:961) together with `"value_template": "{{ value_json.installed_version }}"`. HA's MQTT update platform has no such option: its schema (homeassistant/components/mqtt/update.py:47-59) lists only command_topic, device_class, display_precision, latest_version_template/topic, name, payload_install, release_summary, release_url, retain, title (+ the common schema), so `in_progress_template` is dropped by `extra=vol.REMOVE_EXTRA`. HA obtains `in_progress` exclusively from the *post-value_template* state payload when that payload parses as a JSON object (update.py:74 declares `vol.Optional("in_progress"): cv.boolean` in the state-payload schema, and update.py:223-225 reads it). The daemon publishes exactly the right JSON on the state topic - `{"installed_version":..,"latest_version":..,"in_progress":..}` from Bridge.PublishHubUpdate (internal/north/mqtt/bridge.go:1549-1566) and Bridge.PublishAddonUpdateState (bridge.go:1576-1593) - but the declared `value_template` reduces it to the bare version string first, so HA takes the JSON-decode-failure branch at update.py:190-200 (`json_payload["installed_version"] = str(payload)`) and never sees `in_progress` or `update_percentage`.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator presses Install on the `update.loom_addon_update` entity in HA. The daemon starts the self-update and publishes `in_progress: true`. HA's entity keeps `in_progress = None`, so no progress is shown and the Install button stays active - the operator can press it repeatedly during an in-flight install. The same applies to the CCU firmware-update entity from BuildHubUpdateDiscovery.
findings.verified_by: code trace: HA schema at homeassistant/components/mqtt/update.py:47-75 and the state handler at update.py:185-225 (HA 2026.8.2 checkout); daemon emitters at internal/north/mqtt/addon_update_discovery.go:46-60 and hub_discovery.go:953-968; published payload shape at internal/north/mqtt/bridge.go:1549-1593. Generated payload in $S/repro/J1/nondevice.json, flagged by the key validator as `update.in_progress_template` (2 entities).
findings.fix_sketch: Drop both `value_template` and `in_progress_template` from the two update payloads (and optionally `latest_version_topic`/`latest_version_template`, which become redundant): HA then parses the published JSON natively and picks up installed_version, latest_version and in_progress in one go. Add `update_percentage` to the published JSON if a progress bar is wanted.

findings.title: The whole north.rest.auth.oidc section is consumed once during router assembly but carries no restart-required rule, so saving an SSO configuration answers restart_required:false and SSO stays dead until the operator guesses to restart
findings.claim: north.rest.auth.oidc is its own DB-tier section (internal/configstore/sections.go:30 SectionOIDC) and is edited through a plain SectionEditor with no hint (assets/ui/src/routes/Settings.svelte:697-707 — note the neighbouring ccu_auth tab at :709-715 does carry a hint). Its six leaves (enabled, issuer, client_id, client_secret, redirect_url, role_claim) are read exactly once: cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest_mount.go:355 `OIDC: buildOIDCRest(cfg, logger, d.restAuth)` and :394 `oidc: cfg.North.REST.Auth.OIDC.Enabled && ...Issuer != ""`, both inside mountRESTServer, which cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:781 calls exactly once per process (its returned teardown is only used at shutdown; nothing re-mounts the router). buildOIDCClient (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_north.go:599) returns nil when !Enabled || Issuer == "", so a daemon booted without OIDC has OIDCDeps == nil for its whole life. authRestartRules (internal/config/restart.go:370-416) covers north.rest.auth.ccu, .ha_ingress, .basic_enabled and .bearer_enabled — but NOT .oidc. Consequently config.RestartRequiredFieldPaths() contains no oidc path, so (a) the schema handler badges none of them (internal/north/rest/handlers/admin_config.go:145 + :187), (b) the PUT answers restart_required:false (admin_config.go:690), and (c) the /restart-pending banner stays empty (cmd/openccu-loom/restart_pending_provider.go:42). The contract test tests/contract/config_restart_required_test.go only checks badge<->diff consistency in both directions; it has no notion of 'boot-only field that is in neither list', so nothing fails.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator opens Settings -> Security -> OIDC on a running daemon, fills issuer/client_id/client_secret/redirect_url, ticks Enabled, saves. The toast says saved, no field carries a restart badge, no restart-pending banner appears. They log out and click the Single Sign-On button on the login page (assets/ui/src/routes/Login.svelte:106 renders it unconditionally) and get a 503 from /api/v1/auth/oidc/start, because OIDCDeps is still nil. Nothing anywhere tells them a restart is required. (The comment at cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_north.go:584 'the SPA then hides the SSO button' is also false — Login.svelte always renders it.)
findings.verified_by: code trace: restart.go rule table read in full (no oidc entry) + single call site of mountRESTServer + buildOIDCRest nil path + admin_config.go PUT computing restart_required solely from RestartRequiredDiff
findings.fix_sketch: Add an oidcRestartRule to authRestartRules comparing reflect.DeepEqual(b.North.REST.Auth.OIDC, e.North.REST.Auth.OIDC) with Fields listing all six leaves — the same shape the ccu / ha_ingress block rules already use. Better still, add a contract test that fails when a cfg leaf whose only production read sits under cmd/openccu-loom's boot path is neither badged nor hot-reloaded.
findings.verify_reasoning: Mechanism re-derived and confirmed exactly. restartRules() (internal/config/restart.go:51-70, six groups) contains no rule whose Path or Fields mention north.rest.auth.oidc — I enumerated every Path: in the file and ran RestartRequiredFieldPaths()/RestartRequiredDiff() directly: the three oidc leaves are unbadged and a base->candidate diff that turns OIDC on returns []. The schema badge is an exact map lookup (admin_config.go GetConfigSchema: `_, restart := restartRequiredPaths[f.Path]`), so no prefix rule can rescue it, and the PUT answers `restartRequired := len(config.RestartRequiredDiff(base, candidate)) > 0` (admin_config.go:~700). OIDC is a DB-tier section (configstore SectionOIDC), is NOT in sectionUnmanagedPaths nor dedicatedEditorPaths, and its Settings.svelte tab (l.697-707) carries no hint while the neighbouring ccu_auth tab does. buildOIDCRest/buildOIDCClient return nil when !Enabled||Issuer=='' and mountRESTServer has exactly one production call site (daemon.go:781), so OIDCDeps stays nil for the process lifetime. Two corrections, both immaterial to the mechanism: the failure scenario says the SSO click yields 503 — the routes are only registered `if d.OIDC != nil` (router.go:727-739), so it is a 404; and severity is over-stated: the failure is fail-CLOSED (SSO absent, password login unaffected, no privilege or data effect) and a restart fixes it, which is medium, not high. The finding's sub-claim that the daemon_north.go:584 comment ('the SPA then hides the SSO button') is false is itself CONFIRMED — Login.svelte:106 renders the button unconditionally.

findings.title: north.rest.auth.ha_ingress.role silently escalates any unrecognised value to admin — an unvalidated free-text security field that fails open
findings.claim: HAIngressConfig.Role (internal/config/config.go:1554) is documented as '"admin" (default), "operator" or "viewer"' and its SPA help repeats exactly that (assets/ui/src/lib/i18n.ts:1723 EN, :5830 DE). It is a plain string leaf: config.Validate never touches it (validateOperatorSurfaces -> validateFieldRanges, internal/config/validate.go:30-53, has no ha_ingress check), and the schema endpoint carries no enum/options — SchemaField (internal/north/rest/handlers/admin_config.go:40-60) has only path/class/go_type/restart_required/default, so the SectionEditor renders it as a free-text input (the only Select in the editor is triStateOptions, assets/ui/src/lib/components/settings/SectionEditor.svelte:753). The consumer ingressRole (cmd/openccu-loom/ingress_auth_wiring.go:76-85) switches on auth.Role(s) for RoleViewer and RoleOperator and returns auth.RoleAdmin in the `default:` branch (line 82-83). So 'Viewer', 'read-only', 'operatr', 'guest' — any typo, any capitalisation, any well-meant near-miss — resolves to full admin, with no error at save and no warning at boot (the only log emitted, ingress_auth_wiring.go:66, prints the *resolved* role, i.e. 'admin', which reads as confirmation rather than as a correction).
findings.failure_scenario: An operator running the supervised HA add-on wants Ingress requests limited to read-only, types 'Viewer' (or 'read-only') into the free-text Granted role field and saves. The field IS badged restart-required, so they restart — and every Home-Assistant-proxied request is now granted RoleAdmin instead of RoleViewer: full device writes, config edits, user management, all without a login, exactly the restriction they thought they had applied. The daemon logs `auth.ingress.enabled ... role=admin`, which looks like the intended state rather than a silent widening.
findings.verified_by: code trace: no validator for the field anywhere in internal/config/validate.go or config.Validate; SchemaField has no options member; ingressRole default branch returns auth.RoleAdmin
findings.fix_sketch: Validate the value in validateFieldRanges (reject anything outside admin|operator|viewer, empty = default) so a typo is refused at the save with the field named, and change ingressRole's default branch to be reachable only for the empty string. Fail-closed on an unknown value would be even better than fail-to-admin.
findings.verify_reasoning: Privilege-escalation claim verified end-to-end against the shipped binary. ingressRole (cmd/openccu-loom/ingress_auth_wiring.go:76-85) switches on auth.Role(s) with no strings.ToLower/TrimSpace anywhere on the path and returns auth.RoleAdmin from `default:`; buildIngressTrust passes the resolved Role straight into auth.IngressTrust, and IngressPassthrough injects Identity{Scheme: SchemeIngress, Role: t.Role}. No validator exists: validateFieldRanges (internal/config/validate.go:30-53) calls locale/callback/webhook/mcp/matter/restLimits/floats/durations only, validateRESTLimits touches rate_limit + ws.replay_capacity, and `cfg.Validate()` on a config carrying role='Viewer' returns nil (executed). The schema DTO (SchemaField) has no options/enum member and the SectionEditor's only <Select> is triStateOptions, so the SPA renders free text; the PUT's semantic gate is exactly that same candidate.Validate(). RUN PROOF: daemon booted with OPENCCU_LOOM_SUPERVISOR=1 and `role: "Viewer"`, request carrying X-Ingress-Path from the trusted CIDR -> GET /api/v1/auth/me = {"subject":"ha-ingress","role":"admin","scheme":"ingress"} and admin-only GET /api/v1/audit = 200. Counter-case with `role: "viewer"` -> role viewer and /api/v1/audit = 403. The startup WARN prints the RESOLVED role ('role=admin'), which reads as confirmation. Severity kept at medium, not raised: admin is also the documented default, the passthrough only fires in the supervised add-on behind Ingress, and the shipped add-on pins panel_admin: true, so the blast radius is HA admins whose privileges the operator intended to reduce and silently did not.

findings.title: callback.bin_port: 0 is documented as the dynamic/OS-assigned mode in four places but applyDefaults rewrites it to 8129, so the dynamic BIN-RPC port is unreachable in production
findings.claim: The BIN-RPC listener genuinely supports an OS-assigned port: cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_boot.go:367 composes `host:0`, and :387-388 re-reads the effective port back off `srv.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr).Port` so the value advertised to the CCU is the bound one. The mode is documented as available in four places: the field comment internal/config/config.go:570 ('BIN-RPC; 0 = dynamic'), CLAUDE.md:400 ('bin_port: 0 *is* dynamic', explicitly contrasted with rpc_callback.port), docs/user-guide.md:132 ('0 = dynamic') and example.config.full.yaml:576 ('0 = dynamic'). But internal/config/config.go:1865-1867 `if c.Callback.BinPort == 0 { c.Callback.BinPort = 8129 }` runs on every ingestion path a real daemon uses: Parse (config.go:1797), Default (config.go:1807), and the DB-tier overlay's ApplyDefaults (internal/configstore/store.go:297 and :336). cmd/openccu-loom/main.go reaches the daemon only through config.DefaultWithEnv() (:105) or config.LoadWithEnv() (:114), both of which apply defaults. cfg.Callback.BinPort is therefore never 0 by the time wireBINRPCCallback reads it, and callback.port_range applies only to the XML-RPC listener — there is no other way to request a free BIN-RPC port.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator running two daemons on one host (e.g. one per CCU, or the daemon alongside a second test instance) follows the documented advice and sets `callback: bin_port: 0` on both so each picks a free port. Both are rewritten to 8129; the second daemon's listener fails to bind, logs `callback.binrpc.start.failed` at WARN, degrades to a nil server, and every CUxD push callback for that daemon is silently lost while the daemon otherwise reports healthy.
findings.verified_by: code trace: applyDefaults BinPort branch; the three ApplyDefaults call sites on the production ingestion paths; wireBINRPCCallback's Addr()-readback proving the dynamic path exists but is unreachable
findings.fix_sketch: Drop the `BinPort == 0 -> 8129` branch from applyDefaults and move the 8129 fallback to the point where the config is *created* (a Default() seed / the example YAML), the way port_range already distinguishes 'unset' from 'OS-assigned'. Alternatively keep the rewrite and correct all four documents plus the SPA help ('Same dynamic-port semantics as the XML-RPC port', i18n.ts:1687) to say 0 means 8129.
findings.verify_reasoning: Code is right about the wire and every document is wrong, with a measured consequence. internal/config/config.go:1865-1867 rewrites BinPort 0 -> 8129 inside applyDefaults, which runs on Parse (config.go:1797), Default (1807) and on the DB-tier assembly (configstore/store.go:297 OverlayInto — called on the boot path at cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_boot.go:218 — and :336 Effective). Executed: Default()+BinPort=0+ApplyDefaults() -> 8129. The env overlay does run after applyDefaults (LoadWithEnv = Load -> OverlayFromEnv), so OPENCCU_LOOM_CALLBACK_BIN_PORT=0 momentarily survives, but the boot-path OverlayInto re-applies defaults over it, so the dynamic mode has no reachable ingestion path. RUN PROOF: the shipped binary booted with `callback: bin_port: 0` logged `callback.binrpc.start.failed err="rpcserver: binrpc listen 127.0.0.1:8129: listen tcp 127.0.0.1:8129: bind: address already in use"` — exactly the finding's failure scenario (nil server, WARN only, CUxD pushes silently lost). The dynamic path in wireBINRPCCallback (daemon_boot.go:367,386-388, Addr() readback) is genuinely unreachable. Consequence is if anything under-stated: the repo's own e2e harness sets BinPort: 0 with the comment '0 is genuinely dynamic there' (tests/e2e/harness/config.go:29-30, daemon.go:193), so every e2e daemon actually contends for 8129; and example.config.full.yaml:572 plus the SPA help i18n.ts:1685 make the same false claim for callback.port ('0 lets the OS pick an ephemeral port'), which CLAUDE.md correctly documents as 8120.

findings.title: A further eleven SPA-editable config leaves are consumed only during boot wiring and carry neither a restart-required badge nor any hot-reload path — changing them in the UI reports success and does nothing until restart
findings.claim: restartRules() (internal/config/restart.go:51-70) is the sole source for both the schema badge (internal/north/rest/handlers/admin_config.go:145) and the PUT's restart_required answer (:690) and the /restart-pending banner (cmd/openccu-loom/restart_pending_provider.go:42). Beyond the OIDC / rate-limit / TLS cases reported separately, these leaves are in a DB-tier section, rendered by the section editor, read only from the boot config, and absent from every rule: (1) locale — SectionLocale; read at cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:259 (parameter-label adapter), :270 (naming builder WithLocale), :750 (system-status subscribers), security_wiring.go:45 and daemon_matter.go:231; note cmd/openccu-loom/reload.go:183-186 explicitly logs locale as restart_required for the YAML path, so the two surfaces disagree. (2) north.rest.enabled — cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest_mount.go:206. (3) north.rest.ws.replay_capacity — cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_infra.go:152. (4) north.rest.openapi_spec_path — cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_north.go:827 (its sibling north.rest.openapi_validate IS badged, restart.go:255). (5) north.rest.tracing.otlp_endpoint — cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_infra.go:211. (6-10) north.matter.{prefer_ipv4, expose_secondary_channels, node_label, dev_rotate_unique_ids, enable_time_sync} plus north.matter.attestation.* and north.matter.case.* — all consumed inside wireMatterRuntime (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_matter.go:3345), called once from cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:648; north.matter.{enabled,listen,vendor_id,product_id,discriminator,mdns_advertise,commissioning.*} ARE badged, so the block is demonstrably boot-only and the unbadged remainder is an omission, not a design choice. (11) ccu_data.{translations_path, easymode_path} — cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_ccudata.go:21 and :53. persistence.values_cache.* and persistence.history.* are in the same position (wired from the boot config in daemon_infra.go / history_wiring.go), though a runtime-adopted central re-reads part of the values-cache path, so I list them as adjacent rather than asserting them. tests/contract/config_restart_required_test.go only checks badge<->diff agreement in both directions and therefore cannot see a field that is in neither list.
findings.failure_scenario: Concrete example (locale): an operator switches the daemon language from en to de in Settings. The save reports restart_required:false and no banner appears. Every north-bound surface fed by the boot-time label adapter — MQTT/HA-Discovery entity names, the Matter node labels, the system-status texts — keeps emitting English until the daemon is restarted, while the SPA itself switches immediately, which makes the daemon look half-translated. Concrete example (north.matter.node_label): the operator renames the bridge, saves, sees no restart hint, and Apple/Google Home keep showing the old name.
findings.verified_by: code trace of each listed read site plus the full restartRules() table; single call sites verified for mountRESTServer (daemon.go:781) and wireMatterRuntime (daemon.go:648)

findings.title: A Security & Safety fault whose source disappears from the classification index can never be cleared — `problem` stays ON and the folded severity stays elevated forever after removing the faulty device.
findings.claim: Faults are cleared on exactly two paths. (1) internal/security/fault.go:45 Faults.Clear(ref, reason) is reached only from applyFault, which is called from onDataPoint (subscribe.go:268) for a source that is present in s.agg.sources, and from RebuildIndex's reconcile pass (index.go:97-102) — and that pass iterates `for key, src := range index` (index.go:79), i.e. only sources the *current* index still contains. (2) Service.DetachCentral (service.go:251) calls Faults.ClearByCentral for a whole central. There is no per-source clear for a source that vanished while its central stayed configured. The store confirms the surface: internal/store/sqlite/security_faults.go exposes Raise/Clear(ref,reason)/ClearByCentral/Acknowledge/OpenByRefReason/ListOpen/PurgeClearedBefore — no clear-by-id. REST offers acknowledge only (internal/north/rest/handlers/security.go:96 AcknowledgeFault), and AcknowledgeFault (fault.go:132-157) explicitly does not clear ('the condition is still there'). Retention (service.go:282-308) calls PurgeClearedBefore, which by name and by the partial open-fault index only removes already-cleared rows. So the row stays in s.agg.faults across restarts (loadFaults -> ListOpen, service.go:311-323) and keeps contributing to snapshot severity and the open-fault count.
findings.failure_scenario: A battery-dead or radio-dead sensor raises an `unreachable`/`low_battery` security fault. The operator does the obvious thing and removes the device from the CCU. RebuildIndex drops its source from the index, so the reconcile pass never looks at it again and no clear event fires. The MQTT `problem` binary sensor stays ON, /api/v1/security keeps listing a fault for a device that no longer exists, the folded severity stays elevated, and the only operator action available (acknowledge) does not remove it. The state survives daemon restarts because loadFaults restores it from SQLite. The plane whose whole job is 'what is broken right now' is permanently wrong.
findings.verified_by: code trace index.go:78-102 (reconcile iterates the new index only), fault.go:45/132, service.go:251/282/311, store surface in internal/store/sqlite/security_faults.go, REST surface in internal/north/rest/handlers/security.go:96
findings.fix_sketch: In RebuildIndex, after the index swap, close every open fault in s.agg.faults whose Source.Ref is no longer a key of the new index (a store Clear by ref+reason, then drop the in-memory entry and publish SecurityFaultChangedEvent{Open:false}). Optionally add an explicit operator 'dismiss fault' REST route for rows whose source is gone.
findings.verify_reasoning: Confirmed, and the aggregate code makes it slightly worse than the finder argued. RebuildIndex's reconcile pass iterates `for key, src := range index` - the NEW index (index.go:78-84) - so a source dropped from the model is never revisited; applyFault is the only Clear caller and needs an *indexedSource (fault.go:44-46). The live path cannot reach it either: subscribe.go dispatches only for sources present in agg.sources. The store offers Raise/Clear(ref,reason)/ClearByCentral/Acknowledge/OpenByRefReason/ListOpen/PurgeClearedBefore and no clear-by-id, and PurgeClearedBefore is `DELETE ... WHERE cleared_at_ms > 0` so it never touches an open row. DetachCentral -> ClearByCentral only covers removing the whole central. loadFaults (service.go:311-323) restores the row from ListOpen on every boot, so it survives restarts. The compensating mechanism I expected to find - the severity fold ignoring orphaned faults - does NOT compensate: aggregate.go:193-198 skips a fault only when `src, ok := a.sources[...]; ok && !src.relevant`, i.e. only for a source that still EXISTS but lost relevance; a source that vanished has ok==false and its severity is still raised. snapshot() appends every fault unconditionally (aggregate.go:238), and the MQTT `problem` binary sensor is literally `onOff(len(snap.Faults) > 0)` (security_reconcile.go:54), so it latches ON forever. Configuration: DEFAULT. Kept at medium: it is a permanently wrong diagnostic plane and a stuck folded severity, not a missed detection.

findings.title: A single failed output write marks every alarm panel — all zones plus the master — unavailable on MQTT, so during the alarm the household loses the Home Assistant disarm control for zones that are working fine.
findings.claim: outputs.Manager.outputFailed (internal/alarm/outputs/manager.go:629) is called for any per-output fire or stop failure and calls noteFailure (manager.go:646), which invokes m.health(false, note). That HealthFunc is the fan-out closure built in internal/alarm/service.go:136-143, which publishes hmevent.AlarmHealthChangedEvent{Healthy:false}. alarm.Service.publish routes it (service.go:589-593) both onto the alarm bus and into onPanelHealthEvent (internal/alarm/panels.go:153-175), which sets `p.Available = e.Healthy` on EVERY entry of r.byZone and republishes each panel. The MQTT publisher's onPanelChanged (internal/north/mqtt/alarm_publisher.go:354) signals a reconcile; reconcile reads the single global `healthy` flag (alarm_publisher.go:425) and publishes it as the availability payload for every zone panel (alarm_publisher.go:456 PublishAlarmAvailability(..., healthy)) and for the master panel (alarm_publisher.go:487). The flag is sticky: resolveFailure (manager.go:662) removes the output from m.failed only on a VERIFIED stop of that same output (watchdog.go:118-125), and reports healthy only once m.failed is empty. There is no per-zone or per-output scoping anywhere in this chain.
findings.failure_scenario: Two zones, each with its own siren; the siren of zone A sits on a CCU whose channel is momentarily unresolvable (reconnecting central, renamed channel). Zone B triggers on a real intrusion — or zone A triggers and only its own siren fails. FireCycle returns an error for that one output, health flips false, and the MQTT plane immediately publishes availability=offline on the alarm_control_panel topics of BOTH zones and the master. In Home Assistant every alarm panel entity renders `unavailable` and its arm/disarm buttons are disabled while the siren is sounding; the household has to fall back to the SPA/REST or the keypad. Recovery needs a verified stop of the failing output, which for a device that stays unresolvable never happens.
findings.verified_by: code trace manager.go:629->646 -> service.go:136-143 -> service.go:589-593 -> panels.go:153-175 -> alarm_publisher.go:354/425/456/487, with manager.go:662 and watchdog.go:118-125 for the sticky-clear condition
findings.fix_sketch: Keep the health signal (S7) but stop mapping it onto entity availability. Either scope the failure to the zone that owns the failing output (Manager already knows inst.row.ZoneID) so only that zone's panel is affected, or leave availability tied to daemon/broker liveness alone and surface the degradation as a separate problem/diagnostic entity, so a failed siren never disables the disarm control.
findings.verify_reasoning: The whole chain holds and there is no per-zone scoping anywhere in it. Any per-output fire or stop failure calls outputFailed -> noteFailure -> m.health(false, note) (manager.go:629-651, reached from the FireCycle error join at manager.go:258-263 and from runStop/verifyStop). That HealthFunc is the single service-wide closure at service.go:136-143 which publishes AlarmHealthChangedEvent; service.go:589-593 routes it into onPanelHealthEvent, which sets p.Available = e.Healthy on EVERY entry of r.byZone plus the master (panels.go:152-175). On the MQTT side the publisher keeps one global p.healthy (alarm_publisher.go:147,377) and reconcile publishes it as the availability payload for every zone panel (alarm_publisher.go:457) and the master (:487). The discovery config declares that topic with availability_mode 'all' (alarm_discovery.go:70-83,134-135) and PublishAlarmAvailability writes the literal 'offline' retained (:689-694), so HA renders every alarm_control_panel unavailable and disables arm/disarm. The compensating recomputation I looked for does not exist: the next reconcile tick re-reads the same global flag, and m.failed is only ever cleared by resolveFailure on a verified stop of that same output (manager.go:662-668, watchdog.go:118-125). Configuration: DEFAULT. One correction to the finder's recovery claim, which is why the rating stays at medium rather than rising: a daemon restart builds a fresh Manager with an empty m.failed and a publisher whose healthy defaults true (alarm_publisher.go:169), so the state is not permanent - it is sticky for the daemon's lifetime.
findings.resolution: a failing output marks only the panels it serves unavailable

findings.title: Renaming a device or channel, or changing its room/function assignment, notifies no push plane: HA device names, HA suggested_area and the Matter NodeLabel stay at their boot values
findings.claim: internal/central/central.go:1054-1072 (RenameDevice), :1089-1117 (RenameDeviceWithChannels) and :1124-1145 (RenameChannel) mutate dev.Name / ch.SetName and call the persistence hook; they publish no event and invoke no re-publish. The REST entry point internal/north/rest/handlers/device_admin.go:104-107 (PatchDevice) and :162-166 (PatchChannel) likewise return 202 without any notification, and internal/central/adapter/device_admin.go:128-158 just forwards. A repo-wide grep for a rename/name-changed hook (OnRename|NameChanged|SetName() callers) finds only the mutators themselves. Three planes read those exact fields: (1) MQTT HA discovery puts the device name into the HA device block -- internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:1392-1401 (desc["name"] = ev.DeviceName) -- and the singular room into suggested_area at :1433-1435; (2) the Matter BridgedDeviceBasicInformation NodeLabel is composed from dev.Name plus ch.Name() in internal/north/matter/endpoint/helpers.go:37-58 and stamped at internal/north/matter/endpoint/materialize.go:200; (3) the WS plane has no rename broadcast (the only device-lifecycle topics are created/removed/availability_changed, internal/north/rest/ws/device_lifecycle.go:50-143). The only paths that re-emit discovery are PublishInitialSnapshot (boot / broker reconnect / MQTT config reload via cmd/openccu-loom/reload_deps.go:74-101), CentralSouthboundReadyEvent and DeviceCreatedEvent (eventbridge.go:311-380); Matter only reassembles on ready + DeviceCreated/DeviceRemoved (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_matter.go:3094, :3120-3121). A rename triggers none of them. By contrast a sysvar rename IS handled (hub_mqtt_publisher.go:765-800 re-wires and re-publishes), which shows the asymmetry is accidental rather than a policy.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator renames 'HmIP-PSM 00021BE9957782' to 'Bucherregal' in the OpenCCU-Loom SPA and assigns it to the room 'Wohnzimmer'. The SPA and REST show the new name immediately. Home Assistant keeps showing the old device name and the old (or missing) area for every entity of that device, and Apple Home keeps the old accessory title, until the daemon is restarted or the MQTT broker connection drops. Users conclude the rename 'did not work' and rename a second time in HA, producing two divergent names for the same device.
findings.verified_by: code trace: central.go:1054-1145, device_admin.go (handlers):83-131 and (adapter):128-158, mqtt/discovery.go:1392-1401 + :1433-1435, matter/endpoint/helpers.go:37-58 + materialize.go:200, eventbridge.go:311-380 + :544-606, daemon_matter.go:3089-3123, reload_deps.go:74-101; repo-wide grep for any rename hook returned none
findings.fix_sketch: Publish a device-metadata-changed event from Unit.RenameDevice / RenameChannel / SetRooms / SetFunctions, and subscribe it in the EventBridge (call publishDeviceSnapshot for that device, which is already idempotent) and in the Matter reassemble trigger; add a WS device.renamed broadcast for the SPA. A cheaper interim fix is to have DeviceAdminDomain call the existing per-device snapshot + matter reassemble seams directly.
findings.verify_reasoning: Traced from the mutators outward. Unit.RenameDevice (central.go:1054-1071), RenameDeviceWithChannels (:1083-1116) and RenameChannel (:1119-1144) mutate dev.Name / ch.SetName and call renameDeviceFn; no publish, no hook. DeviceAdminDomain.RenameDevice/RenameChannel (adapter/device_admin.go:126-155) only forwards. SetRooms/SetFunctions/SetChannelRooms (adapter/device_admin.go:373-460) write to the CCU and stamp the model; again no publish. The three consumers read exactly those fields and are only re-materialised on triggers a rename does not fire: MQTT HA discovery composes device.name / suggested_area inside buildPublishEvent-driven publishes whose only re-run triggers are PublishInitialSnapshot (boot, southbound-ready, broker reconnect, MQTT reload) and DeviceCreated; Matter stamps NodeLabel at materialise time (endpoint/materialize.go:200 from ep.FriendlyName, endpoint/helpers.go:37-70 friendlyName(dev.Name, ch.Name())) and Bridge.Reassemble has exactly four production call sites (daemon_matter.go:3385 boot, matter_maintenance.go:35 force-sync, matter_exposures.go:228 exposure change, plus device create/remove hooks) - none of them a rename; the WS DeviceLifecycleSubscriber broadcasts only created / removed / availability_changed (ws/device_lifecycle.go:107-150). I also checked the one plausible second path the finder did not name: the 5-minute devicedetails.refresh job (hub_wiring.go:360-385) only re-fills the DeviceDetails cache - GetName/GetDeviceRooms are read by device_pipeline.go:491-526 at ingest only - so not even a CCU-WebUI-side rename reaches MQTT/Matter. Consequence as described holds; medium is right because the data is cosmetic (names/areas), not control state, and a broker reconnect or restart heals it.

findings.title: Opening a Matter commissioning window (and /matter/share) writes no audit entry, while the handler comment claims a middleware records it and audit.ActionMatterShare has no emitter
findings.claim: internal/north/rest/router.go:1218 mounts POST /matter/commissioning/window as handlers.MatterCommissioningWindow(d.MatterCommissioningOpener, d.MatterEventPublisher) and :1220 mounts POST /matter/share as handlers.MatterShare(d.MatterCommissioningOpener, d.MatterEventPublisher) -- neither receives an audit.Recorder. Every neighbouring mutating Matter route does: force-sync (:1205, d.AuditRecorder), factory-reset (:1206-1207), fabric revoke (:1208), exposable PUT/bulk (:1216-1217) and, notably, the window CLOSE (:1219, d.MatterAuditRecorder -> audit.ActionMatterCommissioning 'window closed'). The handler body (internal/north/rest/handlers/matter.go:142-215) contains no rec.Record call, and MatterShare (internal/north/rest/handlers/matter_exposures.go:437-441) is a straight alias of it. The doc comment at internal/north/rest/handlers/matter.go:137-140 states 'Audit recording for the open is wired through the [MatterCommissioningWindowAudit] middleware in the daemon' -- a repo-wide grep for MatterCommissioningWindowAudit returns exactly that one comment line and nothing else: the identifier does not exist in any package. Independently, audit.ActionMatterShare (internal/audit/audit.go:177) is the single audit Action constant with no production emitter (verified by enumerating every Action* constant and grepping its uses outside internal/audit and _test.go files).
findings.failure_scenario: An admin-token holder (or anyone who obtained an admin session) POSTs /api/v1/matter/share. A commissioning window opens and a third party commissions the bridge onto their own fabric, gaining control of every exposed CCU device. Afterwards the operator opens the change log to find out who opened the window: there is a 'matter_commissioning: window closed' row and rows for every fabric revoke, but no row at all for the open. The audit trail actively misleads -- it shows the harmless half of the operation and hides the privileged half.
findings.verified_by: code trace: router.go:1204-1220 (recorder present on 6 sibling routes, absent on 2), handlers/matter.go:137-215, handlers/matter_exposures.go:404-441, audit/audit.go:162-177; grep for MatterCommissioningWindowAudit (1 hit, the comment itself) and an enumeration of all audit Action constants against their production call sites (ActionMatterShare = 0 non-test uses)
findings.fix_sketch: Pass d.MatterAuditRecorder into MatterCommissioningWindow and MatterShare, record audit.ActionMatterCommissioning ('window opened', duration) and audit.ActionMatterShare respectively (never the passcode), and delete the refuted middleware comment. Add a contract test asserting every audit.Action constant has a production emitter -- it caught this one in a single pass.
findings.verify_reasoning: All three sub-claims verified. (1) router.go:1218 mounts POST /matter/commissioning/window with (opener, publisher) only, and :1220 mounts /matter/share the same way, while force-sync (:1204-1205), factory-reset (:1206-1207), fabric revoke (:1208), exposable PUT (:1216), exposable bulk (:1217) and the window CLOSE (:1219) all receive an audit.Recorder. (2) handlers/matter.go:142-204 contains no Record call; MatterShare (matter_exposures.go:438-441) is a literal `return MatterCommissioningWindow(opener, publisher)`. The close does record (matter_exposures.go:432, audit.ActionMatterCommissioning 'window closed'). (3) A repo-wide grep for MatterCommissioningWindowAudit returns exactly one hit - the doc comment at handlers/matter.go:139 that claims it exists. (4) audit.ActionMatterShare (audit/audit.go:177) has exactly one use in the tree and it is in matter_exposures_test.go:850, i.e. no production emitter. I also hunted for a second audit path: there is no audit middleware in internal/north/rest/middleware (only openapi.go), the opener adapter cmd/openccu-loom/matter_window_adapter.go contains no audit reference, and no WS or MCP surface exposes commissioning at all (grep for 'commissioning' under internal/north/rest/ws and internal/north/mcp: no hits). Severity re-rated from high to medium: the defect is a forensic/audit-completeness gap, not an access-control weakness - both routes remain admin-gated, and an open window is still visible live via GET /matter/status and the matter.commissioning_window_opened WS broadcast. The finder's failure narrative implies a privilege risk that the code does not add; what is real is that the ledger records the close and hides the open.

findings.title: The 0.61.3 "only count interfaces that actually loaded devices" fix skips CUxD, so a CUxD interface whose ingest exhausts every retry is still reported as loaded
findings.claim: 0.61.3 changed `bringUpCentral` to count only interfaces whose ingest succeeded: `wireInterface` now returns `(closer, ingested, err)` and the caller does `if !ingested { continue }` before `loaded++` (internal/central/adapter/ccu_wiring.go:445-464). For the XML-RPC path `ingested` is the real outcome, produced by the new `runXMLRPCActivation` (ccu_wiring.go:1310-1348), which returns false on retry exhaustion or ctx-cancel. The CUxD branch of the same function returns `closer, err == nil, err` (ccu_wiring.go:649) - i.e. `ingested` is the *wiring* outcome, never the ingest outcome. Its sibling driver `runCUxDActivation` (internal/central/adapter/cuxd_wiring.go:368-406) has no return value at all: on exhaustion it logs `wire.interface.ingest_failed`, calls `ensureDisconnectedClientState` and returns void, and the call site (cuxd_wiring.go:277) discards nothing because there is nothing to discard. So the exact condition the fix exists to expose - "wired but carries zero devices" - is invisible for CUxD. The tally reaches the user: `recordCentralReadiness(unit, ReadinessReady, loaded, len(cc.Interfaces))` (ccu_wiring.go:272) -> `Unit.SetReadiness` (internal/central/central.go:544) -> `interfaces_loaded` on GET /system/ccu (internal/north/rest/handlers/system_ccu.go:99), on the `central.readiness.changed` WS push (internal/north/rest/ws/payloads.go:214/230) and in the SPA badge (assets/ui/src/lib/components/ui/CentralStatusBadge.svelte:37).
findings.failure_scenario: A CCU with HmIP-RF + CUxD boots while the CUxD add-on is still starting (or is broken). The XML-RPC interface ingests; CUxD burns its 5 retries and serves zero devices. The daemon logs `wire.interface.ingest_failed` for CUxD, but /system/ccu, the WS readiness push and the SPA badge all report `ready, 2/2 interfaces loaded` - exactly the "latch ready, N/N over a partly-dark central" the 0.61.3 comment says must not happen. An operator sees a fully green central while every CUxD device is missing.
findings.verified_by: code trace: ccu_wiring.go:643-651 (CUxD branch returns err==nil as `ingested`), cuxd_wiring.go:277 + 363-406 (runCUxDActivation returns void), ccu_wiring.go:445-464 (tally), central.go:544 + system_ccu.go:99 + payloads.go:214 (consumers)
findings.fix_sketch: Give `runCUxDActivation` the same `bool` return as `runXMLRPCActivation` (true on success, false on exhaustion/cancel) and return it from the CUxD branch of `wireInterface` instead of `err == nil`. The two drivers are now near-identical; folding them into one helper would prevent the next divergence.
findings.verify_reasoning: The mechanism is exactly as described and is admitted in the code's own comment. wireInterface's CUxD branch returns `closer, err == nil, err` (internal/central/adapter/ccu_wiring.go:644-650); wireCUxDInterface ends in `return closer, nil` (cuxd_wiring.go:312) after runCUxDActivation, which has no return value and on retry exhaustion only logs wire.interface.ingest_failed and walks the client to DISCONNECTED (cuxd_wiring.go:363-406). Its XML-RPC sibling returns false in the same two cases (ccu_wiring.go:1308-1347). So a CUxD interface serving zero devices still increments `loaded` (ccu_wiring.go:445-462) and is reported as loaded by recordCentralReadiness(ReadinessReady, loaded, len(cc.Interfaces)) at ccu_wiring.go:272. The consequence is overstated in two places. First, the outage is not invisible: ensureDisconnectedClientState leaves the CUxD client not-CONNECTED, so ClientCoordinator.Available() is false and EvaluateCentralState demotes the central to DEGRADED (coordinators/client.go:208-238, central.go:1290-1300) — an operator does not see a 'fully green central', they see a degraded one with a wrong interface count, next to an Error-level ingest_failed log line. Second, the SPA badge does not render the tally in the ready state at all: CentralStatusBadge shows loaded/total only in the loading_devices phase (assets/ui/src/lib/components/ui/CentralStatusBadge.svelte:17-42), and Overview/DeviceList render it only for not-ready centrals. The real defect is therefore a wrong `interfaces_loaded` number on GET /system/ccu and the central.readiness.changed WS push — a reporting inconsistency the 0.61.3 fix was meant to close, not a hidden outage.

findings.title: The custom-DP invoke route gained a 423 Locked response that assets/openapi.yaml never declares, so every generated client type says the status cannot occur
findings.claim: internal/north/rest/handlers/custom_data_points.go:401-408 now answers `writeChannelLocked(w, r)` (HTTP 423) when `InvokeCustomDP` returns `device.ErrChannelOperationLocked`. assets/openapi.yaml:3196-3225 (`operationId: invokeCustomDataPoint`) still declares only 204/400/404/422/502/503. The spec already has a reusable `#/components/responses/Locked` component and its sibling write routes use it — the four operations declaring 423 today are PUT /devices/{addr}/channels/{no}/data-points/{param}/value, PUT /devices/{addr}/paramsets/{key}, PUT /devices/{addr}/link-ps/{peer} and POST /sessions/edit — so this is an omission, not a deliberate exclusion. assets/ui/src/lib/api/types.generated.ts is generated from this file (assets/ui/package.json `gen:types`) and therefore carries the same gap. Nothing catches it: tests/contract/openapi_test.go only checks that paths exist, and internal/north/rest/middleware/openapi.go validates requests only (`openapi3filter.ValidateRequest`, openapi.go:186), never responses, so the daemon is not blocked at runtime.
findings.failure_scenario: A generated or spec-driven client (openapi-typescript SPA types, a generated Go/Python client, or an operator reading the published spec) treats 423 from POST /devices/{addr}/cdps/{name}/{operation} as an undocumented/unknown status. A strict client that switches exhaustively over the declared statuses falls into its default branch and reports 'unexpected server error' for what is a normal, recoverable 'lift the channel lock' condition — the fix's whole point was to stop that call being reported as an upstream failure.
findings.verified_by: code trace: custom_data_points.go:401-408 + devices.go:852-856; parsed assets/openapi.yaml with PyYAML and enumerated every operation declaring 423 (four, none of them invokeCustomDataPoint) and confirmed `components.responses.Locked` exists; middleware/openapi.go:186 shows request-only validation.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `"423": { $ref: "#/components/responses/Locked" }` to the invokeCustomDataPoint responses, regenerate types.generated.ts (`make ui-types`) and regenerate the schema digest (`make export-schemas`).

findings.title: TextDisplay's fallback icon and sound vocabularies are invented: 8 of 12 icon labels and all 7 sound labels exist on no CCU, and the doc comments name a source that contradicts the device data
findings.claim: defaultIcons (textdisplay.go:73-86) says it is "Sourced from the DISPLAY_DATA_ICON VALUE_LIST present on all HmIP-SDV* channel 1 MASTER paramsets". Ground truth: the only device carrying DISPLAY_DATA_ICON is HmIP-WRCD, on channel type ACOUSTIC_DISPLAY_RECEIVER in the VALUES (not MASTER) paramset, with a 32-entry list [NO_ICON, LAMP_OFF, LAMP_ON, PADLOCK_OPEN, PADLOCK_CLOSED, ERROR, EVERYTHING_OKAY, INFORMATION, NEW_MESSAGE, SERVICE_MESSAGE, SUN, MOON, WIND, CLOUD, THUNDERSTORM, DRIZZLE, CLOUD_AND_MOOON, RAIN, SNOW, CLOUD_AND_SUN, CLOUD_SUN_AND_RAIN, SNOWFLAKE, RAINDROP, FLAME, WINDOW_OPEN, SHUTTERS, ECO, PROTECTION_DEACTIVATED, EXTERNAL_PROTECTION, INTERNAL_PROTECTION, BELL, CLOCK]. Only ERROR, INFORMATION, NEW_MESSAGE and SERVICE_MESSAGE of the 12 hard-coded labels are real; OFF, ON, OPEN, CLOSED, OK, SIGNAL_NEW_MESSAGE, SIGNAL_SERVICE_MESSAGE and SIGNAL_NEW_INFORMATION appear in no VALUE_LIST in the 399-device fleet and nowhere in openccu-data's OCCU string table. defaultSounds (textdisplay.go:91-99) says it is "Sourced from the ACOUSTIC_NOTIFICATION_SELECTION VALUE_LIST on HmIP-SDV* devices"; the real HmIP-WRCD list is [LOW_BATTERY, DISARMED, INTERNALLY_ARMED, EXTERNALLY_ARMED, DELAYED_INTERNALLY_ARMED, DELAYED_EXTERNALLY_ARMED, EVENT, ERROR] -- zero overlap with the seven hard-coded values (SOUND_OFF, LONG_LONG, LONG_SHORT, LONG_SHORT_SHORT, SHORT, SHORT_SHORT, LONG), which look like a de-prefixed rendering of the CCU's unrelated sound_* string-table keys (openccu-data parameters_en carries sound_long_short_short, sound_no_sound, ...). Impact is bounded because init.go:66-71 overwrites both lists from the runtime paramset whenever the channel exposes the DP, and the write-side validators are gated on iconsFromDevice / soundsFromDevice (textdisplay.go:382, 395), so the bogus labels never block a real write. What does leak is the state payload: on any channel where the DP is absent or its VALUE_LIST is empty, StatePayload advertises available_icons / available_sounds built from these invented labels, and a north-bound client that builds its picker from them will send values the CCU rejects.
findings.failure_scenario: A north-bound client (HA, an external REST consumer, an MCP tool) reads available_sounds from a text-display data point whose channel did not deliver a VALUE_LIST and offers 'LONG_SHORT_SHORT'. Writing it to ACOUSTIC_NOTIFICATION_SELECTION fails on the CCU with an invalid-value fault. The immediate risk is small; the durable cost is that both doc comments assert a provenance the device data refutes, so the next reader trusts the list.
findings.verified_by: code trace (textdisplay.go:70-99, 218-219, 228-244, 382, 395; textdisplay/init.go:37-42, 66-71) + ground-truth VALUE_LISTs at $S/repro/B1/valuelists_by_channel.json (ACOUSTIC_DISPLAY_RECEIVER / VALUES:DISPLAY_DATA_ICON and VALUES:ACOUSTIC_NOTIFICATION_SELECTION) + absence of the invented labels from $S/repro/B1/valuelists.txt and from openccu-data's translation_extract.json.gz
findings.fix_sketch: Replace both fallback lists with the real HmIP-WRCD vocabularies (or drop them entirely and let AvailableIcons/AvailableSounds return nil until the runtime paramset arrives, which is the honest state), and correct the doc comments to name ACOUSTIC_DISPLAY_RECEIVER / VALUES rather than 'HmIP-SDV* channel 1 MASTER'.

findings.title: Climate.SetProfile omits the AUTO-mode switch before writing ACTIVE_PROFILE on HmIP thermostats, so selecting a week program while in MANU has no effect
findings.claim: For a week-program profile the KindIP branch writes ACTIVE_PROFILE alone (climate.go:1059-1065). The reference first brings the device into AUTO when it is not already there: `if self.mode != ClimateMode.AUTO: await self.set_mode(mode=ClimateMode.AUTO, collector=collector); await self._dp_boost_mode.send_value(value=False, collector=collector)` and only then writes _dp_active_profile (climate.py:858-863). A week program is only executed in AUTO, so without the switch the write is stored but ineffective. The asymmetry is visible inside the same function: the KindRF branch of the very same switch does send AUTO_MODE=true + BOOST_MODE=false before the pointer write (climate.go:1076-1082). Reachability is limited because Profiles() only advertises week-program slots while Mode() == AUTO (climate.go:528-550), so the SPA and the HA preset list do not offer them in MANU; a REST/WS/MCP client that names the profile directly is not gated.
findings.failure_scenario: HmIP-eTRV-2 in MANU (heat) mode. A REST/WS/MCP client sends set_profile {"profile":"week_program_2"}. openccu-loom writes ACTIVE_PROFILE=2, records profile=week_program_2 locally (climate.go:1097) and reports success, but the thermostat stays in MANU and keeps its fixed setpoint — the week program never runs. aiohomematic would switch the device to AUTO, clear boost and then select the profile.
findings.verified_by: code trace climate.go:1036-1099 (KindIP vs KindRF branches) and 492-552; reference climate.py:849-863
findings.fix_sketch: In the KindIP week-program branch, when Mode() != ModeAuto first run setIPMode(ModeAuto) and clear BOOST_MODE, then write ACTIVE_PROFILE — mirroring climate.py:858-863 and the existing KindRF branch.
