findings.title: HSToFixedColor's hue banding is off by one segment at every 30°/90°/150°/210°/270°/330° boundary against hs_color_to_fixed_converter
findings.claim: The reference bands hue with a half-open-low / closed-high rule: `30 < hue <= 90 -> YELLOW`, `90 < hue <= 150 -> GREEN`, `150 < hue <= 210 -> TURQUOISE`, `210 < hue <= 270 -> BLUE`, `270 < hue <= 330 -> PURPLE`, everything else RED (light.py:814-834). The Go port uses closed-low / half-open-high: `h < 30 || h >= 330 -> RED`, `h < 90 -> YELLOW`, `h < 150 -> GREEN`, `h < 210 -> CYAN`, `h < 270 -> BLUE`, else MAGENTA (color.go:604-623). The two agree everywhere except at the six exact boundary values, where Go lands one segment clockwise: hue 30 -> YELLOW (reference RED), 90 -> GREEN (YELLOW), 150 -> CYAN/TURQUOISE (GREEN), 210 -> BLUE (TURQUOISE), 270 -> MAGENTA/PURPLE (BLUE), 330 -> RED (PURPLE). The mapping reaches the wire: custom_dp_dispatcher.go:416 and payload.go:481 both feed HSToFixedColor's result into FixedColorLight.SetColor, which writes the resulting label to COLOR (color.go:490-509). Not listed in notes/parity/by_design.md.
findings.failure_scenario: HmIP-BSL signal light. A client sends set_color with hue=330, saturation=100 (a magenta a colour wheel snaps to easily). openccu-loom writes COLOR="RED"; aiohomematic writes COLOR="PURPLE". The LED lights up in the wrong colour.
findings.verified_by: code trace color.go:594-623 vs light.py:814-834; call sites custom_dp_dispatcher.go:410-418 and payload.go:470-482
findings.fix_sketch: Change the comparisons to the reference's exclusive-low/inclusive-high form (h > 30 && h <= 90 -> YELLOW, …, default RED) so the six boundary hues map identically.

findings.title: The hand-authored aiohomematic reference snapshot for TextDisplay/WriteRows asserts a DISPLAY_DATA_SCROLLING parameter that exists neither in aiohomematic nor on any CCU device, validating a Go path that would be wrong on real hardware
findings.claim: The reference layer under tests/contract/wire_snapshots/aiohomematic_reference/ is documented as 'ground-truth records produced directly from the aiohomematic Python library' and 'the authoritative comparator' (README.md:48-53), but _gen_text_display_write_rows (script/aiohomematic_wire_snapshots.py:530-566) hand-writes the expected dict and its docstring claims 'aiohomematic text_display.py: send_text builds a paramset per row with DISPLAY_DATA_STRING, DISPLAY_DATA_ALIGNMENT, DISPLAY_DATA_SCROLLING, DISPLAY_DATA_ICON'. That claim is false: `grep -rn SCROLL` over the whole aiohomematic package returns nothing, the CustomDpTextDisplay field set is ALIGNMENT/BACKGROUND_COLOR/COMMIT/ICON/ID/STRING/TEXT_COLOR (text_display.py:69-77, profile.py:744-750), and send_text writes exactly those plus DISPLAY_DATA_ID and COMMIT to one channel (text_display.py:253-269). The device data agrees: HmIP-WRCD — the only text-display model — exposes DISPLAY_DATA_{ALIGNMENT,BACKGROUND_COLOR,COMMIT,ICON,ID,STRING,TEXT_COLOR} on channel :3 and nothing display-related on :1/:2, which are KEY_TRANSCEIVER channels carrying only PRESS_*. The Go code the snapshot blesses is wrong on two further counts: TextDisplay.WriteRows sends each row to rowAddress(id) — a different *channel* per row (textdisplay.go:643-654), so rows 1 and 2 of an HmIP-WRCD would be addressed to the two key channels — and it omits DISPLAY_DATA_ID, the parameter that actually selects the row (textdisplay.go:618-624). The single-row TextDisplay.Write is correct (textdisplay.go:531-560: DISPLAY_DATA_ID + fields + COMMIT on t.Address) and is the only path production uses; WriteRows has no production caller, which is why this is scored low rather than high. A second, smaller instance of the same fabrication: _gen_climate_rf_set_mode (script/aiohomematic_wire_snapshots.py:926-947) justifies SET_TEMPERATURE=5 for the OFF case with 'the ClimateRF fixture uses a different min_temp=5.0', but the reference hard-codes _OFF_TEMPERATURE = 4.5 there (climate.py:63, :599) and never derives it from min_temp.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer reads a green `make wire-compare` as evidence that TextDisplay/WriteRows matches aiohomematic. If WriteRows is ever wired to a north-bound surface, an HmIP-WRCD multi-row write addresses two key channels and carries a non-existent parameter, so every row fails; the guard that exists to catch precisely that will still be green.
findings.verified_by: script/aiohomematic_wire_snapshots.py:530-566 and :926-947 vs aiohomematic text_display.py:69-77 + :253-269, profile.py:739-750 and climate.py:63/:584-599; `grep -rn SCROLL --include=*.py ../aiohomematic/aiohomematic/` returns no match; device layout from ../godevccu/internal/embed/data/{device,paramset}_descriptions/HmIP-WRCD.json
findings.fix_sketch: Drive the reference generator from the real aiohomematic classes (instantiate the Custom DP against the mock client and call the setter) instead of hand-writing the expected dicts, or at minimum regenerate these two entries from the source; then fix WriteRows to write DISPLAY_DATA_ID on the display channel and drop DISPLAY_DATA_SCROLLING.
findings.resolution: WriteRows delegates per row to Write, so defaults, validation and a per-row COMMIT apply; the reference generator fixture address and its divergence claim corrected
findings.status_verified_at: dea785a1 (pre-#606 HEAD); the open two re-checked on 4eecb1e6

findings.title: GET /devices/{addr} leaks an undocumented AvailabilityInfo.RSSIPeer field into the availability object because the embedded Go struct has no json tags at all
findings.claim: device.AvailabilityInfo (internal/model/device/availability.go:18-45) has five documented fields (IsReachable, LastUpdated, BatteryLevel, LowBattery, SignalStrength) plus a sixth, RSSIPeer *int (line 44), and NONE of the six fields carry a `json:` tag -- confirmed by reading the whole struct body and grepping for a custom MarshalJSON (none exists). With no tag, encoding/json falls back to the literal Go field name as the JSON key, which is why the spec's PascalCase-looking keys (IsReachable, BatteryLevel, ...) already match: the spec was written to match Go's default output, not the other way around. handlers/devices.go:151 embeds this struct verbatim as `Availability device.AvailabilityInfo \`json:"availability"\`` inside DeviceDetail (handlers/devices.go:148-153), the response type of `GET /api/v1/devices/{addr}`. assets/openapi.yaml's DeviceDetail schema (line 8808: `allOf: [DeviceSummary, {required:[firmware,availability,channels], properties:{firmware:{...}, availability:{properties:{IsReachable,LastUpdated,BatteryLevel,LowBattery,SignalStrength}} ...}}]`, availability properties enumerated at lines 8821-8828) declares only those five availability fields -- RSSIPeer is absent from the schema entirely. grep across internal/ and pkg/ confirms device.AvailabilityInfo is embedded in exactly one place (handlers/devices.go:151), so this is not a false positive from a differently-shaped consumer.
findings.failure_scenario: Any call to GET /api/v1/devices/{addr} for a device the CCU reports RSSI_PEER for returns `"availability": {..., "RSSIPeer": -63}` (or `"RSSIPeer": null` when absent) -- a field no client can discover from the OpenAPI contract or from the generated TypeScript type (assets/ui/src/lib/api/types.generated.ts has no RSSIPeer under DeviceDetail's availability, confirmed by inspecting the generated schema.json content for that path). The SPA's own maintenance grid (assets/ui/src/lib/components/device/MaintenanceStatusGrid.svelte:137-142) already shows a peer-RSSI reading, but sources it from a completely separate call (api.listDataPoints(address, 0) reading the raw RSSI_PEER data point), confirming the availability.RSSIPeer copy is genuinely never consumed anywhere -- it is undocumented, untyped dead weight riding along on every device-detail response, and the next engineer who adds a field to AvailabilityInfo for an unrelated reason will silently repeat this pattern since nothing enforces json tags here.
findings.verified_by: code trace: internal/model/device/availability.go:18-45 (struct + field list, no json tags, no MarshalJSON), internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:148-153 (embedding + json:"availability" tag), assets/openapi.yaml:8808-8829 (DeviceDetail.availability schema, 5 declared properties), assets/ui/src/lib/components/device/MaintenanceStatusGrid.svelte:137-142 (SPA sources RSSI_PEER from a different endpoint, proving the leaked field is unused). A live go-run reproducer marshaling the struct was attempted at $S/repro/D1/rssi_repro/main.go but fails to compile from outside the module tree (`use of internal package ... not allowed`) -- writing a _test.go inside the repo to work around this would violate the read-only rule, so this rests on encoding/json's well-established, unambiguous no-tag-uses-field-name behavior, corroborated by the fact that the sibling fields in the same untagged struct (IsReachable, BatteryLevel, ...) are already known-correct in the shipped spec, which only holds if that exact mechanism is in effect.
findings.fix_sketch: Add explicit json tags to device.AvailabilityInfo mirroring the already-documented casing (`json:"IsReachable"` etc.), and either add `json:"RSSIPeer,omitempty"` plus a matching `rssi_peer`/`RSSIPeer` property in the DeviceDetail.availability spec schema, or add `json:"-"` to drop it from the REST payload since the SPA already sources RSSI_PEER through the data-points endpoint.

findings.title: Security & Safety fault-raised notifications render as raw, untranslated i18n keys for six of nine hazard classes
findings.claim: internal/security/render.go:149-155 builds the notification Subject/Message catalogue keys as `security.subject.<class>.<verb>` / `security.message.<class>.<verb>` via plain string concatenation of the SecurityClass and SecurityVerb enum values. internal/security/fault.go:119-127 (applyFault, the raise-edge path) calls s.notify(reportInput{Class: f.Class, Verb: hmenum.SecurityVerbRaised, Fault: true, ...}) for ANY indexed source that develops a non-empty fault reason (internal/security/index.go:252-282 sets src.reason independently of src.class - hazard classes carry a fault reason exactly like diagnostic ones, e.g. index.go:259 'a tamper-typed enrollment... needs a reason', and index.go:253/262/267/281 set reason for every classification branch including the default hazard branch). f.Class at this call site is therefore not restricted to the three diagnostic classes (tamper/battery/technical) - it is any of the 9 hmenum.SecurityClass values, including the six hazard classes (smoke, water, gas, co, intrusion, panic), which are battery-powered/radio sensors that routinely go 'unreachable' or 'low_battery' (hmenum.SecurityFaultReasonUnreachable / SecurityFaultReasonLowBattery) in real deployments. internal/i18n/catalogs/en.json and de.json define security.subject.<class>.raised / security.message.<class>.raised ONLY for battery (line 172/199), tamper (line 190/217) and technical (line 193/220) - confirmed absent for smoke/water/gas/co/intrusion/panic in BOTH locales (grep of both files returns no match for e.g. "security.message.smoke.raised"). internal/i18n/i18n.go:57-73 Catalogs.T falls back through requested-locale -> DefaultLocale -> the raw key itself when nothing matches, with no softer degradation (unlike the two SPA-side cases below). The resulting Subject/Message strings (literally the dotted keys, e.g. "security.subject.smoke.raised" / "security.message.smoke.raised") are then published verbatim: internal/north/mqtt/security_publisher.go:289-299 marshals them into the MQTT `security/fault` state topic; internal/north/webhook/outbound.go:293-301 forwards them as Subject/Message in the webhook alarmPayload; internal/north/rest/ws/security_events.go:277-293 broadcasts them over WS; and assets/ui/src/routes/security/SecurityOverview.svelte:165-166 renders {n.subject}/{n.message} directly with no client-side re-resolution.
findings.failure_scenario: A smoke, water, gas, CO, intrusion, or panic sensor's battery runs low (or the sensor goes radio-unreachable, or reports a device error/duty-cycle/central-lost condition) - a routine, expected, recurring event for any battery-powered fleet, not an edge case. The daemon opens a fault and calls notify() with Verb=Raised. Every consumer (MQTT topic for Home Assistant, the webhook, the WS broadcast, and the SPA's Security Overview 'last fault' card) receives the literal strings "security.subject.smoke.raised" and "security.message.smoke.raised" (or the water/gas/co/intrusion/panic equivalents) as the human-readable Subject/Message, in both English and German, instead of a sentence like "Low battery - Kitchen smoke detector" / "Kitchen smoke detector reports a low battery since 14:32."
findings.verified_by: code trace: internal/security/render.go:149-155 (key construction) -> internal/security/fault.go:119-127 (Raised call site, f.Class unrestricted) -> internal/security/index.go:252-282 (src.reason set for hazard classes too) -> internal/i18n/catalogs/en.json + de.json (grep confirms security.subject/message.{smoke,water,gas,co,intrusion,panic}.raised absent while .battery/.tamper/.technical.raised are present) -> internal/i18n/i18n.go:57-73 (raw-key fallback, no graceful degradation) -> internal/north/mqtt/security_publisher.go:289-299, internal/north/webhook/outbound.go:293-301, internal/north/rest/ws/security_events.go:277-293, assets/ui/src/routes/security/SecurityOverview.svelte:165-166 (Subject/Message forwarded/rendered verbatim on every surface).
findings.fix_sketch: Add the 12 missing key pairs (security.subject.<class>.raised and security.message.<class>.raised for smoke, water, gas, co, intrusion, panic) to both internal/i18n/catalogs/en.json and de.json, mirroring the existing battery/tamper/technical wording pattern ({sensor}/{reason}/{time} placeholders already populated by renderer.args()). Add a table test in internal/security enumerating hmenum.SecurityClasses() x SecurityVerbRaised (and ideally the full reachable (class,verb) set) against Catalogs.T so a future class addition fails the same way i18n.enum-labels.test.ts already protects the SPA-side vocabularies.
findings.verify_reasoning: The catalogue gap is real but it is by design, and the stated failure scenario is refuted by measurement. The verb is chosen by class, not by the device: subscribe.go:225-268 dispatches `if src.class.Hazard() { verb = Triggered|Cleared } else { applyFault → Raised|Cleared }`, and the catalogues mirror that split exactly — hazard classes carry .triggered/.cleared/.test, diagnostic classes carry .raised/.cleared/.test. My reproducer shows the mirror image is equally 'missing' (security.subject.tamper.triggered, battery.triggered, technical.triggered are all raw keys), which is what a deliberate split looks like, not an oversight. The scenario 'a smoke/water/gas/CO sensor's battery runs low → security.subject.smoke.raised' is false: safety.Classify keys on the PARAMETER, and LOW_BAT/LOWBAT → battery, UNREACH → technical on every channel type including SMOKE_DETECTOR and WATER_DETECTION_TRANSMITTER (measured), while every hazard entry in byChannelAndParameter carries Reason="" so applyFault returns at fault.go:39-41 before notifying. Enrollment cannot produce it either: SecurityClassForSensorType maps only to intrusion/panic/tamper and enrolled hazard params still have no reason; and index.go:190 keys the enrollment by (channel, PARAMETER), so a smoke detector's LOW_BAT never inherits the enrolled channel's class. Real residual, narrow: a source override (PUT security source, class not validated against the parameter — security.go:335) or a hand-crafted PUT /alarm/zones/{id}/sensors row (alarm_config.go:216-262 validates the sensor type but not that the (channel,parameter) is an offered candidate) can pair a hazard class with a fault reason; the live-event path then still lands on Triggered, but the index-rebuild reconciliation loop (index.go:79-101) calls applyFault regardless of Hazard(), producing the raw `security.subject.<hazard>.raised`. Misconfiguration-conditional, hence low. Worth fixing as a guard (table test over the reachable (class,verb) set) rather than by adding 12 strings.

findings.title: The Matter session-miss burst tracker allocates a permanent entry per session-id from unauthenticated datagrams and never reclaims any of them
findings.claim: `sessionMissBurst.record` inserts `t.entries[sessionID] = &sessionMissEntry{...}` on first sight of a session id (internal/north/matter/bridge/session_miss_burst.go:66-69) and afterwards only ever mutates the entry in place (:74-90). There is no `delete`, no sweep and no cap anywhere in the file or in its only caller. That caller sits on the pre-decrypt receive path: `decryptIfNeeded` looks up the session, and on a miss — i.e. for a datagram that has not been and cannot be authenticated — calls `b.sessionMissTracker.record(hdr.SessionID, time.Now())` (internal/north/matter/bridge/receive.go:288-303). `hdr.SessionID` is a `uint16` taken straight off the wire, so any host on the LAN that can reach the Matter UDP port (default 5540, internal/north/matter/transport/udp/listener.go) can populate all 65536 slots with 65536 one-line datagrams. The sibling table on the same path was given an explicit cap for exactly this reason — `unsecuredWindowCount` bounds `unsecuredWindows` at `maxUnsecuredWindows` (internal/north/matter/bridge/receive.go:246-251, bridge.go:345-355) because 'without a cap a spoofed-source flood grows unsecuredWindows without bound' (securechannel.go:485) — and `unsecuredWindows` is additionally cleared on teardown (securechannel.go:677-678); `sessionMissTracker` has neither.
findings.failure_scenario: A LAN host (or a misbehaving controller) sprays datagrams with varying session ids at the bridge's UDP port. The map fills to its 65536-entry ceiling — roughly 4-6 MB of live heap on a Raspberry Pi — and stays there for the daemon's whole lifetime, because nothing evicts entries and the map is not even cleared by `Bridge.Stop`. The growth is bounded, so it will not OOM a healthy install on its own; it is a permanent, remotely-triggerable heap floor that is invisible to every operator surface.
findings.verified_by: code trace: allocation site session_miss_burst.go:66-69; no delete/sweep/cap in the file; unauthenticated caller at receive.go:288-303 with a uint16 wire-supplied key; contrasted with the explicitly capped and cleared sibling map at receive.go:246-251 / securechannel.go:677-678.
findings.fix_sketch: Sweep entries whose `firstAt` is older than `sessionMissBurstWindow + sessionMissBurstCooldown` on insert (amortised, like `exchangeRouting.maybeSweepExpiredTimedDeadlines`), or cap the table the way `unsecuredWindows` is capped; also clear it in `Bridge.Stop` alongside `b.unsecuredWindows.Clear()`.

findings.title: Config-UI edit sessions are only reclaimed by an explicit save or discard, so every abandoned channel-config editor leaks its paramset snapshot for the process lifetime
findings.claim: `configui.SessionStore` is a plain `map[SessionKey]*Session` with no TTL, no sweep and no size bound (internal/configui/sessions.go:24-31). Entries are added by `sessionOpenHandler` — `store.Put(key, configui.NewSession(nil, initial))` (internal/north/rest/ws/commands_default.go:1600) — and removed only by `sessionDiscardHandler` (:1693) and `sessionSaveHandler` (:1782). Each `Session` retains two full copies of the channel's paramset values plus its description map (`NewSession` copies `descriptions`, `initialValues` and `currentValues`, internal/configui/session.go:53-63). Nothing else deletes: the WebSocket teardown path (`hub.deregister` → `delete(h.clients, c)`, internal/north/rest/ws/hub.go:429) touches only the client registry, and the daemon never sweeps the store — `grep -rn 'sessionStore\.' cmd/ internal/` finds no purge caller (contrast `cmd/openccu-loom/session_purge.go`, which does exactly this for `auth.SessionStore`). The key is `(central, channelAddress, paramsetKey)`, so the total is bounded by the model size rather than by traffic, and a re-open of the same channel overwrites the stale entry via `store.Put`.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator browses channel configuration in the SPA — opening the MASTER editor on a series of channels and navigating away or closing the tab instead of pressing save/cancel each time. Every abandoned editor leaves one `*Session` holding three copies of that channel's paramset maps in memory for the rest of the daemon's uptime. On a large installation (thousands of channels × 2 paramsets) a thorough configuration session can pin tens of MB on a Raspberry Pi that is never released until restart, and neither `/api/v1/diagnostics` nor any other surface reports it (the store exposes `Len()` but nothing publishes it).
findings.verified_by: code trace: unbounded map at sessions.go:24-31; only Put/Delete callers are the three WS handlers in commands_default.go:1600/1693/1782; no sweeper anywhere (grep over cmd/ + internal/ for SessionStore users); per-session retention shown by session.go:53-63.
findings.fix_sketch: Stamp each session with a `createdAt`/`lastTouchedAt` and reap idle ones from the existing periodic sweeper (or from `Put` itself, amortised), and drop a client's sessions when its WebSocket deregisters — which additionally requires scoping `SessionKey` (or a side index) by the owning connection/subject.

findings.title: synchronous, cache_size and temp_store are applied to a single pooled connection, so 15 of 16 connections run on SQLite's compiled defaults instead of the documented pragma set
findings.claim: dsn.go:6-20 states the rule explicitly: 'Connection-scoped pragmas must ride on the DSN because setting them once via ExecContext primes a single pooled connection and leaves the rest on their defaults.' connectionPragmas (dsn.go:20) carries only busy_timeout, journal_mode and foreign_keys. applyPragmas (store.go:126-146) additionally issues 'PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL', 'PRAGMA cache_size = -20000' and 'PRAGMA temp_store = MEMORY' through db.ExecContext — which, per database/sql pooling, reaches whichever single connection services that call. All three are per-connection settings in SQLite, and the pool is opened with MaxOpenConns=16 (store.go:41). Both file-backed databases are affected: openccu-loom.db (daemon_boot.go:91) and the append-heavy history.db (history_wiring.go:34), which both route through FileDSN and then applyPragmas. Measured with a reproducer that reproduces the exact open sequence and then holds four distinct *sql.Conn: conn0 reports synchronous=1 (NORMAL), cache_size=-20000, temp_store=2 (MEMORY); conn1..3 report synchronous=2 (FULL), cache_size=-2000, temp_store=0 (default file). foreign_keys=1, busy_timeout=5000 and journal_mode=wal are correct on all four, confirming the DSN mechanism works and only these three pragmas are missing from it.
findings.failure_scenario: Not a correctness or durability regression — SQLite's default synchronous=FULL is stricter than the configured NORMAL, so nothing is lost. The effect is that the tuning SPECIFICATION §13.2 documents as applied is in fact applied to one connection out of sixteen: nearly every write does an extra fsync per commit, and every read runs with a 2 MB page cache and file-backed temp storage instead of the intended 20 MB cache and in-memory temp store. On an embedded target (the Raspberry-Pi-class hosts this daemon targets) that is the difference between the measured behaviour and the documented one, and it makes the pragma set look configured while it is not.
findings.verified_by: measurement: $S/repro/E2/pragma reproduces FileDSN + applyPragmas + a 16-connection pool and reads PRAGMA synchronous / cache_size / temp_store / foreign_keys / busy_timeout / journal_mode on four simultaneously held connections. Output: conn0 synchronous=1 cache_size=-20000 temp_store=2; conn1..3 synchronous=2 cache_size=-2000 temp_store=0.
findings.fix_sketch: Move synchronous, cache_size and temp_store onto connectionPragmas as `_pragma=synchronous(NORMAL)&_pragma=cache_size(-20000)&_pragma=temp_store(MEMORY)` so every pooled connection gets them, and keep applyPragmas only for the once-per-database journal_mode decision that depends on the in-memory probe.

findings.title: An alarm schedule whose HH:MM falls in the spring-forward DST gap fires one hour late on the day AFTER the transition as well, because nextFire re-derives the next occurrence from the already-normalized base instant.
findings.claim: `nextFire` (internal/alarm/schedules.go:307-323) builds `base := time.Date(now.Year(), now.Month(), now.Day(), hour, minute, 0, 0, now.Location())` and then walks `base.AddDate(0, 0, i)`. On the spring-forward day the requested wall clock does not exist, so `time.Date` normalizes it forward by one hour (measured: `time.Date(2026,3,29,2,30,0,0,Europe/Berlin)` == 2026-03-29 03:30 CEST). `AddDate` is defined as `Date(y, m, d+days, t.Clock()...)` — it re-reads the *normalized* clock (03:30), not the requested 02:30 — so every subsequent iteration of the loop carries the +1 h. The chain in `chainAt` (schedules.go:181-214) re-arms itself from the fire instant (`now := r.deps.Clock.Now()` at :189), and on the transition day that instant is still 2026-03-29, so the next occurrence it computes is 2026-03-30 03:30 CEST instead of 02:30. Only the re-arm after that (with `now` on 2026-03-30) recovers the correct 02:30. Measured chain for a daily 02:30 schedule in Europe/Berlin: 2026-03-28 12:00 -> fires 2026-03-29 03:30 (unavoidable, 02:30 does not exist) -> fires 2026-03-30 03:30 (the defect; should be 02:30) -> fires 2026-03-31 02:30 (correct). The autumn transition is clean: `time.Date(2026,10,25,2,30,...)` resolves to the second (CET) 02:30 and the re-arm's `!c.After(now)` guard at schedules.go:312 rejects it, so a schedule in the repeated hour fires exactly once, never twice. A weekday-filtered schedule shows the same +1 h (measured: Sunday-only 02:30 from 2026-03-25 -> 2026-03-29 03:30 -> 2026-04-05 03:30, i.e. the following Sunday is also an hour late).
findings.failure_scenario: A zone has an AutoArm schedule at 02:30 for mode `away`. On Monday 2026-03-30 (the day after the EU spring-forward on Sunday 2026-03-29) the zone is armed at 03:30 CEST instead of 02:30 CEST — one hour of the night unarmed, with no log line or journal entry indicating anything unusual. Same for a reminder-only schedule: the `arm_reminder` journal row and `AlarmReminderEvent` land an hour late. Recurs every year, for any schedule time in [02:00, 03:00) local.
findings.verified_by: reproducer at $S/repro/E3-time-clock/dst.go (standalone Go program that replays nextFire verbatim and simulates the re-arm chain across both 2026 Europe/Berlin transitions); output shows the 2026-03-30 03:30 fire for a 02:30 daily schedule and the correct single fire at the second 02:30 CET on 2026-10-25.
findings.fix_sketch: Keep the requested time-of-day out of the normalized instant: iterate over the calendar day rather than over the instant, e.g. `day := time.Date(now.Year(), now.Month(), now.Day(), 0, 0, 0, 0, now.Location()).AddDate(0, 0, i)` and then `c := time.Date(day.Year(), day.Month(), day.Day(), hour, minute, 0, 0, now.Location())` for each i, so every candidate re-applies HH:MM to its own calendar date instead of inheriting the previous day's DST-normalized clock. Add a table test in internal/alarm/schedules_test.go pinning Europe/Berlin and asserting the three consecutive fires around 2026-03-29 and 2026-10-25.

findings.title: A calculated battery-percentage sensor exposed on Matter produces a bridged endpoint with zero clusters, because MatterMeasurementBattery only accepts a boolean source and PowerSource.BatPercentRemaining is never implemented
findings.claim: `OperatingVoltageLevelSensor.MatterMeasurementClass()` returns `interfaces.MatterMeasurementBattery` and its doc comment claims the projection is "PowerSource (0x002F) BatPercentRemaining (P1)" (internal/model/calculated/matter.go:69-73). `FromMeasurementClass` handles that class with `if b, ok := src.(interfaces.MatterBoolMeasurementSource); ok { return ...NewPowerSourceServer(b) }` (internal/north/matter/cluster/measurement/measurement.go:918-921) -- a BOOL source only. `OperatingVoltageLevelSensor` embeds `*generic.Sensor[float64]` (internal/model/calculated/voltage.go:28-29), which the compile-time assertions in internal/model/generic/matter.go:26-27 pin as `MatterFloatMeasurementSource`, NOT `MatterBoolMeasurementSource`; grep finds no `MatterBoolValue` method anywhere under internal/model/calculated/. So the assertion fails and `FromMeasurementClass` falls through to `return nil`. BatPercentRemaining (0x000C) is absent from `PowerSourceServer` entirely -- the file's own comment at measurement.go:1439 calls it "a future float-source path" -- so even the LOW_BAT boolean path only yields BatChargeLevel. The candidate gate does not filter this out: `eligibility.Classify` accepts any measurement source whose class maps to a non-zero cluster id (internal/north/matter/eligibility/eligibility.go:105-119), and PowerSource is 0x002F, so the DP is offered as exposable in the Matter UI. The assembler has no gate either: internal/north/matter/endpoint/assembler.go:355-379 calls `makeMeasurementEndpoint` for any calculated DP with a non-None class, regardless of whether a cluster server will materialise. At dispatch, `ClusterServers()` hits `len(inner) == 0` and returns nil at internal/north/matter/endpoint/materialize.go:88-92 -- BEFORE the mandatory Descriptor and BridgedDeviceBasicInformation clusters are attached at :95 ff.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator enables the derived "Operating voltage level" (battery %) data point for Matter exposure on a battery device -- the UI lists it as exposable. A persisted bridged endpoint is allocated for it and appears in the aggregator's PartsList, but every read of that endpoint returns no clusters at all: no PowerSource, no Descriptor, no BridgedDeviceBasicInformation. The documented capability (a battery percentage in Apple Home / Google Home) silently does nothing, and per this repo's own comment at materialize.go:95-108 an endpoint missing Descriptor + BridgedDeviceBasicInformation makes Apple Home abort pairing with HMMTRErrorDomain Code 9 about nine seconds after CommissioningComplete -- i.e. the whole bridge, not just this endpoint.
findings.verified_by: code trace (calculated/matter.go:69-73; calculated/voltage.go:28-29; generic/matter.go:21-28; pkg/interfaces/matter.go:278-299; measurement.go:880,918-921,1439; eligibility.go:105-119; assembler.go:355-379; materialize.go:63-92). Not verified: the Apple Home pairing abort itself -- that consequence is asserted by materialize.go:95-108 and by notes, not measured here. The zero-cluster endpoint is a pure code fact.
findings.fix_sketch: Either implement BatPercentRemaining (0x000C, uint8 in HALF percent, 0..200 per Matter PowerSource) on `PowerSourceServer` and accept a `MatterFloatMeasurementSource` for `MatterMeasurementBattery`, or make `OperatingVoltageLevelSensor.MatterMeasurementClass()` return `MatterMeasurementNone` and fix the refuted comment. Independently, add a guard so a candidate whose `FromMeasurementClass` yields no server is neither offered by `eligibility.Classify` nor turned into an endpoint by the assembler.
findings.verify_reasoning: MECHANISM CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, CONSEQUENCE REFUTED. A Go test in the worktree ($S/wt/_scratch_v4/e4_5_test.go) constructing the real OperatingVoltageLevelSensor via calculated.NewOperatingVoltageLevelSensorWithIdentity printed: MatterMeasurementClass = 11 (= MatterMeasurementBattery); implements MatterBoolMeasurementSource=FALSE, MatterFloatMeasurementSource=true; measurement.FromMeasurementClass(class, src) -> 0 cluster servers; eligibility.Classify -> state=mappable deviceType=0x0000 clusters=[47]. So the finder is exactly right that the class accepts only a bool source (measurement.go:918-921), that the float battery-% sensor is not one, that BatPercentRemaining is unimplemented, and that the eligibility gate still offers the DP as mappable onto PowerSource 0x002F. BUT THE CLAIMED CONSEQUENCE -- 'a persisted bridged endpoint is allocated and appears in the aggregator PartsList with zero clusters', and via materialize.go:95-108 an Apple Home HMMTRErrorDomain Code 9 pairing abort for the WHOLE bridge -- CANNOT HAPPEN IN THE SHIPPED DAEMON. The calculated-DP measurement branch of the assembler is behind `if !a.cfg.IncludeMeasurements { continue }` (internal/north/matter/endpoint/assembler.go:353), and `IncludeMeasurements` is set to true in EXACTLY THREE FILES, ALL TESTS (bridge/subscribe_report_chunking_test.go:92, bridge/scenario_harness_test.go:111, bridge/measurement_listener_test.go:120). The production literal cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_matter.go:222-232 constructing matterbridge.Config does not set the field, so it is false and the branch that would call makeMeasurementEndpoint for a calculated DP is never entered. (The GENERIC-DP measurement path at assembler.go:477 is NOT gated -- but generic battery only reaches MatterMeasurementBattery via ParameterLowBat/ParameterLowbat, internal/model/generic/matter.go:112-113, which is a BinarySensor and DOES implement MatterBoolValue, so that path materialises a PowerSourceServer correctly.) WHAT IS REAL: eligibility.CollectCandidates emits every calculated DP unconditionally (eligibility.go:269-272) and feeds GET /api/v1/matter/exposable (handlers/matter_exposures.go:35), so the derived battery-% DP is listed to the operator as mappable onto PowerSource and can be switched on -- and then nothing whatsoever is built. That is an inert toggle in the Matter exposure UI, plus a doc comment at internal/model/calculated/matter.go:69-73 asserting a 'PowerSource (0x002F) BatPercentRemaining (P1)' projection that does not exist -- exactly the refuted-comment class this repo's own release checklist sweeps for. Re-rated high -> low: no endpoint, no zero-cluster topology, no pairing risk; a dead UI affordance and a false comment.

findings.title: parameter.asInt narrows int64 and json.Number to a platform int without the 32-bit bounds check its uint/uint64 siblings carry, so an out-of-range write could wrap into a different in-range value on armv7
findings.claim: `asInt` (internal/parameter/coerce.go:168-220) is the write-coercion entry point behind `parameter.Coerce`, which is used by REST PUT .../value (internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:806), the MCP tool write path (internal/north/mcp/tools.go:496), the MQTT command sink (internal/central/adapter/mqtt_sink.go:129,221) and paramset writes (internal/central/adapter/paramsets.go:283,583). It explicitly bounds-checks the `uint` case (coerce.go:181-183) and the `uint64` case (:192-193) with `nolint:gosec // bounds-checked above`, but the `int64` case at :178-179 and the `json.Number` case at :211-216 do a bare `int(v)` / `int(n)`. On the shipped armv7 target `int` is 32 bits, so int64(2^32) narrows to 0 by silent wraparound; the wrapped value is then what `checkNumericRange` and `MatchesSpecialValue(desc, float64(i))` see, so a value that should have been rejected can pass as an in-range one. The codebase solves exactly this elsewhere and says so: pkg/hmtypes/value.go:97-103 (`NewParamValue`) preserves out-of-int-range values as float "relevant on 32-bit builds such as armv7", and internal/client/transport/binrpc/decode.go:184-190 guards its own `int(count)` narrowing.
findings.failure_scenario: Latent. Every located caller feeds `Coerce` a value decoded from JSON into `any` without `json.Decoder.UseNumber()` (verified by grep: no `UseNumber` anywhere under internal/north or internal/central), which always yields float64, and no internal Go call site was found constructing a raw int64 paramset value. So the defective branch is not reachable through any request path in HEAD; the missing guard is a regression waiting for a caller that does use `UseNumber` or hands over a typed int64.
findings.verified_by: code trace (coerce.go:168-220 with the asymmetric bounds checks; hmtypes/value.go:97-103; binrpc/decode.go:184-190) + grep showing no UseNumber and no int64-producing caller. Unverified: any live trigger -- none was found, which is why this is low and PLAUSIBLE rather than a confirmed live bug.
findings.fix_sketch: Apply the same `if v > math.MaxInt || v < math.MinInt { return error }` guard to the `int64` and `json.Number` branches that the `uint`/`uint64` branches already have.

findings.title: GET /service-messages/suppressed is mounted viewer-open although the published contract declares it operator-tier, and nothing cross-checks the two
findings.claim: assets/openapi.yaml declares the operation as `security: [{basicAuth: []}, {bearerAuth: []}, {openIdConnect: [operator]}]` — the repo's convention for 'operator tier', the same shape carried by its write sibling POST /service-messages/unsuppress and by every /alarm/codes route. The router mounts it with no role wrapper: `pr.Get("/service-messages/suppressed", handlers.ListSuppressedServiceMessages(d.Hub))` (internal/north/rest/router.go:1274), i.e. any authenticated identity including viewer. A mechanical diff of the two sides ($S/repro/E5/matrix.py) finds this as the only operation in the whole surface where the spec is strictly stricter than the router for a reason other than a deliberately anonymous endpoint (the other DECLARED-STRICTER rows are /health, /info, /auth/login, /auth/logout, /auth/me, /setup, /setup/status, /auth/oidc/*, /devices/{addr}/icon, all of which are intentionally pre-auth). There is no guard: tests/contract/rest_router_openapi_walk_test.go walks the chi tree for path coverage only and never reads the `security` block, and middleware.NewOpenAPIValidator installs `openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc` (internal/north/rest/middleware/openapi.go:179), so the validator does not enforce security either.
findings.failure_scenario: A viewer-role account (or a viewer-scoped API token) calls GET /api/v1/service-messages/suppressed and receives the full list of service messages an operator has permanently suppressed on every CCU — data the published API contract, and the SPA's own generated client, treat as operator-only. Conversely, an integration written against the spec will assume it needs an operator credential it does not actually need. Either the route or the spec is wrong and no test can tell which.
findings.verified_by: reproducer at $S/repro/E5/matrix.py (declared-vs-enforced diff over 291 OpenAPI operations and 294 router registrations); spec text read back with python/yaml; router.go:1274 read directly.
findings.fix_sketch: Decide the tier once — most likely add `.With(op)` at router.go:1274 to match the unsuppress sibling — and add a contract test that walks assets/openapi.yaml's `security` scopes against the router's `.With(op)`/`.With(admin)` wrappers so the two can never drift again.

findings.title: maskCentralRow strips the CCU host/serial/ports/username from non-admin readers of /centrals, but three sibling viewer-open endpoints publish exactly that data
findings.claim: maskCentralRow (internal/north/rest/handlers/admin_centrals.go:64-79) blanks Host, Serial, Port, JSONRPCPort, Ports, Username, PasswordEnv, TLS and TLSInsecureSkipVerify for any identity below RoleAdmin, and its doc comment states the reason: 'Everything else (host, ports, username, the TLS posture) tells an authenticated viewer exactly where the CCU lives and how it is reached, which is reconnaissance rather than anything those views use. Gating the routes instead would break them, so the row is narrowed and the routes stay open.' The same facts are served unnarrowed to any authenticated identity by three other routes: (1) `pr.Get("/config", handlers.Config(d.Config))` (router.go:787) returns hmapi.ConfigSnapshot whose ConfigCentral carries `Host` (pkg/hmapi/rest_contract.go:106-110), filled from the live client entries in ConfigAdapter.centrals (internal/central/adapter/config.go:97-99) — plus callback_ports; (2) `pr.Get("/system/ccu", handlers.SystemCCU(d.SystemCCU))` (router.go:1086) returns SystemCCUEntry with Host, Hostname, Serial, URL and a per-interface list of Address+Port (internal/north/rest/handlers/system_ccu.go:28-92); (3) `pr.Get("/interfaces", ...)` and `/interfaces/{id}` (router.go:1291-1292) return hmapi.InterfaceState which carries `Host` (pkg/hmapi/rest_contract.go:191). None of the three applies any role narrowing.
findings.failure_scenario: A viewer-role account calls GET /api/v1/system/ccu and gets each CCU's hostname/IP, serial number, WebUI URL and every interface's address and port — the exact set GET /api/v1/centrals deliberately withholds from that same account one route away. The narrowing is therefore a control that does nothing: the confidentiality boundary it was written to draw does not exist anywhere else on the surface, so an operator who reads the maskCentralRow comment is misled about what a viewer can see.
findings.verified_by: code trace: admin_centrals.go:64-79 (the narrowing) against router.go:787/1086/1291-1292 (the three ungated routes) and the DTOs at hmapi/rest_contract.go:106-110 & 185-203, handlers/system_ccu.go:28-92, central/adapter/config.go:97-99.
findings.fix_sketch: Pick one policy and apply it everywhere: either drop the role-scoping in maskCentralRow (keeping the unconditional password mask) and record in the comment that CCU coordinates are viewer-visible by design, or extend the same narrowing to the SystemCCU, ConfigSnapshot and InterfaceState projections. A contract test that asserts no viewer-reachable response body contains a configured central's host would keep it honest.
findings.resolution: one masking rule (hideCCUCoordinates) applied to /config, /system/ccu and the discovery list; discovery reads raised to admin
findings.status_verified_at: dea785a1 (pre-#606 HEAD); the open two re-checked on 4eecb1e6

findings.title: DownloadRPCRecording hand-splices a URL path parameter into Content-Disposition instead of using ContentDispositionAttachment, the exact pattern that helper's doc comment forbids
findings.claim: internal/north/rest/handlers/write.go:67-77 documents ContentDispositionAttachment as mandatory for download handlers: 'Handlers that stream a download must use this instead of hand-splicing the filename into the header string: an unescaped quote or semicolon in filename ... would let the value break out of the filename parameter and inject additional Content-Disposition directives.' Every other download handler complies (backup.go:221, device_definition_export.go:62, diagnostics_capture.go:188). DownloadRPCRecording does not: it writes `w.Header().Set("Content-Disposition", "attachment; filename=\"rpc-recording-"+centralName+"-"+format+".json\"")` (diagnostics_rpc_recorder.go:122-123) where centralName is `chi.URLParam(r, "central")` (line 111) — and the router mounts decodedPathRouting first (router.go:593), so URL params arrive percent-decoded and can contain a double quote or semicolon. The value is not attacker-controlled today: the header is only written after `svc.Export(centralName, format)` returns ok, and RPCRecorderAdapter.Export requires an exact `a.registry.Get(centralName)` hit (internal/central/adapter/rpc_recorder.go:219-222), so centralName must equal a configured central name; the route is additionally admin-gated (router.go:1176). Response splitting is separately impossible because net/http rewrites CR/LF in header values.
findings.failure_scenario: Not currently exploitable — it becomes a real header-injection the moment a central name containing a quote or semicolon is accepted (central names come from the operator-editable /centrals CRUD and are not validated against a character set today) or the ok-gate is relaxed. It is filed because it is a documented invariant that is violated in exactly one place, which is how the invariant stops being true.
findings.verified_by: code trace: write.go:67-77 (the rule), diagnostics_rpc_recorder.go:111-123 (the violation), backup.go:221 / device_definition_export.go:62 / diagnostics_capture.go:188 (the three compliant siblings), rpc_recorder.go:219-222 (why it is not reachable today).
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the string concatenation with `ContentDispositionAttachment("rpc-recording-"+centralName+"-"+format+".json")`.
findings.resolution: closed by the 0.62.0 / 0.63.0 fix waves; confirmed still closed on re-verification

findings.title: north.mcp.path validation tightened from a leading-slash check to a per-segment character class, and a rejected legacy value now aborts startup with no fallback
findings.claim: 1) At v0.55.0 `validateMCP` (git show v0.55.0:internal/config/validate.go:111-122) required only a leading '/' and, unless the value was exactly '/', no trailing '/'. 2) At HEAD it delegates to `NorthMCP.ValidateMountPath` (internal/config/config.go:713-722), which matches `^(/[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+)+$` (config.go:701) — rejecting every character outside that class and rejecting the bare '/' the old rule explicitly allowed. Introduced in-range by commit 667b8921. 3) It runs regardless of `north.mcp.enabled` (validateMCP short-circuits only on an empty Path), inside validateFieldRanges, reached from config.Parse → config.LoadWithEnv → cmd/openccu-loom/main.go:113 `return err` → os.Exit(1). Unlike the MQTT raw/discovery conflict in applyDefaults, which self-corrects with a warning, there is no fallback: the daemon does not start.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator who enabled MCP (off by default) and set `north.mcp.path` to a value the new class rejects upgrades in place, and 0.61.4 exits during config validation before serving REST/MQTT/Matter, requiring a manual YAML edit to recover.
findings.verified_by: The validation change itself is CONFIRMED (diffed v0.55.0's validateMCP against HEAD's ValidateMountPath, read the regex and the Parse→os.Exit(1) chain). What I could NOT verify is that any concrete previously-*working* value now fails: the new code's own rationale (config.go:704-712) is that http.ServeMux panics during registration on a malformed pattern and that the root mount double-registers '/', which means the values the new regex rejects already killed the daemon at bring-up — by panic instead of by message. Severity is set low for that reason; a value that ServeMux accepts but the regex rejects would raise it, and I did not find one.
findings.fix_sketch: If a legacy-accepted, ServeMux-safe value is identified, warn and fall back to the default "/mcp" instead of aborting, mirroring the MQTT auto-correction in applyDefaults. Otherwise note the stricter rule in the upgrade notes, since the failure moves from a panic to a validation error.
findings.resolution: an invalid north.mcp.path falls back to the default with a warn instead of aborting the boot
findings.status_verified_at: dea785a1 (pre-#606 HEAD); the open two re-checked on 4eecb1e6

findings.title: The WebSocket pump is never torn down after logout or session expiry, so an idle login screen reconnects a 401-rejected socket every 15 seconds for the rest of the tab's life.
findings.claim: The shared pump closes its socket only in `subscribe`'s unsubscribe, and only when the handler set empties: `handlers.delete(handler); if (handlers.size === 0) { stream?.close(); stream = null; ... }` (assets/ui/src/lib/stores/events.svelte.ts:82-89). maintenanceStore.ensureBound() calls `subscribe((env) => {...})` and drops the returned unsubscribe (assets/ui/src/lib/stores/maintenance.svelte.ts:45-75), so once any device surface has rendered a maintenance badge the handler set can never reach zero and that branch is dead. /api/v1/events sits inside the authenticated router group (internal/north/rest/router.go:1366, inside the `pr` protected sub-router), so after the session lapses the upgrade is rejected; ws.ts's close listener then reschedules `connect` with `Math.min(15000, 500 * 2 ** Math.min(attempt,5))` and `closed` is only ever set by an explicit close() that now cannot happen (assets/ui/src/lib/api/ws.ts:314-321, 342-349). Meanwhile the REST side does self-heal — a 401 routes through setUnauthorizedHandler -> authStore.expire() -> identity=null (assets/ui/src/lib/api/client.ts:247-249; auth.svelte.ts:77-91,117) — and App then renders <Login/>, unmounting the shell (App.svelte:417-418). The comment at client.ts:189-195 states the intent that the background pollers stop on 401; the WS pump is the one that does not.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator leaves a browser tab open on the device list overnight. The daemon restarts (in-memory sessions are lost) or the session simply expires; the next REST call 401s and the SPA drops back to the login screen. From then on the tab opens a WebSocket to /api/v1/events every 15 seconds, forever: a 401 line in the daemon log every 15 s per idle tab, and continuous radio/CPU wake-ups on a wall tablet that is supposed to be idle. Nothing on screen indicates it.
findings.verified_by: code trace: assets/ui/src/lib/stores/events.svelte.ts:33-52,77-90; assets/ui/src/lib/stores/maintenance.svelte.ts:43-75; assets/ui/src/lib/api/ws.ts:240-249,314-321,342-349; assets/ui/src/lib/api/client.ts:189-195,247-249; assets/ui/src/lib/stores/auth.svelte.ts:77-91,117; internal/north/rest/router.go:1366
findings.fix_sketch: Give events.svelte.ts an explicit `shutdown()` that closes the stream regardless of handler count and call it from authStore.expire()/logout(); re-open lazily on the next subscribe. Alternatively give maintenanceStore a real unsubscribe so the ref-counted teardown can actually fire, and cap the pump's reconnect attempts on a 401-shaped close.
findings.resolution: closed by the 0.62.0 / 0.63.0 fix waves; confirmed still closed on re-verification

findings.title: Every surfaces response resets the Navigation & views editor back to the live profile, so saving changes to the other profile silently switches the editor underneath the operator.
findings.claim: `apply()` ends with `editing = resp.profile` (assets/ui/src/lib/stores/surfaces.svelte.ts:89) and apply() is called from load() (line 116), save() (line 232), setEmbedded() (line 242) and setEmbeddedScope() (line 252). `resp.profile` is the LIVE profile, not the one being edited. NavViewsAdmin renders the editor against `const editing = $derived(surfacesStore.editing)` (assets/ui/src/lib/components/settings/NavViewsAdmin.svelte:52) and offers an explicit profile switcher (`onclick={() => surfacesStore.setEditing(p)}`, NavViewsAdmin.svelte:418), and it calls save/setEmbedded/setEmbeddedScope at lines 283/244/258. The store's own doc comment says editing 'need not be the live one: preparing the Home Assistant layout before switching to it is a normal thing to want' (surfaces.svelte.ts:62-65), and the `resetDraft: false` option exists specifically so the mode PUTs do not disturb the operator's work (surfaces.svelte.ts:69-76) — yet `editing` is overwritten on exactly those calls too, which is what makes this an oversight rather than the documented behaviour.
findings.failure_scenario: Live profile is 'standalone'. Operator opens Settings -> Navigation & views, clicks the 'Embedded' profile tab to prepare the Home Assistant layout, hides three views and clicks Save. The save is applied to the embedded profile correctly, but the editor snaps back to the Standalone tab. If the operator continues hiding views believing they are still in the embedded profile, those toggles now edit the profile that is actually live — views disappear from their own navigation. The same jump happens on the master embedded toggle and the scope selector.
findings.verified_by: code trace: assets/ui/src/lib/stores/surfaces.svelte.ts:77-92,111-125,231-253,255-257; assets/ui/src/lib/components/settings/NavViewsAdmin.svelte:52,244,258,283,418
findings.fix_sketch: Set `editing = resp.profile` only on the first load (when `loaded` is still false) or gate it behind the same `resetDraft` option the row edits already use, so save/setEmbedded/setEmbeddedScope leave the operator on the profile they are editing.
findings.resolution: closed by the 0.62.0 / 0.63.0 fix waves; confirmed still closed on re-verification

findings.title: SystemUpdatePanel restarts its poll after unmount: the post-await ensurePoll() clears the stop latch and installs a 5 s timer nothing can cancel.
findings.claim: onMount is async and calls ensurePoll() only after `await load()`: `onMount(async () => { await load(); if (entries.some(e => e.in_progress)) ensurePoll(); }); onDestroy(stopPoll);` (assets/ui/src/lib/components/settings/SystemUpdatePanel.svelte:136-142). stopPoll() sets `pollStopped = true` and clears the pending timeout (lines 85-91) — the latch exists precisely to defeat a tick that reschedules after unmount (comment at lines 80-83). But ensurePoll() begins with `if (pollTimer) return; pollStopped = false;` (lines 93-95), so when it runs after onDestroy it clears the very latch that was supposed to stop it and then arms `pollTimer = setTimeout(tick, 5000)` (line 101). tick re-arms itself while `entries.some(e => e.in_progress)` holds (lines 96-102) and stopPoll will never run again for this destroyed instance.
findings.failure_scenario: A CCU firmware update is running (started from another tab, the CLI or the MQTT update entity). The operator opens Settings -> System and navigates away before GET /system/update answers. The panel is gone, but a GET /system/update fires every 5 seconds for the rest of the tab session — against a CCU that is mid-reboot, i.e. exactly when the daemon is least able to absorb it — and it never stops even after the install finishes, because a failed request leaves the previous `entries` in place (the load() catch deliberately keeps them, lines 66-77).
findings.verified_by: code trace: assets/ui/src/lib/components/settings/SystemUpdatePanel.svelte:66-77,79-102,136-142
findings.fix_sketch: Do not reset `pollStopped` inside ensurePoll(); reset it only where a poll is deliberately (re)started by a user action, and make ensurePoll() a no-op while `pollStopped` is true. Same guard applies to the install() path at line 128.
findings.resolution: closed by the 0.62.0 / 0.63.0 fix waves; confirmed still closed on re-verification
findings.status_verified_at: dea785a1 (pre-#606 HEAD); the open two re-checked on 4eecb1e6

findings.title: Three label lists are built in plain `const` initialisers that call t(), so they freeze at the locale active when the view mounted and do not follow a live language switch.
findings.claim: t() reads `prefs.locale` and is documented as reactive only for callers inside a reactive context (assets/ui/src/lib/i18n.ts:8197-8206; the same note appears on navClusters at lib/nav.ts:83-85: 'callers must invoke this inside a reactive context if they want it to follow a locale switch'). A plain `const` in a Svelte 5 component script runs once at instantiation and is never re-evaluated. Three such initialisers call t(): `const ALL_TABS: Tab[] = [... label: t('settings.tab.general') ...]` (assets/ui/src/routes/Settings.svelte:271-291), `const requireDisarmOptions = [... label: t('alarm.policies.code.require_disarm.default') ...]` (assets/ui/src/routes/alarm/AlarmPolicies.svelte:139-143) and `const DURATION_OPTIONS` (assets/ui/src/routes/matter/MatterPair.svelte:30). In Settings the frozen array is the source for `visibleTabs` and `visibleGroups` ($derived over ALL_TABS, Settings.svelte:328-345), so re-deriving does not help. The locale toggle is a live one-click action in the sidebar (App.svelte:428 -> setLocale -> preferences.svelte.ts:99-102) and App keeps the route component mounted across it (`<Settings tab={route.tab} />`, App.svelte:523 — no key).
findings.failure_scenario: Operator is on Settings with the UI in German and clicks the language toggle in the sidebar. The page header, the field labels, the help texts and the buttons switch to English; the settings tab list on the left stays German until the operator navigates away and back or reloads. Same for the 'require disarm code' dropdown on the alarm policies view and the commissioning-window duration dropdown on the Matter pairing view.
findings.verified_by: code trace + AST-ish scan of all .svelte files for top-level non-rune const initialisers containing t(): assets/ui/src/routes/Settings.svelte:271, assets/ui/src/routes/alarm/AlarmPolicies.svelte:139, assets/ui/src/routes/matter/MatterPair.svelte:30; assets/ui/src/lib/i18n.ts:8197-8206; assets/ui/src/App.svelte:428,523
findings.fix_sketch: Turn each into `$derived` (or `$derived.by`) so the labels recompute on the locale read. A cheap guard: a lint rule or contract test rejecting `t(` inside a top-level `const`/`let` initialiser that is not a rune.

findings.title: The un-ignore visibility decider is one process-global instance, so a per-central un-ignore rule silently applies to every CCU in the fleet
findings.claim: The daemon constructs exactly one *visibility.Registry for the whole process (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_infra.go:98) and hands the same instance to every central's DevicePipeline (internal/central/adapter/ccu_wiring.go:108-119). ParameterDecider holds one flat `unIgnore []UnIgnoreEntry` and its memo key `ignoreCacheKey` carries no central dimension (internal/store/visibility/decider.go:25-39, types.go:16-22). The REST/SQLite/SPA surface, in contrast, is per-central: VisibilityUnIgnoreStore.List/Patterns/Replace/SeedIfEmpty all take centralName (internal/store/sqlite/visibility_unignore.go:51/84/99/154) and the PUT handler diffs + audits per central (internal/north/rest/handlers/visibility.go). visibilityAdapter.LoadUnIgnore unions every central's persisted patterns and loads the union into the single shared decider (cmd/openccu-loom/visibility_adapter.go:106-136); the adapter's own comment concedes it (:24-28). Both live-read surfaces gate through that shared decider: REST ListDataPoints calls vis.VisibleForChannel per request (internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:735-737) and the MQTT raw/slot plane gates on b.vis.VisibleForChannel (internal/central/adapter/eventbridge.go:1538-1551).
findings.failure_scenario: On a two-CCU install the operator un-ignores a parameter for central A only (PUT /api/v1/visibility/unignore with central_name=A). Central B, whose operator never asked for it, immediately starts exposing that parameter on REST /devices/.../datapoints and publishing it on the raw MQTT plane — and B's own un-ignore list still shows nothing, so the change is neither visible nor reversible from B's surface.
findings.verified_by: code trace: daemon_infra.go:98 (single Registry) + ccu_wiring.go:108-119 (shared into every pipeline) + visibility_adapter.go:106-136 (union load) + decider.go:25-39 / types.go:16-22 (no central in state or memo key) + devices.go:735-737 and eventbridge.go:1538-1551 (live read paths)
findings.fix_sketch: Give the decider a central dimension — one ParameterDecider per central.Unit (mirroring registry.ParamsetRegistry, already per-unit at internal/central/central.go:302), or add `central` to ignoreCacheKey and the un-ignore match. If fleet-wide un-ignore is the intended product behaviour, change the REST/SQLite/SPA surface to say so rather than presenting a per-central control that is not one.
findings.verify_reasoning: Every code fact checks out: one visibility.Registry per process (daemon_infra.go:98), handed to every central's pipeline (ccu_wiring.go:119-121), ParameterDecider holds one flat unIgnore slice with a central-free memo key (decider.go:25-39, types.go:16-22), and both applyVisibilityUnIgnore (visibility_wiring.go:120-176) and visibilityAdapter.LoadUnIgnore (visibility_adapter.go:106-157) union every central's persisted patterns into that one decider — step 3 of applyVisibilityUnIgnore even re-marks EVERY central's devices, not just the requesting one. What kills the 'high' rating is that this is not an undiscovered defect but the documented contract of the backend: visibility_adapter.go:24-28 states 'the single underlying *visibility.Registry is shared across centrals — un-ignore rules are global in the existing backend (one decider, one rule set)', and LoadUnIgnore's own doc (visibility_adapter.go:139-144) spells out the cross-central spill and its timing. The 'immediately' in the failure scenario is also only half right: REST ListDataPoints re-asks the shared decider per request (devices.go:741), so an already-materialised DP on central B does flip visible at once, but a parameter suppressed at hydration on B needs B's next Init/Reassemble. And the effect is a widening of visible diagnostic parameters — no data loss, no write path, no privilege change. Real residual: the REST/SPA present a per-central control whose backend is fleet-wide; that is a UX/API-contract mismatch (fix: per-central decider, or say so on the surface), not a correctness break.
findings.resolution: the un-ignore decider carries a central dimension
findings.status_verified_at: dea785a1 (pre-#606 HEAD); the open two re-checked on 4eecb1e6

findings.title: The cache-clear audit entry always records reinit=[] because the audit hook runs before the re-init assigns CentralsReinit
findings.claim: Service.Clear calls the audit hook and only afterwards fills the field the hook formats: `if s.d.Audit != nil { s.d.Audit(ctx, scope, rep) }` at internal/central/cachereset/cachereset.go:241-243, then `rep.CentralsReinit = s.reinit(ctx, affected)` at :244. The wired hook renders `reinit=%v` from rep.CentralsReinit (cmd/openccu-loom/cachereset_wiring.go:150-159), which is still nil at that point. rep is passed by value into the hook, so the later assignment cannot reach it either.
findings.failure_scenario: Every audit-log row for a cache clear reads 'reinit=[]' regardless of how many centrals were actually re-initialised — including a clear whose re-init was skipped entirely because the central is not managed (cachereset.go:388-392 logs cachereset.reinit_skipped). The operator's audit trail therefore cannot distinguish 'rows cleared and CCU re-pulled' from 'rows cleared and nothing re-pulled'.
findings.verified_by: code trace: cachereset.go:241-244 (ordering, rep passed by value) + cachereset_wiring.go:150-159 (the format string reading rep.CentralsReinit)
findings.fix_sketch: Move the Audit call after `rep.CentralsReinit = s.reinit(...)`, or split it into a begin/end pair if the intent is to record the attempt before the potentially long re-pull.
findings.resolution: closed by the 0.62.0 / 0.63.0 fix waves; confirmed still closed on re-verification

findings.title: The firmware-update callback deletes the paramset-description cache but never re-fetches it, contrary to its own doc comment
findings.claim: CallbackHandlers.UpdateDevice documents that on hint=0 'the firmware cache is invalidated and a background refresh is scheduled to pull fresh device and paramset descriptions' (internal/central/adapter/callback_handlers.go:637-641). InvalidateFirmwareCache deletes every paramset-registry entry for the device and its channels (internal/central/coordinators/device.go:1369-1378), but the follow-up RefreshDeviceDescriptionsAndCreateMissingDevices only calls ListDevices and writes c.descs — it never touches c.paramsets. The same pair repeats in CallbackHandlers.ReaddedDevice. Consumers of the paramset registry treat an empty result as 'no configurable parameters' rather than 'not loaded yet' (internal/central/coordinators/configuration.go:273-276).
findings.failure_scenario: After a firmware update the affected channels' MASTER paramset schema is missing from ConfigurationCoordinator.GetAllParamsetDescriptions / ConfigurableChannels / GetConfigurableDevices until an explicit ReloadChannelConfig or a restart. Blast radius today is nil — those three methods have no production callers outside their own file — so this is a latent defect plus a refuted doc claim, reported because wiring any of them to a REST/WS surface would make it live.
findings.verified_by: code trace: callback_handlers.go:637-641 (the claim) vs. coordinators/device.go:1369-1378 and RefreshDeviceDescriptionsAndCreateMissingDevices (what actually runs); configuration.go:273-276 for the miss-handling shape
findings.fix_sketch: Either correct the comment to say only device-level descriptions are refreshed, or extend the firmware/re-add path to re-pull GetParamsetDescription per affected channel (mirroring DeviceCoordinator.ReloadChannelConfig) before any of those methods is wired to a live surface.

findings.title: `hmcli devices set -priority` advertises the value `normal`, which is not in the API's priority vocabulary and is rejected by the OpenAPI validator.
findings.claim: cmd/hmcli/devices.go:307 registers the flag with the help text 'command priority (e.g. normal, high)' and passes the raw string straight into setValueRequest.Priority (devices.go:325-328), which is serialised as the `priority` field of PUT …/data-points/{param}/value. assets/openapi.yaml's SetValueRequest declares `priority: {type: string, enum: [critical, high, default, low]}` (line ~9231). OpenAPI request validation is on by default — internal/config/config.go:1232-1234 OpenAPIValidateEnabled returns orDefault(n.OpenAPIValidate, true), and cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest_mount.go:211 builds the validator when it is enabled, mounted at internal/north/rest/router.go:693-694 with FailOpen=false (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_north.go:842). openapi3filter therefore rejects `priority: "normal"` with 400 'Request does not match OpenAPI spec'. With validation switched off the value instead falls through internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:1070-1079 parsePriority's default branch and silently becomes CommandPriorityHigh. Neither behaviour is 'normal'. The CLI performs no client-side validation of the flag.
findings.failure_scenario: `hmcli devices set 00021BE9957782 4 STATE true -priority normal` — copied from the flag's own help text — fails with `PUT …: HTTP 400 Bad Request` and exit 1 on a default-configured daemon; on a daemon with openapi_validate: false it succeeds but silently sends the value at `high` priority. The one genuinely supported de-prioritising value, `low`, is not mentioned in the help at all.
findings.verified_by: code trace: cmd/hmcli/devices.go:307/325-328 -> assets/openapi.yaml SetValueRequest enum -> internal/north/rest/router.go:693 + cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_rest_mount.go:211 + internal/config/config.go:1232 (default true) -> internal/north/rest/handlers/devices.go:1070-1079
findings.fix_sketch: Change the flag help to the real enum ('critical, high, default, low') and reject an out-of-enum value in cmdDevicesSet before the request is built, so the CLI fails locally with a usable message instead of relaying a spec-validation 400.

findings.title: `hmcli events tail --json` silently drops the broadcast envelope's `kind` field, contradicting its own 'the original frame is re-encoded' contract.
findings.claim: The daemon's broadcast envelope is internal/north/rest/ws/client.go:416-423 outboundEvent{Seq, Kind, Topic, Type, TS, Payload}, and Kind is always populated — client.go:606-626 defaults an empty Kind to KindChange before marshalling, so every frame on the wire carries `"kind":"initial"|"change"|"refresh"` (ADR 0022). hmcli decodes into eventsInbound (cmd/hmcli/events.go:43-53), which has no Kind field, and printEvent's JSON branch (events.go:419-427) re-marshals *that struct*, not the received bytes, even though its doc comment states 'the original frame is re-encoded as a single compact JSON line'. `kind` is therefore absent from every JSONL line. Secondarily, eventsInbound.Seq is `int64` with `omitempty` (events.go:52) against the server's `uint64` without omitempty, so a seq of 0 would also vanish.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator pipes `hmcli events tail --json --topics device.*` into a script that wants only real changes and filters `select(.kind == "change")`. Every line has no `.kind`, so the filter matches nothing and the pipeline is silently empty — while the same stream read over the raw WebSocket carries the field.
findings.verified_by: code trace: cmd/hmcli/events.go:43-53 and :419-427 vs internal/north/rest/ws/client.go:416-423 and :606-626
findings.fix_sketch: Add `Kind string \`json:"kind,omitempty"\`` to eventsInbound (and drop omitempty from Seq), or — better for the stated contract — keep the raw `data []byte` from ReadMessage and write it through json.Compact in the --json branch so unknown future fields survive too.

findings.title: The diagnostics capture archive contains only logs + a capture-metadata sidecar; the package doc promises build metadata and a diagnostics dump that buildArchive never writes.
findings.claim: internal/diagnostics/capture.go:10-13 states 'the buffered ndjson stream is wrapped in a tar.gz that also contains a snapshot of build metadata + the diagnostics dump at stop time'. buildArchive (capture.go:418-454) writes exactly two members: `logs.ndjson` (the sink snapshot) and `capture.meta.json`, whose map (capture.go:427-438) holds only id/started_at/ends_at/stopped_at/status/anonymised/events/buffer_bytes/triggered_by/overrides — no build version, no commit, no diagnostics dump. Nothing downstream adds members either: Manager.OpenArchive (capture.go:383-399) copies the stored bytes verbatim and handlers.DownloadCapture (internal/north/rest/handlers/diagnostics_capture.go:164-193) writes them unchanged.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator follows the documented support flow, records a capture and attaches the .tar.gz to an issue. The archive cannot be attributed to a build: it contains no version, commit or build date, and none of the runtime diagnostics dump the doc promises, so the first triage question ('which version is this?') needs another round trip.
findings.verified_by: code trace: internal/diagnostics/capture.go:10-13 vs :418-454, :383-399 and internal/north/rest/handlers/diagnostics_capture.go:164-193
findings.fix_sketch: Either add a `build.json` member (internal/build Version/Commit/BuildDate) plus the diagnostics dump to buildArchive, or reword the package doc to describe the two members it actually produces.

findings.title: RemoveFabric does not purge the AccessControl cluster's in-memory per-fabric Extension map, so a fabric index reused by a later commissioning inherits the removed controller's Extension rows
findings.claim: `AccessControl.extensions` is an in-memory `map[uint8][]AccessControlExtensionEntry` keyed by fabric index (internal/north/matter/cluster/core/access_control.go:44-50), written by the Extension write path (access_control.go:624-628) and read per fabric on both the filtered and unfiltered read paths (access_control.go:266, 322). `handleRemoveFabric` (internal/north/matter/cluster/core/operational_credentials.go:1877-1946) deletes the persisted fabric row and relies on FK CASCADE for the DB-backed fabric-scoped tables ('matter_node_identities, matter_group_keys, matter_group_key_map, matter_acl_entries', comment at operational_credentials.go:1891-1897), and the daemon's teardown closure fans out to opMgr.CloseFabric / subMgr.CloseFabric / RemoveResumptionsByFabric (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_matter.go:1087-1117). Nothing in either path reaches the AccessControl cluster instance, and grep shows `extensions` has no delete site at all - the only writes are the map creation and the per-fabric assignment. Fabric indices are reused (AddNOC allocates from the store's free indices), so the next controller commissioned into the freed index reads the previous controller's Extension blobs back as its own. Two related gaps in the same area: the Extension write path does not emit the spec-mandated AccessControlExtensionChanged event (0x0001) that chip and matter.js fire on every Extension mutation - the event is declared in MatterEvents() (access_control.go:668-672) with a comment claiming 'no emission path is wired because Extensions are not implemented in v1.1', and notes/parity/by_design.md BD-Matter-v13-D-AccessControl-Extension-WriteHandler likewise claims 'MatterWrite returns read-only error for the Extension attribute' - both statements are refuted by access_control.go:592-630, which implements the write.
findings.failure_scenario: Controller A is commissioned (fabric index 1) and writes AccessControl Extension metadata. The operator unpairs it (RemoveFabric or the REST revoke). Controller B is later commissioned and is assigned fabric index 1. B reads 0x001F:0x0001 on its own fabric-filtered session and receives A's vendor-opaque Extension blobs as if it had written them. (Today the disclosure is masked by finding F4-matter-behaviour-2, which encodes the attribute as null on the wire; fixing that finding alone makes this one observable.)
findings.verified_by: code trace: access_control.go:44-50 (in-memory per-fabric map), :624-628 (only write site), :266 and :322 (read sites), grep over the file shows no delete/purge; operational_credentials.go:1877-1946 and cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_matter.go:1087-1117 contain the complete RemoveFabric fan-out and neither touches the cluster instance. The stale doc claims were checked against the code at access_control.go:592-630 and notes/parity/by_design.md.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an `OnFabricRemoved`-style hook on AccessControl (mirroring core.OperationalCredentials.SetOnFabricRemoved) that deletes `extensions[fabricIndex]` and bumps the DataVersion, and call it from matterFabricTeardown so every removal surface (wire RemoveFabric, REST revoke, factory reset) purges it. While there, emit AccessControlExtensionChanged on the Extension write and correct the two stale claims (the MatterEvents comment and the by_design entry) that say Extension writes are unimplemented.

findings.title: The readdedDevice callback runs one full interface-wide listDevices refresh per address although the refresh takes no address
findings.claim: CallbackHandlers.ReaddedDevice (callback_handlers.go:714-744) opens one background goroutine with a 30 s budget (line 665/731: context.WithTimeout(h.ctx, 30*time.Second)) and then loops `for _, addr := range addresses` calling BOTH h.unit.Devices.InvalidateFirmwareCache(iface, addr) (correctly per-address) AND h.unit.Devices.RefreshDeviceDescriptionsAndCreateMissingDevices(bgCtx, fetcher, iface) (line 735). The latter is address-independent: internal/central/coordinators/device.go:643-687 takes only (ctx, fetcher, iface) and its first act is fetcher.ListDevices(ctx, iface) (device.go:651), i.e. a full XML-RPC/BIN-RPC listDevices returning every device and channel description on that interface, followed by a descs.Put per entry. Nothing in the loop body varies with addr for that call, so the work is repeated len(addresses) times verbatim. The XML-RPC sibling UpdateDevice (line 664-673) calls it exactly once, which is the correct shape.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator re-pairs several devices in one install-mode session; the CCU answers with a single readdedDevice(interface_id, [addr1..addrK]) callback. The daemon issues K identical full-inventory listDevices calls against the CCU inside one 30 s context. On a large installation a single listDevices already takes several seconds, so the later iterations run out of budget and each logs `callback.readded_device.refresh_failed` with a context-deadline error — the operator sees repeated failures in the log for an operation that in fact only needed one refresh.
findings.verified_by: code trace: callback_handlers.go:730-742 (the loop) against internal/central/coordinators/device.go:643-687 (the callee's signature and body, which never reads an address)
findings.fix_sketch: Hoist the refresh out of the loop: invalidate the firmware cache per address inside the loop, then call RefreshDeviceDescriptionsAndCreateMissingDevices once after it.

findings.title: The XML-RPC callback listener drops an unroutable callback with a 404 and no log record at any level, so a stale or mismatched CCU registration is undiagnosable
findings.claim: XMLRPCServer.ServeHTTP (xmlrpc_server.go:193-225) has two drop branches. resolveCentralForPath returning !ok (line 201-206) and handlers==nil (line 210-214) each do exactly `s.errorCount.Add(1); http.Error(w, ..., 404); return` — neither touches s.logger, which the struct carries (line 33) and which every other failure path in the package uses. resolveCentralForPath (line 282-298) rejects any path that is not exactly /RPC2/<valid-central-name>, and rejects the bare-root legacy shape whenever more than one central is registered (line 291). The BIN-RPC sibling by contrast logs every dropped callback at Warn (binrpc_server.go:300-306) precisely because 'a push channel that silently drops its payload looks identical to a quiet one'. The XML-RPC listener, which carries the events of every non-CUxD interface, does not apply that rule to its own routing layer.
findings.failure_scenario: A central is renamed (or a second central is added while an older CCU firmware still posts callbacks to the bare root, the shape the code comment at line 188-191 exists for). Every event the CCU pushes is answered 404 and discarded. The daemon looks healthy, /health on the callback listener stays 'healthy' with only error_count creeping up, and the log — at any level, including debug — says nothing at all. The operator sees 'device values stopped updating' with no evidence pointing at the callback route.
findings.verified_by: code trace: xmlrpc_server.go:193-225 and 282-298 contain no logger call on either drop branch; contrasted with binrpc_server.go:281-306 which logs both the decode failure (Debug) and the dispatch fault (Warn)
findings.fix_sketch: Log both drop branches at Warn with the (truncated) request path and remote address, mirroring the BIN-RPC listener's reasoning; a rate limit or a first-occurrence-per-path guard keeps a scanner from flooding the log.
