findings.title: assets/openapi.yaml uses the OpenAPI 3.0 keyword `nullable` in a 3.1 document, so six fields the API documents as nullable - and does return as null - are typed non-nullable for every generated client.
findings.claim: The document declares `openapi: 3.1.0` (assets/openapi.yaml:1), where schemas are JSON Schema 2020-12 and `nullable` is not a keyword - a validator ignores it, so `{type: boolean, nullable: true}` means 'boolean, null is invalid'. Six such declarations remain: PUT /history/recording's `record` (:9545, whose own description says 'null clears the override'), PUT /devices/{addr}/channels/{no}/team's `team` (:2839, 'null/empty resets to the default team'), DeviceDetail.availability's BatteryLevel / LowBattery / SignalStrength (:8826-8828) and ConfigField.default (:11775). The file elsewhere shows the rule is known: line 2323 carries the comment 'null - OpenAPI 3.1 has no `nullable` keyword.' Validating the live responses confirms the daemon really does emit null there: GET /devices/{addr} returned availability.BatteryLevel: null, which fails the declared `type: integer`.
findings.failure_scenario: The generated TypeScript/Python types declare batteryLevel: number and record: boolean. A client that validates responses rejects a battery-less device; a client that sends `record: null` to clear a history-recording override - the documented way to do it - is rejected by its own generated validator, and a strict server-side validator (the daemon does load assets/openapi.yaml as a request validator in the Docker image) would reject the request too.
findings.verified_by: spec inspection plus schema validation of the live GET /devices/{addr} response ($S/repro/G1/get_results2.json)
findings.fix_sketch: Replace each `nullable: true` with the 3.1 spelling - `type: [integer, 'null']` or `oneOf: [{type: integer}, {type: 'null'}]` - matching the comment already present at line 2323.

findings.title: Every access-log record contains the key `request_id` twice, producing JSON objects with a duplicate key.
findings.claim: middleware.Logger appends `slog.String("request_id", RequestIDFrom(r.Context()))` explicitly (internal/north/rest/middleware/middleware.go:100) while reqctx.ContextHandler.Handle already appends `slog.String("request_id", rc.RequestID)` for every record that carries a RequestContext (internal/reqctx/handler.go:43). Both fire, so the emitted JSON object carries the key twice. The same file shows the failure mode was recognised for a sibling key and guarded there: 'suppressing a 0-valued elapsed here avoids a duplicate same-name key alongside the StartOp closer's elapsed_ms' (handler.go:46-50).
findings.failure_scenario: Measured: 152 of 152 http.request lines in the daemon log carry `"request_id"` twice, e.g. {...,"request_id":"e9397dc5-...","request_id":"e9397dc5-...","operation":"GET /api/v1/info",...}. Duplicate keys are undefined in JSON: Go's own encoding/json silently keeps the last, jq keeps the last, but strict ingesters (some Loki/Vector/Elasticsearch pipelines) reject the line outright, and a log-shipping config that rejects a record drops the entire access log rather than one field.
findings.verified_by: log inspection (awk count over the daemon log, $S/repro/G1/EVIDENCE.md section 9) plus the code trace
findings.fix_sketch: Drop the explicit slog.String("request_id", ...) from middleware.Logger and let reqctx.ContextHandler supply it, mirroring how elapsed_ms is already deduplicated.
findings.resolution: request_id is emitted once per access-log record
findings.status_verified_at: dea785a1 (pre-#606 HEAD); the open two re-checked on 4eecb1e6

findings.title: The JSON-RPC client only re-logs-in on CCU error code 400, so a session rejected with any other code is never renewed and every hub refresh job fails for the rest of the process lifetime.
findings.claim: callOnce recovers from an expired session in exactly two places: HTTP 401/403 (internal/client/transport/jsonrpc/client.go:305-315) and the JSON-RPC error code ccuAccessDeniedCode = 400 (:112-115, checked at :337). Any other error code falls through to `return c.wrap(method, &hmerr.JSONRPCError{...})` (:342) without invalidating the cached session id, so the client keeps sending the dead session forever. Renew() cannot save it either: it skips the round-trip entirely while lastSessionRefresh is younger than jsonSessionAge (:490-497), and when it does run and the server answers `true`, it keeps the id (:506-510) - which is what happened here, 4 ms before the next call was rejected.
findings.failure_scenario: Observed on a clean daemon against godevccu: at 13:08:41.514 the client logged 'jsonrpc session renewed', and at 13:08:41.518 Interface.listInterfaces failed with -32002 'Session expired'. From that instant every JSON-RPC-backed scheduler job failed on every tick and never recovered - hub.connectivity_refresh, hub.install_mode_refresh, hub.sysvar_refresh and hub.program_refresh were still failing 6 minutes later and, on the second daemon, 50 minutes later. System variables, programs, install mode and the connectivity aggregate silently freeze at their boot snapshot. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: -32002 is godevccu's ErrSessionExpired sentinel (godevccu internal/jsonrpc/errors.go:20), and the repo already carries a TODO for mapping it (tests/e2e/harness/config.go:150, tests/integration/jsonrpc_test.go:183). A real CCU signals an invalid session as HTTP 401/403 or code 400, both of which the ladder does handle - so on real hardware this exact path is not reached, and I could not verify that any real CCU/OpenCCU firmware ever returns a third code. What IS certain is that the whole integration/e2e fleet runs against a CCU whose hub refresh dies ~2 minutes into every run, which makes those suites blind to hub-refresh regressions.
findings.verified_by: measurement on a clean daemon (log evidence above) plus the code trace; NOT verified against real CCU firmware - I could not confirm any real CCU returns a session-error code other than 400/401/403
findings.fix_sketch: Treat the whole auth-failure family, not a single code, as 'session gone': invalidate the cached session and retry once for any error the CCU classifies as authentication/session related (401/403, code 400, and the -32001/-32002 pair the reference simulator emits), which is what the existing TODO asks for.

findings.title: A subscribe frame with a missing, empty or wrongly-typed topics list is silently discarded - no ack, no error - so the client waits forever for the acknowledgement the contract promises
findings.claim: Three silent paths in dispatchMessage (client.go:518-548). (1) A frame whose JSON does not fit inboundMessage - e.g. topics sent as a string - fails json.Unmarshal and is dropped with a server-side Warn and `return true` (client.go:523-527), even though the doc comment two lines above says a binary message is failed rather than silently discarded 'so a client that sends one learns why instead of waiting on a reply that never comes'. (2) sendAck returns without writing anything when len(topics) == 0 (client.go:672-675), so a subscribe with an empty or absent list gets no ack. (3) The op switch has no default, so an unknown or misspelled op ('subscrbe') falls through silently. assets/wsapi.json's subscription_ack section states the daemon echoes one {op:"subscribed"} frame after every subscribe/unsubscribe.
findings.failure_scenario: Sent {op:"subscribe",topics:"notalist"}, {op:"subscrbe",topics:["*"]}, {op:"subscribe"} and {op:"subscribe",topics:[]}: all four produced no frame at all within a 3 s read window, while {op:"subscribe",topics:["device.*.does.not.exist"]} was acked normally. A client that (correctly) waits for the documented `subscribed` ack before considering itself connected hangs; a client that does not wait believes it is subscribed and then silently receives nothing, which is indistinguishable from an idle daemon.
findings.verified_by: measurement + code trace. Live frame probe in this run; trace client.go:518-548 and 672-681.
findings.fix_sketch: Answer every unusable inbound frame: send {op:"error", code:"bad_request"} (or a close with a reason) for an undecodable message and for an unknown op, and ack an empty topics list rather than returning early - silence is the one response the wire contract does not define.
findings.resolution: a malformed or empty subscribe frame is answered instead of discarded
findings.status_verified_at: dea785a1 (pre-#606 HEAD); the open two re-checked on 4eecb1e6

findings.title: WS commands report not-found conditions as internal_error, so a client cannot distinguish a bad id from a broken daemon
findings.claim: Handlers wrap every domain error in NewCommandError(CommandErrorInternal, ...) regardless of its kind, while a neighbouring family gets it right. Measured: devices.get{address:"NOPE"} -> internal_error 'ws: device not found: NOPE'; sysvars.set{name:"DoesNotExist"} -> internal_error 'ws: sysvar not found'; programs.execute{id:"999999"} -> internal_error 'ws: program not found'; programs.delete{id:"999999"} -> internal_error 'hub: program not found'; cdp.invoke{operation:"self_destruct"} -> internal_error 'ws: unknown operation'; calc_dp.get for an absent DP -> internal_error. By contrast alarm_panel.readiness / walktest_status / arm return the correct not_found for an unknown zone, and the same handlers use bad_request correctly for missing or mistyped arguments.
findings.failure_scenario: An external client (or the SPA) that retries or raises an alert on internal_error - the reasonable reading of 'the server failed' - retries or alarms on a plain typo, while a genuine daemon fault looks identical to a bad id. The taxonomy is part of the published contract via the envelope's error.code.
findings.verified_by: measurement. Negative-argument sweep over the WS surface in this run (32 probes); the alarm_panel family is the in-tree counter-example.
findings.fix_sketch: Map hmerr not-found sentinels to CommandErrorNotFound in the shared error-wrapping helper the handlers use, rather than at each call site, and pin it with a table test over the lookup-by-id commands.
findings.resolution: cdp.invoke's unknown operation is classified as not-found, not internal_error
findings.status_verified_at: dea785a1 (pre-#606 HEAD); the open two re-checked on 4eecb1e6

findings.title: install_mode.* takes the bare interface type name in an argument called interface_id, and rejects the interface_id every other surface publishes
findings.claim: installModeEnableHandler / disable / search pass args.InterfaceID straight to the hub's install-mode registry (commands_default.go:888-915), which is keyed by the CCU interface type ('HmIP-RF'), not by the daemon's composite interface id ('<central>-<iface>'). Every other surface publishes the composite form: devices.list returns interface_id "ccu-g2-HmIP-RF", the connectivity.changed broadcast topic is hub.{central}.connectivity.{interface_id}, and ccu.get_signal_quality returns interface_id "ccu-g2-HmIP-RF". install_mode.status is keyed by the bare name, so the two install-mode commands are at least self-consistent - but nothing in assets/wsapi.json says the argument named interface_id means something different here.
findings.failure_scenario: install_mode.enable{interface_id:"ccu-g2-HmIP-RF", duration_seconds:60} -> internal_error 'enable_install_mode: ws: install mode for interface "ccu-g2-HmIP-RF" not registered'; the identical call with "HmIP-RF" succeeds. A client that takes interface_id from devices.list or from the connectivity broadcast - the obvious source, and the only one the schema documents - cannot put the CCU into install mode at all, and the error text reads like a daemon fault rather than a naming mismatch.
findings.verified_by: measurement + code trace. Both argument forms exercised live; trace commands_default.go:888-915.
findings.fix_sketch: Accept both forms in the install-mode handlers (strip a leading '<central>-' when the raw key misses), and say in assets/wsapi.json which identifier the argument expects.
findings.verify_reasoning: First, the premise in my brief is wrong: the finder did NOT rate this critical. G2-ws-mcp-live.json and merged.json both carry severity `low` with _final_severity `low`. So there is no critical rating to defend, and none would be justified. The behaviour itself reproduces exactly. Against my daemon: install_mode.enable{interface_id:"ccu-v12-HmIP-RF"} -> internal_error 'enable_install_mode: ws: install mode for interface "ccu-v12-HmIP-RF" not registered'; the same call with "HmIP-RF" -> success; install_mode.disable behaves the same; ccu.get_signal_quality returns interface_id "ccu-v12-HmIP-RF", so the two id spaces really do collide under one argument name, and assets/wsapi.json documents the argument only as `"interface_id": "string"`. What keeps this low is that the workaround is not merely available but sits in the same command family and is the natural discovery path: install_mode.status returns a map KEYED BY THE BARE NAME -- I measured {"HmIP-RF": {"enabled": false, "observed": true, "remaining_seconds": 0}} -- so a client that reads status and feeds the key into enable works first try, and the REST twin POST /install-mode/interfaces avoids the ambiguity entirely by taking `interface` and `central` as separate fields. Two things sharpen the finding without raising it: HEAD (34b0f4c9, the 0.61.4 install-mode wire-id follow-up) just changed the REST hub-data-points aggregate to publish install-mode entries under the COMPOSITE id (hub_data_points.go:153-165), so the daemon now emits both forms for install mode from two different surfaces; and the error text reads like an internal fault rather than a naming mismatch, which is what makes it cost a client author time. It is a naming inconsistency with an in-surface workaround: low.

findings.title: Removing a central leaves its Matter exposure allowlist rows, so matter/status.enabled_count counts endpoints that can never exist
findings.claim: `removeCentral` purges values-cache, master-values, history and recording rows via `purgeCentralState` (cmd/openccu-loom/central_adopt.go:610) but not the Matter exposure allowlist. GET /api/v1/matter/exposable is derived from the live model and correctly drops the removed central, but the `enabled_count` in GET /api/v1/matter/status is computed from the persisted allowlist and keeps the orphaned rows.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured: enabled 2 Matter exposures on the runtime-adopted central `ccu-g3b`, then deleted the central. GET /api/v1/matter/status then reported `endpoint_count: 0, enabled_count: 2`; after enabling 2 real exposures on the remaining central it reported `endpoint_count: 2, enabled_count: 4`. The operator's Matter page shows a permanent discrepancy between 'enabled' and 'exposed' that nothing in the UI can resolve.
findings.verified_by: measurement — GET /api/v1/matter/status and /api/v1/matter/exposable before and after DELETE /api/v1/centrals/ccu-g3b
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the central's rows from the Matter exposure allowlist store inside purgeCentralState, next to the other per-central row purges.

findings.title: OpenAPI documents an un-ignore pattern grammar the parser rejects, and the endpoint answers 200 with applied_count 0
findings.claim: assets/openapi.yaml:10510 describes `UnIgnoreUpdateRequest.patterns` items as `"MODEL:CHANNEL:PARAMETER pattern; bare names map to *:*:NAME"`. The real grammar in internal/store/visibility/parser.go:83-104 is `PARAMETER` (simple) or `PARAMETER:PARAMSET@MODEL:CHANNEL` (complex); a colon without an `@` is an explicit parse error. The handler still returns HTTP 200 (internal/north/rest/handlers/visibility.go:301-306) with the failures only in a `parse_errors` array.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured: `PUT /api/v1/visibility/unignore {"central_name":"ccu-g3","patterns":["*:*:DUTY_CYCLE"]}` — the exact form the spec documents — returned HTTP 200 with `{"applied_count": 0, "parse_errors": ["invalid pattern \"*:*:DUTY_CYCLE\": invalid format: ':' without '@' in '*:*:DUTY_CYCLE'"], "affected_devices": 4, "patterns": []}`. A client written against the OpenAPI spec silently un-ignores nothing while getting a success status, and the response even claims 4 devices were affected.
findings.verified_by: measurement — live PUT against the daemon; code trace of internal/store/visibility/parser.go:83-104
findings.fix_sketch: Correct the OpenAPI description to the real grammar (`PARAMETER` or `PARAMETER:PARAMSET@MODEL:CHANNEL`), and return 400 when every submitted pattern failed to parse.

findings.title: Every HTTP-Basic-authenticated REST request pays a full bcrypt cost-12 verification with no verifier cache
findings.claim: `MemoryUserStore.AuthenticateBasic` runs `bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword` per call (internal/auth/auth.go:347) at `bcryptCost = 12` (:293), and the unknown-user path runs an equal-cost dummy compare (:343). Nothing caches a successful verification, so every single Basic-auth request on every endpoint pays the full KDF.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured on this (slow, 4-core, contended) machine: GET /api/v1/health took 2.4-3.2 s with `-u admin:pw` and 0.006-0.06 s unauthenticated; GET /api/v1/metrics took 2.3-3.1 s with Basic and 0.007-0.21 s with a Bearer token. A standalone `bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword` at cost 12 measured 2.08-2.30 s here, i.e. the whole request latency is the KDF. On the project's actual deployment targets (Raspberry Pi / CCU add-on) cost 12 is typically several hundred ms to ~1 s, so a polling integration that uses Basic auth serialises behind one KDF per request. Numbers on faster hardware will be lower; the per-request cost is structural.
findings.verified_by: measurement — curl timings against the running daemon plus a standalone Go bcrypt timing program on the same host
findings.fix_sketch: Cache a short-lived (seconds) verification result keyed by subject + a hash of the presented password, or issue a session/token after the first Basic verify. Document Bearer tokens as the intended machine-to-machine path if the cost is deliberate.

findings.title: Five jsonrpc.Client wrappers encode methods, parameter names or result shapes the real CCU does not accept; all are currently callerless, so nothing fails until someone wires them
findings.claim: Each item measured against OttoGo (firmware 3.89.8.20260719) and cross-checked against the CCU's own /www/api/methods inventory. (a) methods.go:65 GetSystemInformation calls System.getSystemInformation -> `401 method not found`; there is no system/getsysteminformation.tcl. IsServiceAvailable (methods.go:650-653) is defined as 'true when the call succeeds', so it would answer false on every real CCU; both are callerless outside the package. (b) methods.go:812-816 GetLinkInfo sends {interface, sender, receiver}, but interface/getlinkinfo.tcl reads `$args(senderAddress)` / `$args(receiverAddress)` - the sibling CcuBackend.GetLinkInfo (backends/ccu_extended.go:984-987) sends the correct names, so the wrapper is the odd one out and would 402. (c) methods.go:676-682 GetSuppressedServiceMessages sends "channel" (live: `402 missing argument (channelAddress)`) AND declares the result as []map[string]any while the CCU returns a JSON string (see finding 3). (d) methods.go:158-162 GetAllDeviceData is documented as 'a map keyed by channel address' but calls Interface.listDevices, which live returns an ARRAY of device descriptions ([{"type":"HmIP-SMO230","address":"0030E2698AFA9D","paramsets":[...],"children":[...]},...]) - decoding that into map[string]any always fails. (e) methods.go:187-191 HasProgramIDs calls Program.getByID -> `401 method not found` (the CCU has program/get.tcl, not getbyid); CcuBackend.HasProgramIDs swallows the error with `return false, nil` (backends/ccu_extended.go:1058-1062), so it would silently answer 'program does not exist' for every program. Also confirmed absent on real hardware and only reachable through documented ReGa-preferred fallbacks: Message.getAll (backends/ccu_extended.go:273) and Interface.getAllDeviceData (backends/ccu_extended.go:566).
findings.failure_scenario: No user impact today - every one of these is either callerless or guarded by a ReGa-preferred branch. The defect is that the wrapper layer looks like a validated CCU contract and is not: the next feature that reaches for jsonrpc.Client.GetLinkInfo or HasProgramIDs gets a call that 402s or silently answers false against every real CCU, with green unit tests, because the simulator does not implement these methods either.
findings.verified_by: live calls for (a), (c), (d), (e) and the CCU's own getlinkinfo.tcl argument list for (b); full method inventory in $S/repro/G4/out/ccu_methods_files.txt and $S/repro/G4/out/ccu_method_args.txt
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the callerless wrappers rather than keep an unverified contract, or fix them to the CCU's own .tcl argument names and result shapes and pin each against a recorded live response. A contract test that diffs every literal method name in internal/client against a committed copy of the CCU method inventory would catch the whole class.
findings.verify_reasoning: Four of the five sub-items reproduce; item (e) is misattributed and, as written about methods.go, is refuted. (a) CONFIRMED: System.getSystemInformation -> 401 method not found; since IsServiceAvailable (methods.go:650-659) is defined as 'true when that call succeeds', it would answer false on this firmware. (b) CONFIRMED live, not just from source: Interface.getLinkInfo with {interface, sender, receiver} -> 402 missing argument (senderAddress); with {interface, senderAddress, receiverAddress} the CCU accepts the arguments and fails downstream on my dummy addresses (502 unknown device or channel), which is the proof the names are wrong in methods.go:810-818. (c) CONFIRMED: the "channel" spelling -> 402 missing argument (channelAddress), and the declared result []map[string]any cannot match the CCU's JSON string. (d) CONFIRMED: Interface.listDevices returns an ARRAY of device descriptions ([{"type":"HmIP-SMO230","address":"0030E2698AFA9D","paramsets":[…],"children":[…]},…]) while GetAllDeviceData (methods.go:158-166) decodes into map[string]any and documents 'a map keyed by channel address'. (e) REFUTED AS WRITTEN: jsonrpc.Client.HasProgramIDs at methods.go:187-194 calls Channel.hasProgramIds, NOT Program.getByID. That method exists on the CCU (/www/api/methods/channel/hasprogramids.tcl is present) and answered live without error (result null for a program ise id, because it asks about a channel). Program.getByID is what CcuBackend.HasProgramIDs calls (ccu_extended.go:1058) - that one is genuinely 401 and genuinely swallowed by `return false, nil`, so the substance of the complaint is real but belongs to a different file, line, method and type than the finding states. The finding's own framing (no user impact today; the wrappers are callerless - I confirmed no non-test caller outside the package, all apparent hits resolve to the same-named backends.Operations methods) makes low the right severity, unchanged.

findings.title: [C21-schedules-7] The climate write path's unsupported-field filter is a permanent no-op, and its comment claims an effect the code cannot have
findings.claim: In the `case "climate", ""` branch of PutClimateSchedule the raw paramset is passed through ExtractSupportedScheduleFields + FilterRawScheduleByFields with a comment saying it filters ENDTIME_*/TEMPERATURE_* keys the device does not expose. ExtractSupportedScheduleFields only recognises keys of the form `<digits>_WP_<FIELD>` (it cuts on the literal "_WP_" and requires an all-digit prefix). A climate paramset contains only `P<n>_ENDTIME_<DAY>_<slot>` / `P<n>_TEMPERATURE_<DAY>_<slot>` or their bare forms, none of which contain "_WP_", so `supported` is always nil and FilterRawScheduleByFields returns raw unchanged on its `len(supported) == 0` guard. The same file already states this two branches earlier.
findings.failure_scenario: A climate device whose MASTER description declares fewer ENDTIME_/TEMPERATURE_ keys than the 13 slots × 7 days the serializer always emits receives the unsupported keys anyway; the CCU rejects the write and leaves CONFIG_PENDING set — exactly the outcome the comment says the filter prevents. A reader auditing the write path is told the guard exists.

findings.fix_sketch: Recognise the bare `P<n>_ENDTIME_*`/`P<n>_TEMPERATURE_*` key shape in ExtractSupportedScheduleFields (or add a climate-specific field-extraction helper) so the climate branch's filter is not a permanent no-op.

findings.title: [C21-schedules-8] MQTT renders an absent schedule duration as "0ms", the daemon's own encoding for a real zero duration
findings.claim: simpleEntryJSON rewrites an empty Duration/RampTime to the literal "0ms" before publishing. In this codebase "" and "0ms" are two different values: weekprofile.ZeroDuration == "0ms" is documented as the genuine (base 0, factor 0) pair the CCU stores, while "" means "no duration — leave the device's value alone". decodeWireDuration returns "" both for factor 0 and for any factor above MaxTimeBaseFactor, which includes the firmware's "permanent" sentinel (base 7, factor 31) that the lock domain uses for auto-relock-end / unlock / standing permission. The MQTT plane therefore reports "permanent" as "0ms", the opposite duration.
findings.failure_scenario: A door-lock slot whose wire pair is (DURATION_BASE 7, DURATION_FACTOR 31) — schedule.LockActionTable's encoding for lock_autorelock_end / unlock_autorelock_end / autorelock_end — decodes to Duration "" and is published on the Zeitplan attributes topic as `"duration": "0ms"`. A consumer reading the attribute sees a slot that reverts immediately where the device holds the state until further notice.
findings.verified_by: code trace against HEAD 34b0f4c9 (re-read the cited file:line region; unchanged since the audit that reported it, or independently re-derived)
findings.fix_sketch: Publish schedule.Duration/RampTime as "" (or a distinct sentinel) on the MQTT plane instead of rewriting to "0ms", which collides with the genuine (base 0, factor 0) zero-duration encoding.

findings.title: [C3-concurrency-2] Program.EnabledDefault is rewritten by the periodic hub refresh with no lock while REST reads it through an equally unguarded accessor
findings.claim: internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:979 `existing.EnabledDefault = hubEnabledDefault(p.IsInternal, meta.description, opts.programMarkers)` writes a promoted field of a live `*hub.Program` directly, outside any lock — while the sibling sysvar upsert 217 lines below routes the identical field through the guarded whole-descriptor write (internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:1196 `existing.ApplyMeta(hub.SysvarMeta{ ... EnabledDefault: ..., ... })`, which takes s.mu). The read side matches: `Sysvar` deliberately shadows the accessor so the field is read under the same lock — internal/model/hub/sysvar.go:427-431 `func (s *Sysvar) EnabledByDefault() bool { s.mu.RLock(); defer s.mu.RUnlock(); return s.HubDataPoint.EnabledByDefault() }`, documented at :422-426 as existing 'so the EnabledDefault field — which the hub refresh rewrites through [ApplyMeta] under s.mu — is read under the same lock'. `Program` has no such shadow, so a program read falls through to internal/model/hub/generic_data_point.go:172-179 `func (h *HubDataPoint) EnabledByDefault() bool { ... return h.EnabledDefault }` — an unsynchronised field read. Both sides of the program path are therefore unsynchronised; the fix that closed this for sysvars was not applied to programs. Contrast: the program path DID get the guarded treatment for its other refreshed fields — internal/model/hub/program.go:264-273 `UpdateMetadata` routes Name through `p.SetName(name)` and IsInternal through `p.mu`.
findings.failure_scenario: Steady-state daemon with at least one CCU program. The scheduler's program-refresh job (wired at internal/central/adapter/hub_wiring.go:410-419 `Programs: gated(func(ctx) error { loadPrograms(ctx, jc, runner, unit.HubModel, writer, scanOpts) ... })`) runs `loadPrograms` on a scheduler worker goroutine and rewrites `existing.EnabledDefault` on every pass (hub_wiring.go:979). Concurrently an operator's `GET /programs` request builds its DTO on an HTTP handler goroutine at internal/north/rest/handlers/hub.go:433 `e.EnabledDefault = p.EnabledByDefault()`, which reads the same field with no lock. The two accesses have no happens-before edge: a -race build flags it, and the response can report the pre-refresh enabled-by-default flag for a program whose markers just changed, so a program the operator just marked shows up with `enabled_default:false` until the next poll.
findings.verified_by: code trace against HEAD 34b0f4c9 (re-read the cited file:line region; unchanged since the audit that reported it, or independently re-derived)
findings.fix_sketch: Give Program the same lock-guarded EnabledByDefault() shadow Sysvar has, and route the hub-refresh write through it (or an ApplyMeta-style setter) instead of a bare field assignment.

The extracted fan-out (matterFabricTeardown, daemon_matter.go:1085-1116) covers EmitFabricRemoved, BasicInformation.EmitLeave, opMgr/subMgr CloseFabric and RemoveResumptionsByFabric, plus withdrawFabric for mDNS. It does NOT cover two things handleRemoveFabric does inline: `o.dataVersion.Bump()` and the `currentFabric`/pending-commissioning-state clear. The DataVersion is what the IM dispatcher answers DataVersionFilter reads from (internal/north/matter/endpoint/dispatcher.go:977 `v := dv.MatterDataVersion()`), so after a REST/factory-reset revoke the OperationalCredentials cluster still advertises the pre-revoke version.

Fabric 1's controller later re-reads OperationalCredentials with the DataVersionFilter it cached before the revoke; the dispatcher resolves the unchanged DataVersion and answers 'unchanged', so the controller keeps showing the removed fabric in its Fabrics/CommissionedFabrics view until something else bumps the cluster or the daemon restarts.

findings.title: [A1-cmd-3] resolveBridgeUniqueID treats a store read error as 'not persisted' and then overwrites the pinned UniqueID it exists to protect
findings.claim: `if v, ok, err := store.GetSetting(ctx, matterstore.SettingUniqueID); err == nil && ok && v != ""` returns the pinned value only on a clean read. On a non-nil err (GetSetting wraps any non-ErrNoRows scan/query failure — internal/north/matter/store/settings.go:46-55) the function falls through, re-derives the UniqueID from the CURRENT mc.NodeLabel, and unconditionally SetSetting()s it, i.e. it overwrites the persisted quality-F value instead of failing or keeping the old one. This is the 'empty vs failed' shape: a failed read becomes an empty-but-successful result.
findings.failure_scenario: An already-commissioned bridge whose node_label was changed after the UniqueID was first pinned reboots while the SQLite handle returns a transient error for the matter_settings SELECT (locked table, I/O error). The read error is swallowed, a new UniqueID is derived from the new node_label and written over the pinned one. UniqueID carries Matter §11.1.5.13 quality F, so every paired controller sees a different device identity and Apple/Google Home treat all bridged accessories as new — the exact failure the function was added to prevent.

findings.fix_sketch: Treat a non-nil GetSetting error as 'unknown', not 'unset' — return without deriving/overwriting a new UniqueID when the store read failed, and log/report the failure instead.

findings.title: [A9-client-infra-3] ExceptionToFailureReason's new Timeout bucket is unreachable for every south-bound transport error, because all three transports wrap deadline errors in ErrNoConnection, which is tested first
findings.claim: The wave added a timeout classification (isTimeoutError, errors.go:519-525) and documented it as one of the reasons an operator is shown for an interface that is not working. But the ErrNoConnection test at errors.go:501 runs before it, and every transport wraps the error returned by its HTTP/TCP round trip — including context.DeadlineExceeded and net.Error timeouts — in ErrNoConnection. So a CCU that accepts the connection and then stops answering is reported as 'network', never 'timeout'; hmenum.FailureReasonTimeout cannot be produced by any real transport error reaching the two production call sites. The only coverage is synthetic: the table in pkg/hmerr/errors_test.go:562-563 constructs `fmt.Errorf("call: %w", context.DeadlineExceeded)` and a hand-written timeoutNetError, neither of which is a shape the transports emit.
findings.failure_scenario: A CCU whose ReGa is wedged accepts TCP but never answers the XML-RPC init. http.Client.Do returns context.DeadlineExceeded; xmlrpc wraps it as ErrNoConnection; Reconnect -> reconnectFailureReason -> ExceptionToFailureReason returns FailureReasonNetwork at errors.go:501-503 before isTimeoutError is ever consulted. The interface state published on ClientStateChangedEvent (and rendered by the SPA/REST) says 'network', sending the operator to check cabling for a CCU that is reachable but hung, and the timeout bucket the wave introduced is dead on every reachable path.

findings.title: [A4-matter-3] north.matter.dev_rotate_unique_ids no longer rotates the root BasicInformation UniqueID, and a value salted while it was on stays pinned after it is turned off
findings.claim: The wave moved the root UniqueID from a per-read derivation to a value persisted on first sight (matterstore.SettingUniqueID) and pinned through core.Config.UniqueID. DeriveUniqueID still mixes bootid.Salt(), but the salt is only consulted on the one boot that first writes the setting; every later boot short-circuits on the stored string. The DevRotateUniqueIDs knob therefore no longer affects endpoint 0 — and once a salted value has been stored, disabling the knob does not restore the deterministic unsalted value either.

Bridged endpoints rotate (endpoint/materialize.go:355), but the root node keeps the UniqueID stored on the first boot, so the root identity Apple caches never changes and the log line 'per-boot UniqueID salt active' overstates what happens. Symmetrically, a developer who ran one boot with the knob on and then turned it off keeps the random salted UniqueID for the life of the database.

findings.title: [A7-alarm-store-3] The custom-DP half of the un-ignore withdrawal cannot fire in the daemon; the test that justifies it uses the reverse of the pipeline's boot order
findings.claim: ApplyUnIgnoredMarks now calls custom.SuppressUndefinedGenericDataPoints(dev) whenever any VALUES data point is not un-ignored (:251-283). In the real pipeline that pass has already run at device_pipeline.go:751, long before applyUnIgnoredMarks at :866, and it force-marks every VALUES/MASTER data point of a custom-DP device that has no forced usage. SetForcedUsage has no clearing counterpart, so by the time ApplyUnIgnoredMarks runs every candidate already satisfies `hasForcedUsage(dp)` and the re-run is a guaranteed no-op — on boot and on every runtime un-ignore reload (cmd/openccu-loom/visibility_wiring.go:176, visibility_adapter.go:153, which call ApplyUnIgnoredMarks alone). The new test asserts the opposite order ('Boot order: the un-ignore mark first, then the custom-DP suppression pass'), which is the only order in which the guarded block can change anything, so the block is unverified by any test that reflects production. The observable outcome is still correct — the mark's withdrawal falls through to the NoCreate forced usage set at step 751 — so this is a dead branch plus a misleading pin, not a wrong result.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator deletes an un_ignore pattern on a custom-DP device (e.g. HmIP-BROLL LEVEL_2). ApplyUnIgnoredMarks re-runs, ClearUnIgnored drops the mark, and the extra SuppressUndefinedGenericDataPoints walk executes but cannot change a single data point because every one already carries a forced usage. If the pipeline order is ever changed so the suppression pass runs before 751-equivalent marking, the regression this block is meant to catch would ship green, because the only test covering it constructs the inverted order itself.
findings.verified_by: code trace against HEAD 34b0f4c9 (re-read the cited file:line region; unchanged since the audit that reported it, or independently re-derived)
findings.fix_sketch: Either reorder device_pipeline.go so suppressUndefinedGenericDataPoints runs after applyUnIgnoredMarks (matching the test's assumed order), or rewrite the test's boot-order comment and drop the now-dead custom-DP branch from ApplyUnIgnoredMarks.

findings.title: [A9-client-infra-1] classifyRPCOutcome books caller cancellations, throttle shedding and semantic CCU faults as failures, unlike the breaker's own isWireFailure — diagnostics-only noise
findings.claim: The wave wired the previously-dead RPC metrics through Config.RPCOutcomeHook. classifyRPCOutcome (interface_client.go:221-230) knows exactly one non-failure: hmerr.ErrCircuitBreakerOpen. Everything else becomes RPCOutcomeFailed, and the hook (internal/central/adapter/reliability_wiring.go:112-113) turns that into metrics.MetricKeys.CircuitFailure(interfaceID) plus ObserveService(method, ms, hadError=true). The circuit breaker in the same package classifies four error classes as NOT evidence about the wire — isWireFailure (internal/client/reliability/circuit.go:367-382) excludes the breaker's own rejection, semantic XML-RPC faults (isSemanticFault, e.g. Unknown Parameter), the caller going away (isCallerGone: ctx.Err()!=nil && errors.Is(err, context.Canceled|DeadlineExceeded)), and the daemon shedding its own load (ErrThrottleQueueFull, ErrThrottleClosed, ErrSuperseded). Only the first of those four is honoured by the new metrics classifier, so a counter named circuit.failure.<interfaceID> now counts exactly the errors the circuit refuses to count. InterfaceClient.Close() -> Coalescer.Clear() (interface_client.go:626) adds a fifth: every caller parked on a coalesced call is released with ErrCoalescerCleared at shutdown and booked as a wire failure.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator opens a device view in the SPA and navigates away while several getParamset calls are in flight. Each REST handler's context is cancelled, the retrier/throttle hand back context.Canceled, and Call returns it. The breaker correctly ignores this (isCallerGone), so circuit_breakers_open stays 0 and no state transition is published — but classifyRPCOutcome returns RPCOutcomeFailed, so circuit.failure.<iface> is incremented once per abandoned call. GET /api/v1/diagnostics then renders, per central, metrics.rpc with failed_requests > 0, a non-zero FailureRate() (internal/metrics/snapshots.go:37-42) and last_failure_time = now, next to circuit_breakers_open: 0 and a CCU on which every wire call succeeded. The same happens for every routine 'Unknown Parameter' fault raised while probing a write-only parameter, for every command superseded by a newer one, and for every in-flight coalesced call at daemon shutdown.

findings.title: [A9-client-infra-2] Coalescer publishes the result before dropping the map entry, so the purge invariant holds only eventually (racy committed assertion; no operator-visible effect)
findings.claim: The rewrite split what used to be one critical section into two steps performed by two goroutines. run() calls call.settle(v, err) at coalesce.go:209, which closes call.done (coalesce.go:98) and releases every awaiter immediately; only afterwards does run() take c.mu and delete the entry (coalesce.go:211-216). await() returns to its caller as soon as call.done is closed (coalesce.go:241-243). There is therefore a guaranteed window in which every Do for a key has already returned while c.calls[key] still holds the settled call. Before the wave the two were atomic: the old leader did `close(call.done); delete(c.calls, key)` inside the same c.mu section before returning, so no caller could observe the result while the entry still existed. Consequences: (a) InFlight()/Stats().InFlight (coalesce.go:290-307) report a call in flight when none is; (b) Do's admission test is `ok && call.active > 0` (coalesce.go:162) and active only drops when each participant runs leave(), so while participants of a finished group are still waking up, a brand-new caller joins the already-settled call and is handed its result with fn never running for it — Do's own contract at coalesce.go:144 says 'Completed calls are purged so a later invocation starts a fresh run'.
findings.failure_scenario: Observed, not inferred: `go test -race -count=2 ./internal/client/reliability/ ./internal/client/ ./internal/client/transport/jsonrpc/` on f356cb40 fails with `--- FAIL: TestCoalescerEvictionStress1000GoroutinesMultiKey (0.38s) coalesce_eviction_test.go:102: InFlight after drain=1, want 0 (calls map leaked entries)`. The committed test fans out 1000 goroutines over 100 keys, waits for every Do to return, and asserts the map is empty — the invariant the old code held structurally and the new code only holds eventually. It passes in isolation and fails under machine load, i.e. it is a new intermittent CI failure. On the production path (InterfaceClient.Call with a setValue coalesce key, interface_client.go:477) the same window means a caller arriving microseconds after an identical write completed is attached to that finished call, gets RequestCoalescedEvent + a success return, and issues no wire call of its own.
findings.verified_by: code trace against HEAD 34b0f4c9 (re-read the cited file:line region; unchanged since the audit that reported it, or independently re-derived)
findings.fix_sketch: Move the c.mu delete before call.settle (or settle under the same lock section) so InFlight()/Stats() and the purge invariant become atomic again, matching the pre-rewrite shape.

findings.title: [C7-matter-parity-4] chunkReportData cannot split a single oversized attribute report and emits it over budget; the cited MTU constant is refuted by the code
findings.claim: addAttributeReport only starts a new chunk when the current chunk already holds something: `if len(body) > budget && (len(current.Reports) > 0 || len(current.EventReports) > 0)` (reply.go:329, mirrored for events at :348). When a single AttributeReport alone encodes larger than reportChunkPayloadBudget (1100, reply.go:288) the guard is false and the oversized candidate is accepted as-is at :338. The Matter list-element chunking matter.js/chip use for this case (AttributeReportIB carrying a ListIndex per element) does not exist on loom's report path. Separately, the constant's own doc comment (reply.go:280-281) asserts 'the IPv6 minimum MTU caps the wire datagram at 1280 bytes ([udp.MaxDatagramSize])' — udp.MaxDatagramSize is 2048 (transport/udp/listener.go:33), so the only hard backstop sits 768 bytes above the MTU the comment claims it is.
findings.failure_scenario: Descriptor.PartsList on the root and aggregator endpoints is a single attribute holding every bridged endpoint id. Past roughly 350 bridged endpoints on one bridge its encoded report exceeds 1100 bytes, and the chunker ships one ReportData datagram larger than the 1280-byte IPv6 minimum MTU (IP fragmentation, which Matter controllers and border routers commonly drop); past ~2048 bytes the send is refused outright at listener.go:243 and the Subscribe-Initial or Read for that path never completes, so the controller never learns the bridge topology.

findings.title: [C2-spec-drift-5] Six operations are published under the global viewer scope although the router requires admin or operator
findings.claim: openapi.yaml's document-level `security` (openapi.yaml:13-16) is `basicAuth | bearerAuth | openIdConnect:[viewer]`. Every other write in the file carries an explicit `openIdConnect: [operator]` or `[admin]` block, so this is omission, not convention.

Every call returns 403; the operator has no way to tell from the spec which role is actually required. findings.title: GET /api/v1/matter/status never emits commissioning_window_duration_seconds, so the SPA pairing panel loses its countdown whenever it rehydrates an already-open commissioning window
findings.claim: handlers.MatterStatusResponse declares WindowDuration `json:"commissioning_window_duration_seconds,omitempty"` at internal/north/rest/handlers/matter_exposures.go:352, and assets/openapi.yaml:10415-10419 documents it (integer, 0..900). The only production producer is matterStatusReaderAdapter.MatterStatus at cmd/openccu-loom/matter_status_adapter.go:34-65: it sets ListenAddr, Listening, EndpointCount, Advertising, FabricCount, EnabledCount and — at :52-55 — WindowOpen from r.window.CurrentWindow(), but never WindowDuration. The identifier `WindowDuration` appears exactly once in the whole non-test Go tree (its own declaration), confirmed by a token scan over every non-test .go under internal/, cmd/ and pkg/. The snapshot it would have to come from carries no duration either: wire.WindowStatusSnapshot at internal/north/matter/cluster/wire/admincommissioning.go:93-99 has only Status, AdminFabricIndex/IsNull and AdminVendorID/IsNull. With `omitempty` and the uint16 zero value the key is therefore absent from every response. The SPA consumes it in two places: assets/ui/src/lib/stores/matter.svelte.ts:300 `const duration = st.commissioning_window_duration_seconds || 0;` which feeds `remaining: duration > 0 ? duration : null` (:314) and gates `if (duration > 0) startCountdown(duration)` (:317), and assets/ui/src/routes/matter/Matter.svelte:90-92 which renders the `(Ns)` suffix on the 'window open' badge only when the value is > 0. The in-session path is unaffected because openWindow (assets/ui/src/lib/stores/matter.svelte.ts:264-273) uses the duration the user just typed, which is exactly why no test caught it — the Playwright/vitest fixture hard-codes the field at assets/ui/src/routes/matter/MatterPair.test.ts:79.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator opens the Matter commissioning window (SPA, hmcli, curl or another controller) and then reloads the page or switches to the Pair tab in a second browser tab. MatterPair.svelte:20 calls hydrateCommissioning(), which — per its own comment at matter.svelte.ts:275-281 — exists precisely to recover this state. It re-fetches the QR code and manual code correctly, but duration resolves to 0, so `remaining` stays null and startCountdown is never armed: the pairing panel shows the codes with no remaining-time indicator and the status badge shows 'window open' without the duration. findings.title: `translation_key` is not an MQTT-discovery option and is silently dropped by HA; the 19 thermostat button-lock `lock` entities rely on it for their label and carry `name: null`, so they show up in HA unnamed
findings.claim: `applyEntityDescription` writes `setOrDeleteString(body, "translation_key", desc.TranslationKey)` (internal/north/mqtt/entity_descriptions_apply.go:56) and the hub builders set it literally (hub_discovery.go:712,754,831,871,913). Home Assistant's MQTT discovery schema has no `translation_key` key at all (grep over homeassistant/components/mqtt/*.py in the 2026.8.2 checkout finds it only as an argument to service-error helpers), and unknown keys are removed by `extra=vol.REMOVE_EXTRA` - a discovered MQTT entity has no translation file behind it, so the key can only ever be dead. In the generated fleet 213 device-plane entities and 13 hand-built entities carry it. For 194 of them a literal `name` is also present, so the drop is cosmetic. The exception is the `lock` aggregate produced for the HmIP thermostat button lock: 19 entities emit `"translation_key": "button_lock"` with `"name": null` (e.g. homeassistant/lock/ccu-01_vcu1371379/0_lock/config on HmIP-WTH-1; also HmIP-eTRV-E, HmIP-eTRV-B1, HmIP-BWTH, HmIP-FAL230-C10, HmIP-eTRV-B-2 R4M, HmIPW-FAL230-C6, HmIP-WTH-2 ...). `name: null` tells HA to fall back to the device name, so with translation_key discarded the entity is presented as the plain device name - identical to the device's `climate` entity, which is also `name: null` - and the intended 'Button lock' / 'Tastensperre' label never appears anywhere.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator enables the (enabled_by_default:false) button-lock entity on a HmIP-BWTH called 'Wohnzimmer'. HA shows a lock entity simply named 'Wohnzimmer' next to a climate entity also named 'Wohnzimmer', with no indication that the lock is the thermostat's child lock.
findings.verified_by: code trace (HA 2026.8.2 mqtt schemas contain no translation_key option; mqtt/discovery uses extra=vol.REMOVE_EXTRA) + fleet dump: 213 device entities carry translation_key, of which 19 have `name: null`, all of them component=lock with translation_key=button_lock; example payload printed from $S/wt/tests/integration/testdata/discovery_snapshot_openccu-loom.json.
findings.fix_sketch: Either stop emitting `translation_key` from the MQTT builders (it is an HA-native-integration concept), or - for the entities that currently rely on it - resolve the translation key through the daemon's own i18n catalogue and emit the resulting string as `name`. The button-lock lock aggregate in particular must not send `name: null`.
findings.resolution: ALREADY FIXED in 0.63.0 — this entry's evidence was stale: the i18n-resolved name and its pinning test were already present

findings.title: Hub sysvar unique_ids are built from a punctuation-collapsing slug, so two system variables whose names differ only in punctuation collide and Home Assistant registers only one of them
findings.claim: `BuildSysvarDiscovery` derives the entity identity as `routingkey.CanonicalUniqueID(serial10, "sysvar", routingkey.HubSlug(sv.Name), "")` (internal/north/mqtt/hub_discovery.go:216) while the discovery *topic* segment stays `safeLower(sv.Name)` (hub_discovery.go:363). `HubSlug` (internal/routingkey/slug.go:44-66) strips combining marks, lower-cases, and replaces every run of non-[a-z0-9] characters with a single '-', trimming trailing dashes. Two CCU system variables named e.g. `Licht (EG)` and `Licht EG`, or `Alarm-Zone 1` and `Alarm Zone 1`, therefore produce two distinct discovery topics but the *same* `unique_id`. Home Assistant registers the first entity and rejects the second with 'Platform mqtt does not generate unique IDs. ID ... already exists', so one of the two system variables is silently missing from HA while the daemon believes both were announced. Measured in a synthetic matrix over the sysvar builder ($S/repro/J1/nondevice.json): 35 unique_id collisions among 190 entities purely from names that differ in punctuation.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator has both `Licht (EG)` and `Licht EG` on the CCU. Only one of the two appears in HA; the other never shows up, and the only trace is one HA error line at startup. Renaming either variable on the CCU makes the missing one appear, which reads as a random HA glitch.
findings.verified_by: code trace of HubSlug (internal/routingkey/slug.go:44-66) and BuildSysvarDiscovery (hub_discovery.go:216, 363) plus a generated payload matrix showing the collision mechanism. Not verified: that a real CCU installation in the wild actually carries such a name pair - the mechanism is certain, the incidence is not.
findings.fix_sketch: Scope the sysvar unique_id on the CCU-side ise_id (Sysvar.Meta().Vid, already used for PathData) instead of the display-name slug, or append a short hash of the raw name to the slug. A contract test that feeds two names differing only in punctuation through BuildSysvarDiscovery and asserts distinct unique_ids pins it.
findings.resolution: sysvar unique_id keyed on the CCU ise_id; two names differing only in punctuation no longer collide. Entities re-key once (migration note in docs/external-clients/ha-unique-id-migration.md)
findings.status_verified_at: dea785a1 (pre-#606 HEAD); the open two re-checked on 4eecb1e6

findings.title: north.mqtt.payload_format is a fully dead config field that the SPA still presents as a working wire-format switch with EN+DE help describing behaviour that no longer exists
findings.claim: The field is declared at internal/config/config.go:1450 with a doc comment claiming 'Empty / "bare" (default) keeps primitive scalar payloads ... "json" wraps state in {"value":..,"available":..}'. The ONLY production reads of `PayloadFormat` in the whole tree are internal/config/config.go:2246 and :2250 — the validator inside validateMQTT that accepts "", "bare", "json". `grep -rn 'PayloadFormat' --include='*.go' --exclude='*_test.go'` outside internal/config returns only two *comments* (internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go:165 and :1020); no struct field, no branch, no publisher reads it. internal/north/mqtt.BridgeConfig has no PayloadFormat member at all (internal/north/mqtt/payload_format_test.go:23-28 constructs BridgeConfig with the field commented out and asserts a JSON envelope in BOTH the 'bare' and 'json' cases). The publisher path is unconditional: Bridge.renderStatePayload (internal/north/mqtt/bridge.go:1986) always json.Marshal's {value, available, modified_at}, and PublishSlotState always emits the pload.PerDPState JSON envelope. The field is nevertheless rendered by the SPA section editor (it is a cfg:"expert" leaf in section north.mqtt, not in configstore.UnmanagedFieldPaths nor dedicatedEditorPaths, see internal/north/rest/handlers/admin_config.go:175-190) with help text assets/ui/src/lib/i18n.ts:1560 (EN) 'bare keeps primitive scalar payloads (backwards-compat); json wraps state with {value, available}. Flip only after every consumer is upgraded.' and :5666 (DE). docs/admin/configuration.md:372 already states the opposite ('payload_format is currently a no-op / reserved'), so the published docs and the field's own in-product help contradict each other.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator running Node-RED/Telegraf against the raw plane reads the SPA hint, sets north.mqtt.payload_format: bare to keep primitive scalar payloads, saves (200 OK, no error, no restart badge), restarts the daemon — and every state topic still carries the JSON envelope. There is no log line, no validation error and no UI hint; the operator concludes the bridge is broken. Conversely someone who sets 'json' believing they are opting IN also changes nothing.
findings.verified_by: code trace: full-repo grep for PayloadFormat/payload_format (only validator + comments + vestigial tests), plus reading Bridge.renderStatePayload and internal/north/mqtt/payload_format_test.go which asserts the JSON envelope for the 'bare' case too
findings.fix_sketch: Either delete the field (and its validator, i18n entries and example.config.full.yaml line 345) so the schema no longer offers it, or implement the bare mode in the slot-state publisher. Minimum viable fix: rewrite both i18n help strings to match docs/admin/configuration.md's 'reserved / no-op' wording and drop the Go doc comment's behaviour claim.
findings.verify_reasoning: The dead-field mechanism is exactly as described. Repo-wide grep for PayloadFormat/payload_format outside tests yields the declaration (config.go:1450), the validator (config.go:2246-2250) and two prose comments in internal/north/mqtt/discovery.go; internal/north/mqtt.BridgeConfig has no such member, so no publisher can branch on it, and internal/north/mqtt/payload_format_test.go states in its own comments that the PerDPState JSON envelope is emitted in the 'bare' case too ('JSON is now the only supported shape'). The validator is live (executed: payload_format 'bogus' -> `config: mqtt.payload_format: invalid value "bogus" (use bare or json)`), and the leaf is a cfg:"expert" field in section north.mqtt that is in neither UnmanagedFieldPaths nor dedicatedEditorPaths, so the SPA renders it with the quoted EN (i18n.ts:1560) and DE (:5666) help promising behaviour. Downgraded from medium to low on consequence only: 'fully documented' overstates it — the two authoritative operator documents already say the opposite in bold (docs/admin/configuration.md:372 'currently a no-op / reserved' and example.config.full.yaml:340-345 'CURRENTLY A NO-OP / RESERVED'), the field cannot break anything when set (both accepted values behave identically), and the residual harm is a misleading in-product hint plus a stale Go doc comment.
findings.resolution: same fix as I1-comment-claims-1

findings.title: The YAML watcher counts logging.level / logging.format as hot-reloaded and logs success, but nothing ever swaps the slog handler — the documented hot-reload is a no-op
findings.claim: daemonServeWithReload's doc comment (cmd/openccu-loom/reload.go:24-30) declares the hot-reloadable matrix as 'logging.level -> swaps the slog handler at runtime; logging.format -> swaps the slog handler at runtime'. The implementation (cmd/openccu-loom/reload.go:103-110) is: `if prev.Logging.Level != next.Logging.Level || prev.Logging.Format != next.Logging.Format { applied++; logger.Info("daemon.reload.logging", ...) }` — it increments the applied counter and emits one log record, and does nothing else. There is no handler rebuild and no level write: `slog.SetDefault` appears exactly once in the daemon, at cmd/openccu-loom/daemon.go:67, during boot (grep over cmd+internal+pkg, excluding tests, returns only daemon.go:67 and the unrelated cmd/openccu-loom-remote/main.go:39). The hmlog level registry that COULD apply it (`stack.Levels`, daemon.go:61, used by the diagnostics log-level endpoint) is never handed to the reload handler — reloadDeps carries no reference to it. The 'note' attached to the log record ('swap takes effect on next slog.Default() use; existing handlers keep their level until rebuild') is itself false: slog.Default() returns the same logger with the same leveller, and no rebuild ever happens. Because the change is counted as `applied`, it is also NOT reported by the restart-required half of the same handler (reload.go:179-213 lists data_dir, locale, callback, listen, public_url, openapi_validate, centrals — not logging), and `logging` is not a DB-tier section so the schema badge cannot cover it either.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator debugging a south-bound problem edits config.yaml `logging: level: debug` on a running daemon. The daemon logs `daemon.reload.logging level=debug` followed by `daemon.reload.applied hot_reloaded_fields=1` — both of which read as 'done' — and keeps emitting at info. No debug record ever appears, and no message suggests a restart is needed. The operator concludes the debug level is broken.
findings.verified_by: code trace: reload.go:103-110 body has no side effect; repo-wide grep for slog.SetDefault / SetLevel / LevelVar shows the only daemon install point is daemon.go:67; reloadDeps has no Levels field
findings.fix_sketch: Either thread hmlog.Stack.Levels into reloadDeps and call Levels.SetDefault(hmlog.ParseLevel(next.Logging.Level)) in the handler (format cannot be swapped without rebuilding the handler, so it belongs on the restart-required side), or move both fields into the restart-required branch and fix the doc comment. Do not leave them counted as applied.
findings.verify_reasoning: Code side is wrong, doc side is the claim: cmd/openccu-loom/reload.go:24-30 declares logging.level/format as 'swaps the slog handler at runtime', and the handler body (reload.go:103-110) contains only `applied++` and one logger.Info — no handler rebuild, no level write. slog.SetDefault appears once in the daemon (daemon.go:67) and the hmlog.LevelRegistry that could apply a level (stack.Levels, daemon.go:61-62) is never handed to the reload path: reloadDeps (cmd/openccu-loom/reload_deps.go:25-64) carries mqttSup, curCfg, reseed, assemble, mdnsTXTRefresh and two test hooks — no levels field. The attached 'note' is false for the reason given (slog.Default() returns the same logger over the same leveller). Behavioural consequence is real but narrower than 'medium': the surface is the YAML watcher alone (there is no `logging` DB-tier section in configstore.AllSections(), so the SPA cannot even reach it), and a working runtime path exists — PUT /api/v1/diagnostics/log-levels/{path} drives the same registry through LogLevelsService.Set. The residual defect is that the edit is counted as `applied` and therefore also excluded from the restart-required branch, so the one operator-visible signal actively misinforms.
findings.resolution: closed by the 0.62.0 / 0.63.0 fix waves; confirmed still closed on re-verification
findings.status_verified_at: dea785a1 (pre-#606 HEAD); the open two re-checked on 4eecb1e6

findings.title: reliability.command_retry_initial_delay's default is documented as 250 ms in five operator-facing places while the code actually delivers 2 s
findings.claim: Zero means 'use the default' and is threaded through unchanged: cmd/openccu-loom -> internal/central/adapter/ccu_wiring.go:749 and cuxd_wiring.go:118 call newClientRetrier(unit, wireID, relCfg.CommandRetryInitialDelay); newClientRetrier (internal/central/adapter/reliability_wiring.go:133-143) sets cfg.Initial ONLY when initial > 0 and hands the config to reliability.NewRetrier, which at internal/client/reliability/retry.go:183-184 does `if cfg.Initial <= 0 { cfg.Initial = hmreliability.RetryInitialBackoff }`. pkg/hmreliability/defaults.go:47 defines RetryInitialBackoff = 2 * time.Second (with a comment explaining the 2 s value is production-hardened). The effective default is therefore 2 s. Five surfaces say 250 ms: the field's own doc comment internal/config/config.go:526-528 ('Zero (default) keeps the OpenCCU-Loom 250 ms default. Set to 2s to match Production behaviour'), example.config.full.yaml:621 ('0 = openccu-loom default (250 ms)'), docs/admin/configuration.md:673 ('`0` (250 ms default)'), the SPA schema's placeholder consumerDefaults["reliability.command_retry_initial_delay"] = int64(250_000_000) at internal/north/rest/handlers/admin_config.go:73, and both i18n help strings (assets/ui/src/lib/i18n.ts:1787 EN 'Default 250 ms; raise to 2 s to mirror the reference implementation', :5837 DE). No contract test pins the value (tests/contract/reliability_constants_test.go contains neither 250 nor RetryInitialBackoff).
findings.failure_scenario: An operator whose CCU shows retry storms reads the SPA field ('Default 250 ms; raise to 2 s to mirror the reference implementation'), types 2s and saves — believing they just made the retrier 8x gentler. Nothing changes: the daemon was already at 2 s. Symmetrically, an operator tuning a fast test rig computes their retry budget from the advertised 250 ms first backoff and gets timings 8x longer than planned.
findings.verified_by: code trace: newClientRetrier's `if initial > 0` guard -> NewRetrier's `if cfg.Initial <= 0` fallback -> hmreliability.RetryInitialBackoff = 2s (pkg/hmreliability/defaults.go:47, also pinned at 2s by pkg/hmreliability/snapshot_test.go:31)
findings.fix_sketch: Change consumerDefaults to int64(2_000_000_000) and fix the four prose surfaces to say 2 s, or (if 250 ms was the intent) set RetryConfig.Initial explicitly in newClientRetrier. Add the value to tests/contract/reliability_constants_test.go so the schema default and hmreliability.RetryInitialBackoff cannot drift again.
findings.verify_reasoning: The doc side is wrong, the code delivers the hardened value, and the chain is exactly as claimed: ccu_wiring.go:749 / cuxd_wiring.go:118 pass relCfg.CommandRetryInitialDelay into newClientRetrier (internal/central/adapter/reliability_wiring.go:133-143), which sets cfg.Initial only `if initial > 0`; reliability.NewRetrier (internal/client/reliability/retry.go:183-184) then applies `if cfg.Initial <= 0 { cfg.Initial = hmreliability.RetryInitialBackoff }` = 2s (pkg/hmreliability/defaults.go:43-47, whose comment says the 2 s value is production-hardened). applyDefaults never pre-fills the field (grep: the only non-test references are the declaration, the two wiring sites and the restart table). All five 250 ms surfaces verified verbatim: config.go:524-528, example.config.full.yaml:620-622, docs/admin/configuration.md:673, admin_config.go:73 consumerDefaults int64(250_000_000), i18n.ts:1787 EN / :5837 DE. Downgraded to low: there is no behavioural defect at all — the daemon runs on the value the reference stack hardened — the harm is confined to operators mis-tuning from an 8x-wrong advertised default, and the field itself works when set explicitly.

findings.title: The SPA advertises './var/ccu_data/*.json.gz' as the effective default of ccu_data.translations_path / easymode_path, while the real fallback is the archive embedded in the binary — the same field's own help text says so
findings.claim: consumerDefaults (internal/north/rest/handlers/admin_config.go:71-128) is documented at :62-67 as pinning 'the runtime defaults ... the SPA reads these as input placeholders so operators see what they get if they leave a field empty'. Entries :120-121 set ccu_data.translations_path to './var/ccu_data/translation_extract.json.gz' and ccu_data.easymode_path to './var/ccu_data/easymode_extract.json.gz'. The actual consumer does not use any filesystem fallback: loadTranslations (cmd/openccu-loom/daemon_ccudata.go:20-44) takes the configured path only when non-empty and otherwise calls ccudata.LoadTranslationsEmbedded(); loadEasymode (:52-70) is the same shape with LoadEasymodeEmbedded(). No './var/ccu_data/...' path is constructed anywhere. The field's own SPA help contradicts the placeholder: assets/ui/src/lib/i18n.ts:1697 'Defaults to the embedded archive bundled with the binary' (DE :5803 identically).
findings.failure_scenario: An operator who prefers explicit configuration copies the greyed-out placeholder into the field and saves. On the next boot the daemon tries to open ./var/ccu_data/translation_extract.json.gz, which does not exist on any normal install, logs `ccudata.translations.load` at WARN with the path, and falls back to the embedded archive — so labels still work but the log now carries a permanent error the operator caused by following the UI. On the CCU add-on (data_dir=/data) the relative path is wrong in a second way.
findings.verified_by: code trace: loadTranslations / loadEasymode have no filesystem default branch; the placeholder strings appear nowhere else in the tree
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the two consumerDefaults entries (an empty path has no meaningful placeholder here) or replace them with a non-path hint matching the help text.

findings.title: A week-profile / climate-schedule change reaches MQTT only; the ratchet reason claiming it also reaches the SPA is refuted
findings.claim: tests/contract/event_subscriber_coverage_test.go:56 declares WeekProfileChangedEvent consumerless with the reason 'the schedule change reaches MQTT/SPA through ProfileDataPoint.OnChange, not through the bus'. The MQTT half is true; the SPA half is not. The two OnChange callbacks the EventBridge installs are eventbridge.go:2637-2641 (climate profile changed -> b.publishCustomDPState) and :2672-2683 (profile pointer changed -> bridge.PublishWeekProfileState). publishCustomDPState (eventbridge.go:2080-2096) returns immediately when b.mqtt or b.mqtt.Bridge() is nil and only ever writes to the MQTT bridge; PublishWeekProfileState is an mqtt.Bridge method. Neither touches b.wsHub. The WS surface has schedule request/response commands only (internal/north/rest/ws/commands.go:113-120, :213-215) and no schedule broadcast -- the full broadcast inventory is the alarm/security/device-lifecycle/device-trigger/hub/system-status/optimistic-rollback/addon-update set, none of which carries a schedule. publishWeekProfileSnapshot itself (eventbridge.go:2577-2587) also bails on a nil MQTT bridge before wiring anything, so with MQTT disabled the profile OnChange subscriptions are never installed at all.
findings.failure_scenario: A heating schedule is changed on the CCU WebUI, by a CCU program, or by a second OpenCCU-Loom operator. The MQTT climate entity's schedule_data attribute updates within the CONFIG_PENDING settle window; an SPA schedule view that is already open receives no push and keeps showing the previous schedule until the user navigates away and back. With MQTT disabled the OnChange wiring is not installed at all, so the change reaches no push plane.
findings.verified_by: code trace: eventbridge.go:2571-2685 and :2080-2096, ws/commands.go:113-120/:213-215, exhaustive grep of ws Hub.Publish call sites (none for schedules), tests/contract/event_subscriber_coverage_test.go:56
findings.fix_sketch: Either broadcast a schedule.changed WS event from the same OnChange callbacks (and drop the ratchet entry by giving WeekProfileChangedEvent a real WS subscriber), or correct the ratchet reason to say MQTT only. Move the MQTT-bridge nil guard in publishWeekProfileSnapshot below the OnChange wiring so the subscriptions exist regardless of MQTT.
findings.resolution: schedules.changed broadcast added; Profile.OnChange fires only on a real change, not on every warm-up load
